entries.title: Config and env: the remaining unset keys (three of the six were already set)
entries.detail:
🔴 RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19 AND THE ROW WAS WRONG ABOUT HALF ITS OWN CONTENTS. Three of the six items were already satisfied, and the row had been telling the owner to go and do them. The previous evidence line said the rest are "Vercel/Resend dashboard state, not readable here", which is the exact shape ADR-1082 names: a blocker phrased as "cannot be checked" is a claim with an expiry date. The SECRET is unreadable from an agent container. Its CONSEQUENCE is sitting in the database.

ALREADY DONE, do not spend anything on these:
  • Supabase -> Pro. The organization (hkveprznovcteywuczcv) returns plan "pro". Capacity and     backups are on the paid tier already.
  • RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Email metrics are NOT dark. public.email_events over the trailing 30     days holds opened=127, delivered=81 and clicked=3. Those three event types cannot be produced     by our own send path -- nothing server-side knows an email was opened -- so they can only have     arrived through the Resend webhook, which means the secret is set AND the signature check is     passing. Most recent delivered event 2026-08-19T13:04:20Z, i.e. the same day this was measured.
  • VAPID, the PUBLIC half. public.push_subscriptions holds 23 rows, 8 of them created in the last     30 days, most recent 2026-08-10. A browser cannot complete pushManager.subscribe() without     NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY being served to it, so that key is live and members have been     granting permission for two months.

STILL GENUINELY OPEN:
  • VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, the SEND half. Subscriptions prove the public key, not the private one.     lib/push.ts:22 warns '[push] VAPID keys not set - push sending disabled.' and returns false     when either key is missing, so the cheap settling move is a runtime-log search for that exact     string rather than another dashboard trip. Note the queue is quiet (1 notification_queue row in     24h), so absence of the warning in a short retention window is not proof either way -- it needs     a window that contains an actual push attempt.
  • Verify frequencylocal.com in Resend, plus SPF/DKIM/DMARC subdomain isolation. Blocking for     volume. The delivered events above prove sending works TODAY at current volume; they say     nothing about domain reputation at scale, which is what this item is for.
  • Secret-scanning push protection.
  • Dismiss the 3 CodeQL false positives.

CRON_SECRET and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY remain satisfied by consequence: ai_usage holds 50 rows in the trailing 7 days, and the crons are firing.

── RE-EVIDENCED 2026-08-19 from the owner's Advanced Security screenshot: CodeQL advanced setup ACTIVE (scan 36 min prior), Copilot Autofix ON, check-run thresholds set (High+/errors-only). Still DISABLED, each one Enable click on that page: Secret Protection (the push-protection ask), Private vulnerability reporting, Dependency graph, Dependabot alerts + security updates. "Security and quality" badge shows 44 open findings to triage once alerts API access or an owner paste arrives. ── ⚙️ THE VAPID ITEM IS NOW CHECKABLE BY ONE CURL, 2026-08-24. The row said the cheap settling move was a runtime-log search for '[push] VAPID keys not set'. That was tried and the Vercel log query timed out twice, which is a bad place for a fact to live anyway: a console.warn in a log is exactly the invisible fail-safe AGENTS.md warns about. So the consequence was PUBLISHED instead, the same move LIVE-053 made for the Sentry DSN — /api/status now reports monitoring.push, booleanized in lib/push.ts (pushSendingEnabled = PUBLIC && PRIVATE), never the key. WHY BOTH HALVES MATTER, and it is the trap this row already half fell into: push_subscriptions proves only that a browser could SUBSCRIBE, i.e. that the PUBLIC key is served. It says NOTHING about the private key the server signs with. Production carries 24 subscriptions, 5 from the last 30 days (newest 2026-08-20) and five live callers of sendPushToProfile (admin actions, outreach, nearby, the event-reminders cron, the journey-prompt cron) — so two dozen members have granted permission and whether a single notification can leave the process was unanswerable from here. Pinned by two tests and mutation-proven: reading the env directly in the route fails both the new assertion and the existing four-var env allowlist. THE OWNER CHECK IS NOW: curl -s https://frequencylocal.com/api/status | grep -o '"push":[a-z]*' — false means set VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY in Vercel production env and redeploy (the value freezes at build); true closes this item.

── ✅ THE VAPID ITEM IS CLOSED, 2026-08-25, on this row's own stated condition. Production GET https://frequencylocal.com/api/status at 18:14:43Z, build commit 61e1ea2 / ref main / env production, returns `"monitoring":{"sentry":false,"push":true}`. The row said in its own words: "true closes this item". VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY is set in Vercel production and push sending is live. The same payload reports sentry:false, which independently re-confirms LIVE-053's premise rather than this row's.
── 🔴 THE RESEND ITEM WAS TWO-THIRDS ALREADY DONE, and the third that is left is not the third the row names. The row asks to "verify frequencylocal.com in Resend, plus SPF/DKIM/DMARC subdomain isolation" as one undone unit. Measured by DNS 2026-08-25:
  • VERIFIED, and on an ISOLATED SUBDOMAIN already. `send.frequencylocal.com` MXes to inbound-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com (Resend's SES backend) and `resend._domainkey.send.frequencylocal.com` publishes a live DKIM public key. Resend issues neither record until domain verification completes. Subdomain isolation — the whole point of the ask — is therefore DONE: product mail sends from the subdomain, so its bounce and complaint reputation cannot touch the apex that Google Workspace mail sends from.
  • DMARC IS PRESENT AND ENFORCING at the apex: `v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; adkim=r; aspf=r; rua=mailto:hello@frequencylocal.com`. Not p=none. No subdomain record exists, so sp defaults to p and the subdomain inherits quarantine, which is the correct shape.
  • Apex SPF resolves to Google Workspace only (`include:_spf.google.com ~all` through one flattening hop) and apex DKIM is a 2048-bit `google._domainkey`. Correct: the apex sends Workspace mail and nothing else.
  TWO RECORDS ARE GENUINELY MISSING, both on the sending subdomain, both at-volume concerns exactly as this row framed them:
  1. `send.frequencylocal.com` publishes NO SPF TXT (ENODATA — the name exists, it has MX, it has no TXT). Resend's own setup adds `v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all` there. Mail is not broken today: DMARC passes on the DKIM leg under relaxed alignment because the d= domain shares the org domain. But every Resend send currently fails the SPF leg, and at volume that is a reputation signal.
  2. The Resend DKIM key is 1024-bit (`p=` opens MIGfMA0..., the 1024 prefix; the apex Google key opens MIIBIjAN..., the 2048 prefix). Google and Yahoo's bulk-sender rules call for 2048. Rotating to a 2048-bit key in Resend is a dashboard action plus one DNS record.
  So the remaining owner surface on this row is: those two DNS records, secret-scanning push protection, and the 3 CodeQL dismissals. Do not re-spend on Resend verification or on subdomain isolation.

── ✅ THE ADVANCED SECURITY LIST IS NOW ONE ITEM LONG, NOT FIVE, 2026-08-25. The 2026-08-19 note above lists five toggles as DISABLED: Secret Protection, Private vulnerability reporting, Dependency graph, Dependabot alerts, Dependabot security updates. A fresh owner screenshot of the same settings page, read today, shows FOUR of the five now ENABLED — private vulnerability reporting, dependency graph, Dependabot alerts and Dependabot security updates all read as on, and Secret Protection itself reads as enabled. So the row should stop asking for them.
  🔴 ONE THING IS STILL OFF, and it is the exact thing this row and OWN-040 both name: PUSH PROTECTION still renders an "Enable" button, so it is not on. Secret Protection being enabled is NOT the same switch — scanning finds a secret AFTER it is pushed; push protection is the sub-toggle that blocks the push that would leak it. This is the difference between detection and prevention, and only detection is live.
  Same screenshot: the Security-and-quality badge has moved 44 → 76 open findings since 2026-08-19, CodeQL last scanned 34 minutes prior, Copilot Autofix ON. The 76 is a triage surface, not a regression signal on its own — turning the dependency graph and Dependabot on is itself what surfaces new findings, so a rise was the expected consequence of the four enables rather than new debt.
  REMAINING OWNER SURFACE ON THIS ROW, all four items: push protection, the 3 CodeQL dismissals, an SPF TXT on send.frequencylocal.com, and a 2048-bit Resend DKIM rotation.

✅ PUSH PROTECTION IS ON, 2026-08-25, same day the gap was named. A fresh screenshot of /settings/security_analysis shows both 'Secret Protection' and 'Push protection' rendering a DISABLE button, which is what an ENABLED feature renders. Detection and prevention are now both live. Also visible on that read: CodeQL advanced setup with a scan 9 minutes prior, Copilot Autofix ON, AI findings OFF (preview, requires CodeQL DEFAULT setup and this repo runs ADVANCED, so it is unavailable here rather than skipped), and the check-run thresholds at High-or-higher / errors-only.
  THREE ITEMS REMAIN on this row, none of them GitHub: the 3 CodeQL dismissals, an SPF TXT on send.frequencylocal.com, and a 2048-bit Resend DKIM rotation.

—— ⚙️ THE TWO MAIL-DNS ITEMS ARE NOW MEASURED BY A COMMAND, AND ONE OF THEM IS NOT AN OWNER TASK AT ALL. 2026-08-25.
  THE INSTRUMENT: `pnpm check:mail-dns` (scripts/check-mail-dns.mjs) resolves public DNS only — no API key, no dashboard, nothing to leak — and prints a verdict per row. It exists because this row kept costing round trips: three of its five original items turned out to be ALREADY DONE when finally measured, and the two that were real were not the two the row named. A sentence in a backlog outlives the fact it describes; a command does not.
  READING, 2026-08-25: ✅ subdomain isolation (send.frequencylocal.com MX -> inbound-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com) · 🔴 NO SPF TXT on send.frequencylocal.com · 🔴 DKIM 1024-bit · ✅ DMARC p=quarantine with rua · ✅ apex SPF Workspace-only.
  The 1024 figure is now DERIVED, not fingerprinted. The earlier reading identified key strength from the base64 PREFIX ('MIGf' = 1024). That is true today and is still a fingerprint rather than a measurement. The checker parses the DER and reads the modulus INTEGER's length, dropping DER's sign byte. It independently returns 1024, so the prefix reading was right — but it is right for a reason now.
  🔴 ITEM 1 IS REAL AND IS ONE RECORD. TXT on host `send`, value `v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all`, at GoDaddy (the zone is on ns03/ns04.domaincontrol.com). Mail is NOT broken without it — DMARC passes on the DKIM leg under relaxed alignment because d= shares the org domain — but every Resend send fails the SPF leg, and at volume that is a reputation signal.
  ✅ ITEM 2 IS WITHDRAWN AS AN OWNER TASK, and this is the ADR-1082 discipline applied to a row I wrote myself yesterday. The row said 'rotating to a 2048-bit key in Resend is a dashboard action plus one DNS record'. THAT WAS ASSUMED, NOT CHECKED. Resend's own documentation (dashboard/domains/manage-domains, dashboard/domains/introduction, add-a-domain) exposes TLS and tracking options per domain and a Records tab that DISPLAYS the DKIM Resend generated. It documents no key-strength choice and no rotation control. The only lever is deleting and re-adding the domain, which would break sending in the interim and has no stated reason to produce a different key length.
  AND THE STAKES WERE OVERSTATED. Google and Yahoo's bulk-sender rules REQUIRE DKIM to be present and passing, and RECOMMEND 2048-bit. A 1024-bit key passes. So this is a soft recommendation against a platform we do not control, not a deliverability blocker — it is an accepted constraint to raise with Resend support if volume ever makes it matter, and it should stop being carried as a thing the owner can go and do. Sending someone to hunt for a control that may not exist is the same failure as the Stripe funds-flow ask struck from OWN-040 today, twice in one session.
  THE ROW'S REMAINING OWNER SURFACE IS NOW TWO ITEMS: the SPF TXT above, and the 3 CodeQL dismissals.

✅ THE SPF RECORD IS LIVE, 2026-08-25. `pnpm check:mail-dns` now reads 4 of 5 passing: send.frequencylocal.com publishes `v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all`. Every Resend send now passes the SPF leg as well as the DKIM one. The only remaining row is the 1024-bit DKIM, which is WITHDRAWN as an owner task above (no Resend control exists, and 1024 passes).
  ⚠️ TWO JUNK RECORDS WERE CREATED ALONGSIDE IT, exactly the failure mode the instruction warned about, and they should be deleted. The GoDaddy zone now also carries `send.send` -> `v=spf1 include:dc-fd741b8612._spfm.send.send.frequencylocal.com ~all` and `dc-fd741b8612._spfm.send.send` -> `v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all`. Both sit at send.send.frequencylocal.com, a name nothing sends from, created by typing the FQDN into GoDaddy's Name field (which appends the domain) and then GoDaddy's SPF-merge helper auto-adding its flattening partner. HARMLESS BUT NOT NOTHING: a future reader diffing the zone cannot tell which SPF is authoritative, and that ambiguity is how a working record gets deleted by mistake. The real one is the bare `send` row.
  THE ROW'S REMAINING OWNER SURFACE IS ONE ITEM: the 3 CodeQL dismissals.

🔴 THE SPF FINDING WAS WRONG, AND THE CLEANUP I RECOMMENDED WOULD HAVE BROKEN MAIL. Retracted 2026-08-25 on the full zone, which the owner sent after acting on the ask. Fourth wrong reading in one session and the only one that was DANGEROUS rather than merely wasteful.
  WHAT I MEASURED: SPF on send.frequencylocal.com, found none, called it a gap.
  WHAT A RECEIVER MEASURES: SPF on the ENVELOPE SENDER (MAIL FROM / Return-Path), never the From: header domain. For a Resend domain X the MAIL FROM is `send.X`, so for send.frequencylocal.com it is send.send.frequencylocal.com — and that name ALREADY published SPF, correctly, through GoDaddy's `_spfm` flattening: `v=spf1 include:dc-fd741b8612._spfm.send.send.frequencylocal.com ~all` -> `v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all`. Two hops, both live. SPF was never missing.
  🔴 AND I CALLED THE MAIL FROM RECORDS JUNK. The note above this one says the `send.send` TXT and its `_spfm` partner were accidental residue from typing an FQDN into GoDaddy's Name field, and recommended deleting them. THEY ARE RESEND'S OWN RECORDS AND THEY ARE LOAD-BEARING. Deleting them removes the envelope sender's SPF and SES's bounce/complaint path in one action. DO NOT DELETE ANY `send.send` RECORD. That recommendation is withdrawn in full.
  THE TELL WAS IN THE ZONE THE WHOLE TIME: `send.send.frequencylocal.com` MXes to `feedback-smtp.us-east-1.amazonses.com`, SES's bounce and complaint host, which appears on a configured MAIL FROM domain and nowhere else. I had read `send.frequencylocal.com`'s MX (to inbound-smtp, the RECEIVING host) and never looked one label deeper.
  THE RECORD THE OWNER ADDED IS HARMLESS AND CAN STAY. A `v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all` on send.frequencylocal.com is simply never consulted for Resend mail, because the envelope sender is the other name. It is not a duplicate at any single name and it would be correct if anything ever did send from there. Leave it; removing it is another edit for no gain.
  ✅ THE INSTRUMENT IS FIXED, WHICH IS THE ONLY DURABLE PART. scripts/check-mail-dns.mjs now resolves the MAIL FROM domain, asserts the feedback-smtp fingerprint as its own row, and FOLLOWS `include:` hops so a flattened record cannot read as absent. It reports 5 of 6 passing. The sixth is the 1024-bit DKIM, and its fix line now says in the script itself that it is not actionable, so the script cannot send the next reader on the hunt this row already sent the owner on twice.
  THE ROW'S OWNER SURFACE IS ONE ITEM: the 3 CodeQL dismissals.

✅ THE 'DISMISS THE 3 CODEQL FALSE POSITIVES' ITEM IS RESOLVED, 2026-08-25, AND THE NUMBER WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. That figure came from a screenshot months ago and was carried unexamined ever since — the same stale-status failure this row has now produced four times. Measured against the live Security tab: 56 open alerts, not 3. 42 code scanning + 12 Dependabot + 2 secret scanning. And they were not all false positives.
  🔴 SIX WERE REAL AND ARE NOW FIXED (PR #2309), each verified by reading the code rather than trusting the alert:
    1. lib/qr/codes.ts — biased random from a CSPRNG. The slug alphabet is 31 characters and a byte holds 256 values, so `byte % 31` gave the FIRST EIGHT characters ~12.5% more often. /q/<slug> is a guessable namespace. Now rejection-sampled, pinned by a test that ENUMERATES all 256 bytes and asserts each character is drawn exactly 8 times — a proof, not a sample.
    2. scripts/check-mail-dns.mjs — missing regex anchor, raised by CodeQL against code this same PR introduced. `/amazonses\.com$/` accepts evil-amazonses.com. Every host match is now label comparison; the pure helpers moved to scripts/mail-dns-lib.mjs so they are testable.
    3. lib/ai/web/index.ts — double unescaping. Six chained replaces re-read their own output, so `&lt;` reached the model as a literal `<`. One pass with a lookup table.
    4. admin/business-seeder/actions.ts — prototype pollution, 5 alerts. Wire paths used as object keys, so `contact.__proto__` writes onto Object.prototype for the whole process.
    5. supabase/functions/embed/index.ts — String(e) returned to the caller on 500.
    6. lib/importer/reframe/run.ts — system prompt injection. Operator free text was concatenated into `system`, giving admin-typed text the same authority as the voice canon beside it. Directions now ride in the user turn, delimited, with verified facts stated as outranking them.
  🔵 FIFTEEN WERE GENUINELY FALSE POSITIVES, with the reason recorded in PR #2309's body so nobody re-derives it: 9 DOM-as-HTML behind lib/safe-image-src.ts (CodeQL does not model custom sanitizers), 4 insecure-randomness in an analytics session-id fallback and demo jitter, the HTML filtering regexp (loops to a fixed point, output feeds an LLM not a DOM), and the e/c/[token] redirect (HMAC signature-bound via timingSafeEqual).
  ⏳ THE OWNER SURFACE THAT REMAINS IS TWO CLICKS, and they are not the ones this row named: dismiss the TWO SECRET-SCANNING alerts. Both are `whsec_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx` in .env.example — literal x's, verified by grepping the whole tree for a real key and finding none. Dismiss as False positive. The 12 Dependabot alerts need no action: 8 are in resonance/, which is not referenced from the root package.json, next.config or vercel.json and therefore does not ship; 3 are root-lockfile and tagged Development; the sharp/libvips one is resonance-only, so the production app's sharp is unaffected.

✅ ROW CLOSED 2026-08-25. The owner dismissed the two secret-scanning alerts, which was the last item standing. Final accounting of a row that started with six asks and ended with two:
    Supabase Pro                 — was ALREADY DONE when first measured
    RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET        — was ALREADY DONE (proven by opened/delivered/clicked events)
    VAPID public key             — was ALREADY DONE (proven by 23 push_subscriptions)
    VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY            — CLOSED on production /api/status monitoring.push=true
    Resend verification + isolation — was ALREADY DONE (MX + DKIM on the sending subdomain)
    SPF on send.frequencylocal.com — NEVER MISSING. Measured on the wrong name; SPF is evaluated on the envelope sender, and send.send.frequencylocal.com had it all along.
    2048-bit DKIM                — WITHDRAWN. No Resend control exists and 1024 passes.
    Push protection              — DONE by the owner
    3 CodeQL false positives     — the count was wrong (56 alerts, not 3) and SIX were real bugs, fixed in PR #2309. Fifteen were genuine false positives with reasons recorded.
    2 secret-scanning alerts     — DISMISSED by the owner, verified placeholders in .env.example
  🔴 THE PATTERN THIS ROW EXISTS TO TEACH, and it earned the right to be stated: of the ten items this row ever carried, FIVE were already done when someone finally measured, ONE was never real, and ONE was not actionable at all. Three were genuine. A row that is 70% wrong is not a tracking failure at the margins — it is what happens when status is written from a dashboard screenshot once and then carried as fact. Every correction here came from measuring a CONSEQUENCE: a DNS answer, a database row, an /api/status payload, a log line. That is ADR-1082 and the backlog's own probe rule, learned again the expensive way.
  THE INSTRUMENT THAT SURVIVES: `pnpm check:mail-dns` reads the envelope sender, follows include: hops, and prints a verdict per row, so the mail half of this row can never again be described rather than measured.

verify.evidence: CLOSED 2026-08-25 on owner action plus measurement. Push protection enabled (settings page renders Disable). Two secret-scanning alerts dismissed by the owner as False positive — verified placeholders (`whsec_xxxx…` in .env.example, no real key anywhere in the tree). CodeQL item resolved: the '3 false positives' count was wrong in both directions — 56 alerts, six of them real bugs now fixed in PR #2309, fifteen verified false positives with reasons recorded. Mail DNS measured by `pnpm check:mail-dns` at 5 of 6, and the sixth (2048-bit DKIM) is withdrawn as not actionable. The SPF item was never real. VAPID closed earlier on production /api/status.

entries.title: Lift 8b: RowCard gets a ring and .press on its surface
entries.detail: Brings the third card primitive level with EntityCard. Today the surface never rings or presses.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='components/cards/row-card.tsx',T='components/cards/row-card.test.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const code=s.split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter(x=>x.trim().indexOf('//')!==0&&x.trim().indexOf('*')!==0).join(String.fromCharCode(10));const bad=[];if(code.indexOf('press')<0)bad.push('RowCard no longer applies .press');if(code.indexOf('ring-focus')<0)bad.push('RowCard no longer applies ring-focus');if(t.indexOf('expect(')<0)bad.push('no assertions in '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The probe was grep-present 'press' in components/ui/cards/row-card.tsx - A PATH NOTHING OCCUPIES (the file is components/cards/row-card.tsx), so the row could never have closed and read as outstanding work rather than as a broken instrument. Same defect class as LIVE-030's probe, found the same day. It now checks the real file for both halves of INTERACTION-STATES section 2: .press (the one sanctioned pressed look) and ring-focus (the card focus ring; the global ring is a box-shadow and lift-1 paints over it).

entries.title: Lift 8b: a loading prop on IconButton, matching Button's
entries.detail: Icon-only controls are exactly the ones where a tap leaves no other evidence it landed.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='components/ui/icon-button.tsx',T='components/ui/icon-button.test.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),test=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const cut=src.indexOf('export function IconLink');if(cut<0)process.exit(79);const B=src.slice(0,cut),L=src.slice(cut);function a(s,k){let i=0;while((i=s.indexOf(k+'={',i))>=0){const aria=s.slice(Math.max(0,i-5),i).endsWith('aria-');const e=s.indexOf('}',i);if(e>0&&s.slice(i,e).includes('loading')&&(k.indexOf('aria-')===0||!aria))return true;i+=k.length}return false}const bad=[];if(!a(B,'disabled'))bad.push('IconButton does not disable while loading; a second tap re-fires the action');if(!a(B,'aria-busy'))bad.push('IconButton does not set aria-busy while loading');if(!a(L,'aria-disabled'))bad.push('IconLink does not set aria-disabled while loading');if(!a(L,'aria-busy'))bad.push('IconLink does not set aria-busy while loading');if(!test.includes('does not fire the handler again'))bad.push('the double-fire assertion is gone from '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The probe that flagged this row as stale was `grep-present /loading/` in the component, which passes because the WORD appears anywhere in the file, including in a comment describing the prop it is supposed to be proving. Replaced with the consequence: IconButton must disable while loading (so a second tap cannot re-fire the action) and set aria-busy; IconLink must use the aria pair INSTEAD of the real `disabled`, because a real disabled drops it out of the tab order mid-navigation; and the double-fire assertion must still exist in the test file. ONE TRAP WORTH RECORDING: both controls live in one file and the string 'aria-disabled=' CONTAINS 'disabled=', so an unscoped regex let each component satisfy the other's check. Two of four deliberate breaks passed before that was caught, which is exactly why a probe is not trusted until it has been seen to fail. It now splits the file at IconLink and judges each half alone; all four breaks fire. A SECOND trap cost another round: the first scoped version used a regex, and this string travels JSON -> shell -> `node -e`, where a lone backslash does not survive intact - "\\b" arrived as a literal BACKSPACE, so every check silently matched nothing and the row read as regressed. The probe is now backslash-free, scanning with indexOf instead of RegExp, and was re-proved through the guard's own shell rather than only standalone.

entries.title: Lift 8b: a visible busy state on ConfirmSubmitButton
entries.detail: The ref guard already blocks the second fire; nothing tells the member the first one took.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='components/ui/confirm-submit-button.tsx',T='components/ui/confirm-submit-button.test.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const code=s.split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter(x=>x.trim().indexOf('//')!==0&&x.trim().indexOf('*')!==0).join(String.fromCharCode(10));const bad=[];if(code.indexOf('aria-busy={')<0)bad.push('ConfirmSubmitButton does not set aria-busy while submitting');if(code.indexOf('dimmed')<0)bad.push('the .dimmed pending look is gone; there is no VISIBLE busy state');if(code.indexOf('disabled={busy')>=0)bad.push('it flips disabled on busy, which cancels the form submission it is guarding');if((t.split('expect(').length-1)<3)bad.push('fewer than 3 assertions in '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. Was manual, waiting on the implementation choice, and the choice is made: .dimmed plus aria-busy, NOT disabled. The probe pins the thing that must never change - flipping the button to disabled inside the submit handler CANCELS the form submission it is guarding, so a bare 'is there a busy state' check would pass the exact bug this component exists to avoid.

entries.title: Lift 8b: an in-flight cue on DirectorySearch
entries.detail: It fetches. Until it says so, an empty result and a pending one look identical.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='components/ui/directory-search.tsx',T='components/ui/directory-search.test.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const code=s.split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter(x=>x.trim().indexOf('//')!==0&&x.trim().indexOf('*')!==0).join(String.fromCharCode(10));const bad=[];if(code.indexOf('useTransition()')<0)bad.push('DirectorySearch does not CALL useTransition(), so it cannot know a search is in flight');const i=code.indexOf('aria-busy={');const seg=i<0?'':code.slice(i,code.indexOf('}',i));if(i<0||seg.indexOf('isPending')<0)bad.push('aria-busy is not driven by isPending');if(code.indexOf('Searching')<0)bad.push('the live-region text is gone; a spinning glyph announces nothing to a screen reader');if((t.split('expect(').length-1)<3)bad.push('fewer than 3 assertions in '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. Was manual pending the implementation. The probe requires useTransition to be CALLED, not merely imported: the first version matched the token and passed while the component tracked nothing, because the import line alone satisfied it. It also requires aria-busy to be DRIVEN BY isPending rather than hardcoded, and the 'Searching...' live-region text to survive - a spinning glyph announces nothing to a screen reader, so the cue has two halves and only one of them is visible.

entries.title: Lift 8d: check:elements requires a state test for every new ui primitive
entries.detail: The gate that stops 8b's sweep from being re-earned every quarter: a new components/ui/* primitive must ship a colocated test naming its required states.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),f='scripts/check-elements.mjs';if(!fs.existsSync(f))process.exit(79);import('./'+f).then(m=>{const r=m.evaluateUiStates();if(!r||!Array.isArray(r.primitives)||r.primitives.length<m.MIN_UI_PRIMITIVES)process.exit(79);const bad=[...r.missing.map(p=>p+': new ui primitive with no colocated state test'),...r.graduated.map(p=>p+': grandfathered primitive gained a state test and was never banked'),...r.vanished.map(p=>p+': ledger entry for a primitive that no longer exists')];if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('\\n'));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)}).catch(e=>{console.error(String(e&&e.message));process.exit(79)})"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. 42 primitives, 6 carry a state test, 36 grandfathered in scripts/ui-state-test-ledger.txt — a SET of paths, not a count, because one primitive gaining a test and one arriving without cancel out inside a total (the ADR-1007 defect). Stricter than its two siblings on purpose: a graduated or vanished entry FAILS rather than warns, because the number is a published metric and an unbanked win makes it fiction. The definition of 'state test' is INTERACTION-STATES.md's, not invented: names 3+ of the nine states in test titles, titles only — exercising a state in a className assertion is not naming it. 36 is not 36 units of neglect: a Display badge owes only `rest`, so the gate over-reports by design and can never certify an untested primitive as covered. Two counts in INTERACTION-STATES.md §6 were wrong and are corrected.

entries.title: Lift 5c: retire the coded marketing bodies, one slug per PR
entries.detail:
Committed order in scripts/render-path-bodies.txt: about → spaces → the-lab → the-quest → the-community → pricing (partial). check:render-path ships an EXACT-MATCH ratchet, so the PR retiring a body edits the baseline in the same PR — a fall is not auto-accepted here. MUST land before EDITOR E3, which replaces EDITABLE_PAGES in the opposite direction.

── RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19 in a premise sweep (ADR-1082). HALF THE COMMITTED ORDER HAS ALREADY SHIPPED, and this row was last checked one day before two of the three landed. scripts/render-path-bodies.txt (last touched c3228d7) records `about` 0 (2026-08-17), `spaces` 0 (2026-08-18) and `the-lab` 0 (2026-08-18); `circles` was already template-only. Remaining: home 5, the-community 5, the-quest 2, pricing 7. NEXT SLUG IS the-quest.

🔴 A TRAP FOR WHOEVER TAKES THE NEXT TWO, and it is exactly the defect LIVE-040 records. app/(marketing)/the-quest/page.tsx and the-community/page.tsx still emit faqSchema() from their ROUTE BODIES, while their templates also carry Accordions. That is fine today. The moment those bodies are retired the FAQPage goes with them, which is precisely how /the-lab ended up emitting no FAQPage for weeks. Move the FAQ into an Accordion in the SAME PR that retires each body, or this row manufactures LIVE-040 twice more. ── 🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-24 (ADR-1082) AND THE NEXT SLUG HAD ALREADY SHIPPED. This row said "NEXT SLUG IS the-quest". scripts/render-path-bodies.txt records `the-quest` at 0, RETIRED 2026-08-19 — five days before this row was read, and the row was last checked 2026-08-17. Remaining coded bodies are now: home 5, the-community 5, pricing 7 (partial, and its figures must never be frozen into a document). NEXT SLUG IS the-community. The FAQ trap this row records is now down to ONE page rather than two, and it is the-community's: its route body still emits faqSchema() while its template also carries an Accordion, so the FAQPage must move into the Accordion in the SAME PR that retires the body. the-quest's retirement handled this correctly and said so on its own line, which is the shape to copy. ── ⏳ the-community RETIRED 2026-08-24. Ledger 5 -> 0; route 639 -> 126 lines; app/(marketing)/the-community/tour.tsx (a 389-line ProductTour client island whose ONLY caller was the retired body) deleted with it. check:render-path now reads 14 of 16 gated slugs template-only, 2 still carrying a coded body (12 components, 3,326 lines). 🔴 THE FAQ TRAP THIS ROW RECORDS WAS ALREADY GONE, AND THE ROW WAS WRONG ABOUT IT: it says the route body still emits faqSchema() beside a template Accordion. It did not — LIVE-040 had already deleted that call and moved the Q&A into the template's tc-faq Accordion. The only schema call deleted here was the legacy branch's articleSchema(), on a branch that could never be taken. MEASURED before/after with renderToStaticMarkup: three ld+json scripts and the multiset { BreadcrumbList 1, ListItem 1, Article 1, WebPage 1, Organization 2, ImageObject 1, FAQPage 1, Question 4, Answer 4 } — byte-identical. That is the second time this row's own trap text has outlived the defect it describes, so the remaining slug it names (home) should be re-measured, not believed. FIVE coded details the template did not draw were recovered VERBATIM into existing blocks: the 'No application, no audition.' guardrail (the template carried it only in a code COMMENT, which no visitor reads), the /pricing link, the /discover link (into an empty designed CTA slot), the 'Circulation, not exclusion.' generosity guardrail, and the FOUNDING_PLACE grounding (interpolated from lib/site.ts, never typed, so it cannot drift). docs/FINALIZE-PLAN.md was corrected in the same pass because deleting tour.tsx falsified its arbitrary-type count. ⚠️ ONE THING WAS DELIBERATELY NOT RECOVERED and is filed as LIVE-100 instead: the coded body's closing PillarNav triptych. NEXT SLUG IS home (5 components, 940 lines), and it is LAST in the series because Splash carries the live-proof band and its own chrome. pricing (7) stays out of the series entirely: its fallback is the coded page rather than getTemplate('pricing'), and its take-rate figures must never be frozen into a document. ── ✅ `home` RETIRED 2026-08-24, and the OWN-043 ruling made it a PURE DELETION rather than a recovery. app/page.tsx 938 -> 137 lines. check:render-path now reads 15 template-only, 1 body - the last is `pricing`, which stays out of the series by design because its take-rate figures must never be frozen into a template. UNREACHABILITY WAS DOUBLE, and verified rather than assumed: the route picks published, then template, then null, and BOTH rungs are well-formed 13-block documents (the live published doc queried from production; getTemplate('home') pinned by templates.test.ts, 17 passing). `data` could never be null, so <Splash> could never render. That is stronger evidence than a snapshot, which is why NO visual baseline recapture was needed - a recapture would have photographed an unchanged page. SCHEMA MEASURED ON BOTH RUNGS, before and after, by the method the-community's retirement used: renderToStaticMarkup over BlockDocJsonLd + BlockRender, every ld+json extracted and diffed. BYTE-IDENTICAL, md5 7203e7bdcd8d096b6e7310866af373aa on both sides, one Article node each. The published fixture was checksummed against the database rather than transcribed. ⚠️ SAID PLAINLY SO IT CANNOT READ AS COVERAGE: faqSchema(HOME_FAQ) was called INSIDE Splash, on the branch that never renders, so `/` has emitted no FAQPage since the template landed and emits none now. This change neither caused nor cured that - the count is 0 on both sides, which is the proof. A FAQPage on `/` needs an Accordion in the PUBLISHED document, an editor change rather than a code one. ORPHANS DELETED: ScrollCue, CountUp, Parallax and Steps had zero remaining references repo-wide including tests, so they went with the body, following the precedent set when the-community took tour.tsx. The route header now records that lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts is UNREACHABLE BY DECISION (OWN-043), with an explicit instruction not to recover copy into it - change the home page in the editor. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-24, AND THE CLOSING QUESTION WAS PRICING RATHER THAN ANOTHER SLUG. This row's OWN committed order named `pricing` last (“about → spaces → the-lab → the-quest → the-community → pricing (partial)”), ADR-1068 wrote the same order down (“circles → about → spaces → the-lab → the-quest → the-community → pricing”), and scripts/render-path-bodies.txt carried it too. So the recent note saying pricing “stays out of the series entirely” was a NARROWING of a committed order that lived only in a note, which is precisely the drift the one list exists to stop. It is now ADR-1116: a decision, with an ADR, and the ledger header plus the pricing row carry it so the next reader does not re-open the question. WHAT WAS MEASURED, not inferred: check:render-path reads 16 gated slugs, 15 template-only, 1 still carrying a coded body (pricing, 7 components, 2,526 route lines). /pricing resolves published → coded — TWO rungs, not three. getTemplate('pricing') is NOT a middle rung even though lib/page-editor/templates/pricing.ts exists and `pricing` is a row in EDITABLE_PAGES. That inversion is ADR-916/918's and it is deliberate: on every other slug the coded body is a RELIC duplicating a static document, here it is the DERIVED page (live prices, the live take-rate vector, the beta-window resolution the checkout itself asks, the operator's live feature-gate overrides, and not one dollar figure or percentage typed in the file) while the Puck template is the snapshot. All seven components were read and ALL SEVEN consume the derived model — Offering (PlanCard / PlanPrice / PlanCta / IndependentStrip), PlanExtra (ExtraCard), the resolved rate string (RateLine), FeatureGrid (ComparisonBlock) — so “partial” had nothing to retire: there is no copy-only block that could move into the template while the figures stayed live. ⚠️ THE LEDGER ROW STAYS GATED EXACT-MATCH. `pricing 7` may fall if the body genuinely shrinks, and a rise is still refused; what ends is the expectation that it reaches 0. ONE THING REOPENS IT (ADR-1116): a block kind that binds a live pricing key the way pricing.ts already binds `livePriceKey` per ADR-918, for EVERY figure the body renders — rates, gates and the comparison grid included. Until a document can carry a BINDING rather than a NUMBER for all of them, moving this page into the editor means quoting figures the product has stopped charging.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const L=fs.readFileSync('scripts/render-path-bodies.txt','utf8').split('\n');const bad=[];for(const line of L){const m=/^([a-z0-9-]+)\s+(\d+)/.exec(line);if(!m)continue;if(m[1]!=='pricing'&&m[2]!=='0')bad.push(m[1]+'='+m[2])}if(bad.length){console.error('a gated slug still carries a coded body outside the ADR-1116 pricing exclusion: '+bad.join(', '));process.exit(1)}const routes={'app/page.tsx':['Splash','LiveProof','PostPreviewCard','EventRow'],'app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx':['LegacyAbout'],'app/(marketing)/spaces/page.tsx':['LegacySpaces'],'app/(marketing)/the-lab/page.tsx':['LegacyTheLab'],'app/(marketing)/the-quest/page.tsx':['LegacyTheQuest'],'app/(marketing)/the-community/page.tsx':['LegacyTheCommunity']};for(const f of Object.keys(routes)){if(!fs.existsSync(f)){console.error('missing route '+f);process.exit(1)}const t=fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8');if(t.indexOf('BlockRender')<0){console.error(f+' no longer renders BlockRender');process.exit(1)}for(const n of routes[f]){if(t.indexOf('function '+n)>=0){console.error(f+' still declares '+n);process.exit(1)}}}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE of Lift 5c, in two halves, and neither half is the row's title. (1) Every slug in the render-path ledger reads 0 except `pricing`, which is out of the series by ADR-1116 - so a NEW gated route arriving with a coded body fires this row, which is the promise regressing. (2) The six routes that retired a body still render <BlockRender> (the positive control: a probe that only asserts absence passes on an empty file) and no longer declare the named bodies - Splash / LiveProof / PostPreviewCard / EventRow, LegacyAbout, LegacySpaces, LegacyTheLab, LegacyTheQuest, LegacyTheCommunity. Pure fs, no subprocess and no test runner (LIVE-034).

entries.notes: FINDING 2026-08-17 that makes the remaining slugs cheaper and safer than this row assumed: the legacy bodies on five routes are ALREADY UNREACHABLE. Every gated route resolves published -> template -> legacy, and the template rung is a static import that is always well-formed, so `data` can never be null and the `data ? <BlockRender/> : <Legacy/>` branch cannot be taken. For about, spaces, the-lab, the-quest and the-community this is deletion of dead code, not a swap needing visual proof, and THE PIXELS CANNOT MOVE - which is a stronger guarantee than a snapshot comparison. DONE: `about`, 327 -> 75 lines, ledger 3 -> 0. REMAINING, in the committed order, one per PR: spaces (284 lines, 2 -> 0), the-lab (382, 3 -> 0), the-quest (498, 2 -> 0), the-community (635, 5 -> 0), then home (939, 5 -> 0) LAST because Splash carries the live-proof band and its own header/footer chrome. 🔴 PRICING IS DIFFERENT AND MUST NOT BE BATCHED WITH THEM: its fallback is the coded page rather than getTemplate('pricing'), and it carries live take-rate bindings. Never freeze those figures into a document. UPDATE 2026-08-18: DONE so far - about (327 -> 75, ledger 3 -> 0), spaces (284 -> 81, 2 -> 0), the-lab (382 -> 86, 3 -> 0). Remaining in order: the-quest (498, 2 -> 0), the-community (635, 5 -> 0), home (939, 5 -> 0) LAST; pricing stays out of the series. check:render-path now reports 4 slugs on the template alone (was 2 before tonight), 19 coded components across 3,284 route lines (was 24 / 3,580). the-lab's unreachability was verified for that slug specifically, not inherited: 7 blocks, every type a string literal, getTemplate identity stable across calls, so isWellFormed is invariant.

entries.title: Lift 5d: the eight seeker articles join EDITABLE_PAGES
entries.detail:
Unblocked — DawnHowToSteps exists and owns its HowTo JSON-LD, with a dedicated test. Needs a shared templates/article.ts seed. Same ordering constraint as LIVE-006 relative to E3.

── RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19 in a premise sweep (ADR-1082). THE STATED BLOCKER NO LONGER EXISTS. This row says it "needs a shared templates/article.ts seed". lib/page-editor/templates/article.ts is 248 lines with articleTemplate(spec), required `answer` and `faq` fields that make the CONTENT-VOICE §10.9 article grammar unexpressible if violated, and a companion article.test.ts that renders a spec through the live block config. It landed 2026-08-17 in 656dac3 (#2143, ADR-1068) and documents the remaining job as a five-step per-article recipe in its own header. It has NO importers, deliberately -- its own ⚠️ STATUS block says "NO live consumer yet".

The row stays OPEN and its probe still fails correctly (all eight slugs are absent from EDITABLE_PAGES). What changes is the shape of the work: it is no longer "build a seed", it is "enroll one article per PR via the recipe in that file's header".

── PROGRESS 2026-08-20: second article enrolled. how-to-build-community joins EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe (spec in templates/how-to-build-community.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, ledger row added). articleTemplate gained four optional seams the pillar needed (media-beat kicker, photo-less hero via the minimal variant, per-section howTo so three tracks ship three HowTo nodes, plural beats). Two enrolled, six remain: calm-down-fast, friendship-as-an-adult, how-to-be-more-social, loneliness, tools-for-community-builders, what-is-frequency. The probe still fails correctly on those six.

── PROGRESS 2026-08-20: third article enrolled. loneliness joins EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe (spec in templates/loneliness.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, ledger row added). articleTemplate gained one optional seam the umbrella pillar needed: media beats may carry `links`, a Buttons row closing the beat's band, because the coded closing ZigZag held TWO buttons and the MediaText block has one cta slot; without the seam a label and an internal link would silently drop. Three enrolled, five remain: calm-down-fast, friendship-as-an-adult, how-to-be-more-social, tools-for-community-builders, what-is-frequency. The probe still fails correctly on those five.

── PROGRESS 2026-08-20: fourth article enrolled. friendship-as-an-adult joins EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe (spec in templates/friendship-as-an-adult.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, ledger row added). articleTemplate gained two optional seams the making-friends hub needed: sections may carry `steps`, plain ordered steps rendered as BuildTimeline with NO HowTo node, because the coded page shows three step lists but asserts only ONE HowTo, and routing the other two through DawnHowToSteps would invent schema claims and the visible name/intro copy that block requires; and the spec may carry `closingBeat`, one beat between the FAQ and the close, where the coded page's final brand Statement sits. Both seams proven backward-compatible: the three prior specs render byte-identically through old vs new generator. Four enrolled, four remain: calm-down-fast, how-to-be-more-social, tools-for-community-builders, what-is-frequency. The probe still fails correctly on those four.

── PROGRESS 2026-08-20: fifth article enrolled. calm-down-fast joins EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe (spec in templates/calm-down-fast.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, ledger row added). No new seam needed: the always-wired page is expressible with the existing grammar, its schema-free Steps list rides `steps` (BuildTimeline, no HowTo node, matching the coded page which asserted none) and its two ZigZags ride media beats. Five enrolled, three remain: how-to-be-more-social, tools-for-community-builders, what-is-frequency. The probe still fails correctly on those three.

── PROGRESS 2026-08-20: sixth article enrolled. how-to-be-more-social joins EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe (spec in templates/how-to-be-more-social.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, ledger row added). The two absorbed pillars (feel-less-awkward-in-groups, social-life-without-drinking) travel as ordinary sections. articleTemplate gained one optional seam the social-confidence pillar needed: sections may carry `note`, a prose line rendered as a Text block AFTER the section's button row, because the coded page closes its Where-to-start section with a "Keep going" cross-link paragraph BELOW the buttons and folding it into `body` would move it above them. Seam proven backward-compatible: all five prior specs render byte-identically through old vs new generator. The page still asserts exactly ONE HowTo, as coded, from section 2's own `howTo`. Six enrolled, two remain: tools-for-community-builders, what-is-frequency. The probe still fails correctly on those two. ── 🔴 THE PROBE ITSELF HAD NEVER RUN, discovered 2026-08-24 while closing the last two articles. Its `need` array was written with DOUBLE-quoted slugs, and the whole probe is a `node -e "…"` string, so the shell ate those quotes and node threw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'for'` on every single invocation. The guard fences a probe that COULD NOT RUN (a signal, a missing binary, exit 79) but a SyntaxError exits 1, which is indistinguishable from an honest "not done" — so for as long as this row was open, its probe AGREED with it by failing to parse. Every "the probe still fails correctly on those N" note above was reporting a parse error, not a measurement. Rewritten with single quotes (verified against a tree where the slugs ARE present: it now exits 0, and against a tree where one is missing: it names the missing slug and exits 1). A static gate now refuses any cmd probe carrying an inner double quote, so this class cannot recur — see the same defect in LIVE-090's probe, caught the same way on 2026-08-23. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24: the last two articles enrolled, and Lift 5d's article set is complete. `tools-for-community-builders` (7th) and `what-is-frequency` (8th) join EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe - spec beside the route, registered in templates/index.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, a ROUTES entry and an annotated ledger row each. All eight slugs now resolve through articleTemplate and every article route is template-only (0 coded components); check:render-path reads 16 gated slugs, 13 on the template alone. `tools-for-community-builders` widened NO seam - the first enrolment that needed none, and evidence the grammar has converged: an article written for a different reader (the Latent Leader assembling a stack, CONTENT-VOICE section 2b, not the Seeker) fit the existing fields exactly. It is the second article to assert NO HowTo, using neither `howTo` nor `steps`, so no DawnHowToSteps block is composed and no node is invented. THREE schema nodes, as coded. `what-is-frequency` widened three, all optional and all mapped to blocks already live in another template: `tiers` (the six-rung price ladder to Tiers, which emits no schema, so no Product/Offer node is invented), `cards` (the three sibling-pillar link cards to FeatureGrid, also schema-free) and `afterSteps` (the taxonomy paragraph the coded page printed BELOW the steps, which `body` and `note` both render ABOVE them). Backward compatibility MEASURED rather than asserted: all seven prior specs render BYTE-IDENTICALLY through the pre-change and post-change generator. FOUR schema nodes, as coded, including exactly ONE HowTo. Copy fidelity checked in BOTH directions by script: 46/46 and 96/96 spec strings found verbatim in the coded routes (with the routes' price interpolations resolved from the same modules), and zero coded sentences dropped. Prices are NOT frozen into the documents: the spec imports priceStrings / PRICING_DEFAULTS / formatBps, the same single source the route read. Verified: tsc clean, vitest run 881 files / 11,910 passing, check:render-path / canon / vocab / one-list green.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const D='lib/page-editor/data.ts',A='lib/page-editor/templates/article.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(D)||!fs.existsSync(A))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(D,'utf8');const i=s.indexOf('EDITABLE_PAGES');if(i<0)process.exit(79);const o=s.indexOf('= [',i),c=s.indexOf(']',o);if(o<0||c<0)process.exit(79);const seg=s.slice(o,c);if(seg.indexOf('home')<0)process.exit(79);const need=['calm-down-fast','friendship-as-an-adult','how-to-be-more-social','how-to-build-community','how-to-start-a-circle','loneliness','tools-for-community-builders','what-is-frequency'];const q=String.fromCharCode(39);const miss=need.filter(function(x){return seg.indexOf(q+x+q)<0});if(miss.length){console.error('not yet in EDITABLE_PAGES: '+miss.join(', '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Probe replaced 2026-08-17. It was grep-present /article/ in lib/page-editor/templates, which went green the moment a file named article.ts appeared - shape, not truth. The shared seed IS built (templates/article.ts, ADR-1068) and that is what this row's DETAIL asked for, but the row's TITLE is the claim that has to hold, and the eight articles have not joined: EDITABLE_PAGES still holds exactly the eight marketing primaries, and the seed's own header records that it has no live consumer until the first article enrolls. The probe now names the eight non-redirect article routes and fails until each is in the list, with a floor (the list must still contain 'home') so a reshaped file exits 79 rather than reporting a clean sweep of nothing.

entries.title: The .dark [data-skin="midnight"] selector never matches on the <html> path
entries.detail: A descendant combinator cannot match an element against itself. app/layout.tsx stamps data-skin on documentElement (the global skin preview path, including marketing); only the shell root is a descendant. So midnight-dark renders a MIXTURE: the generic .dark palette with midnight's light-mode overrides under it. The comment at app/layout.tsx:142-143 asserts the opposite, which is why it survived. One selector, but it repaints every midnight-dark surface, so it wants its own pass with a baseline recapture.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='lib/theme/skins.ts',C='app/globals.css';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(C))process.exit(79);const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8');const ids=[...new Set([...src.matchAll(/\bid:\s*\x27([a-z0-9-]+)\x27/g)].map(m=>m[1]))];const def=(src.match(/DEFAULT_SKIN[^=]*=\s*\x27([a-z0-9-]+)\x27/)||[])[1];if(!def||ids.length<2)process.exit(79);const css=fs.readFileSync(C,'utf8').replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g,'');const bad=[];for(const id of ids){if(id===def)continue;if(!new RegExp('\\\\.dark\\\\[data-skin=\\\\x22'+id+'\\\\x22\\\\]').test(css))bad.push(id+': no compound .dark[data-skin] selector; the <html> preview path paints the generic .dark palette');if(!new RegExp('\\\\.dark\\\\s+\\\\[data-skin=\\\\x22'+id+'\\\\x22\\\\]').test(css))bad.push(id+': no descendant .dark [data-skin] selector; the authed-shell path loses its dark block');}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('\n'));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. Non-vacuity proven by the parent, not taken on report: reverting to the descendant-only selector fails skin-dom-selectors.test.ts with 'A descendant combinator cannot match an element against itself'. The second half matters more than the row did — authoring the selector LIST would have silently dropped the block from check-contrast's resolver, which scored the raw prelude and returned null for any comma-separated selector, so the contrast gate would have kept printing green for midnight-dark while measuring nothing there (ADR-970). Fixed in the same pass; selectorWeight now scores each part of a list independently.

entries.title: The app shell statically imports the entire admin module registry
entries.detail: settings-panel.tsx imports MODULE_COMPONENTS from components/admin/modules/module-map — a 'use client' pure registry with 38 static imports and no hooks, handlers or browser APIs. It reaches crypto-browserify/stream-browserify: 406 kB raw / 121 kB gzip on EVERY authed page, verified as a blocking script tag in served HTML. Fix: next/dynamic per module, import module IDS not components, and add import 'server-only' to lib/journey-plans and lib/practices so the class fails the build. NOTE: needs a route-level first-load measurement, which the agent container cannot produce (next build fails page-data collection without service-role creds).
entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-18 (ADR-1074). TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW'S OWN NUMBERS, both measured. (1) THE HEADLINE WAS STALE. '406 kB raw / 121 kB gzip reaching crypto-browserify on every authed page' was already spent by dc47b89 when the 42 catalog modules moved behind dynamic(); nobody re-measured afterwards. entries.title: Sentry no longer ships to routes with no DSN configured
entries.detail: The static `import * as Sentry` is gone; the SDK is now reached through a dynamic import gated on process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN — the one env form the browser can resolve, since Next inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time. The server-only SENTRY_DSN fallback is deliberately NOT consulted here because it is never inlined into the browser bundle and could only read undefined. The hard part was the export contract: Next reads onRouterTransitionStart off this module's namespace and calls it on every client navigation, so it MUST stay defined with Sentry off — it is now a stable wrapper delegating to an async-loaded hook, with a .catch that leaves it a no-op if the chunk fails, because monitoring must never take down the app it monitors. Stated cost: a navigation in the first few ms of a configured session may go untraced. VERIFIED BEYOND THE ONE FILE (the searchSiteIcons lesson): every importer of lib/observability/sentry was enumerated — only sentry.server.config.ts and sentry.edge.config.ts import it statically, both server/edge runtimes, and lib/maps/diagnostics.ts deliberately reads the value without importing. No client component pulls it, so the SDK cannot re-enter the baseline chunk by a side door.
entries.notes: Artifact-verified 2026-08-17, not inferred: built with no DSN and read the emitted chunks. The 236,682-byte Sentry SDK chunk appears in 0 of 4,149 client entry lists across all 404 page_client-reference-manifest.js files, and the baseline chunk in rootMainFiles contains only the gated async loader. app/error, app/global-error and components/ui/route-error.tsx still import the SDK statically; Turbopack keeps those in async groups, so they are not a baseline regression and were deliberately left alone.

The real count of labels naming nothing is ZERO, not ~105: the row's probe was readFileSync().includes('<Label'), which counts 132 correctly associated labels and 43 SVG captions. entries.title: The header wordmark's keyboard focus indicator is explicitly deleted
entries.detail: app/globals.css removes the focus ring from the wordmark — the first tab stop on every page.

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The rule was `.brandmark-link:focus-visible { box-shadow: none }`, written to suppress a ring 'when clicked' — but :focus-visible is exactly the state a pointer click does not enter, so it never affected the pointer case and removed the indicator from the first tab stop on every signed-in page. entries.title: The sitemap's batched podcast read was silently truncating at 1000 rows
entries.detail: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS STALE AND THE REAL BUG WAS WORSE. The N+1 had already been collapsed — sitemap.ts called a batched reader. But that batch used `.limit(min(n*200, 5000))` with no `.range()`, and `.limit()` does not raise PostgREST's server-side `max_rows` (supabase/config.toml:18 = 1000, and service_role does not escape it). So it declared a 5000-row appetite, received 1000, and reported no error. Because the batch orders `created_at DESC` ACROSS ALL SPACES, the dropped rows were whole trailing Spaces: their /podcasts index and every Show URL vanished from the sitemap with nothing to notice. Collapsing 200 correct small queries into one truncated one traded latency for missing URLs — the third instance today of a fix whose instrument could not tell 'nothing there' from 'I could not see'. Now paged explicitly with `.range()` over a TOTAL order (created_at DESC, id ASC — the tiebreaker is required so a created_at tie cannot straddle a page boundary and be skipped or repeated), stopping on a short page. Still O(rows), never O(Spaces).

verify.note: Probes the CONSEQUENCE — that the batched read pages — rather than the row's words. Backed by app/sitemap.test.ts, which rebuilds the URL list the old per-Space loop would have emitted and requires an exact match, and which was confirmed to FAIL against an unpaged read (expected 1000 to be 1500) before being accepted.

entries.notes:
Closed 2026-08-17. The probe that flagged this row as stale was `grep-present /'app'|"app"/` in check-canon.mjs, which passes on the mere appearance of the string 'app' - shape, not truth. Replaced with the consequence, measured in-process: import the guard, assert SEAM_ROOTS still covers app/ AND lib/, run scanCodeSeam() over the real tree and require zero member-facing violations. MEASURED: 3,398 files under app/ + lib/ + components/, 22,437 member-facing strings judged, 0 violations. The floors (MIN_SEAM_FILES 2000, MIN_SEAM_STRINGS 15000) make a guard that stops finding the corpus exit 79 rather than report a clean sweep of nothing. Proved BOTH ways: a real banned string ('Find your tribe') under a copy key fails it, narrowing SEAM_ROOTS fails it by name, and the SAME words in a comment and in an internal identifier do NOT fire it - the false-positive half is what keeps a widened guard from being routed around.

🔴 RE-SCOPED 2026-08-21, because this probe COST MAIN A RED BUILD. It called scanCodeSeam(), which parses every file in the seam — 3,413 files, 21,947 strings, 7.57s of CPU. check:backlog runs under a 20s CPU budget asserted by scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts, and this ONE row was 41% of it. On 2026-08-21 the budget came in at 20,080ms against the 20,000ms ceiling and main went red for 56 minutes (commit 6127a26), on a merge that had changed nothing but 18 PNGs.

WHAT THE PROBE DROPPED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A LOSS OF COVERAGE. It asserted found.length === 0 — that the whole tree is on-canon. That is precisely what `pnpm check:canon` asserts, and check:canon runs as its own guard in the SAME CI job. Duplicating it bought nothing and cost something real: a canon violation introduced by anyone, anywhere, would fail THIS ROW, reporting a regression in the seam-widening work that shipped months ago. A probe should measure its own row's consequence, not re-grade a neighbouring guard.

WHAT IT STILL MEASURES, which is this row's actual consequence: the seam was WIDENED past content/ to app/ + lib/, and it reaches a real corpus. SEAM_ROOTS must still contain both roots (narrowing it fails by name), and seamFiles() must still return at least MIN_SEAM_FILES. seamFiles is the directory WALK without the parse — newly exported for this, 0.031s against 7.57s, a 244x reduction — so the non-triviality floor survives intact: a walk that breaks or a root that moves still trips it rather than reporting a clean sweep of nothing.

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The row's ORIGINAL probe was grep-present /app/api/ in check-authz-guards.mjs — the second shape-not-truth probe caught this session, and it went stale-green the moment the file was touched. 72 route handlers now carry a verdict, 55 of them under app/api/ which the gate previously could not see at all. 52 call a real gate; 20 are asserted in scripts/authz-route-ledger.json and the guard SAYS SO in its own output — 'HUMAN-ASSERTED, not verified: they are safe because someone read them' — with each one's digest pinned so an edit forces a re-read. entries.detail: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO. It called this 'largely mechanical' over ~698 sites with 3 adopters. Sweeping them means 11px -> 12px, semibold -> bold and 0.025em -> 0.18em - a 7.2x tracking change that widens a label inside a px-2.5 pill it was sized to fit. That is an unreviewed visual change to several hundred surfaces, not a rename. WHAT SHIPPED is the half a machine can settle: of the 15 slots the CODE ITSELF names `eyebrow`, SEVEN hand-rolled the role across five different letter-spacings, all in the shared kit - EditorShell, Toast, StudioWindow, SparkShell, EntityHeader, JourneyBuilder, HostCohostSection. entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17 (ADR-1071). THE ROW WAS STALE ON THE IMPLEMENTATION AND RIGHT ABOUT THE GAP. The three-position ladder and the desktop left-rail fold were already built and already gated. The PERSISTED half had nothing behind it: replacing the whole body of writeStoredRailFolds with `return` left all 38 tests in rail-fold.test.ts PASSING, and deleting railFold from the shell mount in app/(main)/layout.tsx - the entire no-flash path - left 288 tests passing with tsc green. Cause: that suite runs in environment 'node', so with no window and no document both storage functions return on their first line in every case. AND IT SURFACED A REAL DEFECT. writeStoredRailFolds is built to survive blocked localStorage (the setItem throw is swallowed, the cookie still lands) but readStoredRailFolds read localStorage and nothing else. In exactly that case the server paints the folded strip from the cookie, hydration renders it, and the first client snapshot reads blocked storage, answers Auto, and shoves the rail open one frame after paint - the fail-safe fired and the next line cancelled it. The read now falls back to the cookie. The probe EXECUTES the round trip rather than grepping for it: it fakes window.localStorage and document.cookie, chooses Strip/Open, drops the in-memory snapshot (a reload) and asserts the fold comes back AND that the cookie the server reads agrees. Verified myself, not just reported: gutting the write prints 'a reload lost the fold' and exits 1; removing compact={leftStrip} names the desktop fold and exits 1. No baseline recapture needed - the rail's state at rest is unchanged, and the new behaviour only fires when localStorage is empty AND a cookie exists, which a fresh capture browser never has.

entries.title: Send the three prod-ahead tokens back to DAWN (NOT the fourth)
entries.detail:
CORRECTED 2026-08-19: this row listed FOUR tokens and one of them must not be sent. --color-focus-ring, --color-text-on-broadcast and --color-text-subtle are genuinely correct in production and wrong in DAWN's artifact, and SYNC.md requires they go back on the next round or the next handoff silently reintroduces the AA failures they fixed. --color-text-on-primary is NOT one of them and has not been since 2026-08-06. Production is #FFFFFF and DAWN is #FFFFFF; verified in both files 2026-08-19, and lib/theme/dawn-divergence.test.ts derives the divergence set from both stylesheets on every pnpm test and agrees. What happened was a SPLIT, not a revert: while on-primary was ink every rank core inherited an ink glyph and gold, the lightest core by design, fell to 2.46:1. The glyph moved to its own token (--color-text-on-rank) and the button label went back to white. SENDING THE OLD ROW WOULD ASK DAWN TO MAKE ON-PRIMARY INK, reintroducing, from the very sheet meant to prevent regressions, the exact failure the split fixed. design_handoff/PROD-AHEAD.md section 4 is the authority and says so under the heading "Do not send"; that sheet is machine-checked and this row was not, which is why the row drifted and the sheet did not. PROD-AHEAD section 5 also lists twelve additions DAWN has no row for, including --color-text-on-rank itself, which the outbound handoff should carry as new rows rather than corrections. ── ⏳ RE-MEASURED 2026-08-24, THE PREMISE HOLDS EXACTLY, AND THE ROW MOVES TO `blocked` BECAUSE NO CODE UNBLOCKS IT. Both stylesheets were diffed directly (app/globals.css vs design_handoff/dawn/tokens/colors.css, parsed per top-level block, not via the test runner): --color-focus-ring light prod #B86A15 vs DAWN #E2912F · --color-text-on-broadcast prod #1A1206 vs DAWN #FFFFFF in BOTH modes · --color-text-subtle prod #6E6558 / #A2957D vs DAWN #8F8675 / #7E735F. THREE tokens, five rows, unchanged since 2026-08-19. 🔴 --color-text-on-primary AGREES in both modes (#FFFFFF on both sides) and is still the row that must NOT be sent. Dark focus-ring agrees (#F2B14E), and --color-text-on-rank (#1A1206) is prod-only — an ADDITION for §4 of the handoff, not a correction. THE SEND HAS NOT HAPPENED: design_handoff/CHANGES.md is still the 2026-08-03 round, so no inbound reply references the 2026-08-19 handoff. 🔴 IT IS OWNER-ONLY. DAWN is an external Claude Design project and design_handoff/README.md's loop is copy-the-bundle, owner-mediated in both directions; there is no repo-side action that delivers a doc to it. THE PAYLOAD IS NOW ONE STEP: HANDOFF-TO-DAWN-2026-08-19.md opens with a paste block naming the one file to give DAWN and the one sentence to say, mirroring the “▶ Paste this into Claude Code” block CHANGES.md uses in the inbound direction. Nothing else is pending on this row — the doc, the machine-checked token set and the do-not-send note are all already in the tree.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25. THE SEND HAPPENED AND DAWN APPLIED ALL OF IT. The row's own closing condition was 'when a CHANGES.md reply references the 2026-08-19 handoff, or the owner confirms delivery'. Both are now true. design_handoff/CHANGES.md's H1 reads 'DAWN round of 2026-08-25 (reply to HANDOFF-TO-DAWN-2026-08-19.md)', and its §2 lists every correction as applied value-for-value: focus-ring #B86A15, text-on-broadcast #1A1206 both modes, text-subtle #6E6558 / #A2957D, primary-strong #965C12, surface-post aliased to var(--color-surface), plus all twelve additions from PROD-AHEAD §5 including --color-text-on-rank. DAWN also corrected its own .theme-light-lock scope in step, which carried private copies of five of those values — an extension the handoff did not know about and DAWN volunteered.
  🔴 AND CLOSING IT EXPOSED THE DEFECT UNDERNEATH, WHICH IS LIVE-127. The corrections were applied in DAWN, not in the vendored photocopy: design_handoff/dawn/tokens/colors.css is still the 2026-08-03 export and still holds --color-focus-ring #E2912F. So PROD-AHEAD.md — the sheet the NEXT outbound handoff copies — was still asking DAWN to apply work DAWN finished three weeks ago, and lib/theme/dawn-divergence.test.ts was green throughout, because green there means 'found == declared' and both sets are eight rows. Green never meant the files agree. That is the same stale-row failure this row was CORRECTED for on 2026-08-19, recurring one level up: not a stale row in the sheet, a stale FILE under the whole sheet.

entries.title: The vendored DAWN bundle is a photocopy three rounds old; the token half is now reconciled, the design half is not
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while syncing DAWN's reply, and the finding is the guard, not the files. design_handoff/dawn/ is a hand-copied snapshot of an external Claude Design project. design_handoff/CHANGES.md is DAWN's prose reply. They are copied ACROSS SEPARATELY and nothing measured whether they were the same round. On 2026-08-25 the reply arrived and the bundle did not.
  MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: every marker CHANGES.md says it wrote is absent from the file it names. tokens/effects.css has no 'hero-zone' (the four legibility rungs), ui_kits/marketing/sections.jsx has no 'data-hero-zone', tokens/colors.css has no 'on-media' family, ui_kits/app/index.html has none of the rewritten banner copy, ui_kits/app/nav-rail.jsx has none of the five corrected admin keys. guidelines/on-media.card.html was never copied at all. And colors.css still holds --color-focus-ring #E2912F, the pre-correction brand amber. The bundle is the 2026-08-03 export.
  🔴 WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. lib/theme/dawn-divergence.test.ts reads that colors.css on every pnpm test and was GREEN, because it asserts found-divergences == declared-divergences and both sets are eight rows. Green means 'they disagree in the ways we wrote down'. Read as freshness — which is how it was read — it says the opposite of what is true. The cost was already banked: design_handoff/PROD-AHEAD.md, the sheet the next outbound handoff copies verbatim, was asking DAWN to apply five corrections DAWN applied on 2026-08-25 (LIVE-027).
  ✅ WHAT LANDED WITH THIS ROW. scripts/check-dawn-bundle.mjs declares which round the bundle is and fails BOTH ways. The dangerous direction is the second: if the bundle is re-exported and the declaration is not moved, a refreshed colors.css silently closes five declared divergences, and a sheet that still lists them either re-sends applied work or gets 'reconciled' by pushing DAWN's old values back into app/globals.css — un-fixing three measured AA failures. The guard's failure text names the three files that must move together. PROD-AHEAD.md §0 now carries the do-not-re-send banner, and the divergence test's header says in full what a green run there does not mean.
  THE OWNER STEP IS ONE ACTION: re-export design_handoff/dawn/ from the DAWN project and drop it in. Everything else is already wired and will tell you what to update.

── ✅ THE COLOUR HALF IS CLOSED, 2026-08-26, WITHOUT AN EXPORT. The owner could not download the DAWN bundle, so the question became: how much of this round can be reconciled from what is already written down, and where is the line?
  THE LINE IS TRANSCRIPTION vs INVENTION. CHANGES.md §2 documents every colour value DAWN applied, and PROD-AHEAD §5 carries the twelve additions' hexes (CHANGES.md names them but prints no values). Copying those into design_handoff/dawn/tokens/colors.css is TRANSCRIPTION of two independent written statements - DAWN's own changelog, and the owner confirming it in-thread. Writing tokens/effects.css's four hero rungs, the nav-rail keys, the banner copy or guidelines/on-media.card.html would be INVENTION: those are design artifacts, described in prose, not specified in it. DAWN made precisely that mistake this round - it drew a hero plate from a description production had deleted on an owner ruling (PROD-AHEAD §6a). So the token half was done and the design half was deliberately left.
  ✅ RESULT, AND IT IS COMPLETE FOR ITS HALF: all EIGHT declared divergences closed at once, and prodOnly went empty in both modes. lib/theme/dawn-divergence.test.ts derives the set on every pnpm test and both ledgers are now empty - not because nobody looked, but because the two stylesheets agree on every colour token, re-proven each run. Twelve corrections across :root, .dark AND .theme-light-lock (the lock carried private copies of five, which CHANGES.md §2 flagged), plus eight new tokens.
  🔴 THE GUARD HAD TO CHANGE SHAPE, and that is the durable part. It modelled ONE round for the whole bundle. The moment one file was current and five were not, a single BUNDLE_ROUND was false in BOTH directions: '2026-08-03' rejects the file that IS current, '2026-08-25' demands five that are not. Provenance moved onto each marker - `transcribed` / `exported` / `pending` - where it can actually be true, and the guard now fails per-file in either direction. It caught this partial sync itself: after colors.css changed it went red naming the exact three files that must move together, which is what it was built to do.
  WHAT IS LEFT IS GENUINELY OWNER-ONLY and is now five markers plus one absent file, all design work: tokens/effects.css (hero rungs), ui_kits/marketing/sections.jsx (data-hero-zone), ui_kits/app/index.html (banner copy), ui_kits/marketing/beta.jsx (Funnel induction), ui_kits/app/nav-rail.jsx (five admin keys), guidelines/on-media.card.html (never arrived). ⚠️ NONE OF IT IS LOAD-BEARING: design_handoff/ is eslint-ignored and every reference to it from app code is a COMMENT citing a path. It cannot reach production. This row is housekeeping, and the sheet that could actually mislead - PROD-AHEAD.md - is now correct.

── PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-09-08 (premise sweep, ADR-1269) and it HOLDS exactly as stated: five markers in scripts/check-dawn-bundle.mjs are still declared `pending` (effects.css hero rungs, sections.jsx, app/index.html, beta.jsx, nav-rail.jsx), design_handoff/dawn/guidelines/on-media.card.html still does not exist, and the probe's two green arms (the corrected focus ring and the on-media family in colors.css) are still green. Still design work, still not load-bearing.

verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE in the BUNDLE ITSELF, independent of what scripts/check-dawn-bundle.mjs declares about it - a probe reading our own declaration would close on a constant edit. Four arms: the corrected focus ring AND the on-media family in colors.css (both now PASS, transcribed 2026-08-26), the hero-zone rungs in effects.css, and the on-media card's existence (both still FAIL, design work awaiting a real export). Half green is the honest reading of a mixed bundle.
