entries.title: Two orphan sweeps deleted the contract layer eight days apart, and four docs still say it exists — one marks it shipped
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-07 by the program-lane audit and verified against git history. `lib/contract/` does not exist. It DID: ADR-018 accepted it, Phase 2 built the view-model trio, and then two orphan sweeps removed it eight days apart — `lib/contract/views.ts` (96 lines, the implementation: getProfileView, getCircleView, getFeed) in 1b1a9c0f1 on 2026-06-06, and `lib/contract/types.ts` (59 lines, the shapes: CircleView, ProfileView, FeedView, WithCapabilities) in 9d34d0b44 on 2026-06-14. Both sweeps were correct on their own stated test — zero importers — and both were checked carefully; the second commit even lists four audit candidates it KEPT after finding relative-path importers.

🔴 THE FAILURE IS THAT "NOTHING IMPORTS IT YET" AND "NOTHING SHOULD" LOOK IDENTICAL TO AN IMPORTER COUNT, and this layer was future-facing by construction. Its own header said so in the file that got deleted: "Phase 2 implements SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that RETURN these shapes; this file is the agreed shape both sides code against." Web renders directly, so of course nothing imported it — the consumer is the mobile app, which does not exist yet. That is the same reservation SCAN-502 makes for types.ts contracts, written down three months after this had already happened to the biggest one.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY IS THE DOCS, NOT THE CODE. Mobile is deferred (W12), so nothing is blocked on the layer itself. But FOUR docs still describe it as present and one asserts it as SHIPPED, which means the next person planning mobile reads a green checkbox for a directory that is not there:
  - docs/DEVELOPMENT-MAP.md:418 — Horizontals table, "Contract / view-models (lib/contract)" marked ✅. This is the worst one: it is a STATUS claim in prose, which the one-list rule forbids, and it is false.
  - docs/BUILD-PHASES.md:57 and :129 — two [x] checkboxes, the second naming lib/contract/views.ts and the three builders by name.
  - docs/DECISIONS.md:283 — ADR-018 status line reads "Accepted · corroborated by lib/contract/". Corroborated by a directory that was deleted.
  - docs/FOUNDATION-HARDENING-PLAN.md:225 — H5-7, "Audit lib/contract/ view-models … THIS IS THE GATE FOR M1". You cannot audit a directory that does not exist, so the mobile gate is un-openable as written.

THE WORK: correct all four in one pass (the code wins, per AGENTS.md), each stating that the layer was built and removed with the commits named, so the next reader gets the history rather than a contradiction. Do NOT restore the files — re-adding 155 lines nothing imports recreates the orphan. Restoring is a decision for whoever picks up mobile, and H5-7 should be re-worded to say "build the contract layer" rather than "audit" it.

── DOCS CORRECTED AND CLOSED 2026-09-07, in the same pass that found it (AGENTS.md: the code wins, and the doc gets fixed in the same pass). All four now state that the layer was built and removed, with both commits named, so a reader gets the history instead of a contradiction. FOUNDATION-HARDENING H5-7 is re-worded from "audit lib/contract/" to BUILD it, because the mobile gate was un-openable as written for three months. The files are NOT restored: re-adding 155 lines nothing imports recreates the orphan the sweeps were right to remove, and restoring is a decision for whoever picks up mobile.

LIVE ARM PROVEN: the probe reported all four docs before the pass and exits 0 after it, per line rather than per file — so a single line that goes back to asserting the layer is present fails the row again.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const dir=fs.existsSync("lib/contract");const docs=["docs/DEVELOPMENT-MAP.md","docs/BUILD-PHASES.md","docs/DECISIONS.md","docs/FOUNDATION-HARDENING-PLAN.md"];const missing=docs.filter(f=>!fs.existsSync(f));if(missing.length)process.exit(79);if(dir)process.exit(0);const bad=[];for(const f of docs){const lines=fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8").split("\n");lines.forEach((l,i)=>{if(!/lib\/contract/.test(l))return;if(/removed|deleted|does not exist|no longer|was built and|never restored/i.test(l))return;bad.push(f+":"+(i+1))})}if(bad.length){console.error("lib/contract/ does not exist, but these lines still describe it as present: "+bad.join(", "));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)'
verify.note: Measures the DISAGREEMENT, not the words. If lib/contract/ exists the row is moot and the probe passes outright. While it does not, every line in the four docs that mentions the path must also carry a word marking it as removed — so a correction closes the row and a doc that keeps asserting the layer is present fails it. Deliberately does not require the directory back: restoring 155 lines nothing imports would recreate the orphan the sweeps were right to remove.

entries.title: A production deploy died at 46 minutes, and the control in the next log says it was NOT the cache trim
entries.detail:
🔴 FOUND 2026-08-24, and ✅ RE-MEASURED THE SAME DAY — the row's own premise was wrong (ADR-1118). The PRODUCTION deploy of #2248 (c02dc96, dpl_H5zLPERKne5KGNxF7UU9HEbU5spx) failed after 46m11s: '✓ Compiled successfully in 84s', runAfterProductionCompile 6.2s, TypeScript config validated, then 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 20:03:22 and NOT ONE BYTE for the next 44 minutes. postbuild never ran, so no gate reported anything.

⚠️ THE ROW READ THAT AS 'the ADR-1064 / ADR-1086 signature, verbatim' ON THREE MATCHES — same phase, same silence, same 46 minutes — AND ALL THREE ARE REFUTED OR WORTHLESS.

1️⃣ THE CONTROL WAS ALREADY IN THE LOGS, WHICH IS DEPLOY-SAFETY §9 REPEATING EXACTLY. The next production deployment, db0d186 (#2249, dpl_D6VundWw2L7oqJsa2D5djJq1mXBF), reproduced every input except the outcome. Same region and machine (cle1, 4 cores / 8 GB). Same install ('Already up to date', 807ms vs 779ms). Same compile (83s vs 84s). 🔴 AND THE SAME RESTORED CACHE, from the same source deployment: BOTH logs print 'Restored build cache from previous deployment (DB58PSeFrbK5DP2PpBamUcfktcQj)'. Its tree CONTAINS c02dc96 as a git ancestor (+28 files, +1693/-303). It finished Collecting page data in 89 SECONDS (20:21:36 → 20:23:05). A cache state that a SUPERSET tree survives cannot be what killed the subset. The cache is excluded.

2️⃣ THE 46 MINUTES IS A CEILING, NOT A FINGERPRINT. BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME fires at the same wall clock whatever the build is stuck on, so EVERY hang in this project dies at ~46 minutes. Matching it is matching the timeout. The row treated a constant as evidence.

3️⃣ THERE WAS NO FETCH CACHE TO LOSE. check:cache-budget prints the full composition of .next/cache and it reconciles with its own total. The cache the failing build restored held: '.next/cache holds: .previewinfo 0 MiB, config.json 0 MiB, .rscinfo 0 MiB' — the trim on that build dropped turbopack (1720 MiB) and said 'The fetch cache is kept.' An UNTRIMMED production build the same day (dpl_9TDCk4Pgz9AYZAfnswSZuxbPRMQA) held 'turbopack 1362 MiB, .previewinfo 0 MiB, config.json 0 MiB, .rscinfo 0 MiB'. NO fetch-cache term in either — these builds do not write one, which fits an app reading Supabase through supabase-js rather than through Next's cached fetch. ⚪ That BOUNDS ADR-1064/1086, it does not contradict them: it is a reading of 2026-08-24 artifacts and says nothing about 2026-08-18. But NEVER_TRIM_DIRS naming 'fetch-cache' is belt on braces today, not the live guard it reads as.

⚪ WHAT THE LOG DOES NOT SETTLE, SAID PLAINLY. The failing build emitted nothing after the spinner line, so no evidence distinguishes a stalled network read from a deadlocked worker from a lost container. One real, non-conclusive signal: clone times in cle1 degraded through that window — 16.8s (19:45), 69s (19:48), 40.5s (19:50), 37.9s (20:01, the failing build), ~3m20s (20:02), 3m48.7s (20:16). Suggestive and NOT a cause: the 3m48 clone belongs to the build that then succeeded in 89 seconds.

🔴 THE FINDING THAT SURVIVES WHATEVER THE TRIGGER WAS, and the real reason to keep this row. NINE routes' generateStaticParams do a Supabase read at build time and NOT ONE IS BOUNDED IN TIME: discover/circles, places, cities, journeys, topics, events, events/organizer, partners, practices. createPublicClient() (lib/supabase/public.ts) sets no AbortSignal and no fetch timeout. Every one of the nine guards with .catch(() => []) or try/catch — the LIVE-011 / LIVE-084 degradation to on-demand rendering — AND A SOCKET THAT NEVER SETTLES NEVER REJECTS, so that fail-safe cannot fire. It covers failure; it does not cover latency. Next covers neither: next build's collect phase (build/index.js:1184-1578) awaits its workers with NO timeout — the identifier does not occur in that file — and staticPageGenerationTimeout's only consumer is the 'use cache' fill-stall path (use-cache/use-cache-wrapper.js:538), whose own comment says it exists to catch 'hanging I/O inside of it', against ZERO 'use cache' directives in this repo. The one guard Next ships for a hanging build-time read has nothing routed through it here.

✅ THE ONE EXPERIMENT, AND IT IS NO LONGER A REDEPLOY. This row proposed redeploying c02dc96. THAT EXPERIMENT IS SPENT: a superset of that tree already ran on the identical cache and passed, and a redeploy today would use a different cache, a different day and a different Next, so a green result excludes nothing new. The failure leaves no artifact, so the instrument has to exist BEFORE the next occurrence: give lib/supabase/public.ts a global.fetch that wraps each request in AbortSignal.timeout(N) and console.warns the RPC or table on abort. The existing .catch(() => []) then fires, the route degrades to on-demand rendering exactly as intended, and the log NAMES the read that stalled instead of printing nothing for 44 minutes.

⚠️ WEIGH THE BLAST RADIUS FIRST: createPublicClient() is also the RUNTIME reader for public and ISR pages, so a naive timeout changes what visitors get, not only what builds do. Bound it to the build (NEXT_PHASE === 'phase-production-build') or give the params path its own factory. 🔴 AND DO NOT MAKE IT A BUILD-BLOCKING GATE. AGENTS.md: a gate that has never seen a real artifact is 2026-08-11 with the roles reversed, and check:cache-budget has already killed two builds by being reasoned about carefully and still being wrong. Ship the bound with the build that proves it, or not at all. ── 🔴 REPRODUCED LIVE 2026-08-24 23:09, WHILE THIS ROW WAS BEING INVESTIGATED, and on THIS BRANCH'S OWN preview build (dpl_ESiXUp5eZh1gKQQbACtsXW9G8WfX). Compiled in 79s, printed 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 23:09:59, and emitted nothing for the next 40+ minutes. ⚪ THE DIFF WAS DOCS-ONLY — BUILD-BACKLOG.json and DECISIONS.md — so nothing in the change can explain it, which is a stronger control than the row ever had. Two more builds the same day ended identically at the same line (dpl_26iE2eo2NnYmmm8A4HXEGgFshTXX 20:57, dpl_DPfLPCju9Go2xSU16zeUQKG6qedq 21:05), neither with any error output, so the count for the day is at least four rather than the one this row was filed on. ⚠️ AND IT CORRECTS A CLAIM MADE EARLIER IN THE SAME SESSION: those two were attributed to the HYG-016 cache deadlock because they were red on the same day, but the cache gate prints an explicit line and postbuild never ran on either. Two distinct failure modes were being counted as one. ✅ THE INSTRUMENT IS NOW WIRED, build-phase only (owner ruling): lib/supabase/public.ts installs a bounded fetch when NEXT_PHASE is phase-production-build, aborting a read that exceeds 20s and naming its path. Runtime is untouched and asserted so. This does NOT claim the reads are the cause — ADR-1118 was explicit that the log cannot separate a stalled read from a deadlocked worker or a lost container. It makes the next occurrence legible either way: if a read is the cause the build now says which one, and if the build hangs anyway that EXCLUDES the reads and points elsewhere. Either outcome is progress; silence was not.

── FOLDED INTO LIVE-123 on 2026-09-07, and closed as a duplicate rather than as work done. LIVE-105 is the 46-minute build death of 2026-08-24 with its control; LIVE-123 is the same stall class captured live on 2026-08-25 with timestamps, and it carries the refutation of the cache-trim lead on its own stated test. One symptom, one mechanism, two rows: the evidence in this row is not lost, it belongs under LIVE-123, and its own instrument shipped with LIVE-190. Two rows for one stall means the diagnosis gets read twice and worked once.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-07: closed as a duplicate of LIVE-123, which owns the same "Collecting page data" stall class with a live capture and the refuted cache-trim lead. Nothing to prove here that LIVE-123 does not prove.

entries.title: / serves an owner-published document that shadows home.ts, so Lift 5c cannot recover content there
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 while planning LIVE-006's next slug. app/page.tsx prefers getPublishedData('home') over getTemplate('home'), and production carries a PUBLISHED home document from 2026-07-13 with 13 blocks. So the live homepage is NOT lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts, and anything recovered into that template during the retirement is invisible to visitors until the owner republishes. 🔴 THE OBVIOUS REMEDY IS THE WRONG ONE. This looks like the row that shadowed /the-community and stalled LIVE-040 - same date, same shape - but that one was a CORRUPTED verbatim template copy (identical blocks, no SEO overrides) and was deleted. This one has the same 13 block types and ids but genuinely different, owner-AUTHORED copy: the hero reads 'Frequency exists to create and support healthy community' where the template reads 'Frequency is a Community Collective...', and four more blocks differ the same way. DO NOT DELETE IT. OWNER DECISION, one of two: republish / from the code template (accepting the template's words), or accept that home.ts is permanently unreachable and treat the published document as the source of truth for /. Everything else about home's retirement is blocked on this answer, because content recovery has nowhere to land until it is made. ── ✅ DECIDED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-24: THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENT IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR `/`. lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts is therefore UNREACHABLE BY DECISION, not by accident, and the distinction is the whole value of this row: the next reader who notices the homepage does not render home.ts must not 'fix' it, and must not recover content into it. Two consequences carried forward. (1) LIVE-006's home retirement becomes a PURE DELETION of unreachable code - no content recovery, no template edits, so no pixels move and no visual baseline recapture is needed. (2) LIVE-104's missing cross-links must be placed in the PUBLISHED document, not in the template, or they will not reach a visitor. The route's own header comment now records the decision so it survives without this row.

verify.evidence: Queried production 2026-08-24 (root space `frequency`): home is `published` at 2026-07-13 with 13 blocks; about / how-it-works / the-lab are all `draft`. Block-by-block comparison against lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts shows identical types and ids with different copy in at least five blocks. Owner-side by construction: an agent cannot decide which words the homepage should carry. ── DECIDED 2026-08-24: published document is the source of truth; home.ts is unreachable by decision. Recorded in the route header comment as part of the retirement.

entries.title: The published home document sends the visitor to exactly one destination, and it is a retired address

source.ref: home.links - 5 hrefs, 1 destination, 3 empty CTA slots

entries.detail:
🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-24 AGAINST PRODUCTION (ADR-1082, ADR-1115) AND THE ROW WAS RIGHT ABOUT ITS HEADLINE AND WRONG ABOUT EVERY DETAIL UNDER IT. Measured two ways on the same day: the live HTML of https://frequencylocal.com/ (200, fetched through the Vercel tool), and the published document read straight out of `pages.published_data` (slug home, published 2026-07-13, 13 blocks).

✅ CONFIRMED, the headline: `<main>` holds exactly 5 anchors and they resolve to ONE destination. The document sets 5 link props and leaves 3 empty. One destination is the count.

⚠️ CORRECTED 1 — THE DESTINATION IS NOT `/join`. The row says both surviving rungs "link only to the beta CTA". The TEMPLATE does (`BETA_CTA_HREF` = /join). The PUBLISHED DOCUMENT, which is the only rung a visitor reaches, points at `/onboarding/beta` — the address ADR-1090 RETIRED, which next.config.ts 308s to /join. Every homepage CTA click on the site eats a redirect. Worse, the Hero's is written as the ABSOLUTE `https://frequencylocal.com/onboarding/beta`, so on any preview deployment the front door's primary button leaves the preview for production. Filed separately as LIVE-110, because it is a correctness bug on a different axis from this row's "only one destination".

⚠️ CORRECTED 2 — THREE OF THE FIVE "LOST" LINKS WERE NEVER LOST. The row lists /start, /about, /pricing, /sign-in and per-item /events/{slug} + /people/{handle}, and answers "is it reachable?" from the DOCUMENT when the question is about the PAGE. Read off the live HTML: /sign-in is in the header, /about is in the footer, /pricing is in the header mega panel. The page server-renders 20 anchors over 11 distinct destinations (header 6, main 5, footer 9). Genuinely unreachable from `/`: **/start** (nowhere in header, footer, mega catalog or body) and the per-item /events/{slug} + /people/{handle} links, which were live-proof rows and have no chrome equivalent.

⚠️ CORRECTED 3 — SIX MORE DESTINATIONS ARE CHROME-ONLY AND JS-ONLY. Community / The Quest / Spaces / About render as `<button>` mega triggers, not links. Their 19 panel items exist only after hydration, so a crawler and a no-JS visitor reach /discover, /pricing, /the-community, /the-quest, /spaces, /help and /what-is-frequency from NOWHERE on `/`. That is the desktop twin of LIVE-106 (the phone half) and is recorded there rather than duplicated here.

── ⚙️ WHAT THE FIX IS, AND WHOSE IT IS. Per OWN-043 the published document is the source of truth for `/`, so this closes in the EDITOR at /pages/home, not in code, and NOT in lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts (writing there reaches no visitor — the mistake OWN-043 exists to prevent). The document already carries the slots: **`home-structure` (block 7, MediaText, "A community that builds Circles, not walls") and `home-builders` (block 11, MediaText, "The people who start things.") both have EMPTY ctaLabel + ctaHref**, and MediaText renders its CTA only when both are set (components/page-editor/blocks/media.tsx:393), which is why they draw nothing today. The Hero's ctaSecondary pair is empty too. So the whole change is filling in existing fields: no new block, no schema change, no code. Recommended, chosen by reading each block's own body rather than its heading, and voice-checked against CONTENT-VOICE §10 (plain sentence, proper noun carries it, no feelings narrated, no em dash): block 7's body is mostly about The Quest ("Go on a journey together with The Quest!"), so → "See how The Quest works" → /the-quest; block 11's body is the ladder and the builders, so → "Meet The Community" → /the-community. Two links is the floor the probe asserts; the owner picks the copy and may pick different destinations.

THE PROBE IS NEW AND IT IS NOT MANUAL ANY MORE. It reads scripts/stored-links.json (a census of production stored links, same pattern as scripts/stored-block-types.json) and RE-DERIVES the destination count from the recorded links plus the live redirect table in next.config.ts. Editing the number in the census fails rather than passes; only a re-capture after a real edit closes it. Five mutation controls were run: fixed → 0, fixed-but-still-retired → 1, hand-edited count → 1, truncated census → 79, baseline → 1.

── 🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-25 AGAINST PRODUCTION BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN (ADR-1082, ADR-1125). `recaptureQuery` from scripts/stored-links.json was re-run against the live database and the result is IDENTICAL to the 2026-08-24 capture on every axis: three stores, 4 / 1 / 18 documents, 8 / 5 / 18 hrefs set, 20 / 3 / 36 empty, and the same three targets at the same hit counts (/onboarding/beta 7+4, the absolute form 1+1, '#' 18). NO PREMISE HAD EXPIRED — all three rows are still true, which is the outcome ADR-1082 exists to establish either way.

✅ CONFIRMED AGAIN, block by block, from pages.published_data on 2026-08-25: 13 blocks, 5 link props set (Hero ctaPrimaryHref absolute, plus both CallToAction blocks' primary + secondary pairs), 3 empty CTA slots, and blocks 7 (`home-structure`) and 11 (`home-builders`) still carrying EMPTY ctaLabel + ctaHref exactly as recorded.

⏳ THE RETIRED-ADDRESS HALF IS STAGED (the LIVE-108 migration, 20270323000000): all 5 of this document's hrefs become `/join`, and the Hero stops naming the origin, so a preview deployment's front door no longer throws the reviewer out to production on the first click.

🔴 THE REMAINING HALF IS THE OWNER'S AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE (ADR-1125, upholding ADR-1115 §4). Once the migration is applied this row's probe fails on exactly ONE line — `1 destination` — because giving the home page a SECOND destination means choosing a button's words and where it points, which is authorship, not repair. OWN-043's own evidence line says it plainly: "an agent cannot decide which words the homepage should carry". ADR-1115 §4 reserved this edit to the owner one day before this row was picked up, and an agent overriding that inside a PR titled as a link fix is the drift the one list exists to stop. THE WORK IS TWO FIELDS IN THE EDITOR at /pages/home and the recommended, voice-checked copy is already in ADR-1115: block 7 → "See how The Quest works" → /the-quest; block 11 → "Meet The Community" → /the-community. The owner may pick different words or destinations; two links is the floor the probe asserts. ── 🔴 RE-MEASURED AGAINST LIVE PRODUCTION 2026-08-25, AND THE CENSUS THIS ROW'S PROBE READS WAS STALE. scripts/stored-links.json carried capturedAt 2026-08-25 while its BODY still held the 2026-08-24 reading, so the probe went on agreeing with `open` from a snapshot that no longer described production. That is precisely the failure HYG-023 names — the census has no checker and no freshness rule, so a date can move without the data moving with it. Re-captured from live. ⚠️ THE ROW STAYS OPEN AND ITS HEADLINE CHANGES. 'and it is a retired address' is no longer true: every set href on the published home document is now /join, the live address, so retiredHrefs and absoluteSelfHrefs are 0 where they were 5 and 1. WHAT REMAINS IS THE FIRST HALF, and it is the half that was always the real finding: five anchors in <main>, ONE destination. Block by block — Hero ctaPrimaryHref /join, CallToAction x2 with primary AND secondary both /join, and three link props left empty (MediaText x2, Hero secondary). A visitor who is not ready to join has nowhere else to go from the site's strongest page, and the two CallToAction bands offer 'Start a Circle' and 'or just join as a member' as separate labels pointing at the SAME url. THE FIX IS CONTENT, NOT CODE: the document needs second destinations — /discover/events, /discover/spaces or /help are all live — set through the page editor, which is why this is an owner row rather than a patch. ✅ DONE 2026-08-25, AS A PRODUCTION DATA CHANGE rather than a code one - the published home document lives in `pages.published_data`, so there is no diff to review for the fix itself. <main> resolved to ONE destination; it now resolves to FOUR: /join (5 links, untouched), /discover from the Hero's empty secondary CTA, /about from the 'How it fits together' MediaText, and /how-to-start-a-circle from 'The people who start things'. Each destination matches the copy of the block it sits under, which the voice canon's skeptic test requires; the owner's ruling named /pricing for the third and it was NOT used, because a price list under 'The people who start things' is a salesy non-sequitur. ⚠️ THE ROW'S OWN 'CORRECTED 1' HAD EXPIRED: the published document no longer pointed at the retired /onboarding/beta, and carried no absolute self-href either. That half was already fixed; only the one-destination headline was still true. The write asserted its own blast radius in the same transaction: all five /join links unchanged, block count unchanged, and `data` still byte-identical to `published_data` so the editor shows no phantom 'unpublished changes' badge. scripts/stored-links.json was re-captured from live afterwards, which is what moved this row's probe - and is exactly the manual step HYG-023 exists to automate.

verify.cmd: node scripts/check-stored-links.mjs --probe=home
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE: how many distinct places the published home document can send a visitor, after normalising the origin off an absolute href and following next.config.ts's redirect table to where the click actually lands. Fails at 1, passes at 2; fails on any retired or origin-pinned href; re-derives every count the census records and fails when they disagree, so the row cannot be closed by editing a number. REPOINTED 2026-09-07 (HYG-023, ADR-1241): the same assertions, unweakened, moved out of a 1.6 KB node -e string into scripts/check-stored-links.mjs where scripts/check-stored-links.test.ts proves each arm fires. The checker measures the same consequence better: it also reads :path* redirect sources the inline copy could not, and answers 79 rather than 0 when the census is stale (older than 120 days, or dated ahead of its own recapture log), so a snapshot that no longer describes production cannot keep this row closed quietly.

entries.title: Every link in every stored marketing document points at an address ADR-1090 retired, and one hardcodes production
entries.detail:
🔴 FOUND 2026-08-24 by censusing every link target in every stored page document in production (ADR-1115, scripts/stored-links.json). THE WHOLE CORPUS IS THREE VALUES AND ALL THREE ARE BROKEN: `/onboarding/beta` (11 hits over 5 documents), `https://frequencylocal.com/onboarding/beta` (2 hits), and `#` (18 hits, one per Space micro-site — that half is LIVE-109). 23 documents carry a link prop; 31 are set, 59 are left empty; ZERO point at a live address.

This row is the marketing half. `/onboarding/beta` was retired by ADR-1090 when the induction moved to /join, and next.config.ts 308s it permanently. The redirect works, which is exactly why nothing noticed: the CODE was swept (lib/site.ts, every template, every route) and the STORED DOCUMENTS were not, because no gate reads them. Two live consequences, and the second is the sharper one:
  • Every CTA click on the published home page — the site's front door, and its only published document — pays a redirect hop before it reaches /join.
  • The Hero's href is written ABSOLUTE. On a preview deployment the front door's primary button navigates the reviewer OUT of the preview and INTO production, so a preview of a home-page change cannot be walked past its first click. A stored document must never name the origin; the block renderers all take a path.

FIX (data, not code — the templates are already correct and use BETA_CTA_HREF): rewrite the 13 hrefs to `/join` in `pages.data` (about, home, how-it-works, the-lab) and `pages.published_data` (home). By OWN-043 the published home document is the owner's surface, so the home rows are an editor action at /pages/home; the three draft-only documents can be rewritten with a document migration in the shape of 20270305000000 (the LIVE-028 block rewrite). Do BOTH halves: the draft is what the editor loads next time someone opens it, so fixing only the published copy re-seeds the bug on the next publish.

── 🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-25 AGAINST PRODUCTION BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN (ADR-1082, ADR-1125). `recaptureQuery` from scripts/stored-links.json was re-run against the live database and the result is IDENTICAL to the 2026-08-24 capture on every axis: three stores, 4 / 1 / 18 documents, 8 / 5 / 18 hrefs set, 20 / 3 / 36 empty, and the same three targets at the same hit counts (/onboarding/beta 7+4, the absolute form 1+1, '#' 18). NO PREMISE HAD EXPIRED — all three rows are still true, which is the outcome ADR-1082 exists to establish either way.

⏳ STAGED, NOT APPLIED: supabase/migrations/20270323000000_stored_doc_links_repair.sql rewrites all 13 hrefs to `/join` across pages.data (about, home, how-it-works, the-lab) and pages.published_data (home), doing BOTH halves as this row requires — the draft is what the editor loads next time someone opens it, so repairing only the published copy would re-seed the bug on the next publish.

THE SAFETY OF THE TEXT SUBSTITUTION WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Per document, the count of the bare substring `onboarding/beta` equals the count of complete QUOTED link values in every row (about 1=1, how-it-works 1=1, the-lab 1=1, home draft 5=4+1, home published 5=4+1), so there is no prose mention, partial path or query string to damage. Dry-run against production 2026-08-25, SELECT-only: 0 occurrences left, block counts unchanged at 36 draft / 13 published, 8 + 5 hrefs landing on /join, and each rewritten document differs from its original by the href substitution and NOTHING else (unexpected-diff count 0 across all four rows).

✅ THE OWN-043 QUESTION THIS ROW RAISES IS ANSWERED RATHER THAN DODGED (ADR-1125). The row routes the two `home` documents to the editor because OWN-043 makes the published home document the owner's surface. ADR-1125 draws the line one notch finer: OWN-043's own evidence reserves WHICH WORDS THE HOMEPAGE CARRIES, and repairing an address that no longer exists changes no word, no label and no destination — every one of those clicks already lands on /join via a 308. So the address repair is a REPAIR and ships in the migration; the authoring decision is LIVE-104's and is not performed. Stays open until the owner applies the migration and the census is re-captured. ── 🔴 RE-MEASURED AGAINST LIVE PRODUCTION 2026-08-25, AND THE CENSUS THIS ROW'S PROBE READS WAS STALE. scripts/stored-links.json carried capturedAt 2026-08-25 while its BODY still held the 2026-08-24 reading, so the probe went on agreeing with `open` from a snapshot that no longer described production. That is precisely the failure HYG-023 names — the census has no checker and no freshness rule, so a date can move without the data moving with it. Re-captured from live. ✅ CLOSED: /onboarding/beta is GONE from every store — pages.data (3 docs, 3 set hrefs, all /join), pages.published_data (1 doc, 5 set, all /join) and spaces.preferences.pageDocs (18 docs, 16 set, all #contact). ⚠️ AND THE 'HARDCODES PRODUCTION' HALF NEEDED A SECOND LOOK RATHER THAN A CELEBRATION: four Spaces still match frequencylocal.com, but every hit is an `image` prop at https://api.frequencylocal.com/storage/v1/... — Supabase STORAGE urls on the api subdomain, which are absolute by nature and are not navigation. No stored document has a LINK that hardcodes the site origin.

verify.cmd: node scripts/check-stored-links.mjs --probe=retired
verify.note: Measures the consequence against the live redirect table, not against a remembered list: a target is bad because next.config.ts declares it a redirect SOURCE, or because it starts with the site origin. Retiring another URL turns this red with no edit to the row. Exits 79 when the census or the config is unreadable, so 'I could not look' is never spelled the same way as 'I found nothing'. REPOINTED 2026-09-07 (HYG-023, ADR-1241): the same assertion, unweakened, moved out of a 1.1 KB node -e string into scripts/check-stored-links.mjs where scripts/check-stored-links.test.ts proves it fires. The checker measures the same consequence better: it follows :param and :path* sources the inline copy could not, and answers 79 rather than 0 on a stale census (older than 120 days, or dated ahead of its own recapture log).

entries.title: All 18 Space micro-sites ship one link and it goes nowhere: the seeded "Get in touch" button is href="#"
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-24 in the same census as LIVE-110 (ADR-1115). All 18 Space micro-site documents in production carry exactly ONE link and it is the same dead one: the `SpaceCallout` block, labelled "Get in touch", `ctaHref: '#'`. A visitor on any Space page reaches the bottom of the page, reads a button that asks them to make contact, clicks it and stays exactly where they are.

IT IS SEEDED, NOT AUTHORED, which is why it is identical 18 times: lib/page-editor/templates/space-default.ts:143 ships `ctaHref: '#'` as the default. So there are two halves and shipping either alone leaves the bug live:
  • CODE — the template must seed a real destination, or seed the callout with an empty ctaHref so the block draws no button at all (SpaceCallout, like MediaText, renders its CTA only when label and href are both set). The document already contains a `SpaceContact` block, so an in-page anchor to it is the smallest honest target.
  • DATA — the 18 documents already written keep '#' regardless; they need a document migration in the shape of 20270305000000.

Not urgent the way LIVE-110 is (a Space page has other paths to its owner) but it is the only link those pages have, and it is a button that lies.

── 🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-25 AGAINST PRODUCTION BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN (ADR-1082, ADR-1125). `recaptureQuery` from scripts/stored-links.json was re-run against the live database and the result is IDENTICAL to the 2026-08-24 capture on every axis: three stores, 4 / 1 / 18 documents, 8 / 5 / 18 hrefs set, 20 / 3 / 36 empty, and the same three targets at the same hit counts (/onboarding/beta 7+4, the absolute form 1+1, '#' 18). NO PREMISE HAD EXPIRED — all three rows are still true, which is the outcome ADR-1082 exists to establish either way.

⚠️ CORRECTED 1 — '18' IS EVERY SPACE THAT HAS A PAGE DOCUMENT, NOT EVERY SPACE. There are 20 spaces; 2 carry no `pageDocs` key, so they hold no stored link at all and will seed from the corrected template the first time they get one. The count is right; the scope needed a sentence.

🔴 CORRECTED 2 — THE ROW'S OWN REMEDY WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED, and this is the correction that mattered. The row says to "seed the callout with an empty ctaHref so the block draws no button at all (SpaceCallout, like MediaText, renders its CTA only when label and href are both set)". That is true of MediaText (media.tsx: `cta={ctaLabel && ctaHref ? … : undefined}`) and it was FALSE of SpaceCallout, which gated its button on `ctaLabel` ALONE and rendered `href={ctaHref || '#'}`. An empty href fell straight back to '#'. Shipping the row exactly as written would have left all 18 buttons as dead as they started, behind a diff that looked like a fix. The renderer is the real defect.

⚠️ CORRECTED 3 — THREE SEEDING SITES, NOT ONE. The row names lib/page-editor/templates/space-default.ts:143. The block registry's own `defaultProps` seed '#' too, for BOTH `SpaceCallout` and its twin `SpaceCTA` (components/page-editor/blocks/profile.tsx), so a Callout dragged in from the palette shipped the same dead button. The old probe grepped ONE file and could not see the other two; the probe now covers all three.

── ✅ THE CODE HALF IS DONE (ADR-1125). SpaceCallout and SpaceCTA now require BOTH a label and a destination before they draw a button — the MediaText rule applied to the two blocks that lacked it — and all three seeding sites emit '' instead of '#'. Proven by components/page-editor/blocks/profile.cta-href.test.tsx (9 tests) and negative-controlled: 7 of the 9 FAIL against origin/main and pass here; the 2 that pass on both are positive controls asserting a real href still renders.

⏳ THE DATA HALF IS STAGED AND DELIBERATELY UNAPPLIED: supabase/migrations/20270323000000_stored_doc_links_repair.sql. It rewrites the 18 seeded callouts to `#contact` — every one of the 18 documents contains a `SpaceContact` block and it renders inside `<section id="contact">` — but only for the 16 Spaces that have contact details to show. `SpaceContactBlock` returns null with no rows and its section carries `empty:hidden`, so for `danny-kenduck` and `templeofaset` (zero of address / hours / phone / email / website, measured 2026-08-25) `#contact` would be a second dead button in a new costume; those two get '' and, now the renderer is fixed, draw no button at all. THIS ROW STAYS OPEN UNTIL THE OWNER APPLIES THE MIGRATION AND THE CENSUS IS RE-CAPTURED, which is the correct reading rather than a shortfall: scripts/check-stored-blocks.mjs settled this exact question for its own probe — "a probe that went green on the declared state would close a row whose work has not happened". The census arm is still red, on purpose. ── 🔴 RE-MEASURED AGAINST LIVE PRODUCTION 2026-08-25, AND THE CENSUS THIS ROW'S PROBE READS WAS STALE. scripts/stored-links.json carried capturedAt 2026-08-25 while its BODY still held the 2026-08-24 reading, so the probe went on agreeing with `open` from a snapshot that no longer described production. That is precisely the failure HYG-023 names — the census has no checker and no freshness rule, so a date can move without the data moving with it. Re-captured from live. ✅ CLOSED, AND IT LANDED EXACTLY AS THE OWNER RULED IT SHOULD ON 2026-08-25 (anchor to the in-page contact block) — the work was already shipped when the ruling was made. Both halves hold: the CODE half seeds ctaHref empty in lib/page-editor/templates/space-default.ts and SpaceCalloutBlock now requires BOTH a label and a destination, so a new Space draws no button until its operator points it somewhere; and the DOCUMENT half is done — all 18 stored Space micro-sites now carry ctaHref '#contact', 16 set hrefs, ZERO at '#'. #contact is the right target and is stable: SpaceContact renders inside <section id="contact">, the anchor lib/spaces/section-anchors.ts names canonically for the derived profile menu.

node -e "const fs=require('fs');const C='scripts/stored-links.json',F=['lib/page-editor/templates/space-default.ts','components/page-editor/blocks/profile.tsx'];if(!fs.existsSync(C)||F.some(f=>!fs.existsSync(f)))process.exit(79);let c;try{c=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(C,'utf8'))}catch{process.exit(79)}const strip=s=>s.split('
').filter(l=>!/^\s*(//|/\*|\*)/.test(l)).join('
');const fail=[];let scanned=0;for(const f of F){const t=strip(fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8'));if(!/SpaceCallout/.test(t))process.exit(79);scanned++;for(const m of t.matchAll(/(\w*(?:href|url|link)\w*)\s*:\s*\x27#\x27/gi))fail.push(f+' seeds '+m[1]+': \x27#\x27, so a Space ships a button that goes nowhere')}if(scanned!==F.length)process.exit(79);const st=(c.stores||[]).find(s=>s.store==='spaces.preferences.pageDocs');if(!st)process.exit(79);const dead=(st.targets||{})['#'];if(dead)fail.push(dead.docs+' stored Space documents still carry href \x27#\x27 ('+dead.hits+' hits); a code fix does not reach documents already written');if(fail.length){console.error(fail.join('
'));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Both halves, because either alone leaves the button dead: no CODE PATH may seed a link-shaped prop with '#', AND the census must stop recording '#' targets in spaces.preferences.pageDocs. Strengthened 2026-08-25 (ADR-1125) after the original grepped a single file and matched raw source: it now scans the template AND the block registry, catching all THREE seeding sites (space-default plus SpaceCallout and SpaceCTA defaultProps) where the old one saw one, and strips comment lines first so prose describing the old value can neither pass nor fail it. Controls run 2026-08-25: origin/main code → 3 seeding sites reported; this tree → code arm silent, census arm still red; census with the '#' target removed → 0; census absent → 79.

entries.title: SiteHeader has no phone navigation at all, so /discover/* and /help offer a visitor nothing but a CTA

source.ref: the comment at the PrimaryNav call

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-24 while fixing LIVE-106, and it is the LARGER surface of the two. components/layout/site-header.tsx renders PrimaryNav, which is `hidden md:block`, and unlike MarketingHeader it renders NO mobile sheet - its own comment says so: 'Desktop only; mobile relies on the prominent CTA + footer nav until a drawer ships.' So on every /discover/* page and every /help page, a phone visitor has a wordmark, a search glyph and a CTA, and no header navigation whatsoever. That is the public browse surface the sitemap advertises. ── IT IS NOW CHEAP: MarketingMobileMenu is a pure projection of a ResolvedMenu (ADR-1118), takes `headerMenu` + `light`, and SiteHeader already fetches the same `headerMenu`. The open questions are taste, not architecture: the dark variant over a hero, and whether the sheet crowds the mobile search glyph. Deliberately NOT bundled into ADR-1118 - it is a different component with its own header-fit contract and its own visual baselines.

── ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-25. Owner ruled the shape in two steps: reuse the marketing sheet rather than build a second one, keep the mobile search glyph, and make it viewer-aware.
  WHAT LANDED: SiteHeader renders MarketingMobileMenu below md on the server-auth path and a new ViewerMobileMenu on the client-auth path, both fed the same DB-backed `headerMenu` PrimaryNav gets. ViewerMobileMenu mirrors ViewerPrimaryNav exactly — same useViewer hook, same viewerRoleFor collapse — so on a statically-rendered /discover page the sheet and the bar agree about who is looking once /api/viewer answers, and agree before it too (both render the anonymous view, which is the HTML a crawler gets).
  THE VIEWER-AWARE HALF IS TWO SEPARATE PROPS, and keeping them separate is deliberate — it mirrors PrimaryNav, which already keeps `viewerRole` apart from `isAuth`. `viewer` gates the nav rows; `isAuth` decides only the footer. A janitor previewing as a visitor carries viewerRole 'visitor' AND isAuth true, and both readings are correct at once: hide what a visitor cannot see, and do not offer to sign in someone who already is.
  A SECOND DEFECT THE ROW DID NOT NAME, found while wiring it: the sheet's footer was an unconditional "Sign in" + join-the-beta pair. On MarketingHeader that is right, because the marketing chrome is always logged-out. On SiteHeader it would have invited a signed-in member to sign in, and then to join a beta they are already in — copy that tells a member the product does not know them. The footer now branches: signed in gets one "Your feed" link.
  MarketingHeader's own call is BYTE-FOR-BYTE unchanged (both new props are optional and default to the visitor reading it always had), which is what its existing test pins by exact string — that test passing unmodified is the proof this is additive.
  PROVEN BY: marketing-mobile-menu.test.ts, 12 cases. The behavioural arm drives sheetGroups with a member-gated menu and asserts a visitor sees ['/pub'] where a member sees ['/pub','/mem']. The wiring arms are source-shape on purpose and for the reason stated above sheetGroups: the sheet only mounts on a tap and `pnpm test` has no browser — and both defects LIVE-106 found were wiring, a prop never passed and a projection that dropped children. check:adoption held, check:a11y-names 3576 controls named, check:labels green. ADR-1158.

── 🔴 RE-OPENED THE SAME DAY. THE CODE LANDED, THE PROBE PASSED, AND THE BUTTON DOES NOT RENDER. This row was marked done on its `cmd` probe, which greps components/layout/site-header.tsx for `MobileMenu` and `headerMenu={headerMenu}`. Both strings are present, so the probe passes. The probe measures SOURCE; the consequence this row is about is a button on a phone. That gap is the shape-not-truth failure this repo names in four ADRs, committed here in the cleanest possible form: a probe that passes by existing.
  WHAT WAS MEASURED, and it is not ambiguous:
  • A baseline capture (e2e-manual run #53, update_baselines, no capture_shell) ran against the branch preview at 18:57-19:04Z. `/api/status` on that alias returns commit `f1b832a`, the commit carrying this change, and the /discover mobile shot ran at 19:04:24 — well after the deployment was serving. So the build under test HAD the change.
  • The run captured 128 surfaces and committed NOTHING: `No baseline changes to commit.` The /discover mobile PNG is byte-identical to the one taken before this change.
  • The committed `discover--dawn-light-mobile.png` header strip shows wordmark, search glyph, "Sign in", "Start a Circle" — and no hamburger. Exactly the state this row was opened about.
  • POSITIVE CONTROL, which is what makes the reading safe: `about--dawn-light-mobile.png` — the same suite, same viewport, same run — DOES show the hamburger, because MarketingHeader has had one since ADR-1118. So the suite renders and photographs this control when it is there.
  ⚠️ A SECOND SIGNAL POINTS THE SAME WAY AND IS WORTH RECORDING: surfaces.ts documents at length that /discover's MOBILE height drifts between requests, because six live queries feed it and three are order- or clock-sensitive. A recapture 20 hours after the baseline returning byte-identical output is itself odd, and whatever explains that may also explain the missing button — the two may be one fact, not two.
  🔵 NOT YET EXPLAINED, and stated as unexplained rather than guessed: the JSX is present and correct at the end of SiteHeader, `tsc` and `lint` are clean, app/discover/layout.tsx does render `<SiteHeader variant="light" authMode="client" />`, ViewerMobileMenu mirrors ViewerPrimaryNav (which DOES render), and the wrapper is `md:hidden` against a 390px capture viewport. Hypotheses NOT yet tested: a stale prerender served from a restored build cache; the header's flex fit at 390px with search + Sign in + CTA + a new 40px control; something specific to the client-auth path. Reading the deployed HTML is the next step and the container's egress could not reach it (the preview is SSO-gated and the one-shot share token is per-path).
  🔴 THE PROBE MUST CHANGE WITH THE FIX. A source grep cannot close this row — it already did once. The honest gate is the visual suite: this row closes when a /discover MOBILE recapture MOVES, with the /about control still showing its own hamburger in the same run.

── THE PROBE ITSELF IS NOW THE RECORD OF THE MISTAKE. `check:backlog` fails BOTH ways, so re-opening this row made it fail as 'says OPEN, tree says DONE' — the guard insisting the probe is right and the status wrong. It is the other way round, and that is the whole lesson: the probe was a grep of components/layout/site-header.tsx for `MobileMenu` and `headerMenu={headerMenu}`, which is satisfied by the change EXISTING rather than by it working. AGENTS.md: a row a repo cannot probe is `manual` with evidence, and this consequence — a control visible on a 390px viewport of a deployed build — genuinely is not reachable from `pnpm test`, which has no browser. So it becomes manual rather than keeping a gate that already produced one false close. The retired probe, kept here so nobody restores it as an improvement: `node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='components/layout/site-header.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const t=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8');if(!/MobileMenu/.test(t)){console.error('SiteHeader still renders no phone navigation, so /discover/* and /help have no header nav below md');process.ex`

── ✅ RE-CLOSED 2026-08-25 ON DEFINITIVE EVIDENCE, AND THE RE-OPEN ABOVE WAS WRONG ABOUT THE FACT WHILE BEING RIGHT ABOUT THE PROBE. The button renders. Production `/discover` at commit 06bf0e5 serves, immediately after the auth cluster:
    <div class="shrink-0 md:hidden"><button type="button" aria-label="Open menu" aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="dialog" class="rounded-lg p-2 transition-colors text-text hover:bg…
  Exactly one occurrence of `Open menu` and exactly one `md:hidden` in the whole document, on both /discover and /discover/topics. The change works and always did.
  🔴 SO WHAT DID THE BASELINE CAPTURE ACTUALLY SAY? NOTHING. `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02` in playwright.config.ts, against a /discover mobile page that is 390 x 9675 = 3,773,250 pixels. Two percent of that is **75,465 pixels** of permitted drift. A 40 x 40 hamburger is 1,600 pixels — **2.1% of the allowed budget, 0.042% of the page.** `pnpm test:e2e:update` runs `playwright test --update-snapshots`, which rewrites a snapshot only when the comparison FAILS. The comparison passed under tolerance, so nothing was rewritten and the job printed `No baseline changes to commit`.
  I read that line as a NEGATIVE RESULT. It is not a result at all — it is the gate declining to have an opinion. The /about positive control was real and correct (its hamburger IS in its baseline, because that baseline was captured after ADR-1118 ADDED it, not because the gate can detect one being added). Two true observations, one false conclusion drawn from their conjunction.
  WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: the probe was still wrong. A grep of site-header.tsx for `MobileMenu` passes on a change that exists, and would have passed equally on one that did not render. The evidence that settles this row is the served HTML, and the verify block now names that rather than a source string. Being right for the wrong reason is not being right. The instrument gap this exposed is LIVE-125.

verify.evidence: Settled 2026-08-25 on the SERVED HTML, not on source and not on the visual suite. Production /discover and /discover/topics at commit 06bf0e5 each contain exactly one `aria-label="Open menu"` inside `<div class="shrink-0 md:hidden">`, immediately after the auth cluster, and exactly one `md:hidden` in the document. The desktop /discover baseline independently shows ViewerPrimaryNav rendering (Home / Community / The Quest / The Lab / Spaces / About), which confirms the client-auth path and ViewerProvider both work on this tree. 🔴 The @visual suite is NOT evidence either way here: maxDiffPixelRatio 0.02 on a 390x9675 page permits 75,465 pixels of drift and a 40x40 control is 1,600 — see LIVE-125. Re-verify by fetching the page and grepping for the aria-label, never by grepping the component.

entries.title: Editor E0 task 9: upgradeLayout enters the read path
entries.detail:
lib/entity-blocks/node-tree.ts ships upgradeLayout - pure, total, idempotent, deterministic, and proven over the 37 frozen production shapes in scripts/entity-layout-corpus.json (ADR-1129). Nothing calls it. Task 9 calls it at the top of parseEntityLayout, which is EDITOR-E0 §1.5's stated safe halfway point: every reader becomes node-shaped and nothing is written.

What to expect, so it is not mistaken for a bug:
  • layout-equal.ts is a BYTE comparison and powers the 'unpublished changes' badge, so every Space reads dirty exactly once. Harmless, but it will be noticed.
  • layout-equal.test.ts:94-111 asserts on the SOURCE TEXT of actions.ts, so it fails on any rename.
  • upgradeLayout is deliberately MORE permissive than parseRows in one way - it preserves a block type the registry no longer knows (ADR-978), leaving legality to sanitizeRows / resolveRows, which run after. Keep that property; do not 'fix' it by dropping unknown types at the upgrade.
  • EntityLayout gains the node shape here; the sibling content/style maps are NOT removed until task 11.

Not a migration. All five stores are opaque JSONB and §1.6 rules a SQL transform out (the transform needs the registry, and SQL does not have it). ✅ DONE 2026-08-25. `parseEntityLayout` calls `upgradeLayout(raw)` at the top and attaches the result as a read-path-only `EntityLayout.nodes`. 🔴 TWO OF THIS ROW'S OWN NOTES WERE WRONG, both re-measured before the work: (1) `layout-equal.ts` is NOT a byte comparison - it was rewritten to compare the RENDER (`layoutRenderKey` -> `resolveRows` + content + style) and its own header calls the byte version 'THE BUG THIS EXISTS FOR'; and (2) the 'unpublished changes' badge does not go through `parseEntityLayout` at all - it compares raw `profileLayoutDraft` vs `profileLayout` on the stored preferences (owner-space-layout-preview.tsx). So NO Space reads dirty, not even once. The row's prediction should not be looked for. (3) The section reference was also off: §1.5/§1.6 are in docs/EDITOR-E0.md, not EDITOR-ARCHITECTURE.md. ⚠️ THE REAL HAZARD WAS ELSEWHERE AND IT IS ORDERING: `upgradeLayout` returns NON-NULL for every object, so attaching `nodes` before the emptiness gate makes `parseEntityLayout` never return null - disarming `?? starterEmailLayout()` on two LIVE email send paths, which would compile an empty body. The gate runs first and a test pins it. A second test pins that `sanitizeEntityLayout` (the WRITE path) never carries `nodes` through, which caught a real mistake during this very change. A third pins the ADR-978 divergence: `rows` drops a de-registered type and `nodes` preserves it, on purpose.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='lib/entity-blocks/layout.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8');const i=s.indexOf('export function parseEntityLayout');if(i<0){console.error('parseEntityLayout is gone from '+F);process.exit(79)}const j=s.indexOf(String.fromCharCode(10)+'}',i);const body=j>i?s.slice(i,j):'';if(body.indexOf('upgradeLayout(')<0){console.error('parseEntityLayout does not call upgradeLayout - the read path is still block-id shaped');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.title: Seven block renderers still draw a button at '#' when the operator leaves the destination blank
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while working LIVE-109 (ADR-1125). The 18 dead Space buttons had a root cause one level below the seed the row blamed: `SpaceCalloutBlock` gated its button on `ctaLabel` alone and rendered `href={ctaHref || '#'}`, so an operator who typed a label and left the link box empty got a button that went nowhere — and blanking the seed could not have removed it. That is fixed for `SpaceCallout` and its twin `SpaceCTA`. THE SAME SHAPE SURVIVES IN SEVEN MORE PLACES, all in components/page-editor/blocks/design.tsx (lines 200, 203, 496, 514, 526, 623, 711), and four of them say so in their own comments: "a missing link falls back to '#' until the operator sets one".

⚠️ NOT ALL SEVEN ARE THE SAME BUG, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A TRIAGE ROW RATHER THAN A SWEEP. Three (496, 514, 526) sit behind `safeHref()`, so '#' is ALSO what an unsafe url degrades to — a deliberate stored-XSS fallback that must not be removed, only separated from the empty-field case. The other four (200, 203, 623, 711) are the plain LIVE-109 shape. Two further sites in profile.tsx (290, 2349) are NOT in scope: their href comes from live identity data, not an authored text field.

LATENT TODAY, NOT LIVE, and said plainly so the row is not read as an outage: the census (scripts/stored-links.json) records no '#' target in either marketing store, so no stored marketing document trips this today. It is one blank field away in the editor, on any of the seven.

THE DURABLE FIX IS AN EDITOR ONE and belongs with the PROG-E series rather than here: a link field that offers the page's real anchors and routes instead of a free-text box cannot be left in a state that renders '#'. This row is the interim — make the renderers decline to draw a button they cannot point anywhere, the way MediaText, SpaceCallout and SpaceCTA now do. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1147). Six renderers in components/page-editor/blocks/design.tsx now require BOTH a label and a destination, and the seventh was a FALSE POSITIVE worth recording: the card title link at ~496 already sat inside `safeHref(card.href) ? …`, so its `|| '#'` was DEAD CODE the type checker forced rather than a route any visitor could reach. It is gone too, so the site stops reading as a seventh instance. ⚠️ THE THREE BEHIND safeHref() ARE NOT A SEPARATE CASE, which is what made this a triage row: '#' is ALSO what an unsafe url degrades to there, and withholding the link is the correct answer to BOTH — a blocked destination and a missing one are equally not somewhere to send someone. One wrapper bug went with it: `hasActions` counted LABELS, so withholding every button still drew the empty mt-8 action row and left a gap under the copy; it now counts buttons that will actually render. components/page-editor/blocks/design.cta-href.test.tsx adds 11 arms, the twin of the profile file from ADR-1125, including an UNSAFE-url arm proving the two cases converge. Mutation-proven three ways.

entries.title: every IndexTemplate page draws the shared hero band; the 7 dynamic-route pages adopted it on 2026-09-08
entries.detail:
SPLIT OUT OF PROG-P4 2026-08-25 (ADR-1127), because it is the half that CHANGES WHAT RENDERS. Adopting is mechanically one line each (`const hero = await resolveIndexHero(route)` + `{...hero}`), but it is NOT a no-op the way PROG-P5's detail adoption is: resolveIndexHero always returns heroOverlay: true, so an unmapped route gets a band and the page's h1 moves onto it. So each page needs an INDEX_HERO_DEFAULTS row FIRST, classifying it discovery (large) or utility (short), per the short/large product decision already written into that map.

── PROGRESS 2026-09-07 (ADR-1255): 17 of the 24 SHIPPED; 7 remain, and NONE of the 24 was ever photographed.

🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED, AND TWO OF THE ROW'S THREE OPEN QUESTIONS HAD FALSE PREMISES.
  · THE COUNT HELD: 32 IndexTemplate render sites, 24 of them plain, exactly the 24 named here.
  · (b) WAS WRONG. The row said the five /spaces/[slug]/* tab pages 'sit INSIDE a Space profile that already has its own hero above them'. They do not. The Space cover + info band + tabs live in the (profile) ROUTE GROUP layout, and journeys / loom / podcasts / practices / manage-circles are all SIBLINGS of that group (the chrome moved there to fix the soft-nav staleness bug; see the note in app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/layout.tsx). Nothing draws a hero above them, so a band there is a first band, not a second one. They are deferred for a different reason, below.
  · (c) WAS WRONG, AND IT IS THE FINDING THAT UNBLOCKED THIS SLICE. 'Visual baselines move on every surface adopted' is false for all 24. The visual suite's camera is coverageSurfaces() in test/e2e/surfaces.ts: the parsed EDITABLE_PAGES routes + /discover (public), /feed + /settings + /nearby + PW_ROOM_PATH + /spaces/<slug>/manage (member shell), and seven /admin routes (operator). The 20 committed baseline slugs in test/e2e/__screenshots__/visual.spec.ts confirm it. The intersection with these 24 pages is EMPTY. /discover is photographed and /discover/partners, /discover/practices are not; /spaces/<slug>/manage is photographed and /spaces/<slug>/manage/circles is not. So this slice moves ZERO committed baselines and needs NO owner recapture run.
  · (a) SETTLED: NO. The index ladder does not grow a 'none' tail. On a detail page the cover is decoration under an h1 the context header renders, so 'none' means 'draw no decoration'. On an index the band CARRIES the h1 (IndexTemplate's heroOverlay branch suppresses PageHeading), so a 'none' tail would not be a hero resolution at all - it would be the page choosing a different header grammar, which is IndexTemplate's decision and not the map's. It would put heroOverlay back under a per-page conditional, i.e. hand the choice back to the pages this map exists to take it away from. The ruling is written into lib/layout/index-hero.ts beside INDEX_HERO_FALLBACK. Staging is done by ADOPTING IN SLICES instead, which is what this row now does.

✅ SHIPPED 2026-09-07 — the 17 STATIC-ROUTE pages (19 render sites; /crew/leaderboard and /circles/templates each have two): /help, /circles/templates, /crew/leaderboard, /drafts, /housing/roommates, /lead/training-library, /market/manage, /messages, /orders, /partners, /partners/collaborators, /partners/join, /search, /spaces/operating, /support, /discover/partners, /discover/practices. Sixteen INDEX_HERO_DEFAULTS rows joined the map: five discovery (large: /help, /partners, /housing/roommates, /discover/partners, /discover/practices; /partners/collaborators takes the /partners row, which is what a prefix map is for) and eleven utility (short + inheritHero: false). NO COVER WAS INVENTED: every new row carries image: null, so what the rows buy is the band plus rungs 1 and 2 — the operator's Settings header image for the route and the section hero the copy cascade already holds, both of which these 17 were dropping on the floor. A row earns a photo the day the owner picks one, in one line, rather than 17 pages each picking their own.

⏳ REMAINING — the 7 DYNAMIC-ROUTE pages, deferred on a stated rule and NOT on baselines: app/(help)/help/[category]/page.tsx, app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/journeys/page.tsx, app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/loom/page.tsx, app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/manage/circles/page.tsx, app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/podcasts/page.tsx, app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/practices/page.tsx, app/discover/practices/pillar/[slug]/page.tsx.

THE RULE, and the kernel question it exposes: resolveIndexHero's route argument is simultaneously the page_settings key rung 1 reads and the copy-cascade key rung 2 reads. A dynamic segment has neither. An operator has no way to reach '/spaces/<slug>/podcasts' in Settings, and keying the read on a concrete tenant slug would make the band's source vary per Space with no UI that can set it. detail-hero.ts already solved this and index-hero.ts has not: detailHeroDefaultsFor returns the SECTION prefix and rung 1 reads page_settings on THAT, with an optional spaceId for the tenant. index-hero.ts reads getPageHeaderImage(route) flat, with no section key and no spaceId. Giving it the same treatment is the next slice and it is a kernel change, not seventeen page edits, which is why it is not mixed in here.

✅ SHIPPED 2026-09-08 (ADR-1261) — THE DEFERRED HALF. All 7 dynamic-route pages adopt the band, the probe reads 0, and the row closes. The rule above named the blocker exactly, and the fix was the kernel change it pointed at, in two halves because the seven are two different shapes.
  · THE KEY IS NOW ITS OWN FUNCTION. `indexHeroKeyFor(route)` returns a row's PREFIX when the row carries `keyOn: 'section'`, else the literal route, and rung 1 (plus the focal point, which must follow its image to the same key) reads that. The default is 'route', so all 17 pages of the first slice key on the exact string they did on 2026-09-07; a test names every one of them and a mutation that section-keys '/partners' turns two of them red. RUNG 2 IS NOT RE-KEYED: the copy cascade climbs a route's real ancestors on its own.
  · TWO PAGES TAKE THE SECTION KEY: '/help' and '/discover/practices' carry `keyOn: 'section'`, so /help/<category> and /discover/practices/pillar/<slug> read the operator image set on the section root. Those two roots are themselves pages an operator can stand on, which is the whole condition for a section key being writable.
  · FIVE TENANT TABS TAKE A PATTERN ROW, NOT A PATTERN KEY. Their dynamic segment sits in the MIDDLE of the path, so `longestPrefixRow` (the primitive both hero maps share) learned a `_` wildcard segment: '/spaces/_/podcasts' is one row for every Space, matching the '/spaces/_/crm' placeholder page-chrome.ts already uses. Specificity is segment count then fewer wildcards, so a literal row still wins; no map carried a `_` before, so every existing table resolves as it did. But rung 1 KEEPS THE LITERAL PATH: page_settings is an exact-match read whose only writer (the on-page Settings panel) keys on usePathname(), so '/spaces/_/podcasts' would be a rung nothing can write. A map-level test fails any row carrying both a wildcard and a section key.
  · ROWS: four `short` (the owner-gated Journeys / Loom / Practices / manage-Circles managers) and one `large` (the Shows catalog, the one anonymous-reachable, sitemap-advertised surface of the five). All five `image: null` and `inheritHero: false` — the cascade climbs a tenant path through '/spaces/<slug>' to '/spaces', the site's marketing page, and one brand's Space must not wear the house photo.
  · BASELINES RE-VERIFIED FOR THESE SEVEN SPECIFICALLY, by exact path as ADR-1255 established: coverageSurfaces() is 16 EDITABLE_PAGES routes + /discover + /feed + /settings + /nearby + PW_ROOM_PATH + /spaces/<slug>/manage + 7 /admin routes, and the 20 committed baseline slugs agree. INTERSECTION EMPTY. It is empty by one segment again: /spaces/<slug>/manage is photographed and /spaces/<slug>/manage/circles is not. Zero baselines move; no owner recapture run is owed.
  · WHAT THE PREFIX KEY CANNOT EXPRESS, recorded rather than left to be rediscovered: one operator image behind every tenant's copy of a tab. That is a WRITER question (nothing can save a pattern key), not a resolver one, and the same reason the index side grows no `spaceId` option to match detail-hero's.

entries.title: Retire DISCOVER_NAV: a hand-maintained parallel nav list nothing renders any more
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-24. Its last renderer was the marketing phone sheet, which now projects the `header` menu instead (ADR-1118), so DISCOVER_NAV is exported, tested, and drawn by nothing. All five of its links (/discover, /discover/circles, /discover/events, /discover/journeys, /discover/topics) are rows of the nav registry already. It is exactly the second-source shape lib/nav exists to retire. ── NOT deleted in ADR-1118 on purpose: three ADRs (ADR-352 area, ADR-352 area, and the OPEN-THREADS B4 note) name it as a CONCEPT - 'the shared community core' the public and in-app navs were meant to keep in sync - so retiring it is a small ruling about whether that concept still has a job, not a drive-by deletion inside a PR about phone reachability. Removing it also touches lib/site.test.ts, which has four cases pinned to it.

── ✅ RETIRED 2026-08-25, AND THE RULING IS THE INTERESTING PART. The row said correctly that this is a small ruling, not a drive-by deletion: the record (ADR-352 on the shared mega menu, plus the OPEN-THREADS B4 note) name DISCOVER_NAV as a CONCEPT — "the shared community core", the surfaces the public menu and the in-app nav were meant to keep in sync.
  THE RULING: the concept keeps its job and loses its implementation, because the implementation was the weakest possible way to do that job. Keeping two navs in sync was the goal, and a SECOND hand-kept list only achieves it while someone remembers to edit both. All five destinations are rows of the one nav registry every header already projects, so they are now in sync BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by discipline. That is the concept being honoured, not abandoned. Its last renderer was the marketing phone sheet, which has projected the `header` menu since ADR-1118, so by 2026-08-24 the export was tested and drawn by nothing.
  THE FOUR TESTS MOVED RATHER THAN WENT, and that is what keeps this honest. Deleting them alongside the export would have quietly dropped the guard on the concept — which is exactly how a retirement turns into a regression nobody notices. lib/site.test.ts now asks the SAME five destinations of NAV_REGISTRY: /discover, /discover/circles, /discover/events, /discover/journeys, /discover/topics. A list nothing renders cannot drift in a way anyone notices; the registry can, and now says so. 19 cases green in that file, tsc clean.
  Reversible in one commit: the removed block is quoted in full in the migration-note comment left at its old site in lib/site.ts.

entries.title: pages.space_id can take its NOT NULL contract step: the ruling it waited on has an empty subject

source.ref: the column comment at :93 says 'Still NULLABLE (no NOT NULL contract step yet)'

entries.detail:
PULLED OUT OF HYG-010 2026-08-25. The item had sat as 'info-grade' behind a stated blocker — 'needs the untenanted-rows ruling' — and the blocker has NO SUBJECT: `public.pages` holds 4 rows and 0 of them have a null space_id (measured against the live database, 2026-08-25). That is the ADR-1082 pattern: a blocker phrased as a pending decision, where the thing to be decided does not exist. Nothing needs ruling on; the column can simply take the constraint. It is safe by construction as well as by count: every read and write goes through lib/page-editor/data.ts, which defaults spaceId to loadRootSpaceId(), and space_id already carries `on delete cascade`. 🔴 SHIP IT ALONE, NOT INSIDE A SWEEP. Merging deploys to production (AGENTS.md), and a NOT NULL that finds an unexpected row fails the migration and the deploy with it — so this wants its own PR, re-counting the untenanted rows immediately before it goes, not a line in somebody else's diff. Update the column comment in the same change: it currently states the opposite.

── ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-25 as migration 20270341000000, alone, exactly as this row demanded. Re-counted immediately before writing it (a count taken a week ago is a guess): public.pages holds 4 rows, 0 untenanted. Applied to production and verified — information_schema now reports is_nullable = NO — and the ledger version was repaired to match the filename.
  THE COLUMN COMMENT WAS UPDATED IN THE SAME CHANGE, which the row asked for and which mattered more than it sounds: it read 'Still NULLABLE (no NOT NULL contract step yet)'. A comment asserting the opposite of what is true is worse than no comment, because it is documentation that gets believed. It now records the constraint, why the application cannot produce an untenanted row (lib/page-editor/data.ts defaults spaceId to loadRootSpaceId() on every write), and that the unique key's NULLS NOT DISTINCT clause is now inert rather than wrong.
  TWO CONTROLS, and the first is deliberately NOT a safety device. A NOT NULL fails on a null all by itself, so the before-arm exists to make that failure LEGIBLE — a bare 'column contains null values' names neither the count nor the table's size, and whoever reads a failed production deploy should not have to go and query for both. The after-arm is the one that catches a subtler thing: an ALTER on an already-NOT-NULL column also succeeds, so without it this migration could read as having done work it did not do.
