Two test files were rewritten rather than dropped — every unique assertion was re-pointed at the surviving door. TWO FOLLOW-UPS this created, both on SCAN-502: useEditMode().toggle now has no caller, and offersPeriod lost its last external consumer (still used internally, so it is an unexport, never a delete).

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const path=require('path');const D=['app','components','lib','scripts','supabase','test'];const EXT=new Set(['.ts','.tsx','.js','.jsx','.mjs','.cjs','.mts','.cts','.sql']);const DEAD=['createSpacePlanCheckout','sendBookingReminderEmail','sendListingClaimInviteEmail','reserveFounding','foundingBusinessTakenInCity','EditModeButton','SITE_NAV_MEMBER'];const CONTROL='StartEditingLink';const strip=s=>s.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g,'').replace(/([^:])\/\/.*$/gm,(m,a)=>a).replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm,'');const files=[];const walk=d=>{let ents;try{ents=fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true})}catch{return}for(const e of ents){if(e.name==='node_modules'||e.name==='.next'||e.name.startsWith('.'))continue;const p=path.join(d,e.name);if(e.isDirectory())walk(p);else if(EXT.has(path.extname(e.name)))files.push(p)}};for(const d of D)walk(d);if(files.length<2000){console.error('probe cannot run: walked only '+files.length+' source files, so a clean verdict would be about the WALK');process.exit(1)}const bad=[];let control=0;for(const f of files){const raw=fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8');let code=null;if(raw.includes(CONTROL)){code=strip(raw);if(code.includes(CONTROL))control++}for(const n of DEAD){if(!raw.includes(n))continue;if(code===null)code=strip(raw);if(code.includes(n))bad.push(f+' :: '+n)}}if(control===0){console.error('probe control failed: '+CONTROL+' is live in an edited file and was not found, so this search proves nothing');process.exit(1)}if(bad.length){console.error('orphan still in executable code:\n'+bad.join('\n'));process.exit(1)}"
verify.note: Measures EXECUTABLE code, not text: every deleted symbol deliberately survives in a comment saying what was removed and why, and a probe that forbade those would push a future session to erase the record to go green. Carries its own control — the same search must still find StartEditingLink, a live sibling in one of the edited files — so it cannot pass by having been broken.

entries.title: One trim sweep over the ~154 lib modules carrying dead exports
entries.detail:
MS25 Phase 5. RE-SCOPED 2026-08-25 by an exact-identifier index over the whole tree (the original number came from a token-presence scan, which under-reports by construction). Two findings changed the row. (1) THE ORIGINAL SCAN MISSES .mts: lib/help/drift.ts and lib/ai/autodoc.ts scored fully dead and are both LIVE, consumed by scripts/help-drift.mts and scripts/help-autodoc.mts. Any sweep that skips .mts/.cts/.cjs/.yml deletes live code — this is the load-bearing correction. (2) ~85% of the row is not deletable: of 860 dead value exports across 707 lib modules, 734 are used INSIDE their own file, so the sweep for those is dropping the `export` keyword, not deleting. Only 126 are declaration-only. Exactly one module is fully dead — lib/help/drift.ts — and that one is the false positive above. So this is an API-surface trim plus a small delete list, not the M-sized code sweep the row described. A ranked 15 is scoped (each with all four searches clean), with three flagged for a ruling before touching, not a sweep: lib/verticals/registry.ts, lib/nav/admin-rail.ts and lib/admin/modules/spine.ts are registry/menu-adjacent — a parallel rail registry with no consumer is a MENU-CONTRACT finding in its own right. Two items carried over from SCAN-501: useEditMode().toggle (no caller since EditModeButton went) and offersPeriod (internal-only now; unexport, and its own test updates with it). Excluded on purpose: lib/profile/spotlight-flags.ts belongs to SCAN-501. ── ⚠️ RE-DERIVED AND RE-CLASSIFIED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1145). The index is now a committed, documented report — scripts/maintenance/dead-exports.mjs — rather than a number in a row, so the next reader re-runs it instead of trusting this sentence. Reading: 6,137 files walked, 5,765 consumers (INCLUDING .mts/.cts/.cjs/.mjs/.yml/.json/.md/.sql), 1,213 lib modules, 7,688 attributable exports, 1,343 dead outside their own file, 45 DECLARATION-ONLY. 🔴 AND THE ROW'S FRAMING NEEDS A CORRECTION: 'an API-surface trim' is only two thirds true. Classifying the 19 unreferenced lib FUNCTIONS by hand splits them three ways, and only one third is safe to delete blindly. (a) BUILT BUT NEVER WIRED: runContestSweep (lib/beta/referral-contest.ts) documents itself 'idempotent + bounded, so it is safe to run on a schedule' and NONE of the 27 crons in vercel.json calls it, so the beta referral contest never tallies. Deleting it removes a finished feature; filed as SCAN-510. (b) GENUINELY RETIRED WITH A STALE DOC: spaceTrailingProcessedCents still cites ADR-552 for the "you'd have saved $X" upgrade nudge, but billing-body.tsx records that ADR-811 RETIRED that nudge. The code is dead and its own comment advertises a feature that no longer exists — which is exactly how it reads as a gap when it is not. (c) CONVENIENCE WRAPPERS, the majority: dropping the `export` keyword is the whole change. ⚠️ THE GENERAL LESSON, and it is the same one SCAN-508 landed on from the other side: a doc comment is not evidence of a caller. Two of the three categories are indistinguishable from their comments alone.

── 🔎 RE-RUN AND TRIAGED 2026-08-25, no code moved yet; this is the scoping the sweep needs before it touches anything. `scripts/maintenance/dead-exports.mjs` now reads 6,150 files / 5,778 consumers / 1,213 lib modules / 7,678 attributable exports / 1,343 dead outside their own file / **45 declaration-only**. Two of the row's named examples are already gone from that list: `runContestSweep` went with SCAN-510, and `spaceTrailingProcessedCents` no longer appears.
  THE 45 SPLIT THREE WAYS BY RISK, and the split is the point — a single sweep over all of them would be wrong in two directions at once:
  • 6 are under `resonance/` and belong to DEF-RESON, which is GO-gated. NOT this row's to touch.
  • 7 are declared in a `types.ts`. A type exported from a module literally named types.ts is plausibly deliberate public surface, and 'nothing imports it yet' is not the same as 'nothing should'. Each needs a per-item read, not a rule.
  • 32 are the rest, and those are where the sweep actually lives.
  ⚠️ TWO OF THE 32 LOOKED LIKE UNENFORCED GATES AND WERE CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because a gate nothing calls is a correctness bug, not hygiene. Both came back clean:
  • `aiDepthFor` (lib/spaces/function-access.ts) is a re-export of `spaceAiDepth`, and the real one IS live — app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/crm/crm-body.tsx:150 and lib/spaces/entitlements.ts:246. Safe wrapper, category (c).
  • `canSellTickets` wraps `ticketSellerVerdict`, and THAT one has no real caller either: its only other mention in the tree is a COMMENT in lib/pricing/gates.ts:74 saying the predicate 'is what Phase 1 reversed' (ADR-914). The live wall is elsewhere and is stronger — lib/billing/tickets.ts checks `payoutsLive()` at BOTH money entry points (:162 create, :690 refund) and reads `getConnectStatus`. **No hole; do not read this row as a payout finding.**
  🔴 BUT IT IS A REAL CATEGORY-(b) FINDING, and a worse-than-average one. THREE separate comments in the tree point the next reader at this module as the place the rule lives — components/marketplace/events-header-actions.tsx:17, components/crew/upgrade-lightbox.tsx:18 and app/(main)/events/index-data.ts:305 all say 'the wall now lives at the price field (lib/events/ticket-eligibility.ts)'. The half of that module they would land on (`ticketSellerVerdict`, `canSellTickets`, `NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT`, and the three types feeding them) is dead. The module is NOT dead — `TICKETS_NOT_READY` is imported by lib/billing/tickets.ts:31 — so this is a partial retirement with three signposts still pointing at the retired half. Deleting the dead half means fixing three comments in the same change, or the signposts start pointing at nothing.
  NEXT: work the 32, item by item, with the three-way category call recorded per item. The types.ts seven and the resonance six stay out of scope until someone rules on them.

── ✅ ALL 32 CLASSIFIED 2026-08-25, each one independently verified rather than trusted from the report: a whole-tree grep across .ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts/.mjs/.cjs/.json/.md/.sql returned **exactly one reference for every one of the 32 — its own declaration line**. No consumers, no tests, no docs, no SQL. The report's 'declaration-only' call is confirmed.
  🔴 AND THAT IS WHY MOST OF THEM MUST NOT BE DELETED. Reading each one's own doc comment splits the 32 far more sharply than the row's three categories did:

  (a) FINISHED CAPABILITY, NEVER WIRED — 13 of 32. Deleting these removes working code and the only record that the capability was built. Each is a product question, not hygiene:
      · uncompleteLesson          'Undo a lesson completion (toggle off)' — a member can complete a
                                  lesson and cannot un-complete it.
      · updateBlock               'Edit a block's title/body' — Journey blocks can be created and
                                  not edited.
      · setEventIntakeInputs      persists the intake INPUTS jsonb (consent, source notes). A
                                  consent persister with no caller is worth its own look.
      · listRelationships         the ACTIVE relationships for a CRM contact.
      · listAcceptedSharesForSpace  'the events another host brought here'.
      · getRecording / listAttachmentsOfRecording  Airwaves reads; the second one's comment names a
                                  view ('used in N places') that does not exist.
      · saveSplashOverride        the writer beside a getter.
      · resolvePlaceSelectorProfileIds  messaging place-selector resolution.
      · memberInRecovery          'should surface a banner' — the dunning banner is unbuilt (billing
                                  is OFF, so this one is expected-dark).
      · resolveViewerGamification 'e.g. the leaderboard compete affordance'.
      · THEME_PRESETS             'One-tap starting points' for the Spotlight editor — a whole preset
                                  feature with no consumer.
      · PREFILL_THRESHOLD         the 'pre-select the guess but flag it for review' tier of the CRM
                                  import confidence system. AUTO_THRESHOLD beside it IS live, so the
                                  two-tier design shipped as one tier.

  (b) RETIRED WITH LIVE SIGNPOSTS — the ticket-eligibility half. Escalated to its own row, LIVE-126,
      because it turned out not to be dead code at all. See that row.

  (c) GENUINELY INERT — the remainder: appendSignature, aiDepthFor, resolvedAmounts, locationSummary,
      resetGoogleMapsLoaderForTests, BLURHASH_ALPHABET, JOURNEY_FULL_MESSAGE, DEFAULT_BLOCK_MARGIN,
      DEFAULT_FUNNEL_STYLE, the vocabulary arrays (STAGE_KINDS, TASK_FILTERS,
      FOLLOWER_REMINDER_LEADS, COLUMN_VALUES, SPACE_LOCATION_PRECISIONS, AI_DEPTH_CAPABILITY_KEYS)
      and the three types (StoredHarvest, DesignBlockType, FieldChoices). Even here two carry a
      claim worth noting rather than deleting silently: BLURHASH_ALPHABET is 'exported so a validator
      can check a string' and there is no validator, and locationSummary is 'the one-line summary the
      settings form shows back' and the form does not show it.

  🔵 THE ROW CANNOT CLOSE ON A SWEEP ANY MORE, and that is the finding. 'Trim ~154 lib modules carrying dead exports' assumed a hygiene task. Thirteen of the 32 are finished features nobody wired; deleting them is a product decision about whether the capability is wanted, and it needs an owner ruling per group rather than a blanket answer. The (c) list is the only part a sweep can take, and it is worth roughly twenty lines.

── ✅ setEventIntakeInputs INVESTIGATED FIRST, ON THE OWNER'S RULING, AND IT IS NOT A CONSENT GAP. I flagged it as 'a consent persister with no caller' above; that framing was wrong and the investigation is the correction.
  • CONSENT IS CAPTURED AT CREATION. `createEventIntake` (lib/events/seed/store.ts:83) inserts `inputs: input.inputs`, and `inputs` carries `consent`. Both live doors build it — from-scan.ts:62 and from-chat.ts:53. `setEventIntakeInputs` is only the UPDATE path, i.e. 'change the consent or source notes afterwards'. Nothing calls it, which is an unwired edit, not a missing capture.
  • THE POSTURE IS SAFE BY DEFAULT, and it is stated in both doors' headers: 'Every staged event is a DEMO (consent.isDemo): the apply materializes it as an unlisted [event]'. Everything read out of a scan or a chat is marked demo and lands unlisted, so third-party material cannot become a public listing by omission.
  • WHAT IS GENUINELY UNBUILT is the PROMOTION path. `organizerConfirmed` — 'Set once the real organizer has confirmed they want this event listed' — appears exactly ONCE in the whole tree, its own type declaration at lib/events/seed/intake.ts:40. It is never set and never read, so there is no way to record that an organiser agreed and nothing that would act on it. That is the missing half, and it is a feature gap rather than a compliance one, because the default is unlisted.
  • AND NOTHING HAS GONE THROUGH THE DOOR: `public.event_intake` holds **0 rows**. The seeder has never run in production. So this is latent, to be closed before the seeder is first used, not an incident to chase.
  CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: `setEventIntakeInputs` stays in group (a) as unwired, but it is the LOWEST-urgency member of that group, not the highest as I first read it. Whoever builds the promotion path wires it and `organizerConfirmed` together; whoever decides the seeder is not coming back deletes all three.

── 📋 THE 13 TRIAGED BUILD-OR-DELETE, 2026-08-25, per the owner's ruling. Method: for each, ask whether the SURFACE that would call it exists, is half-built, or was never started — by grepping app/ and components/ for the sibling writer, the table name and the module path. Nothing deleted; this is the list to rule on.

  BUILD — the surface exists and only this half is missing (4):
   1. uncompleteLesson      `completeLesson` IS wired at app/(main)/journeys/[slug]/learn/
                            actions.ts. A member can tick a lesson and cannot untick it. The
                            smallest real member-facing gap in the whole list.
   2. listAcceptedSharesForSpace  event-share is live on three surfaces including
                            spaces/[slug]/settings/calendar/page.tsx. A Space's calendar can share
                            OUT and cannot show what other hosts shared IN.
   3. THEME_PRESETS         lib/spotlight/theme is imported by three surfaces, so the Spotlight
                            theme editor is live; the 'one-tap starting points' it was built with
                            are simply never offered.
   4. PREFILL_THRESHOLD     confirmed: AUTO_THRESHOLD is used inside map.ts:334 and by its test,
                            so the auto-apply tier IS live and the 'pre-select but flag for review'
                            tier is not. The wizard (components/crm/import/import-wizard.tsx) is
                            the surface. A two-tier design shipped as one tier.

  DELETE — a second, unused way to do something the live code already does (4):
   5. memberInRecovery      resolveMemberPaymentState is called DIRECTLY by
                            components/billing/past-due-banner.tsx and settings/billing/section.tsx.
                            The banner exists; this is a redundant convenience over it.
   6. resolveViewerGamification  crew/leaderboard/page.tsx already imports gamification-access. The
                            combined helper is a convenience nothing reached for.
   7. listRelationships     relationship-actions.ts mentions contact_relationships only in a
                            comment; the classifier folds those rows in elsewhere. A second reader.
   8. aiDepthFor            (from group c, restated here) a re-export of the live spaceAiDepth.

  NEEDS ONE MORE LOOK before either (5):
   9. updateBlock           `createBlock` has no caller either, so the whole block CRUD may be
                            unwired at the surface rather than just the edit half.
  10. saveSplashOverride    getSplashOverride IS read by app/join/[slug]/page.tsx and there is an
                            edit surface at pages/splash, but that surface's actions do not appear
                            to call this writer — so there is probably a second save path.
  11. resolvePlaceSelectorProfileIds  `parsePlaceSelector` has no caller either; the whole
                            place-selector resolution looks unwired, not just this wrapper.
  12. getRecording / listAttachmentsOfRecording  Airwaves is live on three surfaces, so these are
                            two specific reads that are not; `RecordingAttachment` has no surface,
                            so the 'used in N places' view was never started.
  13. setEventIntakeInputs  already investigated above — lowest urgency, 0 intake rows, safe by
                            default. Wire it with the organizerConfirmed promotion path or delete
                            all three together.

  🔵 RECOMMENDATION: take #1 alone first. It is one server action plus a toggle, it is the only one
  a member feels today, and it needs no ruling. The four DELETEs are a single tidy commit once
  someone confirms the reasoning. The five in the middle are each a short investigation, not work.

── RE-MEASURED AND PARTLY SWEPT 2026-09-07. Declaration-only exports are 15 -> 13, and 9 -> 7 excluding resonance/ (excluded on its own package.json, which says it is designed to lift out into its own repo and Supabase project). The blocker this row named, SCAN-510, is done.

🔴 THE ROW'S OWN INSTRUCTION DOES NOT APPLY TO ANY REMAINING ITEM. It says "drop the export keyword where it is used in-file" — but declaration-only means the ONLY reference in the tree is the declaration line, so none of the nine is used in-file. And seven of the nine are types.ts contracts this row had already reserved from a blanket sweep ("a type exported from a module literally named types.ts is plausibly deliberate public surface"); reading each confirms it (LibraryAsset mirrors the migrations column-for-column; EmailTemplate is the seam the later send/template agents import; AppAction says LP3/LP4 read it). They stay, and forcing them would be the delete-a-working-feature failure this row exists to avoid.

SWEPT: spaceTrailingProcessedCents deleted (23 lines including a stale ADR-552 doc comment; the nudge it cites was retired by ADR-811). offersPeriod unexported but kept — it is used in-file by memberCheckoutPriceKey and its test was the only external consumer, with zero coverage lost because PERIODS_BY_KEY is asserted identically and the behaviour is exercised through memberCheckoutPriceKey. eventHeroHeightClass deleted (a three-line inert delegate). NOMINATIM_USER_AGENT deleted — unused AND misleading, a module-eval snapshot of env, which is the exact trap the 2026-09-05 blank-GEOCODER_CONTACT_EMAIL fix removed; the live header already calls nominatimUserAgent() per request.

⚠️ NEITHER named specific appeared in the declaration-only list, because the script counts .md and .mjs DOC MENTIONS as references: spaceTrailingProcessedCents was "referenced" only by DECISIONS.md and by dead-exports.mjs's own comment. That comment cited both symbols as live examples and both are now gone from the tree, so it was rewritten to name CATEGORIES instead, with a rule: do not cite a symbol here as a live example.

WHAT REMAINS IS A RULING, NOT A SWEEP: the (a) group of finished-but-unwired capabilities. Nothing an agent can decide.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-07: declaration-only exports measured at 13 (7 excluding resonance/), down from 15/9. The four inert ones are swept; the remaining 7 are types.ts contracts this row explicitly reserved from a blanket sweep. Closes when the owner rules on the finished-but-unwired (a) group — whether each capability gets wired or deleted.

entries.title: The three world-dashboard Manage widgets hand-declare ~35 rows the catalog already owns
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 5. The growth/community/operations Manage widgets type ~35 {label,desc,href,Icon} cards duplicating STUDIO_LEAVES - exactly the class MENU-CONTRACT admits check:menu cannot see, and it has already drifted twice (copy vs the leaf desc; gates: the host+marketing Growth dashboard shows janitor-gated destinations that bounce to /feed). Render from studioLeaf(id) (exported for this at lib/nav/studio.ts:468) and filter by the leaf's gate.

entries.title: Housing has no Studio manifest and the listing-seeder hand-rolls its review model
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 5. Both sibling seeders derive their review boards from manifests + the review kernel; the listing-seeder declares its own field list with no lib/studio import - partly because LISTING_MANIFEST covers classifieds only and housing sits outside Studio entirely (its member form is acknowledged as bespoke). Write the housing manifest (or widen listing's), then point the seeder's field list at the manifests like its siblings. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1151). lib/studio/entities/housing.ts declares all 31 fields of the member form, registered in the catalog beside LISTING_MANIFEST. Housing is its OWN entity rather than a widening of listing: they share five paths and diverge on twenty-six, including an address-privacy model a classifieds post has no use for. The seeder's two spec arrays are now DERIVED from the manifests via an explicit join (manifest field + draft key), with seeder-only fields and exclusions each declared with a reason, and a guard asserting the join covers every draft key. Required a kernel addition: amenities and accessibility are closed vocabularies backed by DB CHECK constraints, and `tags` (the only multi-value kind) is free text, so it would have collected values the database rejects at write - `multiselect` was added to FIELD_KINDS and CHOICE_KINDS with its own renderer arm, because the renderer default is a text Input and a kind with no arm fails silently rather than loudly.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");function read(p,label){if(!fs.existsSync(p)){console.error(label);process.exit(1)}return fs.readFileSync(p,"utf8")}const m=read("lib/studio/entities/housing.ts","housing still has no Studio manifest");if(!/export const HOUSING_MANIFEST/.test(m)){console.error("lib/studio/entities/housing.ts exists but exports no HOUSING_MANIFEST");process.exit(1)}const reg=read("lib/studio/registry.ts","the Studio registry is gone");if(!/HOUSING_MANIFEST/.test(reg)){console.error("the housing manifest is not registered, so the Spark and the review board cannot derive from it");process.exit(1)}const rm=read("app/(main)/admin/listing-seeder/review-model.ts","the listing-seeder review model is gone");if(!/from .@\/lib\/studio\/entities\/housing./.test(rm)||!/from .@\/lib\/studio\/entities\/listing./.test(rm)){console.error("the listing-seeder no longer derives from BOTH manifests");process.exit(1)}if(!/specsFrom\(/.test(rm)){console.error("the listing-seeder stopped deriving its field list and is hand-rolling it again - the exact drift this row exists to close");process.exit(1)}for(const p of ["bedrooms","rentDollars","amenities","priceNote"]){const re=new RegExp("\\{\\s*path: ." + p + "., label:");if(re.test(rm)){console.error("the listing-seeder hand-declares a spec for " + p + " again instead of deriving it");process.exit(1)}}'
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE, not the filename: the manifest EXPORTS HOUSING_MANIFEST, the registry LISTS it (an unregistered manifest is a file nothing derives from), the seeder imports BOTH manifests and still calls specsFrom, and four representative paths are NOT hand-declared as specs any more. The first version of this probe only checked that a file matching /housing/i existed in lib/studio/entities - which an empty file passes, and which says nothing about the second half of the row.

entries.title: Route chunks have no weight gate: the shell gate's documented blind spot
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 5. check:shell-weight watches the app shell's eager JS and named admin fingerprints, but a heavy library statically imported by a route-level client component (SCAN-302's react-markdown) is invisible to it. A small fingerprint gate over the member hot-route chunks (feed/events/circles/messages) closes the class, not just the instance. CLOSED 2026-08-25 as ARM C of check:shell-weight, and it is a FINGERPRINT arm, never a budget: from each member hot route page.tsx (feed/events/circles/messages — page, not layout, because the layout IS the shell Arms A/B already measure) it walks the static import graph, marks everything below the first `use client` boundary as client code, and fails if a NAMED heavy module is statically imported inside that subtree. What it can prove without a build is the half a build cannot prove cheaply: a static import below a client boundary is not code-split by any bundler setting, so "statically reachable" IS "in that route first-load JS". dynamic() and bare import() are not static edges and are correctly invisible. It CANNOT see bytes or a chunking change — only Arms A/B can, and only on the artifact. Reading on the real tree: 0 leaks, 668 client modules walked across the four routes, 2 detector controls firing. IT LIVES IN THE CI HALF (scripts/check-shell-weight.test.ts), NOT in postbuild, for two reasons: main() only runs on Vercel, i.e. after the merge, and a filesystem-only arm has no reason to wait for a build; and in postbuild it broke the artifact arms own mutation fixtures, which run the script from a cwd that is deliberately not this repo, where its controls do not exist. Teaching it to skip when the source tree is absent would have given it a way to pass without looking (ADR-970). Two controls keep it honest: two REAL client files that genuinely import a heavy library today, and a 150-module walk floor against 668 measured. Proven by mutation: a static react-markdown import added to components/feed/post-replies.tsx turns it red and names the chain feed/page.tsx -> feed-list.tsx -> post-card.tsx -> post-replies.tsx.

verify.cmd: node -e "import('./scripts/check-shell-weight.mjs').then(m=>{const fs=require('fs');for(const c of m.ROUTE_HEAVY_CONTROLS){if(!fs.existsSync(c.file)){console.error('Arm C detector control is gone: '+c.file+' — repoint it, never delete it');process.exit(1)}const s=fs.readFileSync(c.file,'utf8');if(!m.declaresUseClient(s)||!m.heavyModulesIn(s).includes(c.heavy)){console.error('Arm C detector control no longer fires: '+c.file+' — the detector broke, or the file was fixed and the row needs repointing');process.exit(1)}}let t=0;const leaks=[];for(const e of m.HOT_ROUTE_ENTRIES){if(!fs.existsSync(e)){console.error('Arm C hot route is gone: '+e);process.exit(1)}const w=m.walkRouteClientGraph(process.cwd(),e);t+=w.clientFiles.size;for(const l of w.leaks)leaks.push(e+'  <-  '+l.heavy+'  imported by  '+l.file)}if(t<m.CLIENT_GRAPH_FLOOR){console.error('Arm C walked only '+t+' client modules, under the floor of '+m.CLIENT_GRAPH_FLOOR+' — the walk is not descending');process.exit(1)}if(leaks.length){console.error('a heavy library is statically imported by client code on a member hot route:\n'+leaks.join('\n'));process.exit(1)}}).catch(e=>{console.error('Arm C could not run: '+e.message);process.exit(1)})"
verify.note: Runs Arm C itself — both controls included — so it fails when the ARM stops firing as well as when a route regresses. Not `vitest run`: LIVE-034 forbids a probe that spawns a test runner, and this way costs 0.2s instead of 1.9s. A grep for the words in the title would pass by existing.

entries.title: The app-space-console visual baseline is 21px stale, so pr-compare is red on every PR that reaches it
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 0. The @visual suite's four app-space-console checks (/spaces/<slug>/manage, dawn-light + dawn-dark, desktop + mobile) fail on EVERY branch that runs them, with the baseline 21px shorter than what the app now renders. Proven not-branch-specific by identical pixel arithmetic across two unrelated branches: editor/e0-foundations (run 32806462760, merged as #2281) and claude/frequency-codebase-audit-vii214 (run 32810507921) both report 'Expected an image 390px by 3133px, received 390px by 3154px. 25507 pixels (ratio 0.03)' on app-space-console--dawn-dark.png, with 140 other checks passing in both. Main drifted past the baseline (the loading-skeleton and hero work) and nothing recaptured it. THREE PRs have since merged with this red (#2275, #2277, #2281), which is the failure mode this repo names directly: a check that is red for a reason nobody owns trains everyone to ignore it, and then it reads as coverage (ADR-970, and the e2e workflow's own header on why a meaningless red X is worse than no gate). No code change unblocks it - the baselines are recaptured by the maintainer-triggered job in .github/workflows/e2e-manual.yml, so this is an owner action. ✅ The four app-space-console baselines are recaptured. ⚠️ AND THE ROW'S INSTRUCTION WAS INCOMPLETE: `update_baselines` alone would NOT have taken them. /spaces/<slug>/manage is a MEMBER SHELL surface (appSurfaces in test/e2e/surfaces.ts), so the run also needs `capture_shell: true`, which mints a session - and e2e-manual.yml's own header named the wrong precondition for it (see the note added there: it asked for web_role = 'admin', a role zero production accounts hold).

verify.evidence: CLOSED 2026-08-25. The owner dispatched e2e-manual.yml with update_baselines + capture_shell against production; run #52/#53 succeeded and the smoke summary read '4 of 4 member-shell surfaces ran ... Photographed: /feed, /settings, /nearby, /spaces/danieltyack/manage', which is the app-space-console. The four PNGs were taken and are carried here. ⚠️ THE CAPTURE'S OWN BRANCH IS NOT SAFE TO MERGE AND WAS NOT MERGED. The runner committed to `claude/visual-baseline-recapture-cc3nen`, a STALE branch whose merge base is b429fe5d3, not current main - a two-dot diff against main shows 135 files it would DELETE, including every baseline added since that point. Nothing was deleted by the capture itself; the branch is simply 135 commits behind. The 12 PNGs here were cherry-picked onto a fresh branch off main instead. ⚠️ 22 further PNGs from the same capture were deliberately LEFT: app-feed, app-nearby, app-settings, discover (mobile) and the-community all moved, none of them was failing, and re-recording a passing baseline launders drift nobody has explained. The 8 home PNGs ARE taken, because LIVE-104 added two buttons to the published home document in the same session and its baselines have to move with it.

entries.title: Every public event advertised a start time seven hours early to search and answer engines
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 by driving the real builders and reading their OUTPUT rather than their source. `events.starts_at` stores the WALL CLOCK as UTC parts (lib/time/zone.ts), and eventSchema published it raw. Measured against production: `breathe-connect-expand-2026-08-27` starts 6:30pm Pacific and its Event node said `2026-08-27T18:30:00Z`, which every consumer reads as 11:30am. All five upcoming public events were wrong, and so was the /events ItemList. This is SCAN-101 on the SEO surface — the same convention read as an instant, which in SQL closed the guest RSVP door before lunch. CLOSED: lib/time/zone.ts gains eventIsoWithOffset, which keeps the host wall clock and attaches the zone offset AT THAT INSTANT, and both builders use it. Its own test found a defect while being written — reading the offset independently disagreed with eventInstant by an hour inside the spring-forward gap — so the offset is now derived from eventInstant own answer and the two cannot disagree by construction. THREE ASSERTIONS IN lib/jsonld.test.ts WERE PINNING THE BUG and were updated. ⏳ FOLLOW-UP: public_events / public_event_by_slug do not return time_zone, so the /discover pages fall back to the community zone. Correct for 61 of 61 events today; widening those RPCs is the durable fix.

entries.title: hide_address was a render-layer control: the address leaked through grants, two feeds and the .ics

source.ref: the rule, now with one copy

entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 in the final security pass, reproduced AS ROLE ANON on production before anything changed: 59 event rows readable, 18 of them with hide_address = true and every one still returning `street`, and 24 returning `organizer_contact` — host phone numbers and personal email addresses. public.events carried no table-wide SELECT for anon (claim_token and rsvp_requires_approval were correctly withheld) but COLUMN-level SELECT on nearly everything else. The ADR-964 shape verbatim, and scripts/table-grants.txt warns about it in its own header: check:grants cannot see column grants at all. 🔴 THE FIRST PROPOSED FIX WAS WRONG AND CHECKING CAUGHT IT — "revoke select on events from anon, every reader uses the admin client" is true of 244 of 245 sites; app/discover/events/_data.ts reads it with the anon key and a blanket revoke would have dark-screened the public events hub. entries.title: A host could pin an announcement into any circle: the scope check named only `group`
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 in the final security pass. createPost coerces an announcement to `cluster` visibility, then checked membership only for `group` — so the scope check never ran on the one post type that pins itself to the top of a feed and broadcasts beyond the circle. The host+ check above it answers a different question: it proves the author may announce, not where. THE DATABASE WAS NOT SILENT — `posts: insert (crew+ in scope)` requires, for cluster, `scope_id = ANY (private.get_my_circle_ids()) OR EXISTS (select 1 from circles c where c.id = posts.scope_id and c.host_id = private.get_my_profile_id())`. The action accepted exactly what the policy would refuse, and because it inserts through createAdminClient() the policy never ran to say so. Six of 56 profiles hold host+. CLOSED: the check now mirrors the predicate — active membership, or hosting that circle, with the host arm admitted only for cluster.

entries.title: The /events ticket-tier read truncates at max_rows, so trailing events silently lose their from-price
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 while closing SCAN-303, by measuring the OTHER .in() reads in the same loader rather than stopping at the one the row named. PostgREST caps a response at max_rows (1000, supabase/config.toml) SERVER-SIDE: service_role does not escape it and .limit() does not raise it. Active ticket tiers scale as events x tiers and are bounded by neither, so past 1,000 rows the trailing events silently lose "From $X" — the same truncation class as ADR-962 (CRM import dedupe), ADR-969 (QR capture counts) and SCAN-303 itself, which is now the FOURTH occurrence. The other two reads in that loader were measured and are safe: myRsvpRows is bounded by event_rsvps_event_profile_uniq (at most one row per event per profile) and circlesRows by the number of distinct hosting circles. FIX: the same shape SCAN-303 used — chunk the input well under the cap, or aggregate in the database, and fail safe. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25. Premise re-tested first (ADR-1082): the read was still a single unbounded .in(), and production carried 2 active tiers on 1 event against 60 published events — so this is the first of the five caught BEFORE it fired rather than by its consequence. 🔴 CHUNKING THE INPUT WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT, and that is the difference from SCAN-303: that RPC returns at most one row per id, so 500 ids bounded the response. Tiers are many-per-event, so 500 ids at 5 tiers each is 2,500 rows and truncates just the same. The response had to be bounded AT THE SOURCE, so the fix is an AGGREGATE — event_tier_price_summary (20270332000000, applied, ledger repaired to the repo version, 640 to 640) returns exactly one row per event carrying the three things the label needs: tier_count, min_priced_cents and has_flexible. lib/events/tier-prices.ts prefers it and falls back to a PAGED read folded locally, so the migration was safe to merge unapplied. A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME SHAPE was found while wiring it: lib/spaces/content-data.ts ran its own raw .in() for the Space card. It was bounded — listEventsForSpace caps at 24 — but only loosely, since 24 events at 42 tiers each still reaches 1,000, and a bound that depends on nobody building a long ticket ladder is not a bound. Both surfaces now share the helper, and eventPriceLabel was RETIRED rather than left as a second definition of the label. ⚠️ THE MIGRATION'S OWN PROBE CAUGHT TWO OF MY ERRORS BEFORE ANYTHING LANDED, both applies failing atomically with no function, no ledger row and no probe rows left behind: a fixture built on pricing_mode 'sliding' (the schema allows fixed/free/pwyc/sliding_scale/donation), and a grant that revoked from PUBLIC only — Supabase's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES (ADR-959) grants EXECUTE to anon and authenticated as NAMED roles, so both must be named in the revoke. That is the ADR-964 shape one level over: there it was column grants nobody narrowed, here a function grant that arrives pre-opened. 27 tests, four of them mutation-proven to fire, including an 8-case arm pinning the new path against the RETIRED implementation preserved verbatim as an oracle.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const rd=function(f){return fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8")};const raw=/from\\((["\u0027])event_ticket_types\\1\\)/;const listing=rd("app/(main)/events/index-data.ts");if(raw.test(listing)){console.error("the /events listing reads event_ticket_types raw again - that read is unbounded and truncates at max_rows");process.exit(1)}if(listing.indexOf("tierSummariesByEvent(eventIds)")<0){console.error("the /events listing no longer calls tierSummariesByEvent");process.exit(1)}const space=rd("lib/spaces/content-data.ts");if(raw.test(space)){console.error("the Space card reads event_ticket_types raw again - the second instance of the same shape");process.exit(1)}if(space.indexOf("tierSummariesByEvent(ids)")<0){console.error("the Space card no longer calls tierSummariesByEvent");process.exit(1)}const h=rd("lib/events/tier-prices.ts");if(h.indexOf(".range(fetched, fetched + TIER_PAGE - 1)")<0){console.error("the helper fallback stopped paging, so it can truncate exactly like the read it replaced");process.exit(1)}if(h.indexOf(".order(\u0027id\u0027, { ascending: true })")<0){console.error("the paged fallback lost its total order, so rows can straddle a page boundary");process.exit(1)}const mig="supabase/migrations/20270332000000_event_tier_price_summary_rpc.sql";if(!fs.existsSync(mig)){console.error("the aggregate migration is gone: "+mig);process.exit(1)}const m=rd(mig);if(m.indexOf("group by t.event_id")<0){console.error("the RPC stopped aggregating, so its response is no longer one row per event");process.exit(1)}if(m.indexOf("from public, anon, authenticated")<0){console.error("the RPC grant stopped naming anon/authenticated - Supabase default privileges re-open it");process.exit(1)}const t=rd("lib/events/tier-prices.test.ts");if(t.indexOf("legacyEventPriceLabel")<0){console.error("the retired-oracle parity arm is gone; nothing pins the new label against the old behaviour");process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Six arms, each a CONSEQUENCE rather than a title: neither surface reads event_ticket_types raw, both call the helper, the helper's fallback still pages AND still orders by the primary key (an unordered page can double-count across a boundary), the migration still aggregates and still names anon/authenticated in its revoke, and the retired-oracle parity arm still exists. Each was mutation-tested and each names its own fix. Not `vitest run`: LIVE-034 forbids a probe that spawns a test runner.

entries.title: Scoped rooms and three USING(true) tables admit anon with no identity check

source.ref: the authenticated verdicts the gate cannot verify

entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 in the final security pass, and filed rather than fixed because both need a policy decision rather than a patch. (1) `rooms_read_public_or_member` admits `visibility IN (circle, hub, nexus, outpost, channel)` with NO identity check at all, and room_messages / room_members carry the same channel branch. Live: anon reads the one channel room metadata; messages and members return 200 [] rather than 42501, so only EMPTINESS is withholding them today — and room_messages is in the realtime publication. (2) dispatch_poll_votes, spotlight_top_friends and listing_comments have `USING (true)` with the anon grant intact; poll votes carry (profile_id, option_id) on member-only dispatches. Latent at 0 rows, which is exactly when it is cheap to fix. ⚠️ THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS: of the tables verdicted `authenticated`, 65 were PROVEN to filter anon against real data, and 72 more are empty and therefore prove nothing. These findings live in that second group, which is the group table-grants.txt says the gate cannot verify. The other side is clean: 79 of 79 `internal` tables fail closed with 42501. ── ✅ RULED AND CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1149). OWNER RULING: TIGHTEN BOTH. 20270334000000 applied; ledger repaired to the repo version and verified as an EXACT BIJECTION by hash, not just by count (642 ⇄ 642, md5 e870925394181ea1cd8d0a2c48c7abac on both sides). ROOMS: the three scoped branches now require an authenticated caller; `visibility = 'public'` stays open to anon and membership still grants what it always did. Identity rather than membership, deliberately — browsing a circle's rooms before joining is a plausible flow and there is no data to say whether it is used, so this row closes the anon hole rather than redesigning room visibility. THE THREE TABLES: poll votes scope to your OWN vote, top friends to the OWNER's rows, listing_comments to `authenticated` (it is public-adjacent community content on public listings, so owner-scoping would be wrong rather than merely strict; what it stops is a signed-out bulk enumeration). ✅ WHY IT WAS FREE, AND THE CHECK THAT MADE IT SAFE: every application reader of all three tables goes through createAdminClient(), which bypasses RLS entirely, so those policies served NO application path — they only widened what the publishable anon key could ask PostgREST for. The rooms side is the same: the one non-admin reader (app/(main)/messages/popover-actions.ts) already calls auth.getUser() and scopes to the caller's own memberships. That question is not a formality — 20270330000000 nearly shipped as a blanket table revoke until app/discover/events/_data.ts turned out to be the ONE anon reader of 245 sites. ⚠️ AND A SECOND PASS WENT FURTHER THAN THE POLICIES: anon's SELECT GRANT was revoked on all five tables that have no anon path, because a policy the caller misses returns 200 [] — the very shape this row criticised ('only EMPTINESS is withholding them') — while removing the grant makes the same refusal arrive as 42501. public.rooms KEEPS its anon grant on purpose, or the public branch would go with it. VERIFIED AS ROLE ANON AFTER: rooms 1 → 0 readable (the channel room is now withheld, and that is the policy rather than emptiness), messages/members/poll votes/top friends all 0. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 by 20270334000000 + 20270335000000. Production now holds ZERO anon SELECT grants across all six tables and retains all six for authenticated. The follow-up migration exists because the first one spared public.rooms on an unmeasured premise; db-tests failed its positive control and no anon reader of rooms turned out to exist (ADR-1150).

scoped rooms and three USING(true) tables would admit anon again");const b=pick(/rooms_drops_the_vestigial_anon_grant/,"the public.rooms anon-grant revoke is gone; rooms would admit the publishable anon key again");const need=[[/rooms_read_public_or_member/,"the rooms policy"],[/room_messages_read_members/,"the room_messages policy"],[/room_members_read/,"the room_members policy"],[/dispatch_poll_votes/,"dispatch_poll_votes"],[/spotlight_top_friends/,"spotlight_top_friends"],[/listing_comments/,"listing_comments"]];for(const pair of need){if(!pair[0].test(a)){console.error("the migration no longer covers "+pair[1]);process.exit(1)}}if((a.match(/auth\.uid\(\)/g)||[]).length<3){console.error("fewer than three scoped-room branches require identity; the middle branch that asked nothing of the caller is the original bug");process.exit(1)}if(!/revoke select on public\.listing_comments\s+from anon/.test(a)){console.error("the anon SELECT revokes are gone, so a withheld read returns 200 [] rather than 42501 - the exact ambiguity this row named");process.exit(1)}if(!/revoke select on public\.rooms\s+from anon/.test(b)){console.error("public.rooms kept the vestigial anon SELECT grant that no migration ever created - ADR-1150");process.exit(1)}const pairs=[[a,"20270334000000"],[b,"20270335000000"]];for(const p of pairs){if(!/_auth_grants_before/.test(p[0])){console.error(p[1]+" lost its before/after snapshot, so its positive control names an absolute grant again - the defect ADR-1150 records");process.exit(1)}if(!/this took too much/.test(p[0])){console.error(p[1]+" lost its positive control - nothing now fails if a revoke takes more than it meant to");process.exit(1)}}if(!/qual like .%public%./.test(b)){console.error("the public-room discovery control is gone; an authenticated member could lose sight of public rooms silently");process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE across BOTH migrations that carry this row: all six relations covered, at least three auth.uid() branches (one per scoped-room policy), the anon revokes present on all six INCLUDING public.rooms, and each migration still carrying its before/after snapshot plus its "this took too much" arm. The last two matter because the FIRST version of the positive control asserted an absolute grant ("anon lost SELECT on public.rooms"), which db-tests failed on a fresh apply - see ADR-1150. A control stated as a difference is true in every environment; one stated as an absolute is only true in the one it was written against.

entries.title: #2286 (the 2026-08-25 meta-scan) is unmerged, conflicts with main, and is a second agent's in-flight draft

source.ref: the add/add conflict against main's copy of the same version

entries.detail: HANDOFF 2026-08-25 from the merge-queue session that landed #2274, #2276, #2277, #2278, #2279, #2280, #2281, #2282, #2284, #2285 and #2283. #2286 is the ONE open PR that session did not land, and it is blocked on ownership rather than on code: it is a DRAFT belonging to a different agent that was still pushing to it during the queue run (its head moved three times: 44153f2e -> 09e793e8 -> b5908fe8). Pushing a merge commit into a branch another agent is actively rewriting risks colliding with them, so the queue session deliberately did not. ── ITS CONFLICT IS UNDERSTOOD AND CHEAP: two files. (1) docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json — #2286 adds 30 SCAN-* rows; a 3-way merge by row id resolves it with no losses (measured: base 223 / ours 253 / theirs 225 -> 255 entries, 0 duplicate ids, no both-sides row edits). (2) supabase/migrations/20270327000000_restore_listing_saves.sql — an add/add where BOTH SIDES ARE FUNCTIONALLY IDENTICAL: same table, same PK, same two FKs, same covering index, same private.get_my_profile_id() RLS policy. Main's copy is already merged AND already applied to production, so keep MAIN's file; the only thing worth taking from #2286's copy is its comment block, which answers the question main's copy leaves open (see LIVE-123's sibling finding below). 🔴 DO NOT re-derive the listing_saves provenance: #2286 established it. 20260925000000 dropped public.listing_saves claiming '0 code references', and that claim was FALSE — lib/listings/index.ts holds four live call sites (saveListing / unsaveListing / listSavedListingIds / listSavedListings) reaching the UI through components/marketplace/save-listing-button.tsx and the /housing pages. Every path failed SAFE (the write discarded its error, the reads fell back to 'nothing saved'), so from 2026-09-25 until the restore, hearting a housing listing wrote to a table that did not exist and the heart silently reset on reload. No gate noticed because the saves tests mock the client. NEXT STEP: decide who owns #2286, then resolve those two files and land it, or close it and re-file its 30 SCAN rows. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25, and NOT by merging #2286. That branch reached 112 changed files, and ci.yml's PR-size gate fails anything over 40 unless the title carries [sweep] — owner-directed after a 215-file PR killed production deploys for a day (ADR-1002). [sweep] is reserved for a single-purpose mechanical change where every file takes the same one edit, which a branch carrying four high-severity fixes, an SEO round, a speed round, an a11y round and an orphan sweep is not. So it was split by backlog row, which is the remedy the gate's own message names: #2288 (phase 1, correctness), #2289 (phase 2, SEO/GEO), #2290 (phase 3, speed + a11y) and #2291 (phase 4, hygiene). Four branches off main with DISJOINT paths, each carrying only the rows it closes, each run through the full battery on its OWN branch rather than on the tree it was carved from. That last part earned itself twice: it surfaced two cross-slice dependencies the combined branch could never have shown (two Spark modules importing a FieldError from another slice, and a route-chunk gate that stays red until the slice fixing its instance lands). This row's own conclusions were both confirmed and used: the listing_saves migration kept MAIN's copy, and the provenance it recorded was not re-derived. #2286 itself is closed as superseded, not merged. ADR-1140 §5 records the decision.

verify.evidence: PR #2286 closed as superseded on 2026-08-25 after #2288/#2289/#2290/#2291 replaced it. Each replacement is <= 40 changed files and passed the PR-size gate, which #2286 could not. Split by path with disjoint sets; each verified on its own branch (tsc, eslint, full vitest suite, all 24 contract guards, check:backlog) before push.

entries.title: Every agent hand-resolves the same two ledger-doc conflicts, because the fold tooling is never committed

source.ref: the file half of the conflict; no committed tool folds it or DECISIONS.md

entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 by driving eleven PRs through the queue in one session. EVERY open PR appends to the tail of docs/DECISIONS.md and adds rows to docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json, so EVERY merge to main re-conflicts EVERY other open PR on those exact two files — and on nothing else (verified with `git merge-tree --write-tree` across all remaining branches: the conflict set was those two paths, every time, with zero code conflicts). The queue session hit this eleven times and resolved it eleven times by hand or by throwaway scripts, and this is at least the second session to do so. ── THE TWO RESOLUTIONS ARE MECHANICAL AND ALWAYS THE SAME. DECISIONS.md: both sides append ADR entries at the tail, so keep main's block first and the branch's after (theirs-then-ours), then `node scripts/check-adr.mjs` proves it. BUILD-BACKLOG.json: a 3-way merge BY ROW ID — for each id, if ours == base take theirs, if theirs == base take ours, if both changed STOP and report rather than guess; emit in main's order and append ids only this branch has. Both are ~30 lines. 🔴 THE JSON HALF MUST NOT BE HAND-EDITED: doing so has already produced an invalid file (a dropped `},{` between two rows) and a duplicated row id in this repo's history, each costing a CI round. 🔴 AND IT MUST NOT SILENTLY PICK A WINNER when both sides edited one row: that case is real (HYG-020 was edited on both sides in this session, main holding it `open` and the closing PR holding it `done`) and it needs a human, so the tool must exit non-zero and name the id. Write it to reproduce byte-identical output (the repo file has NO trailing newline; json.dump(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) plus no final write matches it exactly) or the diff becomes unreviewable. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25: scripts/maintenance/fold-ledger-docs.mjs shipped in #2291, and it obeys both 🔴 rules above. It refuses when both sides edited the same row and NAMES the id, which is not theoretical — this very branch is the case: main and the handoff both amended LIVE-123, the tool stopped, and a human folded it (main 06:16 spine, plus the terminal-error finding main was missing). It also gained a CI half, scripts/maintenance/fold-ledger-docs.test.ts, and writing that test found three real defects: a trailing newline docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json does not have (one byte, but it costs a spurious last-line hunk on every branch that merges after), a duplicate row id arriving on EITHER side being silently swallowed by new Map() — which would have resolved a conflict by losing a row — and an unguarded main() that shelled out to git on import. The byte-fidelity rule this row wrote down was itself recorded backwards in the tool header; the file was measured with od -c to settle it.

entries.title: 🔴 PICK THIS UP FIRST: #2283 is unmerged and the migration ledger is deliberately one row AHEAD of main until it lands

source.ref: the two-step apply/ledger-repair protocol; 20270326000000 lives on #2283, not yet on main

entries.detail: HANDOFF 2026-08-25 06:00 UTC, and the FIRST thing the next thread should read. #2283 (housing/natal-matching, head dac3a9d96) is the last PR of the merge queue. THIRTEEN of its fourteen checks are green — checks, lint, test, CodeQL, analyze, db-tests, drift, autodoc, preflight all passed — and it is blocked on ONE thing: its Vercel preview stalled at 'Collecting page data' (see LIVE-123; this is that bug's SECOND occurrence). ── 🔴 WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY BE ABANDONED. production's migration ledger currently holds 635 rows while main's tree holds 634 files, because the ledger row `20270326000000 natal_chart_matching` was restored BEFORE the merge, which the sequence requires: check:migrations runs pre-merge, so a PR carrying a migration file reads repoOnly drift unless its row is already there. That means main is in a deliberate, temporary ledgerOnly drift RIGHT NOW, and `check:migrations` reads red on main and on any branch lacking that file until #2283 merges. ── ✅ THE FIX IS TO MERGE #2283, NOT TO DELETE THE ROW. The migration is genuinely applied: all five functions (housing_safe_float, housing_aspect_score, housing_natal_compat, housing_match_candidates, housing_roommate_matches) were verified present in production with signatures matching the repo file exactly, and db-tests proves the file replays on a fresh database. Deleting the ledger row would be the lie in the other direction — a fresh `db reset` would then not create functions production has. If the Vercel stall persists, re-push the branch to retrigger a build (the queue did exactly this for #2285 and the retry succeeded in 2m50s on the same cache), or merge once Vercel reports. ── ALSO STILL OPEN ON #2283, advisory only: the autodoc bot flagged content/help/connecting/matching-and-romance.md, whose line 'Only your sign is used. We work out your sun sign from your birth date and use that.' becomes FALSE once #2283 lands, since a full natal chart is then derived and stored from the birth date. The privacy half of that sentence ('your birth date itself is never shown to anyone') stays true, and no chart is ever returned by an RPC. Fix the first half in the same pass, on voice, per docs/CONTENT-VOICE.md. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25: #2283 MERGED (main 0ab3b4abb, "Natal charts are computed in-process at save and stored; matching reads them natal-first"). The deliberate one-row-ahead ledger drift this row existed to protect is therefore resolved the way it said it must be — by merging, never by deleting the row. Verified after the fact: the ledger and supabase/migrations/ are an exact bijection again (636 ⇄ 636 as of 08:0x, which includes 20270328000000 guest_rsvp_zone_aware_gate applied and ledger-repaired by the meta-scan phase 1 PR). The advisory half is still OPEN and now has its own row: content/help/connecting/matching-and-romance.md still says "Only your sign is used", which #2283 made false.

On voice per docs/CONTENT-VOICE.md: plain sentences, no em dashes, never narrate the reader's feelings. ── ✅ ALREADY TRUE WHEN THE ROW WAS FILED, and the probe is what said so on its first run — the ADR-1082 rule paying for itself again, this time within a minute. The article does NOT carry the sentence the autodoc bot flagged: content/help/connecting/matching-and-romance.md:18 already reads "Your chart is worked out, never shown. We build a birth chart from your birth date and use it to spot quiet overlaps. Nobody sees your birth date or your chart, and nobody gets a breakdown of the score." That is accurate for what #2283 computes AND keeps the privacy claim intact, which is exactly the shape the fix was supposed to take.
