entries.title: 572 requests died at Vercel's 300s ceiling across 30 routes, and no row named it
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 by reading the project's runtime errors, not by a gate — the same way LIVE-053 was found, and the second time that read has paid. Vercel's grouped runtime errors for the trailing 7 days hold 42 groups. The largest by a wide margin: `Vercel Runtime Timeout Error: Task timed out after 300 seconds`, count 572, users 48, first 2026-07-15T16:02Z, last 2026-08-25T02:47Z. Thirty routes are named. Fourteen are crons, where hitting a 300s ceiling is a budget problem. The rest are not: `/`, `/feed`, `/events`, `/nearby`, `/settings`, `/classifieds`, `/spaces/directory`, `/spaces/[slug]/manage`, `/middleware`. On those, the number means a real visitor waited five minutes and got nothing.
── WHAT IS ALREADY EXCLUDED. A large share of the 7-day window is one incident: between 02:18 and 02:53 on 2026-08-25, Supabase was unreachable from the runtime — Cloudflare 521, 522 and 525 against the project host, plus `Timed out acquiring connection from connection pool` and `upstream request timeout`. Thirty-five of the 42 groups both start AND end inside that 35-minute window, so they are that incident and not a standing defect. This row is about what is left: the timeout group spans SIX WEEKS, which no single outage explains.
── AND IT IS NOT THE BUILD STALL. The obvious move is to join this to LIVE-105 and LIVE-123, which are both builds hanging at 'Collecting page data'. That was tested and the evidence points the other way — see those rows and ADR-1159. The two phenomena are anti-correlated in every window measured, not linked.
── FIRST STEP, and it is cheap: split the 572 by route and by whether the timestamp falls inside a known Supabase incident. A cron at 300s and `/feed` at 300s are different bugs sharing an error string, and the count is currently their sum.

── ✅ THE SPLIT IS DONE, 2026-08-25, and it shrinks this row to less than half its size. The row's stated first step was to split the 572 by route and by whether the timestamp falls inside a known Supabase incident. Both cuts, measured:
  • BY ROUTE: filtering to the six MEMBER-FACING page routes (/settings, /events, /classifieds, /, /nearby, /feed) gives **258 of 572, across 6 users**. The other 314 are on crons, RSC payloads and API routes, where a 300s ceiling is a budget question rather than a visitor waiting.
  • BY WINDOW, and this is the answer: the six days from 2026-08-19T00:00Z to 2026-08-25T02:00Z — everything before the outage — returned **ZERO** timeouts on those six routes. Three error groups in that whole window, all count=1: two Stripe Connect config errors and LIVE-053's known TypeError. Re-querying 02:00-04:00Z on 2026-08-25 returns **258**, the entire count.
  🔴 SO EVERY ONE OF THE 258 MEMBER-FACING TIMEOUTS HAPPENED INSIDE THE 35-MINUTE SUPABASE OUTAGE. There is no standing defect on the routes a member actually loads: when the database is up, they do not time out. The group's `first=2026-07-15` is the group's lifetime first-seen and was the thing that made this look like a six-week bleed; it is not a per-window count, and reading it as one is the mistake this row was opened on.
  ⚠️ WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT ROW'S SHAPE: the 314 non-page timeouts. Fourteen distinct /api/cron/* routes appear. A cron that runs past 300s is a work-per-invocation problem — it wants batching or a smaller window, not a page-performance fix — and it is the half that survives this measurement. Scope this row to those, or close it and open the cron-budget row cleanly.
── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 BY RE-MEASUREMENT, thirteen days after the split. Fresh Vercel grouped runtime errors, trailing 7 days, project frequency-web: the `Vercel Runtime Timeout Error: Task timed out after 300 seconds` group DOES NOT APPEAR AT ALL. Not on the six member-facing page routes, not on crons, not on API routes, not anywhere - the whole 572-count group is gone from the window. Four groups remain in the entire project and none of them is a timeout.

That closes this row on its own terms rather than by assertion. The row's scope after the split was the MEMBER-FACING half, whose standing rate the split already measured at zero for the six days before the outage; a second independent window thirteen days later, on a different set of deployments, reads zero again. Two windows either side of the incident, both zero, is the evidence a manual row is supposed to close on.

⚪ THE RESIDUE HAS A HOME AND IS NOT BEING SMUGGLED OUT. The 314 non-page timeouts on crons and API routes belong to LIVE-190, which was filed from this row's own tail on 2026-09-06 precisely so the cron-budget question would stop being homeless. That row stays open. The same fresh read is recorded there.

verify.evidence: Split completed 2026-08-25 with three Vercel queries. (1) 7d, all routes: 572 timeouts / 48 users / 30 routes. (2) 7d filtered to the six member-facing page routes: 258 / 6 users. (3) The same six routes from 2026-08-19T00:00Z to 2026-08-25T02:00Z, i.e. six days ending just before the Supabase outage: ZERO timeouts, only three count=1 groups (two Stripe Connect config errors, LIVE-053's TypeError). Re-querying 02:00-04:00Z returns the full 258. So 100% of member-facing timeouts are outage-attributable and the standing rate is zero. The residue is 314 timeouts on crons and API routes, which is a work-per-invocation budget question. ── 2026-09-07 RE-MEASURED AND CLOSED: a fresh Vercel 7-day grouped-runtime-error read returns FOUR groups for the whole project and the 300s timeout group is not among them - zero on the six member-facing routes, zero on crons, zero on API routes. Two independent windows either side of the outage both read zero on this row scope. The cron/API residue is LIVE-190 and stays open.

entries.title: The visual gate cannot see a control-sized change, and the taller the page the blinder it gets
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 the expensive way: it cost a correct change being marked broken, re-opened, and then re-closed. playwright.config.ts sets `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02` globally for `toHaveScreenshot`, with the stated reason 'tolerate sub-2% pixel drift (fonts/AA)'. That reason is sound and the number is not, because the suite takes FULL-PAGE screenshots of very tall pages and a ratio scales with the canvas:
    /discover mobile    390 x 9675  = 3,773,250 px  ->  2% = 75,465 px of permitted drift
    /about    mobile    390 x 9457  = 3,688,230 px  ->  2% = 73,764 px
    /discover desktop  1280 x 7538  = 9,648,640 px  ->  2% = 192,972 px
  On desktop /discover a block of roughly 440 x 440 can change with the gate reporting a pass. A whole header control is 1,600 px, i.e. 2.1% of the mobile budget. THE GATE IS AT ITS BLINDEST ON EXACTLY THE PAGES THAT MATTER MOST, because tall pages are the content-rich ones.
  🔴 AND THE FAILURE IS SILENT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. `pnpm test:e2e:update` runs `playwright test --update-snapshots`, which rewrites a snapshot only when the comparison FAILS. A sub-threshold change therefore (a) passes `pr-compare`, and (b) is NOT written into the baseline — so the baseline silently drifts further from reality with every such change, and the next real regression is measured against a stale reference. `No baseline changes to commit` reads like 'nothing moved' and actually means 'nothing moved by more than 2% of a four-megapixel canvas'.
  WHAT TO DO IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT AN OBVIOUS FIX, which is why this is a row and not a one-line patch. `maxDiffPixels` (an absolute count) does what the comment intends — tolerate font and antialiasing noise — without scaling to the canvas; a few thousand absolute pixels would catch a button while still absorbing AA. But the number has to be measured against real capture noise on this suite rather than guessed, or the gate starts failing on nothing and gets routed around, which is ADR-970's whole subject. Measure the noise floor across a few consecutive no-op captures first, then set the absolute value above it.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-26. `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02` is gone; the suite now tolerates `maxDiffPixels: 400`, an ABSOLUTE count that does not grow with the canvas.
  🔴 THE ROW SAID DO NOT GUESS THE NUMBER, AND IT WAS MEASURED. Production could not be captured from this container (the agent proxy answers 403 to CONNECT for frequencylocal.com), so the floor was measured where it actually lives: the RENDERER. The tolerance exists for 'fonts/AA', which is a property of the browser build, not of the site. Six consecutive full-page captures of a purpose-built 390x63392 page and a 1280x29790 page - dense antialiased text, gradients, box-shadows, rounded edges - each taken from a FRESH BROWSER CONTEXT, which is what a CI re-run actually does rather than the best case of one warm page. Result: **0 differing pixels, every pair, both viewports.** Chromium is deterministic within one pinned build and CI pins the build, so the noise this tolerance was sized for is CROSS-environment, not per-run.
  WHY 400 AND NOT 0. A floor of zero is brittle: one Chromium patch bump that shifts a single subpixel would fail every surface at once, and a gate that fails on nothing gets routed around (ADR-970). 400 is a quarter of the 1600 pixels of a 40x40 header control - the smallest thing this gate must be able to see - and 0.0016% of a 24-megapixel canvas, so scattered AA differences are still absorbed while a control cannot hide.
  ⚠️ WHAT THIS MEASUREMENT DOES NOT COVER, stated rather than papered over: it is one container and one browser build. If the CI runner's font set differs from the run that captured a baseline, real drift could exceed 400. That is exactly why this lands as a PR whose own `pr-compare` job exercises the new threshold against the COMMITTED baselines - the repo's rule is to wire a gate in the same change as the run that proves it. A red pr-compare here is not a setback, it is the measurement, and the number moves to just above whatever it reports.
  THE PROBE HAD TO CHANGE TOO, and the reason is worth keeping: the original grepped the whole file for `maxDiffPixelRatio`, so the COMMENT explaining why the setting was retired failed it. A probe that cannot tell use from mention would have forced the history out of the file to make itself pass. It now strips line comments first, and gained two arms it did not have: an absolute tolerance must be SET, and it must be under 1600, so the row cannot be closed by deleting the tolerance or by setting one too loose to see a control.

── ⏳ RE-OPENED 2026-08-26, AND THE ROW IS NOW WORTH FAR MORE THAN IT WAS. The change was made (`maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02` -> `maxDiffPixels: 400`), pushed, and MEASURED by pr-compare against the committed baselines on #2312. It came back RED, and the red is the finding.
  ✅ FIRST, THE THRESHOLD IS VINDICATED: **123 of 144 surfaces PASS at 400 absolute pixels.** That is empirical proof from CI itself that the noise floor is under 400 there, confirming the 0-differing-pixel result measured locally across six fresh-context captures. 400 is not too tight.
  🔴 SECOND, 21 SURFACES CARRY DRIFT THE OLD RATIO WAS HIDING. Ten distinct readings: **669, 899, 1439, 2345, 5507, 5973, 8890, 8928, 8973, 8990** differing pixels, across discover (all four themes), app-feed (light+dark), app-nearby (light+dark), app-settings and app-space-console. EVERY ONE reported ratio 0.01 or less, i.e. every one was UNDER the old 2% and therefore passing. This is precisely what this row predicted: `--update-snapshots` rewrites a baseline only when the comparison FAILS, so these changes were neither caught NOR banked, and the baselines have been drifting away from reality for as long as the ratio has been in place.
  🔴 SO RAISING THE NUMBER IS THE WRONG MOVE, and it is the move the red run invites. A threshold above 8990 is 5.6x the 1600 pixels of a header control -- it would restore exactly the blindness this row exists to remove. The threshold is right; the BASELINES are stale.
  ⚠️ AND THEY MUST NOT BE RECAPTURED BLIND. Nobody has looked at what those 21 diffs contain. Recapturing bakes in whatever is there, including any real regression the gate has been hiding -- which would convert a measurement problem into a permanent one.
  🔵 A READING OF THE SPLIT, offered as a hypothesis and labelled as one. The four `/discover` diffs are 8890 / 8928 / 8973 / 8990 -- nearly identical across dawn-light, dawn-dark, midnight-light AND midnight-dark. A theme-independent delta of the same size in all four reads as STRUCTURE, not colour. And test/e2e/surfaces.ts already documents that /discover's height drifts between requests because six live queries feed it and three are order- or clock-sensitive. So the likeliest split is: content-dynamic surfaces (/discover, /feed, /nearby) where NO absolute threshold can ever be stable and the answer is `mask` or `viewportOnly` -- both of which visual.spec.ts already supports -- versus genuinely stale baselines (/settings, /spaces/.../manage) that just need a recapture. NOT CONFIRMED: the diff PNGs live in a 256 MB artifact that was not opened.
  THE CONFIG CHANGE WAS WITHDRAWN from #2312 rather than carried red. SCAN-520 in that same PR is finished and already applied to production; holding it hostage to a baseline recapture would be the wrong trade. The change is three lines and re-applies in a minute once the baselines are sound.
  WHAT CLOSES THIS ROW, in order: (1) open the pr-compare artifact from run 32915754788 and look at the 21 diff images; (2) mask or viewportOnly the content-dynamic surfaces; (3) recapture the rest via e2e-manual.yml with `update_baselines` AND `capture_shell: true` -- the shell flag is required or the member surfaces silently do not run (LIVE-... records that same instruction being incomplete once already); (4) re-apply maxDiffPixels: 400 and confirm pr-compare is green.

── 🔴 THE CONTENT-CHURN HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, 2026-08-26, from the pr-compare log alone (run 32915754788). It was written above as a hypothesis and labelled as one; it is now tested and WRONG, and the true reading is worse.
  TWO FACTS KILL IT. (1) **No size mismatches.** Playwright reports a dimension change as 'Expected an image WxH, received WxH2'. Not one of the 21 failures is that shape - every single one is a pixel diff at IDENTICAL dimensions. If /discover's six live queries were churning content, the page height would move; surfaces.ts documents exactly that drift. It did not move. (2) **The counts are byte-stable across all three retries.** discover--dawn-dark reads 8890, 8890, 8890. app-nearby--dawn-dark reads 5507, 5507, 5507. app-settings and app-space-console read 899 three times each. Live-data churn varies between runs by definition. This does not vary.
  SO THESE ARE REAL, STABLE, REPRODUCIBLE VISUAL CHANGES that the 2% ratio has been swallowing - not noise, not timing, not data. Something changed on /discover, /feed, /nearby, /settings and /spaces/.../manage, and the gate never told anyone. The four /discover readings (8890 / 8928 / 8973 / 8990) sitting within 100 pixels of each other across dawn-light, dawn-dark, midnight-light AND midnight-dark is one structural change rendered in four palettes, which is what a theme-independent delta of constant size means.
  ⚠️ ONE GENUINE EXCEPTION, and it is the only one: app-feed--dawn-dark reads 1439, then 669, then 669. That surface DOES carry a non-deterministic element and is the single candidate for mask/viewportOnly treatment. Every other surface is stable.
  WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE CLOSE CONDITION: step 2 shrinks to one surface (app-feed dark) instead of three, and step 1 stops being 'decide if these are churn' and becomes 'find out WHAT changed', because the answer is no longer in doubt that something did. A recapture without that answer banks an unreviewed change on five member surfaces.
  🔵 AND THE ARTIFACT IS ON A CLOCK: playwright-report-pr-compare (id 9588625085, 245 MB) EXPIRES 2026-09-02. After that the diff images are gone and the only way back to them is re-running pr-compare with the threshold re-applied. An agent cannot fetch it: api.github.com is reachable from the build container but the artifact 302s to productionresultssa16.blob.core.windows.net, which the egress proxy denies with a 403 on CONNECT. Tested 2026-08-26, not assumed.

── ✅ STEP 1 ANSWERED 2026-08-26 WITHOUT THE ARTIFACT, from git history. The row's step 1 was 'find out WHAT changed'. The diff images could not be fetched (the artifact 302s to Azure blob storage, which the egress proxy denies), so the question was answered from the baselines themselves, which are committed PNGs with a git log.
  1. EVERY failing mobile baseline was last captured on 2026-08-21, commit 6127a26c1 ('Visual baselines: capture against ...'). Desktop ones are older still - 2026-08-18 and 2026-08-13. So the reference is FIVE DAYS and 72 commits stale.
  2. app/globals.css has ZERO commits in that window. So the drift is not tokens, not colour, not a skin - it is STRUCTURE. That independently explains the shape the log showed: four /discover variants drifting by 8890 / 8928 / 8973 / 8990, i.e. the same change rendered in four palettes.
  3. WHAT MOVED, by name: components/layout/site-header.tsx changed on 2026-08-25 (c82bcfff1, +29 lines, with viewer-chrome.tsx), and components/layout/marketing-mobile-menu.tsx on 2026-08-24 (f1fccec97, +201, with mega-menu.tsx). app/discover/page.tsx itself is UNTOUCHED. So /discover's diff is its HEADER, not its body.
  🔵 AND THAT CLOSES A LOOP WITH ADR-1161. The site-header change is LIVE-106 / ADR-1158: the phone menu button landing on the browse surface. ADR-1161 is the record of this very gate 'declining to have an opinion' about that hamburger, because 1600 px was 2.1% of the mobile budget. With an absolute threshold the gate SEES it. The 21 failures therefore include the exact control ADR-1161 was written about, which is the strongest available validation that maxDiffPixels: 400 is measuring the right thing.
  ⚖️ THE JUDGEMENT: these are NOT regressions. They are five days of intended, shipped, ADR-documented work (ADR-1118 phone sheet, ADR-1158 mobile menu, PROG-P4/P5 hero and cover resolvers) that the 2% ratio never banked. The baselines are stale; the code is fine.
  SO THE CLOSE IS ONE CHANGE, NOT TWO: recapture the baselines AND re-apply maxDiffPixels: 400 together. Either alone leaves the gate wrong - a recapture under the ratio re-arms the blindness, and the threshold without a recapture is red on 21 surfaces that are not defects. The recapture is e2e-manual.yml with `update_baselines` AND `capture_shell: true` (the header moved, so the shell moved; the workflow's own header says a header change is exactly when you want both).
  ⚠️ STILL WORTH A HUMAN EYE BEFORE THE RECAPTURE, and this is the residual risk stated plainly: the reasoning above identifies what changed by CORRELATION - the right files moved in the right window and the deltas have the right shape - not by looking at the pixels. app-feed--dawn-dark's non-determinism (1439 / 669 / 669) is unexplained by any of it. A glance at the four /discover diffs would convert this from a strong inference into a fact, and the artifact expires 2026-09-02.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P1 on 2026-09-07 in the full re-prioritisation pass: an instrument that keeps a gate honest, and the most load-bearing one on this list: the visual gate cannot see a control-sized change, which is the mechanism behind LIVE-186 and LIVE-040 both going stale under a green board.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-08 (ADR-1258). The instrument is fixed, the number is derived from both ends, and the arithmetic itself now has a test.
  BEFORE, re-measured on the 144 COMMITTED baselines at their real dimensions rather than on the estimates this row carried (the row's figures were the pre-2026-09-05 baselines; the shape is identical). `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02` forgave:
    pricing                desktop  1280x16110 = 20,620,800 px  ->  412,416 px
    how-to-build-community mobile    390x21777 =  8,493,030 px  ->  169,860 px
    discover               mobile    390x 9541 =  3,720,990 px  ->   74,419 px
    app-space-console      mobile    390x 2859 =  1,115,010 px  ->   22,300 px
    app-feed               mobile    390x  844 =    329,160 px  ->    6,583 px
  One setting, 144 different tolerances, a 62.6x spread, widest on the page nobody scrolls to. In terms a reader can act on: the smallest control this product draws is 676 px (26x26 -- `--tap-min` is 32px by default and dips to 26px in one preset, app/globals.css, which is SMALLER than the 40x40 this row assumed). So on pricing desktop, 610 whole controls could change together with the gate green; on discover mobile, 110.
  AFTER: `maxDiffPixels: 400`, exported as SCREENSHOT_MAX_DIFF_PIXELS from playwright.config.ts, no ratio beside it. The forgiven count is 400 on every one of the 144 baselines, from 329,160 px to 20,620,800 px, i.e. 59% of one control everywhere instead of 9 controls at one end and 610 at the other.
  WHY 400 AND NOT A ROUNDER-SOUNDING PICK: floor and ceiling are both measured. FLOOR -- 0 differing pixels across six fresh-context captures (ADR-1165), and pr-compare then read 123 of 144 committed surfaces UNDER 400 against baselines captured on a different runner. That is the only cross-runner reading that exists, so anything lower is unmeasured, and a gate that fails on nothing gets routed around (ADR-970). CEILING -- 676 px, the smallest control, read off the sheet by the test rather than hardcoded, so a preset that lowers the tap floor re-opens the question instead of widening the blind spot silently.
  THE UNIT TEST IS THE POINT, not the config line: test/e2e/screenshot-tolerance.test.ts (plain vitest, on the required `test` check, no browser and no baseURL) imports the real config, reads the IHDR of all 144 PNGs (24 bytes each, not 195 MB), and fails if the forgiven count varies across them, if it grows with height on synthetic canvases up to 100,000px, if a ratio returns, or if the budget reaches the smallest control. It carries the positive control the others would be worthless without: the retired ratio, through the same model, must still show the growth. Three mutations of the LIVE config were run before commit and each fired on its own arm (ratio restored; budget 700; budget 800).
  ⚠️ WHAT THE STRICTER TOLERANCE WOULD NEWLY CATCH, stated as far as it can be from here. The 21 surfaces of #2312 are NOT that set any more: those were baselines from 2026-08-21, and #2366 recaptured ALL 144 on 2026-09-05 (67ada96a5) -- which is precisely the recapture ADR-1165 said had to come first. Since that recapture 2 commits touched app/globals.css and several touched marketing/discover routes, so a newly-red capture is possible and CANNOT be ruled out from this container: the suite needs a deploy URL, so no capture was run and none was re-captured here. The one failure KNOWN today is unaffected either way -- the four /spaces/<slug>/manage captures fail on a DIMENSION mismatch (LIVE-186), and `toHaveScreenshot` fails a size mismatch before it counts a pixel, so no tolerance value changes that verdict. If pr-compare reds on anything else, read it as this gate finally reporting: look at what moved, then recapture (e2e-manual.yml, `update_baselines` AND `capture_shell`). Raising the number back above the drift is the one move that undoes this row.
  Docs corrected in the same pass so nothing still explains the gate by the retired ratio: test/e2e/README.md, test/e2e/overflow.spec.ts, test/e2e/surfaces.ts.

── RE-CONFIRMED 2026-09-08 (ADR-1273). The floor reading this budget rests on ("0 differing pixels across fresh-context captures") was re-measured at the strongest level git can express: two production captures fifteen minutes apart (runs 34181605405 / 34182476256) were byte-identical on 144/144 PNGs, so the runner adds nothing and 400 px forgives only what the page does. LIVE-212's "138 over budget at identical heights" was the 2026-09-04 CTA sweep the committed set predated, not a runner, and it was cleared by a recapture, never by a bigger number.

verify.cmd:  node -e "eval(Buffer.from(process.env.P,'base64').toString())"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE on real data in three arms, with STRING BODIES blanked and then block AND line comments stripped, so the note explaining the retired ratio does not read as using it: (1) an absolute maxDiffPixels must be readable (the identifier is resolved to its exported number); (2) computed over every committed baseline at its true PNG dimensions, the forgiven pixel count must be IDENTICAL on the shortest and the tallest, so the tolerance cannot scale with page height; (3) it must stay under the area of the smallest --tap-min in app/globals.css (676 px), so a whole control cannot hide inside it. 🔴 STRINGS ARE BLANKED FIRST SINCE 2026-09-08 (ADR-1270) AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING: `testMatch: '**/*.spec.ts'` in playwright.config.ts contains a literal `/*`, so the raw block-comment strip read that glob as an OPEN comment and swallowed the file up to the next `*/`. It was inert only while no block comment followed it; the day HYG-057 added one, the swallowed region was the expect.toHaveScreenshot block itself and this probe reported "no absolute maxDiffPixels" against a config that declares 400. Controls re-run 2026-09-08 on the fixed probe: budget 700 fires arm 3 alone; restoring maxDiffPixelRatio 0.02 fires all three (6583 vs 412416 forgiven); deleting the setting fires arms 1+3; the committed 400 exits 0.

entries.title: The payout nudge at the price control is state-blind, and the predicate that would fix it is the 'dead' code
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while classifying SCAN-502's dead exports, and it is the reason that row cannot close on a sweep: this looked like retired code and is actually an unbuilt affordance.
  THE MONEY PATH IS CORRECT AND FAILS CLOSED. lib/billing/tickets.ts reads `getConnectStatus(payeeProfileId)` before every ticket sale and refuses when the host has no ready connected account, with a comment that earns its length: 'letting a buyer pay into an account Stripe cannot pay out of does not under-collect, it takes someone's money and strands it between two parties who both think the other has it.' Nothing here is unsafe.
  THE HOST HALF DOES NOT EXIST. That same comment states the intended design: 'The BUYER sees a neutral sentence. A stranger is never told anything about the host's account state; the HOST gets the real line (NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT) beside the price control, where it is an actionable two-minute setup step rather than a dead end.' `NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT` has ZERO renderers. So a host prices an event, buyers hit checkout and get 'Tickets aren't on sale for this event yet.', and the host is never told why or what to do.
  FOUR SIGNPOSTS POINT AT THE MISSING HALF, which is what makes this read as built when it is not:
      lib/billing/tickets.ts:313          'the HOST gets the real line (NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT)'
      components/marketplace/events-header-actions.tsx:17  'the wall now lives at the price field'
      components/crew/upgrade-lightbox.tsx:18              'the wall now lives at the price field'
      app/(main)/events/index-data.ts:305                  same
  The predicates those comments name — `ticketSellerVerdict` and `canSellTickets` (lib/events/ticket-eligibility.ts) — have no callers. They are the unrendered half, not retired code: `TICKETS_NOT_READY` from the same module IS live at billing/tickets.ts:31.
  ⚠️ IT COMPOUNDS WITH OWN-040. Production Stripe refused `accounts.create` twice on 2026-08-20 (platform profile incomplete, loss responsibilities unreviewed), so today a host who DID work out what to do could not connect anyway. Fixing the affordance without clearing that is a button that leads to a 400.
  THE FIX IS SMALL AND ALREADY DESIGNED: call `ticketSellerVerdict` at the price control with the host's `payoutsReady`, and render `NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT` with a link to the connect step when it refuses. The predicate, the copy and the setup-step token (`'connect_payouts'`) all already exist and are tested-by-construction; only the render is missing.

── 🔴 THIS ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND I WROTE IT BEFORE READING THE FORM. Corrected same day, before anything was built on it. The affordance EXISTS, and it is good. app/(main)/events/new/event-form.tsx, in the `priceMode === 'paid'` branch, already renders:
      'Sets a ticket price. To take the money you need a payout account. [Set that up] in about two minutes, before or after you publish.'
  — with a link to /settings/billing, and a comment above it stating exactly the reasoning I credited as missing: 'this reads as a SETUP STEP with somewhere to go, never as a refusal: production has zero completed onboardings today precisely because the funnel is open and nothing ever asks.' So a host IS told, at the price control, in the two-minute framing. I claimed otherwise on the strength of `NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT` having no renderer, without checking whether the same SENTENCE had been written by hand somewhere. It had.
  WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, and it is much smaller: the notice is STATE-BLIND. It renders whenever `priceMode === 'paid'`, with no reference to whether this host already has a ready connected account. A host who finished payout onboarding last week still gets told they need to set it up, which is the product not knowing them — the same class of defect as the sheet footer offering 'Sign in' to a signed-in member (ADR-1158).
  AND THE FIX IS THE 'DEAD' CODE. `ticketSellerVerdict(ctx)` takes exactly one input, `payoutsReady`, and returns either `{allowed:true}` or `{allowed:false, step:'connect_payouts', reason: NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT}`. That is precisely the branch this render needs. So those three exports are not dead and should not be deleted — they are a predicate waiting for a render that got hand-written instead. Wiring them makes the copy state-aware AND retires the duplicate sentence.
  COST, stated because it is the whole decision: `getConnectStatus` is ONE indexed read on `profiles` (lib/billing/connect.ts:89-92) — no Stripe call, that is `getOrCreateConnectedAccount`. But EventForm is rendered from THREE places (app/(main)/events/new/page.tsx, app/(main)/events/[slug]/edit/page.tsx, app/(main)/events/event-spark.tsx), so a `payoutsReady` prop has to be threaded through all three or the notice is state-aware on some surfaces and not others, which is worse than uniformly state-blind.
  🔵 THE RULING NEEDS RE-TAKING. The owner ruled 'build it now' on the premise that a host is never told. They are told. The remaining change is 'stop nagging hosts who already connected', across three call sites. That is a different, smaller decision and it is theirs, not mine to assume.

── ✅ DONE 2026-08-25 (ADR-1162), and I took the re-ruling myself rather than parking it. The owner had already ruled "build it now" on the stronger version of this problem (a host is never told). The corrected premise makes the remaining work STRICTLY SMALLER than what was ruled, not different in kind, so building it is inside that ruling rather than beyond it. Stated here because the row asked for a re-take and did not get one.
  SHIPPED: the paid-price notice now calls `ticketSellerVerdict` and branches. Ready → "Sets a ticket price. Your payout account is ready, so ticket money lands in your bank." Not ready → the shared `NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT` sentence plus the /settings/billing link, which RETIRES the hand-written duplicate of that sentence so the buy path and the price control can no longer drift.
  THE THREADING PROBLEM WAS REAL AND THE ROW UNDER-STATED IT. The row said "three EventForm renderers"; there are two SERVER entry points (events/new/page.tsx via EventSpark, and events/[slug]/edit/page.tsx), and the harder half is that THE PAYEE IS NOT ALWAYS THE CALLER — a space-hosted event pays the space owner (ADR-819), and on create the scope is not picked until the host picks it. Passing the caller's own readiness would have been wrong on exactly the surfaces where a manager runs events for a space they do not own. So readiness is resolved PER PICKABLE SCOPE and published as a map keyed by a new pure `payoutScopeKey`, which normalises the three encodings the form's scope state holds so a map built on one page cannot silently miss on the other.
  COST, measured not estimated: ONE batched read on create (`getConnectReadyMap`, new in lib/billing/connect.ts, over the distinct payees, and it returns {} when payoutsLive() is false), and one `getConnectStatus` on edit where there is exactly one payee. No Stripe call on either path.
  ⚠️ NOTHING VISIBLE CHANGES IN PRODUCTION YET, said here so it is not re-discovered as a regression: zero profiles hold `charges_enabled && payouts_enabled` today because accounts.create is refused for the OWN-040 platform-profile reasons, so every host correctly still sees the setup line. The change earns out the moment that answer is fixed.
  🔵 AND IT SETTLES SCAN-502: those three exports are NOT dead and must never be swept. "No callers" proves a symbol is unreferenced, not that the behaviour is unbuilt — here someone had built it BESIDE the seam instead of through it, which leaves the export looking dead and the duplicate looking finished.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const path=require("path");const rd=f=>{try{return fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8")}catch{return null}};const h=(f,s)=>{const t=rd(f);return t!==null&&t.includes(s)};const r=(f,re)=>{const t=rd(f);return t!==null&&re.test(t)};const walk=d=>{let o=[];let es=[];try{es=fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true})}catch{return o}for(const e of es){const q=path.join(d,e.name);if(e.isDirectory())o=o.concat(walk(q));else if(e.name.endsWith(".tsx"))o.push(q)}return o};const F="app/(main)/events/new/event-form.tsx";process.exit(h(F,"ticketSellerVerdict({ payoutsReady: payoutsReadyByScope")&&!h(F,"To take the money you need a payout account")&&h("app/(main)/events/[slug]/edit/page.tsx","payoutsReadyByScope={payoutsReadyByScope}")&&h("app/(main)/events/event-spark.tsx","payoutsReadyByScope={payoutsReadyByScope}")&&h("app/(main)/events/new/page.tsx","getConnectReadyMap")&&h("lib/events/ticket-eligibility.ts","export function payoutScopeKey")?0:1)'
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE, not the title, in four independent ways. (1) The price control must BRANCH on the verdict, not merely mention payouts. (2) The hand-written duplicate sentence must be GONE — that negative is the half that proves the shared constant is actually the one rendering, and it is the only assertion here that a re-hand-rolling would trip. (3) The prop must reach BOTH server renderers plus the spark pass-through, or the notice is state-aware on some surfaces and not others, which is worse than uniformly state-blind. (4) The create page must resolve readiness per scope through the batched helper, since the payee is not always the caller (ADR-819). NO TEST RUNNER: lib/events/ticket-eligibility.test.ts pins the behaviour and runs in `pnpm test` on every PR; a probe that re-spawns vitest is what the LIVE-034 meta-guard forbids, and it correctly rejected the first version of this probe. 2026-09-07 (HYG-062): rewritten from a grep pipeline to a node -e body that reads the same files for the same strings, so the probe reports its own cost; verdict checked identical before and after the rewrite.

entries.title: Three natal-chart SQL helpers ship without a pinned search_path, repeating a fix the same function family already took

source.ref: general scan 2026-08-25, live Supabase security advisors

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 by reading the LIVE security advisors against scripts/maintenance/accepted-advisories.json rather than by reading the tree. Supabase returns 145 security lints; 142 are adjudicated by name or target (78 rls_enabled_no_policy, 60 security_definer_function_executable, 3 extension_in_public, 1 spatial_ref_sys). THREE ARE NOT: function_search_path_mutable on public.housing_safe_float, public.housing_aspect_score and public.housing_natal_compat, all created by 20270326000000_natal_chart_matching.sql (ADR-1138, the natal-chart work). `function_search_path_mutable` appears in NEITHER acceptedByName NOR acceptedByTarget, so the next weekly maintenance sweep surfaces all three as novel, unadjudicated findings.

WHY THIS IS A MISSED CONNECTION AND NOT JUST A LINT. The same function family already took this exact fix once. 20261133000000_housing_matching_v2.sql created housing_safe_date/housing_safe_int without a search_path, the advisor flagged them, and 20261134000000_housing_matching_v2_search_path.sql exists for no other purpose than to re-declare those two with `set search_path = public`. The new migration's own comment cites those functions as the pattern it is following ("same pattern as housing_safe_date/housing_safe_int") and then omits the one thing that dedicated migration was written to add.

SEVERITY IS LOW AND SHOULD BE STATED HONESTLY. All three are SECURITY INVOKER, not DEFINER, and the migration revokes EXECUTE from public, anon and authenticated by name (ADR-959), so no browser role can call them; they run only inside the SECURITY DEFINER match RPCs. Internal references are schema-qualified. So this is convention drift and advisor noise, not a live exposure -- but it is the kind that goes unadjudicated and then reads as coverage.

NOTHING IN THE REPO COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT. check:rls, check:grants and check:function-grants replay migrations for RLS and for grants; none of them looks at search_path. The advisor sweep that would have is weekly and advisory. The durable fix is a guard, not just a migration -- but the migration is the part that closes the finding.

THE FIX. One migration mirroring 20261134000000: re-declare the three with `set search_path = public`, bodies unchanged. Per docs/DATABASE.md the file and the prod apply travel together (ADR-1111) -- the file alone turns check:migrations red from the unapplied side, so ship the repo file and apply the DDL via MCP execute_sql plus an explicit ledger insert at the file's own version in the same sitting. Consider adding function_search_path_mutable to accepted-advisories.json ONLY if the owner decides the three should stay unpinned; the default is to pin them.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),p=require('path');const D='supabase/migrations';if(!fs.existsSync(D))process.exit(79);const DQ=String.fromCharCode(36,36);const files=fs.readdirSync(D).filter(f=>f.endsWith('.sql')).sort().map(f=>fs.readFileSync(p.join(D,f),'utf8').toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g,' '));if(files.length<400){console.error('read only '+files.length+' migration(s); a probe that scans nothing passes everything');process.exit(79)}const pinned=(n)=>{const needle='create or replace function public.'+n+'(';for(const s of files){let i=s.indexOf(needle);while(i!==-1){const e=s.indexOf(DQ,i);const head=e===-1?s.slice(i):s.slice(i,e);if(head.indexOf('set search_path')!==-1)return true;i=s.indexOf(needle,i+1);}}return false;};const control=['housing_safe_date','housing_safe_int'].filter(n=>!pinned(n));if(control.length){console.error('POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED: '+control.join(', ')+' are pinned by 20261134000000, but this detector cannot see it, so a negative result below would be meaningless');process.exit(1)}const missing=['housing_safe_float','housing_aspect_score','housing_natal_compat'].filter(n=>!pinned(n));if(missing.length){console.error('no migration pins search_path on: '+missing.join(', '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes:
Closed 2026-08-26, and the close is a RECOVERY rather than a fix, which is the part worth reading. Between this row being filed and being worked, the DDL was applied to production ahead of any repo file: the three helpers carried `search_path=public` live, while the only migration naming them (20270326000000) still did not pin them. That left ledger row 20270342000000 `natal_chart_helpers_take_the_search_path_pin` with NO repo file -- production running SQL the tree could not reproduce, and `check:migrations` red from the unapplied side (649 repo files vs 650 ledger rows).

The repair was to recover, not to re-author. `supabase/migrations/20270342000000_natal_chart_helpers_take_the_search_path_pin.sql` carries the statements pulled VERBATIM from the ledger's own `statements` column: md5 285a642176b0b53a60b301a709089e76, 2061 bytes, identical on both sides, so the tree and the applied schema are byte-identical rather than merely equivalent. Parity re-verified after: 650 repo files <=> 650 ledger rows, versions sha256 7b5f651b... and version+name sha256 acc30d35... matching on both sides.

Live confirmation, not inference: pg_proc now reports search_path=public on all three (housing_safe_float, housing_aspect_score, housing_natal_compat), and a census of the 155 non-extension public functions returns missing_pin=0 and definer_missing_pin=0 -- so the class is empty repo-wide, not merely quiet on these three. `function_search_path_mutable` consequently stays OUT of scripts/maintenance/accepted-advisories.json: there is nothing left to accept, and adding it would bank a class that is currently at zero.

The lesson this row keeps earning is the one ADR-1111 already states, and that this repo has now hit from BOTH directions in two days: the file and the apply travel together. Applied-before-merged turns every branch red; merged-before-applied turns main red; and applied-with-no-file-at-all is the only one of the three that a fresh environment silently fails to reproduce.

entries.title: No guard reads search_path, and the obvious one is wrong by ~47 false positives
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-26 while closing SCAN-520, which is the SECOND time this class has drifted: 20261134000000 exists solely to re-pin eight housing helpers after the advisor flagged them, and 20270326000000 then created three more without the pin while citing those very helpers as the pattern it was following. check:rls, check:grants and check:function-grants all replay supabase/migrations/, and NONE of them looks at search_path.
  🔴 THE OBVIOUS GUARD IS WRONG, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. A static pass that reads each `create [or replace] function public.x(...)` header and asserts `set search_path` reports FIFTY unpinned functions across 183. Production disagrees: set_updated_at, trg_increment_member_count, handle_new_auth_user, public_circle_by_id, get_my_hub_ids, is_blocked_between, mkt_growth, density_by_city, circle_momentum and member_engagement_stats were each checked in pg_proc and every one carries a pin. So the naive instrument is ~47 false positives out of 50, and the live advisor agrees with production, not with the static read: it reports zero.
  WHY THEY DIVERGE, AS FAR AS IT WAS TAKEN: pins do not only arrive on the create header. 20270101000000 pins through a DYNAMIC CATALOG LOOP (`execute format('alter function %s set search_path = public, private, pg_temp', f.sig)`) over a named helper list, which no static reader can see — check-function-grants.mjs already knows this shape and carries CATALOG_LOOP_PROOF for the grants half. That loop's named list does not cover all 47, so at least one more mechanism is in play (most likely later re-creations the throwaway scanner's header extraction missed). NOT RUN DOWN, and deliberately recorded as unfinished rather than guessed.
  ✅ WHAT A CORRECT GUARD LOOKS LIKE: the same stateful replay check-function-grants.mjs already does for ACLs — per-function state, create/replace/alter/drop events in file order, a catalog-loop escape hatch — with search_path as one more tracked attribute. That is why this is M and not the XS it looks like, and why bolting it onto SCAN-520 would have shipped a build-blocking gate measured against nothing. Its positive control is free: hold back 20270342000000 and the three natal-chart helpers must light up.
  BOUNDED BY A REAL NUMBER: production currently has 866 of 1021 public functions unpinned, but that headline is dominated by PostGIS — the advisor excludes extension-owned functions, and the guard must too, or it inherits the same ~47:3 noise ratio in a louder form.

── ⚠️ PREMISE RE-MEASURED 2026-09-07 AGAINST PRODUCTION, AND THE NUMBERS IMPROVE THE ROW RATHER THAN CLOSING IT.

Queried pg_proc directly, excluding extension-owned functions the way the advisor does:
    163 non-extension public functions, 163 PINNED, 0 UNPINNED.

Two things follow, and the second is the useful one.

1. THE ROW'S HEADLINE WAS DOMINATED BY POSTGIS EXACTLY AS IT SUSPECTED. "866 of 1021 unpinned" becomes ZERO of 163 once extension-owned functions are excluded, so the guard is not chasing a live gap - it is a RATCHET protecting a clean state. That lowers the urgency and raises the bar: a guard that reports anything at all today is reporting a false positive.

2. 🔴 AND THAT MAKES THE ORACLE FREE, WHICH THE ROW DID NOT KNOW. The row worried a naive instrument was "~47 false positives out of 50" and had no way to tell which were real. Production answers that completely: every one of the 50 is a false positive, because nothing is unpinned. So the guard can be validated ABSOLUTELY rather than by argument - replay the migrations, and the guard is correct if and only if it reports zero against a tree whose production truth is 163 of 163. Any name it emits is a bug in the guard.

⚪ A CAVEAT ON THE STATIC SIDE'S OWN NUMBERS: a second, cruder header scan run today reports 23 rather than 50, so the "50" is an artifact of one scanner's header extraction, not a stable count. Do not treat either number as the target. The target is zero, and the oracle is pg_proc.

WHAT REMAINS IS UNCHANGED and is still the M the row describes: search_path as one more tracked attribute on check-function-grants.mjs's stateful replay, with the same create/replace/alter/drop ordering and the same catalog-loop escape hatch (20270101000000 pins through execute format(...), which no static reader can see). The free positive control still stands: hold back 20270342000000 and the three natal-chart helpers must light up.

── CLOSED 2026-09-07. search_path is now a tracked attribute on check-function-grants.mjs's stateful replay, exactly as this row prescribed, and it is enforced through vitest (scripts/check-function-grants.test.ts), which the required test job runs.

🔴 THE ORACLE MADE THIS TRACTABLE, AND IT WAS FREE. Production carries 163 non-extension public functions and ALL 163 pin search_path, so the bar is absolute rather than argued: the arm is correct if and only if it reports NOTHING on this tree, and any name it prints is a parser bug until the catalog says otherwise. That turned a design problem into a measurement loop, and the loop found THREE parser bugs the row could not have predicted:

  129 false positives  a single character. Written (=|to)\b the detector matches TO and never =, because = and the space after it are both non-word characters and there is no boundary between them to match. Nearly every migration here spells it "= public".
    2 false positives  Postgres takes the attribute list on EITHER side of AS <body>, and this repo uses both spellings. A header-only reader calls the trailing form unpinned. trg_increment_reply_count and trg_decrement_reply_count are written that way.
   18 phantom-live      already solved: they are the RLS helpers moved to private by 20270101000000 through dynamic SQL, and RETIRED_BY_DYNAMIC_SQL already declares exactly those 18. The guard inherited the fix.

Final agreement with production is EXACT in both directions: 180 live in the replay, minus the 18 declared retired, is 162 - the oracle set, name for name - with zero unpinned.

⚠️ THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS NOT A GREP, and it is the reason the row was right to call it M. create or replace REWRITES the definition and proconfig comes from the NEW one, so a replace with no set clause UNPINS a function that was pinned. The ACL two lines away in the same switch is PRESERVED by a replace. A one-line static scan cannot model that; a stateful replay gets it for free.

CONTROLS. Six fixture arms, each testing both directions, plus the free positive control this row named: hold back 20270342000000 on the REAL tree and exactly its three natal-chart helpers light up. Three mutations proven red - restoring the regex bug (9 tests), reading only the header (5 tests), and preserving the pin across a replace (1 test) - and the real-tree control alone catches two of the three.

⚪ ONE ROW MOVED WITH IT: LIVE-020's probe builds a fixture to exercise the ACL arm, and that fixture did not pin, so the new arm failed it. Its fixture is pinned now. A probe measuring one arm has to satisfy every other arm or it stops measuring anything.

verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE in both directions, and carries its own positive control so it can never pass by being silent. Arm 1: the search_path arm reports NOTHING on the tree as it stands - the absolute bar, because production carried 163 of 163 pinned on 2026-09-07, so any name is a parser bug. Arm 2: holding back 20270342000000 - the migration that pinned three natal-chart helpers 20270326000000 had created unpinned - must flag exactly those three. An arm that only checked silence would pass on a guard that had been deleted.

entries.title: A PR whose pull_request event never fires can never be posted the required db-tests context, and no dispatch path exists

source.ref: general scan 2026-08-26, hit live on PR #2310

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-26 by hitting it. PR #2310 was opened after its branch had already been pushed, so no `pull_request` event ever fired for it: GitHub reported ZERO workflow runs of any kind on that head. Not red — never run, which on the PR page is visually identical to "waiting". `ci.yml` and `codeql.yml` were recoverable because both declare `workflow_dispatch`; a manual dispatch produced checks/lint/test/analyze green on the PR's own head SHA. `db-tests` is a REQUIRED context (ruleset 17640795) posted either by db-tests.yml — path-filtered to supabase/** and dispatchable — or, for PRs touching none of those paths, by db-tests-fallback.yml, which triggered ONLY on `pull_request` and declared no `workflow_dispatch`. So for a PR that (a) never fires a pull_request event and (b) touches no migration paths, the required context had no producer and no manual path, and `bypass_actors` is null so an admin could not force it either.

── CONFIRMED A SECOND TIME 2026-09-07, BY A THIRD ROUTE, and the third route is more common than the first. RETARGETING A PR'S BASE BRANCH FIRES NO `synchronize` EITHER. Three PRs of the audit stack (#2388, #2390, #2391) were retargeted from a stacked base onto main and sat with zero required contexts; the merge was refused with "5 of 6 required status checks are expected", and later "Required status check 'Vercel' is expected". A `workflow_dispatch` of ci.yml recovered checks/lint/test — exactly as the row predicted — but those dispatched runs do NOT satisfy the required contexts, and db-tests had no manual path at all. All three escaped the same way PR #2310 did: by needing a real push for an unrelated reason. A PR needing no such push would have been stuck. That is now three distinct routes to one deadlock (PR opened after push · base retargeted · path filter), which settles the "is this worth a per-workflow escape hatch" question the row left open.

── CLOSED 2026-09-07. db-tests-fallback.yml takes a `workflow_dispatch` with a required PR NUMBER input, and every decision is recomputed from the API for that PR rather than assumed from event context: its open state, its base branch, its CURRENT head SHA, and its changed-file list. The "runs on every PR, decides for itself whether the real gate ran, posts ONLY when it did not" property is preserved exactly.

🔴 THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS NOT TAKEN, as the row warned. A bare `workflow_dispatch:` has no PR context and therefore no changed-file list, so it could post a green `db-tests` having looked at nothing — the vacuous green this file's own header warns about — and stamp it over a PR that DID change migrations.

🔴 AND THE HEAD SHA IS READ FROM THE API RATHER THAN FROM `github.sha`, which is the subtle trap in the dispatch path. `github.sha` is the ref the workflow was dispatched on, not the PR's head; dispatching on a branch whose tip has moved would post the status onto a commit the PR does not point at, leaving the context absent where the merge looks for it — reproducing the very deadlock the file exists to break. A dispatch naming a closed or merged PR, a non-numeric input, or a PR not targeting main is refused rather than served.

⚪ THE UPSTREAM QUESTION THE ROW RAISED IS ANSWERED BY THE THIRD ROUTE. "Open the PR first, then push" would fix the 2026-08-26 shape and would NOT fix a base retarget, because retargeting happens long after the PR exists. A convention cannot cover an event GitHub simply does not emit, so the escape hatch is the durable answer rather than a workaround for a bad habit.

entries.title: RSVP closed at the event's START instead of its END, so a live event could not be joined
entries.detail: The event page computes isPast (has STARTED) and hasEnded (past ends_at), and its own comment says 'RSVP stays changeable until the event actually ENDS (not merely starts)'. Both answer branches gated on !isPast, so the whole RSVP surface vanished the moment an event began. entries.title: A draft squatted the canonical event slug, so a published event's shared link led to an unviewable draft

It went unnoticed because the visual half only runs when a preview resolves before the job reaches it. Recaptured on 2026-08-29 by an e2e-manual.yml dispatch with update_baselines ON and capture_shell OFF: 120 public PNGs moved, zero member-shell or /admin ones. The capture commit was pushed by GITHUB_TOKEN and produced exactly one check run, so the compare did NOT re-run on it - the proof is the next PR's pr-compare completing instead of timing out. ✅ THE PUBLIC HALF IS PROVEN, AND IT UNCOVERED A SECOND HALF (2026-08-31, PR #2322). pr-compare on #2322 COMPLETED in 11.1 minutes with 128 passing rather than timing out, which is exactly this row's stated close condition for the public surfaces. Those are stale for the SAME reason and were never recaptured: `git show 11d1ccb --name-only` is 120 files with ZERO matching app-(feed|settings|nearby|space-console) or app-admin, because that dispatch ran capture_shell OFF. The shell baselines date to 2026-08-24 (#2270) and 2026-08-25 (#2303); #2317 (eb087aa) landed 2026-08-26 and DID move the member shell — it deleted banner-measure.tsx, deleted announcement-banner's inline card, and rewired app-shell.tsx to mount the bar through a new `banner` slot. entries.title: The event RSVP bar hung 53px above the tab bar with the page scrolling through the gap
entries.detail:
Owner, off a phone capture of the Meld event page. The bar was pinned `bottom-[var(--tab-bar-clearance)]` — the bottom lane's TOP, which is the correct number for a NARROW FLOATING thing (a toast, a teaser pill) that cannot dodge the Zap catch or the chat tab sideways. This bar is `inset-x-0` and OPAQUE, so it has no sideways to dodge to and its underside is a window onto scrolling content rather than empty air. It therefore floated 53px clear of the tab bar with the page visible underneath.

FIXED as the distinction the lane was missing: a full-bleed bar takes the lane as PADDING, not as an OFFSET. Background at var(--tab-bar-h) (flush, no gap), content pushed past the new var(--lane-rise) token (no overlap), so the Zap catch and the chat tab ride ON the bar and both stay pressable. Neither half alone works — flush without padding re-opens the 2026-08-11 overlap on the page's primary conversion control, padded without flush is the gap. Recorded as SLOT 0c + rule 7 of the mobile stacking contract and pinned by three mutation-tested assertions in components/vera/dock-tab-clearance.test.ts.

── SUPERSEDED 2026-08-31: THE BAR IS GONE. The owner removed it outright — it duplicated the Join box the interior already renders (the SIDE column stacks FIRST on a phone, so the RSVP control is the first thing under the header) and cost the fixed bottom lane plus a `pb-24 lg:pb-0` reservation on every event page to say the same thing twice. The component, the template's `actionBar`/`hasActionBar` slot and that padding all went with it.

THE ROW STAYS DONE AND THE PROBE CHANGES SHAPE. The defect it records was real and the reasoning it produced outlived its occupant: SLOT 0c and rule 7 of the mobile stacking contract stand, because they explain why a full-bleed opaque bar takes the lane as PADDING and not as an offset — which the next such bar would otherwise rediscover from a phone capture, the way this file's three earlier entries each were. The probe now measures the consequence that is actually true today: the bar does not exist, and the rule that outlived it does.

entries.title: The event cover cropped 47% off the width of a poster, and its own title with it
entries.detail:
Owner: 'the text and graphics work on web but not on mobile.' The cover band was a fixed-height box with `object-cover`. The Meld poster is 1400x600 (2.33:1); the phone band was 380x306 (1.24:1) at a 412px viewport and this app's 17px root, so `object-cover` scaled by HEIGHT and cropped by WIDTH — 380 of 714 rendered pixels, i.e. 53% shown. The missing half contained both ends of the event's name; the capture reads 'Creating What's N', 'eld @ Roy', 'nity Coworking'.

MEASURED ACROSS ALL 24 DISTINCT PRODUCTION COVERS as the fraction of artwork AREA surviving: mobile median 81% / worst 53% (8 of 24 lose >25%); desktop median 36% / worst 24% (23 of 24 lose >25%). 13 of the 24 are 1:1 and 6 more are portrait, because Luma and Partiful both tell hosts to upload a square cover — so the app renders square-by-convention artwork inside a letterbox band and asks the crop to be kind.

FIXED for phones (components/media/poster-band.tsx): `object-contain` below sm over a blurred, scaled copy of the poster filling the letterbox, in a band one rung shorter (306 -> 221px at the standard tier). No stored dimensions needed, which is the point — sharp is budget-gated here (69/100 og-trace) and a render-time header fetch would add a blocking subrequest on a marquee page. The desktop half is LIVE-131.

The phone band CROPS again, and this row's fix still holds, because the band it crops in is a different shape: 412x221 full bleed (1.86:1) rather than the 380x306 (1.24:1) box photographed here. `object-cover` scales to cover the shorter axis, so at 1.86:1 it scales by WIDTH for any source narrower than that - 19 of the 24 covers are square or portrait, and they now reach both edges whole and lose height instead, which is the axis the focal picker aims.
