verify.cmd: node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('scripts/check-canon.mjs','utf8');process.exit(s.includes('EXTRA_MEMBER_MD')&&/EXTRA_MEMBER_MD = \\[[^\\]]*'docs\\/CHANGELOG.md'/.test(s)&&s.includes('...mfiles') === false&&/for \\(const file of \\[\\.\\.\\.mdFiles\\(ROOT\\), \\.\\.\\.EXTRA_MEMBER_MD\\]\\)/.test(s)?0:1)"
verify.note: Measures the consequence: the canon guard's content arm actually iterates EXTRA_MEMBER_MD alongside content/, and that list still names docs/CHANGELOG.md. Emptying the list or reverting the loop fails. `node scripts/check-canon.mjs` is the enforcing arm and fails on any violation the widened scope now sees.

entries.title: Eight segmented controls and menus nested a 14px radius inside a 24px card, the same mismatch the RSVP picker had
entries.detail:
Found while fixing the RSVP picker's corners. The repo's radius ladder is authored BY ROLE (docs/DESIGN.md: control = 14px, card = 24px), which is right for siblings and wrong for NESTING — two corners share a centre only when the inner radius is the outer minus the gap. A `rounded-control` (14px) child inside a `rounded-card` (24px) box with `p-1` between them reads 5.75px too square, because `p-1` is 4.25px at this app's 17px root (--density-root 106.25%).

`--radius-control-nested` (app/globals.css, `calc(var(--radius-card) - 0.25rem)` so it tracks both the skin's radius and the generation's density) now carries it, and eight surfaces use it: components/events/rsvp-controls.tsx, components/quest/board-controls.tsx (scope + track), app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/settings/airwaves/airwaves-console.tsx, app/(main)/connections/new/creator.tsx, app/(main)/events/events-sort.tsx, components/spaces/spaces-sort.tsx, components/ui/facet-dropdown.tsx and components/ui/underline-tabs.tsx.

⚠️ THE ROW'S FIRST PROBE WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and it is the useful part of this entry. It was `grep-absent 'rounded-control px-3 py-1.5'` over three files — a string that also matches three SIBLING controls (a dropdown's trigger button, the leaderboard's hide-me toggle) that are correct at 14px, so satisfying the probe would have meant breaking them, while the four menu surfaces it named none of stayed broken. Nesting is the claim, so nesting is what is now measured: scripts/check-nested-radius.mjs walks app/ and components/ for a container carrying both `rounded-card` and `p-1` with a bare `rounded-control` in its subtree.

🔴 That detector printed a clean ✓ on its first run and was more than half blind: a mutation sweep reintroducing the defect at each of the 15 fixed sites showed EIGHT walking past it (a multi-line JSX tag closes its own `>` at the opening tag's indent, so the subtree window ended before any child). Fixed, plus a second arm that follows a capitalised child into a same-file helper component. The sweep is now scripts/check-nested-radius.test.ts (18 tests), and the guard is registered in VITEST_ENFORCED so vitest auto-discovery keeps it running rather than an array in ci.yml.

verify.cmd: node scripts/check-nested-radius.mjs
verify.note: Fails when a bare `rounded-control` appears inside a `rounded-card` + `p-1` container. A helper imported from ANOTHER module is the declared blind spot (resolveLocalComponent says so in its own doc comment); scripts/check-nested-radius.test.ts drives every arm against fixtures that must fail, and asserts a floor on the denominator so an empty walk cannot read as compliance.

entries.title: `truncate` on an inline <Link> drops the ellipsis and keeps white-space:nowrap (found while chasing the Space console overflow, which it does NOT fix)
entries.detail:
🔴 AMENDED 2026-09-01, BEFORE MERGE: this row was written claiming the defect CAUSED the /spaces/<slug>/manage overflow. It does not. With the fix live on #2328's preview the offending box still measures `x 17→447, width 430` at 320/360/390px — identical to the pre-fix reading. The overflow is unfixed and is now HYG-037. What this row still closes is the defect itself, which is real: on a non-replaced inline box `overflow`/`text-overflow` do not apply, so an inline <a class="truncate"> gets no ellipsis and keeps nowrap. Six were fixed and a guard prevents more. Read the rest as the mechanism, not the diagnosis.

Caught by test/e2e/overflow.spec.ts, not by review: /spaces/<slug>/manage ran 57px past a 390px viewport in TWO <section>s at once, on a shell root carrying overflow-x-clip — so nothing scrolled and the dashboard was cut off.

Both sections reported the SAME width because they are the two items of one single-column grid, and a grid track is sized by the widest item's min-content. Tailwind's `truncate` is overflow:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis + white-space:nowrap; the first two do NOT apply to a non-replaced inline box, and <Link> renders an inline <a>. So two thirds evaporated and the harmful third survived: nowrap made the element's min-content the full title string, which is the floor no grid track can shrink below.

`min-w-0 flex-1` on the wrapper is why this hides in plain sight — it looks like shrinking is handled, and it is, for the WRAPPER. `flex-1` is `flex: 1 1 0%` on an ITEM; its children stay inline.

Six real defects fixed: components/spaces/dashboard/space-dashboard.tsx, components/spaces/checkin-roster.tsx, components/spaces/membership-event-access.tsx, components/events/event-share-approvals.tsx, components/events/placement-approvals.tsx, components/widgets/quest/quest-leaderboard.tsx.

🔴 THE FIRST GUARD WAS WRONG THREE TIMES AND POINTED AWAY FROM THE BUG. Resolving each link's parent by indentation picked a SIBLING in dock-chat.tsx and skipped an inline-flex wrapper in calendar-repeats-strip.tsx (two false positives), and an earlier pass read `min-w-0 flex-1` as a flex CONTAINER — which is exactly the wrapper the real defect lives in, so the audit reported the six broken files as fine. The shipped rule is coarser and unfoolable: a <Link> with `truncate` must carry an explicit display class. It over-requires by 15 links whose flex parent already blockifies them (CSS Display §2.7), and an explicit `block` there is a no-op.

verify.cmd: node scripts/check-link-truncate.mjs
verify.note: Fails when any <Link> whose className carries `truncate` lacks a display class. A CLI rather than a vitest run because LIVE-034 forbids a backlog probe from spawning a test runner — and it caught this row doing exactly that. scripts/check-link-truncate.test.ts is the enforcing arm: it imports this same detector and drives it against fixtures that must fail, including flex-1 / flex-col / flex-wrap, the three tokens whose misreading caused the original wrong answer, plus a floor on the denominator.

entries.title: The Space console is cut off 57px past a 390px phone, and the cause is NOT the truncate defect that was blamed for it
entries.detail:
test/e2e/overflow.spec.ts, /spaces//manage, FAILING at all three widths the gate drives: 320px -> not reported separately (same box) 360px -> 87px past 390px -> 57px past ·
x 17→447, width 430, class: (none), text 'Latest activityOpen ResonanceLead captured…' ·
x 17→447, width 430, class: (none), text 'Coming upBookingsMeld - Community Cowork…' The shell root carries overflow-x-clip, so this does not scroll — it is amputated on a phone. 🔴 WHAT IS RULED OUT. HYG-036 (inline ) was blamed and is NOT the cause: with that fix live on #2328's preview the box measures x 17→447, width 430 — byte-identical to the pre-fix reading. Also ruled out by reading the source: no fixed/min/max width anywhere in components/spaces/dashboard/space-dashboard.tsx, components/ui/section-header.tsx or components/ui/empty-state.tsx; ActivityRow and the Upcoming row both already use `min-w-0 flex-1` with a truncating block child. WHAT THE NUMBER SAYS. 430px is CONSTANT across 360 and 390 viewports and the box starts at x=17 (the shell's one px-4 gutter at this app's 17px root). The parent `grid gap-8 lg:grid-cols-2` is NOT reported, and the spec reports only the outermost offender — so the grid container is within bounds and its single auto track is being sized to a descendant's min-content of 430px, which the items then inherit. That is why BOTH sections read the same width: one of them is the widener and the other is along for the ride. NEXT STEP, and it is a tooling step not a guess: the gate names only the outermost box, which is exactly the box that is NOT the cause here. Either teach overflow.spec.ts to also print the deepest descendant whose min-content matches the track, or read error-context.md out of the playwright-report artifact (run 33452854458, artifact 9780958772) which carries the DOM. Three rounds of source reading did not find it; stop reading and measure. ── 🔎 DIAGNOSED 2026-09-01, AND THE FIX IS APPLIED BUT NOT YET MEASURED. Cause: the two
s at space-dashboard.tsx:191 and :248 are GRID ITEMS with no class, and below `lg` the container at :72 (`grid gap-8 lg:grid-cols-2`) declares no grid-template-columns at all - so there is one IMPLICIT column, `minmax(auto, auto)`. A grid item defaults to `min-width: auto`, which contributes its content-based minimum, and the rows inside carry `truncate`, whose `white-space: nowrap` makes min-content the WHOLE string. The track is therefore sized by the longest event title, not by the phone. THE ARITHMETIC MATCHES ALL THREE RECORDED NUMBERS (1rem = 17px): shell `px-4` x2 leaves a 356px content column starting at x=17 (matches 'x 17'); li `px-4` 34 + `w-7` icon 29.75 + `gap-3` 12.75 = 76.5 of fixed chrome, so the longest nowrap string is 430 - 76.5 = 353.5px ~ 48 characters at --text-body-sm, which is the length of the observed 'Meld - Community Cowork...' title. Track 430 > 356 available, so both items stretch to 430 and the right edge is 17 + 430 = 447 (matches). 447 - 390 = 57 and 447 - 360 = 87, both recorded. 🔴 AND IT IS THE ONLY THEORY THAT PREDICTS THE BYTE-IDENTICAL RE-MEASUREMENT, which is what makes it better than the withdrawn one. Making the `block` (HYG-036) restored overflow:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis - the VISUAL ellipsis - but did not touch white-space:nowrap, which is the only one of the three that participates in intrinsic sizing. And the activity row's widener was always a

, already a block, so its min-content never moved at all. lg:grid-cols-2 was never implicated: Tailwind emits `repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))`, which already carries the floor. FIX APPLIED: `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)]` at the BASE breakpoint on :72 - at the track rather than as `min-w-0` on today's two children, so a third section added later inherits the floor. ⚠️ STAYS OPEN. The diagnosis is static reasoning plus arithmetic; nothing has re-measured the page. This row has already carried one confidently-wrong attribution and the correction cost more than the bug, so it closes on a MEASURED overflow run and not before. Two one-line browser probes settle it in seconds if someone has the preview open: setting `min-width:0` on `main section`, or `white-space:normal` on `.truncate`, should each snap the sections from 430 to 356. ⚪ THE LINE NUMBERS IN THIS ROW ARE PRE-FIX AND WILL MISLEAD A MEASURER. The row's own applied fix added a 7-line explanatory comment above the grid, so in the current tree the container is space-dashboard.tsx:79 (was :72) and the two sections are :198 / :255 (were :191 / :248). A row that ends 'stop reading and measure' should not send the measurer to the wrong lines. ── ✅ MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-09-01 06:00Z. The row said "stop reading and measure"; this is the measurement. `e2e (manual)` run 33474947762, dispatched against https://frequencylocal.com on main at 639859398 with capture_shell ON and BOTH capture flags OFF, so it measured and committed nothing. All three cases RAN and PASSED — the distinction this row exists to insist on, because a green job with the cases skipped is exactly what a false close looks like: ✓ 269 overflow › shell › /spaces/danieltyack/manage fits 320px @overflow @shell (6.9s) ✓ 270 overflow › shell › /spaces/danieltyack/manage fits 360px @overflow @shell (23.9s) ✓ 271 overflow › shell › /spaces/danieltyack/manage fits 390px @overflow @shell (6.4s) 166 passed, 0 failed, 112 skipped (the theme-matrix contrast variants, not this gate). The session minted, and the summary reads 'App shell covered: 4/4 surfaces, 24/40 checks'. SO THE DIAGNOSIS HELD. `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)]` at the BASE breakpoint was the fix: a grid item defaults to min-width:auto, the rows inside carry `truncate` whose white-space:nowrap makes min-content the whole string, and the single implicit track was therefore sized by the longest event title rather than by the phone. The 447px right edge on a 390px viewport is now within bounds at all three widths. This row's arithmetic predicted 430 and 57/87px, and the re-measurement agrees by passing. ⚠️ AND THE ROW'S OWN BLOCKER HAD EXPIRED — ADR-1082's lesson for the third time. This sat OPEN needing 'a measurement' while `e2e-manual.yml`, a dispatch-only maintainer workflow built for exactly this, was one tool call away. The row is not at fault for being cautious after carrying a wrong attribution; it is at fault for never re-testing whether looking was actually hard.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-01 06:00Z: e2e (manual) run 33474947762 against https://frequencylocal.com (main @ 639859398), capture_shell=true, update_baselines=false, update_a11y=false. The three `/spaces/danieltyack/manage fits {320,360,390}px @overflow @shell` cases each RAN and PASSED (job 99752149997, cases 269/270/271); 166 passed / 0 failed. Pre-fix the same cases measured <section> x 17→447, width 430 — 57px past 390 and 87px past 360 (PR #2328, job 99686402855). Fix: grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)] at the base breakpoint in components/spaces/dashboard/space-dashboard.tsx.

entries.title: Two ledgers still pointed at files that had been deleted, and one of them would have misdirected an operator
entries.detail:
Found by sweeping every committed baseline/ledger for entries whose target no longer exists. Two real ones, both left behind by a change that removed the target and not the pointer.

1. scripts/admin-client-baseline.txt named lib/beta/referral-contest.ts. SCAN-510 deleted that file (423 lines) on the owner's ruling that there is no beta referral contest; the RLS-bypass ratchet's baseline kept the line. Consequence was small but real and self-reported: check:admin-client printed a standing '1 baseline entry no longer imports it - shrink the baseline' advisory on every run, which is one more line of routine noise on a gate whose whole job is that a NEW adopter stands out. Now 742 importers against a 742 baseline, exact.

2. scripts/store-shelf.json carried quarantineProposal = 'docs/proposals/LIVE-013-cosmetic-fulfillment.sql', and the header of scripts/check-cosmetic-renders.mjs named the same path in prose. #2153 applied those proposals, promoted that SQL into a real migration (20270312000000_store_cosmetic_fulfillment.sql) and deleted docs/proposals/ entirely. THIS ONE IS AN OPERATOR-FACING DEFECT, not just staleness: the quarantine arm's message reads 'Clear them by applying ${quarantineProposal}', so had a SKU ever been quarantined the guard would have told an operator to apply a file that has not existed for weeks, when the remedy had in fact already shipped. It has not fired because quarantine is [] today, which is exactly why it survived - a signpost on a branch nobody walks rots unobserved.

The key is removed rather than repointed: there is no pending SQL to name, and the message already carried a `?? 'the proposal SQL'` fallback for that case. The comment now records where the SQL went, so the next reader is not sent looking for a deleted directory.

NOT A FINDING, checked and dropped: check:cosmetic-renders appears in no workflow, which looks like the exact violation scripts/guard-wiring.test.ts exists to catch. It is not - that guard's VITEST_ENFORCED map records scripts/check-cosmetic-renders.test.ts as the enforcing arm, which vitest auto-discovers. All 12 check:* scripts absent from the workflows are accounted for the same way or by the documented UNWIRED list.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const dead=[];const base=fs.readFileSync('scripts/admin-client-baseline.txt','utf8').split('\\n').map(l=>l.trim()).filter(l=>l&&!l.startsWith('#'));if(base.length<500)process.exit(1);for(const f of base)if(!fs.existsSync(f))dead.push('admin-client-baseline:'+f);for(const j of ['scripts/store-shelf.json','scripts/stored-block-types.json']){const t=fs.readFileSync(j,'utf8');for(const m of t.matchAll(/\"(docs\\/proposals\\/[^\"]+)\"/g))dead.push(j+':'+m[1])}process.exit(dead.length?1:0)"
verify.note:
Sweeps the ledgers for entries whose target is gone, rather than reconstructing one old sentence. Also asserts a FLOOR on the baseline (>=500 entries), so an emptied file cannot pass as 'nothing dangling'.

🔴 THE PREVIOUS PROBE ASSERTED THE ABSENCE OF ONE EXACT PHRASE - the pre-fix header text, verbatim. Re-adding the same dead path in any other wording passed. It also swept exactly ONE ledger while the row's premise is 'every committed baseline/ledger', and `dangling.length === 0` was satisfied by an EMPTY baseline file.

entries.title: Twenty-one tree walkers asked the filesystem twice, and the row's own first probe could only see twelve of them
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-01 by CodeQL, on the way in. #2337 added scripts/check-metadata-images.test.ts with the walker idiom this repo uses everywhere:

    if (statSync(full).isDirectory()) walk(full)
    else readFileSync(full, 'utf8')

CodeQL raised TWO HIGH-SEVERITY js/file-system-race alerts on that one file. The path is resolved once to ask whether it is a directory and a second time to open it, and nothing holds the answer still between the two. In a repo scanner the exploitable risk is near zero; the cost that is not near zero is a guard file that trips the security scanner, because a guard nobody trusts is a guard that gets routed around (ADR-970, again).

THE FIX, already applied to that one file: readdirSync(d, {withFileTypes: true}) returns the entry TYPE from the same syscall that returned the name. There is no window because there is no second question. Both of that file's walks now share one helper, which also repaired a second defect - the corpus-floor test had its own duplicate walker, so it was a floor for a walk the detector did not use.

WHAT THIS ROW CARRIES is the other twelve, none of which are fixed:
  scripts/check-detached-client-methods.test.ts, scripts/check-module-reachability.mjs,
  scripts/check-client-server-boundary.mjs, scripts/check-event-hero-parity.test.ts,
  scripts/build-fanout.test.ts, scripts/check-docs-links.mjs, scripts/check-phantom-classes.mjs,
  scripts/check-shell-weight.mjs, scripts/visual-surface-census.mjs, scripts/sweep-type-roles-2a.mjs,
  lib/theme/eyebrow-role.test.ts, lib/astrology/chart.test.ts

WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A GREEN CI RUN: CodeQL only alerts on files a PR CHANGED. Every one of these is silent today and fails the next PR that touches it - which will be a PR about something else, whose author has no idea why a walker they did not write is now a high-severity security finding. That is the shape this backlog exists to make visible rather than to discover twelve more times.

NOT SWEPT INSIDE THE CI FIX ON PURPOSE. A twelve-file mechanical change riding inside a one-file CI fix is the pattern docs/DEPLOY-SAFETY.md was written about. It wants its own [sweep] PR, and each file wants its symlink behaviour checked the way the first one did: Dirent.isDirectory() is FALSE for a symlink to a directory where statSync().isDirectory() was true, so any walker over a tree that contains symlinks changes what it covers. app/ has none; the other roots are unverified.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-01. All of them converted to readdirSync withFileTypes, plus a gate so the shape cannot return: scripts/check-walker-dirents.test.ts runs on every PR, and its detector lives in scripts/walker-dirents.mjs, imported by BOTH the gate and this row's probe so the two can never drift. Reading: 0 offenders across 1,976 files in scripts/ + lib/.

🔴 THE COUNT IN THIS ROW WAS WRONG WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN, AND THE ROW SAYS SO RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXING IT. It said TWELVE. The true number is TWENTY-ONE. The row's first probe was a regex, and it under-counted twice over — the second under-count only surfaced while doing the sweep the row asked for:
  1. `statSync\([^)]*\)\.isDirectory\(\)` cannot cross a nested paren, so `statSync(join(ROOT, rel)).isDirectory()` in check-docs-links.mjs was invisible. Caught the same day the row was written, and the row already recorded it.
  2. IT MISSED THE VARIABLE FORM ENTIRELY. Seven walkers write `let s; try { s = statSync(p) } catch { continue }` and then `if (s.isDirectory())` — the same check-then-use across two statements instead of one. check-canon.mjs (twice), check-labels.mjs, check-a11y-names.mjs, check-collective.mjs, check-crm-parity.mjs, check-admin-client.mjs and maintenance/dead-exports.mjs. A line-shaped probe cannot see a two-line shape.
  3. And two more recurse instead of looping — check-backlog.mjs and marketing-figures.test.ts stat their ARGUMENT and readdir the children, so the stat on a readdir-produced path happens in the NEXT call. Neither probe form would have found those.

SO THE INVARIANT IS AST-SHAPED AND FUNCTION-SCOPED: no function may contain both a bare readdirSync (one without withFileTypes) and a statSync. With the dirents in hand the type is already known, so a statSync beside them is the defect by definition — whatever syntax it is written in. ⚪ FUNCTION scope rather than FILE scope is load-bearing: check-backlog.mjs legitimately stats a CALLER-NAMED root that may be a file or a directory, then walks with dirents from a nested function. One stat on a path this repo names is not a race; a stat on a path readdir just handed you is.

⚠️ THE SWEEP BROKE TWO GUARDS AND THE BEFORE/AFTER COMPARISON IS WHAT CAUGHT IT. check-labels.mjs and check-a11y-names.mjs hold their readdirSync a few lines above the loop; converting the loop body to entry.name without converting the readdirSync made both throw ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE on the first directory. A mechanical sweep across 21 files is exactly where that happens, which is why every affected guard was run BEFORE and AFTER and diffed: all twelve outputs are byte-identical, corpus counts included (618 labels across 1,868 files; 3,576 accessible names across 1,868 files; the visual-surface census unchanged). Identical output is the claim — not that the guards still pass.

⚪ SYMLINKS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. Dirent.isDirectory() is FALSE for a symlink to a directory where statSync().isDirectory() was true, so the conversion is only behaviour-preserving in a tree without them. `find . -type l` (excluding node_modules and .git) returns nothing, so every walked root here is identical.

FIVE CONTROLS IN THE GATE, and the mutation: reverting check-canon.mjs's mdFiles to the variable form turns the gate RED naming `scripts/check-canon.mjs:156`, and the probe exits 1 with the same line. The gate also pins the inline form, the nested-paren form, the variable form, a clean withFileTypes walk, and the caller-named-root exemption.

verify.cmd: node scripts/walker-dirents.mjs
verify.note:
Measures the CONSEQUENCE directly: exits 1 and NAMES every function in scripts/ + lib/ that pairs a bare readdirSync with a statSync. It shares its detector with the PR gate (scripts/check-walker-dirents.test.ts) via scripts/walker-dirents.mjs, so probe and gate cannot disagree. Reading: 0 offenders across 1,976 files. Spawns no test runner (LIVE-034).

🔴 THIS REPLACES A REGEX THAT UNDER-COUNTED BY NINE. The first version matched only `statSync(...).isDirectory()` on one line: it could not cross a nested paren, and it could not see the two-statement variable form at all. It reported twelve walkers where there were twenty-one, and it would have gone green on a sweep that left nine behind — the exact shape-not-truth failure a probe exists to prevent, committed by the probe.

⚪ THE PROBE HAS A FAST PATH AND THE GATE DOES NOT, ON PURPOSE. `import typescript` costs 525ms against 176ms for the actual work, and scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts runs every probe TWICE (with and without ripgrep on PATH) inside a 60s timeout it already fills to 78% on an idle machine — so half a second of compiler import is not free. The probe therefore skips files a cheap regex rules out (a strict SUPERSET of the AST rule: an offender needs a bare readdirSync and a statSync in one FUNCTION, which implies both in the FILE), and in the clean state never loads the compiler at all: 150ms, down from 820ms. The GATE takes no such shortcut — it parses every file carrying both tokens — so a bug in that regex can only slow the probe, never blind the arm that enforces. A test asserts the two arms return the same findings on the real tree, and blinding the pre-filter was watched turn the probe GREEN ON A DIRTY TREE while that test went red. That is the failure the split exists to make visible.

entries.title: Two tests in the backlog contract now run against timeouts they have outgrown, because 224 probes run serially
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-01 by hitting it. `scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts > gives identical results with and without ripgrep on PATH` runs EVERY backlog probe twice, once with ripgrep on PATH and once without. Measured alone on an idle machine it takes 46.7s against its own 60s timeout — 78%. Under full-suite contention it exceeded 60s and failed the run.

WHAT TRIGGERED IT: adding HYG-041's probe, which imported the TypeScript compiler (525ms) and so cost ~1.7s per pass, ~3.4s doubled. That probe was then made 5x cheaper (150ms, by not loading the compiler in the clean state) and the failure went away — but THE HEADROOM PROBLEM IS NOT FIXED, only postponed. 226 probes now run twice inside one 60s budget, and every probe added from here narrows it further. The next person to add a probe will hit this, and the failure will look like their probe rather than like the budget.

⚠️ AND THE FAILURE MODE IS THE WORST KIND: a TIMEOUT, not an assertion. It says nothing about what is slow, it appears only under load so it does not reproduce when re-run alone, and it reads exactly like a flake — which this repo's own rules correctly say is never a root cause. Someone will re-run it, watch it pass, and move on.

WHAT THE FIX PROBABLY IS (not decided, hence open): the test's value is proving the probe engine does not depend on ambient ripgrep. That does not obviously require running all 226 probes twice — the probes that could differ are the ones that shell out to a search tool, and those are identifiable. Narrowing the second pass to that set would keep the guarantee and drop most of the cost. The alternative — raising the timeout — buys time and hides the trend, which is what this backlog exists to make visible.

A CPU BUDGET ALREADY EXISTS BESIDE THE TIMEOUT and it is the healthier half: guardCpuMs=26,860 is printed on every run and is a NUMBER someone can watch. The timeout is a cliff.

⚪ THE COMMENT ABOVE THE TEST WAS ALSO STALE BY A FACTOR OF THREE AND IS CORRECTED IN THE SAME PASS. It said '~13s of real work, 60s of budget — headroom for a loaded runner', measured 2026-08-17 when the guard cost ~6s a pass. It now costs 23.4s a pass. A comment that states a measurement is a claim with an expiry date, and this one had quietly gone from 'plenty of room' to 'four seconds of contention away from red' without anyone re-reading it.

🔴 A SECOND TEST HIT THE WALL THE SAME DAY, WITH NO PROBE ADDED. `the real tree > satisfies both contracts` timed out at the DEFAULT 30s during a full-suite run. It runs check:backlog + check:one-list, measured 2026-09-01 at 23.66s + 0.11s = 23.8s — 79% of the default, the same fraction as the ripgrep case against its 60s. Nothing was added to probe cost in that change (it was a docs correction plus one code comment), so this is the budget, not a regression.

Two tests, both at ~79% of their limit, both failing only under contention: that is not two flakes, it is one cause. THE CAUSE IS THE SERIAL RUNNER — scripts/check-backlog.mjs walks 224 probes in a `for` loop of spawnSync, and the ripgrep case runs that whole set twice.

⚪ WHAT WAS DONE NOW, AND WHAT WAS NOT. `satisfies both contracts` was given an EXPLICIT 90s budget with the measurement recorded beside it, because the 30s it had was never a decision — it was vitest's default, which this test quietly outgrew. That makes the failure legible; it does not fix it, and this row stays open saying so. THE REAL FIX IS PARALLELISM: the probes are independent child processes that only read the tree, exactly like the 24 contract guards in ci.yml, which were already converted from a serial loop to a capped-concurrency pool for this same reason ("Run wall clock was the SUM of 26 guards; it is now bounded by the slowest single guard"). The same treatment here would cut ~24s to a few seconds and retire both timeouts. It was NOT attempted in the same change as a docs correction: check-backlog.mjs is the gate the whole backlog depends on, its runner is fully synchronous top to bottom, and its output ordering and cost accounting both key off that loop. That is its own change, with its own before/after comparison.

🔴 THE FIX THIS ROW NAMED IS REFUTED — BY MEASUREMENT, NOT ARGUMENT (ADR-1190). The paragraph above says "THE REAL FIX IS PARALLELISM". It is not. Per-probe CPU is a delta of cutime+cstime from /proc/self/stat — the kernel's cumulative CPU of REAPED CHILDREN, which is PROCESS-WIDE. Serially that attributes exactly, because one child is reaped per window. In a pool a probe is charged for whatever else was reaped inside its window. Demonstrated 2026-09-01: a probe truly costing ~50ms of CPU was attributed 3,780ms because an expensive sibling completed during its window — off by ~75x — and the total double-counted.

ADR-1107 built THREE assertions on that number and the pool retires all three silently: the 4,500ms per-probe ceiling starts firing on innocent rows AND NAMES THE WRONG ONE; the BASE + 180ms x n total breaches spuriously; and the self-report stops being a second view of the same quantity as the external reading. The per-probe ceiling is the signal the gate exists for (LIVE-034, nine rows converted). A change that makes it accuse the wrong row is worse than the 24 seconds it saves.

The demonstration is committed as scripts/maintenance/probe-cpu-attribution-demo.mjs, runnable, because this is precisely the claim the next reader of that serial loop will want to re-litigate and a paragraph cannot be re-run.

⚠️ AND THE REFUTED FIX WAS MINE, QUEUED AS THE NEXT TASK BEFORE I READ THE CODE IT WOULD CHANGE. "Independent child processes that only read the tree" was true and irrelevant: the constraint was never the work, it was the measurement, and two of the three assertions sit forty lines from the loop.

🔵 NOW BLOCKED ON AN OWNER DECISION, deliberately not taken here, because it changes a gate whose constants came from paired CI/local readings:
  (a) KEEP THE SERIAL RUNNER and set both budgets deliberately. Already half-done: `satisfies both contracts` has an explicit 90s against 23.8s of work, and the ripgrep-parity case has 60s against 46.7s. Cheap, honest, nothing about the metric changes. The cost is that ~24s stays ~24s and both budgets need re-reading as n grows.
  (b) HAVE EACH `node -e` PROBE REPORT ITS OWN process.cpuUsage() ON EXIT. Attribution then survives any amount of parallelism because it no longer comes from the parent. This is the real solution — and it changes how a measured gate measures, and does not cover cmd probes that are not node, so the ceiling would go blind on exactly the probes most likely to be expensive.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-06 BY OPTION (a), WHICH IS THIS ROW'S OWN STATED CLOSE CONDITION: "the timeout was deliberately widened with the reason recorded". THE CLIFF WAS REACHED, by the person this row predicted would reach it: the backlog audit of 2026-09-06 added 16 probes and the ripgrep-parity case went red. THEN THE MEASUREMENT CORRECTED THE STORY, which is why it is recorded rather than assumed. On the tree BEFORE that audit added anything, at 371 probes, one guard run took 33.6s and 34.0s wall on a 4-core container at load 0.90 — so the case's two runs already needed ~67s against its 60s budget, and it had ALREADY timed out at 60.4s. The audit's probes cost ~1.4s per pass, ~2.8s doubled: they widened a gap they did not open, and blaming the newest probe is exactly the misattribution this row was filed to prevent. The budget is now 150s against ~68s of measured work, set the way the sibling case's 90s was, with the numbers in the comment beside it.

⚪ WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, said plainly so a raised number is not mistaken for a fix: the probes still run serially, attribution still comes from the parent, and both budgets still need re-reading as n grows. That is option (b), and it is now HYG-062. The owner decision this row was blocked on is not erased by taking the reversible half of it; it is narrowed to whether (b) is worth building.

verify.cmd: node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts','utf8');const m=s.match(/gives identical results with and without ripgrep on PATH[^\n]*timeout:\s*([0-9_]+)/);if(!m){console.error('could not read the timeout on the ripgrep-parity case');process.exit(1)}const ms=Number(m[1].replace(/_/g,''));console.log('ripgrep-parity timeout: '+ms+'ms');process.exit(ms>60000?0:1)"
verify.note:
Measures the CONSEQUENCE the row asks for and nothing else: the row is about HEADROOM, so it closes only when the ripgrep-parity case no longer runs against a 60s cliff — either because the second pass was narrowed and the budget raised to match, or because the timeout was deliberately widened with the reason recorded. It exits 1 today (the timeout is exactly 60000ms), so the row is correctly open.

⚪ IT DOES NOT TIME THE TEST. A probe that ran the suite to measure 46.7s would spawn a test runner (LIVE-034 forbids it), take three quarters of a minute on every backlog run, and be the flakiest row in the file — measuring the very contention it is reporting.

⚠️ THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS PROBE READ THE NUMBER WRONG and printed 'ripgrep-parity timeout: 60ms'. The source says `{ timeout: 60_000 }` and the pattern was `(\d+)`, which stops at the numeric separator. It still exited 1 — the right answer for the wrong reason, which is the kind that survives review. Now `([0-9_]+)` with the separators stripped.

entries.title: A plan grant overrides a hand revoke, so CRM cannot be subtracted from a paid Space

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
spaceEntitlements (lib/spaces/entitlements.ts) reads the union of the TOP-LEVEL manual grants and the reserved `billing` namespace, and the union is written `if (granted) out[key] = true`. That is one-directional: a billing `true` can add a key, but a top-level `false` can never remove one.

For the three keys whose FUNCTION key and ENTITLEMENT key are the same string — `crm`, `email`, `program` — this means an operator cannot turn the tool off on any Business+ Space. Setting `{ crm: false }` by hand is silently overridden by `billing.crm: true` on the next read. The partition comment above the function describes the intended behaviour correctly ("an add-on toggling OFF removes only what the plan granted and never nukes a hand-grant") but the code only implements half of it: it protects a manual grant from the resolver, and does not protect a manual REVOKE from a plan.

This is the exact control surface a per-operator toolset needs, so it blocks PROG-BUNDLE. The fix is a third state: an explicit top-level `false` must win over a billing `true`, while an ABSENT top-level key keeps today's union semantics (so nothing that works today changes).

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='lib/spaces/entitlements.ts',T='lib/spaces/entitlements.test.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8').replace(/\\s+/g,' ');const t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const naive=s.includes('for (const [key, granted] of Object.entries(spaceBillingEntitlements(space))) { if (granted) out[key] = true }');const proven=/revoke/i.test(t)&&/billing/i.test(t);process.exit(!naive&&proven?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when the naive one-directional union is gone AND the test file proves a manual revoke beats a billing grant.

entries.title: The admin Features and access off-switch is a silent no-op for CRM, Email, Shop and Program

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
app/(main)/admin/spaces/[id]/actions.ts branches on `def.entitlement`. For a function that carries one, disabling runs `delete next[def.entitlement]` — it never writes `false` anywhere. But spaceFunctionEnabled (lib/spaces/functions.ts) keys on `def.key` and treats an ABSENT key as ON, by design (universal default-on, ADR-517 Phase F).

So for the four functions with a non-null entitlement the toggle writes the wrong key and deletes rather than disables:
  * crm      — key 'crm',  entitlement 'crm'      -> deletes 'crm', reads back ON
  * email    — key 'email', entitlement 'email'    -> deletes 'email', reads back ON
  * program  — key 'program', entitlement 'program' -> deletes 'program', reads back ON
  * shop     — key 'shop',  entitlement 'storefront' -> touches a key the reader never consults at all
The other 18 functions take the else branch and work correctly. A janitor turning CRM off sees the switch move and nothing happen.

Fix by extracting the decision into a PURE, testable function rather than fixing it in place inside a server action: the defect exists precisely because the branch was unreachable from a test.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='lib/spaces/function-toggle.ts',T='lib/spaces/function-toggle.test.ts',A='app/(main)/admin/spaces/[id]/actions.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T)||!fs.existsSync(A))process.exit(79);const a=fs.readFileSync(A,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const wired=/nextEntitlementsForFunctionToggle/.test(a);const proven=/spaceFunctionEnabled/.test(t)&&/'crm'/.test(t)&&/'shop'/.test(t);process.exit(wired&&proven?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when the action delegates to the pure toggle resolver AND its test proves the consequence through spaceFunctionEnabled for the entitlement-carrying functions.

entries.title: The niche funnel builds ?mode= and the create-a-Space wizard never reads it

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
lib/funnels/definitions.ts builds operator destinations as `/spaces/new?mode=business:packages`, and lib/funnels/routing.test.ts asserts that URL is produced. But app/(main)/spaces/new/page.tsx takes NO argument — it is `export default async function NewSpacePage()` — so Next hands it searchParams that nothing reads, and CreateSpaceForm falls back to `choices[0]?.id`, which is 'Coach'.

The visible consequence: every operator arriving from a niche funnel is asked to re-declare the thing they just clicked, and if they accept the default they land on the wrong Mode regardless of which door they came through. The page's own comment claims the wizard "auto-includes every operating model the registry offers (no hardcoded list here)" while WIZARD_CHOICES is a hardcoded 7 of the registry's 10.

This is the first link of the funnel -> bundle chain (PROG-BUNDLE) and is worth fixing on its own.

── FIXED 2026-09-03, AND THE FIX FOUND A SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME SEAM. Wiring searchParams was the easy half. NICHE_FUNNEL_DESTINATIONS routes `communities` to `business:cohort`, and WIZARD_CHOICES offered seven Modes that did not include it — so even once the parameter was read, that door would still have landed every arrival on 'Coach'. The cohort choice is added using the registry profile's OWN modeLabel and focusLabel rather than new copy, and app/(main)/spaces/new/mode-param.test.ts now fails the build if any niche destination names a Mode the wizard cannot show. Verified adversarially: removing the choice again makes the test name the exact broken pair.

verify.note: Passes when the page accepts searchParams AND a test proves a funnel mode string selects that Mode rather than the first choice.

entries.title: The grace-window comment records a production state that is not production’s

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
lib/pricing/beta.ts carries a red-flagged block stating: "THE LIVE ROW TOOK THAT OPT OUT ON 2026-08-19 (ADR-1087, migration 20270314000000). Production reads {\"until\": null}, so the grace window is GONE and featureGatesLive() is true: the ladder bites today."

The live `pricing_settings` row reads `{"until": "2026-10-01"}`. The grace window is OPEN and no paid gate bites until 1 October. The claim was made false by this repo's own commit #2347 ("Open the beta grace window to October 1"), which changed the setting and left the comment.

The fix is NOT to update the date. AGENTS.md forbids recording status in prose precisely because prose cannot be verified, and a comment that names a live DB value will go stale again on the next change. Remove the production-state claim and leave the mechanism description, which is correct and durable. Point the reader at the setting.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=fs.readFileSync('lib/pricing/beta.ts','utf8').replace(/\\s+/g,' ');process.exit(/Production reads/.test(s)||/THE LIVE ROW TOOK THAT OPT OUT/.test(s)?1:0)"
verify.note: Passes when beta.ts no longer asserts what the live pricing_settings row contains.

entries.title: Nine of ten Mode presets recommend an add-on that cannot be bought

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
lib/spaces/modes.ts declares `recommendedAddons` values of 'marketing', 'team', 'branding' and 'ai'. ADDON_ENTITLEMENT_KEYS (lib/pricing/plans.ts) has exactly one member, `ai`; marketing / team / branding were folded into plan depth by ADR-472 and sit in RETIRED_ADDON_ITEM_KEYS. The Mode settings page renders these straight to the operator as chips, so nine of the ten presets advertise a product with no Stripe price and no entitlement.

The guard that should have caught it is itself the defect: lib/spaces/modes.test.ts asserts membership against `new Set(['marketing','ai','team','branding'])` — a LITERAL, not a reference to ADDON_KEYS. It green-lights the three retired values by construction. This is the shape-not-truth failure the repo names in four ADRs, in a test.

Fix both: correct the data, and re-point the test at ADDON_KEYS so the next retirement fails the build instead of shipping.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const strip=t=>t.replace(/\\/\\*[\\s\\S]*?\\*\\//g,'').replace(/^\\s*\\/\\/.*$/gm,'');const m=strip(fs.readFileSync('lib/spaces/modes.ts','utf8'));const t=strip(fs.readFileSync('lib/spaces/modes.test.ts','utf8')).replace(/\\s+/g,' ');const stale=[...m.matchAll(/recommendedAddons:\\s*\\[([^\\]]*)\\]/g)].some(x=>/marketing|team|branding/.test(x[1]));const literal=/new Set\\(\\[ ?'(marketing|ai|team|branding)'/.test(t);process.exit(stale||literal?1:0)"
verify.note: Comments are stripped before the assertion, so an ADR reference that QUOTES the retired literal does not read as the literal. Passes when no Mode recommends a retired add-on AND the test derives its allowed set from ADDON_KEYS.

entries.title: Capability bundles: one named, curatable toolset per kind of operator

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
The audit found the three pieces of a per-operator product already built and never wired to each other:
  1. THE DOOR — lib/marketing/funnel-config.ts, five niche landing pages, each declaring `mode: { type, variant }`. Consumed by the page render, llms.txt and sitemap.ts only; the mode never reaches signup.
  2. THE TOOLSET — lib/spaces/modes.ts, ten curated operator presets. `navEmphasis` reaches the console; `defaultToggles` has ZERO runtime consumers; `recommendedAddons` renders as decoration (see SCAN-535).
  3. THE GATE — spaces.entitlements jsonb + the 22 SpaceFunctionKeys, which already gate the whole admin rail through `gate: { kind:'feature', fn }`. Turning a key off removes the row, its children and its surfaces.
space_function_type_defaults + seedSpaceConfigFromDefaults is already a bundle-at-provision mechanism — keyed on SpaceType, which has three values.

What is missing is a NAMED SET. There is no bundle object anywhere; lib/pricing/loadout.ts is not one despite the name (it hard-codes `business_base` plus the single add-on and carries an unused seatQuantity parameter).

SCOPE, per the owner ruling of 2026-09-03: ship the MECHANISM, not the curation. A pure CapabilityBundle registry, a setSpaceBundle writer, and the funnel -> provision carry-through, seeded with ONE pass-through bundle that grants the current default set so no existing Space changes behaviour. The per-niche tool lists are the owner's to author afterwards, as data, with no further code change.

Blocked by SCAN-531 and SCAN-532: both bugs are in the exact write path a bundle uses.

── SHIPPED 2026-09-03: the registry (lib/pricing/bundles.ts), its drift guard (bundles.test.ts, every function key checked against the LIVE registry) and the writer (space-bundle.ts). Seeded with the pass-through `general` bundle, which lists every function so applying it writes no off-switch and changes no Space.

⚠️ ONE DESIGN CHANGE FROM THE ROW AS WRITTEN, and it makes the mechanism safer rather than smaller. The row imagined setSpaceBundle writing `spaces.plan` and set-to-targeting `entitlements.billing`. It does neither. A bundle SHAPES a Space (which of the 22 tools are on, and who may reach each) and never touches money: setSpacePlan / setSpaceAddons stay the only writers of the billing namespace, and the Stripe webhook stays their only automatic caller. Shaping and charging are two decisions on two surfaces, and ADR-874 records what this repo paid the last time a pair like that was conflated. `suggestedPlan` on a bundle is a hint for a checkout to read; nothing acts on it. A bundle is therefore subtractive over the default-ON registry and COMPOSES with the plan instead of replacing it.

🔴 THE THREE-STATE ENTITLEMENT READ (SCAN-531) IS LOAD-BEARING HERE. A bundle subtracts by writing a top-level `false`, which is exactly the state that now beats a plan grant. Without that fix landing first this whole module would be inert on every paid Space, which is why the two shipped in the same branch.

⚪ THE PROVISION CARRY-THROUGH IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED. See LIVE-149: with only a pass-through bundle registered, teaching lib/spaces/provision.ts to apply one would add a branch to the Space creation path that can only ever be a no-op. Speculative code in the highest-risk path in the product, to serve curation that does not exist yet, is the trade this program was scoped to avoid. Wire it in the same change as the first curated bundle.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const R='lib/pricing/bundles.ts',T='lib/pricing/bundles.test.ts',W='lib/pricing/space-bundle.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(R)||!fs.existsSync(T)||!fs.existsSync(W))process.exit(79);const r=fs.readFileSync(R,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8'),w=fs.readFileSync(W,'utf8');const registry=/CapabilityBundle/.test(r)&&/SpaceFunctionKey/.test(r);const drift=/SPACE_FUNCTIONS/.test(t)&&/BILLING_MANAGED_KEYS/.test(t);const writer=/setSpaceBundle/.test(w);process.exit(registry&&drift&&writer?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when the pure registry, its drift test (every function key real, every entitlement key real) and the writer all exist.

entries.title: Thirty static redirect pages are route files doing a job next.config already does

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
49 of 398 page.tsx files (12%) contain a redirect and render no JSX. Classified by whether they can move to next.config.ts:
  * 30 are STATIC — they import only next/navigation, take no params or searchParams, and redirect to a string literal. 15 of those are the retired (marketing) SEO guides. These are route files, build entries and function-budget lines paying for what a config line does at the edge.
  * 12 carry a route param but no other logic and are mechanically convertible to `:slug` patterns — deliberately OUT of scope here, they need a per-file read (see HYG-044).
  * 7 carry real logic (auth lookup, cookie read, claim-token lookup) and must stay routes: /profile, /marketplace, /settings/profile/spotlight, /events/drafts, /friends, /people/[handle]/profile-preview/edit, /events/claim/[token].

This row covers the 30 static ones only. Every consolidation in this repo has so far ADDED the new surface and left the old one running; the standing rule this row establishes is that a consolidation is not finished until the thing it replaced is deleted.

⚠️ MEASURED 2026-09-03 BEFORE ATTEMPTING IT, AND THE JOB IS BIGGER THAN THE FILE COUNT. The 30 pages are mechanical, but four other files hold paired state that a deletion invalidates, and missing any one of them is how this job goes wrong quietly:
  · scripts/check-seo.mjs INTENTIONALLY_EXCLUDED — 15 of the 30 are listed there with a verified reason. The guard WARNS on an entry with no backing page ('stale exclusion, remove it'), so the entries must go in the same change.
  · lib/analytics/vitals-budgets.ts — budgets ~11 of the retired marketing routes. It is already stale prose about routes that 308 today; deleting the pages makes that visible rather than causing it.
  · scripts/templates-baseline.txt and scripts/admin-client-baseline.txt — both name files under directories in this set. Note the admin ones name actions.ts SIBLINGS, not the page: deleting a page.tsx leaves a live actions.ts and a route-less directory, which needs a per-directory read rather than a sweep.
  · lib/analytics/vitals-budgets.test.ts asserts '/how-it-works' specifically.
The extraction and the exact source -> destination -> permanence mapping for all 30 is done and verified; what remains is the paired bookkeeping. Do it as one change with all five files, not as a delete followed by guard chasing.

── DONE 2026-09-04 (ADR-1199). All 30 static stubs deleted and replaced by next.config rules, permanence preserved exactly (15 stayed 307, the 15 marketing guides stayed 308 — turning a 307 into a 308 is an irreversible decision, not a tidy-up). The paired bookkeeping landed in the SAME change, as the row demanded: the 15 marketing entries came out of check-seo.mjs INTENTIONALLY_EXCLUDED (leaving them would have traded one stale record for another, since that guard warns on an entry with no backing page), and two lines came out of templates-baseline.txt.

⚠️ THE SURVEY UNDERCOUNTED THE LIVE INBOUND LINKS. The plan named 6; a post-edit sweep found 10. The four extras were app/manage-emails/page.tsx, components/connections/resonance-matches.tsx, components/feed/romance-strip.tsx and components/widgets/crm/today.tsx, each pointing at a /settings/* path that now 307s. They worked either way, which is exactly why nobody would have noticed the extra hop.

admin-client-baseline.txt needed no edit after all: every entry it holds under these directories names an actions.ts sibling that survives, because only page.tsx was deleted wherever a live sibling existed.
