verify.note: Counts page.tsx files that are a bare literal redirect with no params and only a next/navigation import. Passes at zero.

entries.title: Twelve param-only redirect pages could be :slug rules, one read each

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
The residue of HYG-043. Twelve redirect-only pages take a route param and import nothing but next/navigation, so each is probably a next.config `:slug` rule — but 'probably' is why they are a separate row: four of them are circle tab stubs whose targets differ by tab, and two are Space settings stubs that may or may not preserve a query string.

The files: admin/crm/deals/[...slug], circles/[slug]/(circle)/{events,journey,leaderboard,practice}, circles/[slug]/crm, events/[slug]/manage/crm, spaces/[slug]/crm/inbox, spaces/[slug]/settings, spaces/[slug]/settings/{enroll,services}, admin/marketing/contacts/[id].

Do them one at a time, reading the target each time. Do NOT batch-convert.

── DONE 2026-09-04 (ADR-1199), one read each as the row required. The four circle tab stubs do NOT share a destination — events/journey/practice go to whats-on, leaderboard goes to stats — so they are two rules, not one, which is precisely the mistake a batch conversion would have made. Eleven converted; app/(main)/admin/marketing/contacts/[id] stays a route file (requireAdmin plus a DB lookup to derive its destination).

Four directories kept their page.tsx deleted but the directory alive, because a sibling is imported elsewhere: circles/[slug]/crm/actions.ts, events/[slug]/manage/crm/actions.ts, spaces/[slug]/settings/enroll/{enroll-body,section}.tsx and spaces/[slug]/settings/services/new/.

🔴 The two dangerous rules are now GUARDED, not merely written carefully. lib/marketing/redirect-shadow.test.ts fails if any rule shadows a live route; widening /spaces/:slug/settings to :path* makes it name all 19 sub-pages it would have taken out. The guard found two bugs in its own matcher before it found anything else, both of which would have made it pass while checking nothing.

verify.evidence: Each of the twelve is either a next.config rule or has a recorded reason it must stay a route.

entries.title: A completed migration plan that still read as live work

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
THE ROW AS FILED WAS WRONG ABOUT THE PREMISE, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE INTERESTING PART. It said docs/PUCK-MIGRATION-PLAN.md 'describes migrating off a library the repo does not have' and proposed deleting it.

Re-read before acting: the plan's own recommendation is four steps ending '(4) delete the package'. The package IS gone from package.json. So the migration SUCCEEDED and nobody came back to say so. The audit read a finished plan as an abandoned one, because the only thing distinguishing the two was prose nobody updated — which is the failure this repo names in ADR-1043, arriving from the other direction.

⚪ DELETION WOULD ALSO HAVE BEEN WRONG on its own terms. ADR-493 cites the file as its full plan and check:docs-links enforces relative .md links, so removing it breaks the ledger. The repo's established retirement mechanism for a doc is a superseded banner (18 docs carry one); deletion is the mechanism for CODE. Retiring a document and retiring a module are not the same act.

🔴 AND lib/spotlight/puck/ IS NOT DEAD CODE. convert.ts / resolve.ts / metadata.ts are imported by lib/page-editor/templates/linktree.ts, components/spotlight/spotlight-shell.tsx and components/admin/modules/personal-appearance-module.tsx. They survive because the plan's central constraint was keeping the persisted { content, root } shape byte-for-byte so no stored document is migrated. The package left; the document shape, and therefore the name, stayed. The banner says so explicitly, because 'finish the migration by deleting that directory' is the obvious wrong next move for the next reader.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const D='docs/PUCK-MIGRATION-PLAN.md';if(!fs.existsSync(D))process.exit(0);const d=fs.readFileSync(D,'utf8').split('\\n').slice(0,25).join(' ');process.exit(/Superseded/i.test(d)?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when the plan carries a superseded banner in its first 25 lines, or has been removed entirely. It does NOT assert the package is absent: a future reinstall would be a real decision, not a regression of this row.

entries.title: Hub and Nexus detail pages are hand-maintained twins that have already drifted

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
app/(main)/hubs/[slug]/page.tsx (243 lines) and app/(main)/nexuses/[slug]/page.tsx (232 lines) have identical import blocks and identical structure — HierarchyBreadcrumb, StatusBadge, DetailTemplate, resolveDetailHero, InlineText, OpenAdminBarButton, surfaceAccess, showsScopedInsight, StatCard, SectionHeader, EmptyState, ProgressTrack — differing only in getHubCapabilities vs getNexusCapabilities. The same holds for their admin-actions.ts files (220 and 217 lines). After normalising the hub/nexus and guide/mentor tokens roughly 60% of lines still differ. They are not copies kept in sync; they are copies that have drifted, which is the worse failure mode: a fix applied to one silently does not reach the other. Both tiers are thin in production (hubs 27 code refs, nexuses 19, and neither is a member-facing nav noun). Extract one parameterised implementation rather than reconciling two. ── CLOSED 2026-09-07, AND THE PREMISE WAS UNDERSTATED: THREE OF THE DIFFERENCES WERE DEFECTS, NOT COSMETICS. The pages were diffed token-normalised (hub↔nexus, guide↔mentor) before anything was touched. 1. ROUND TRIPS. The Hub page batched four reads in one Promise.all (the site-audit PERF-6 fix). The Nexus page batched caps and hero, then awaited surfaceAccess serially, then queried children serially — three latencies for four reads. PERF-6 never reached it. 2. 🔴 ARCHIVED HUBS WERE LISTED AND COUNTED, and this is the member-visible one. The Hub page filtered circles with .neq(status,archived); the Nexus page had NO filter on hubs. So archived Hubs appeared in the only listing of Hubs the product has, and their members were counted in the Nexus member total AND in the Insight "Members" and "Avg per hub" stats. archiveNexus/archiveHub document archiving as existing "so it drops out of listings" — that was simply not true on one tier. 3. A LEADING SEPARATOR. The name row wrapped on Hub and not on Nexus, and the meta was a

on one and an inline flex row with a literal · on the other, so a Hub with no Guide rendered a leading "·" on the Nexus page. THE FIX MAKES 1 AND 2 STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE ON ONE TIER ONLY: lib/hierarchy/tier-detail.ts owns the single round trip and the archived-child exclusion, and components/hierarchy/tier-detail.tsx owns the frame, header slots, Insight band, child row and empty state, all derived from childLabel/childNoun. Pages fell 243→122 and 232→117; what remains is irreducibly tier-specific — the entity query, the row type it returns, and the view mapping. ⚪ THE PAGE STILL RENDERS DetailTemplate ITSELF. tierDetailHeader() returns the template's SLOTS rather than the shell, because a page owning no layout would push check:templates backwards. Pinned by a test, not only by the gate. ⚠️ THE ROW'S PROBE WAS HALF HONEST AND THE DISHONEST HALF WAS NOT SATISFIED. Its delegation arm measured the right consequence. Its "<90 lines" arm did not: a line count cannot tell an extraction from a relocation, and it is trivially gamed by moving the entity query into a sibling load.ts — a pattern this repo already uses — which buys 40 lines while removing zero duplication. The line count survives as a RATCHET at 125 (may shrink, never grow) rather than as the definition of done, and the probe now measures delegation, the shared loader being the only route to Insight and cover, the archived-child exclusion, and that neither page re-declares the empty state or hard-codes an Insight label. ⚪ A vitest-spawning probe was proposed and REJECTED: LIVE-034 forbids it, because ten such probes are why check:backlog costs 24s. The 37 tests still run under pnpm test in CI; the probe is a cheap source-shape gate beside them. Mutations, each watched red: against the pre-extraction tree the suite fails 11 of 18 — including "serialises exactly one read", which fails only for nexus and so independently reproduces defect 1. Six more against the fixed tree, each caught by exactly the intended test. The installed probe was re-verified here: reverting the Nexus page trips the delegation arm, and renaming the loader's archived filter trips the exclusion arm.

entries.title: The slate inside the verified backlog is itself unverified, and half of it is stale

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
meta.slate.waves lists 77 ids. Their current statuses: 39 done, 35 open, 2 parked, and one id (LIVE-113) that does not exist in entries at all. So 51% of the sequenced slate is finished work still presented as the queue, and W0 ("active now") is 23 done, 1 missing and exactly 1 genuinely open.

Separately, 25 open/blocked rows are absent from the slate entirely and therefore have no sequencing position — including four live production incidents (LIVE-123 build stalls, LIVE-124 the 300s ceiling, LIVE-105 a dead deploy, LIVE-142 a firing serialization error) and OWN-046.

This is check:one-list's own failure mode reappearing INSIDE the one list: the rows are probed, the object that orders them is prose. Give the slate a probe: no done ids, no phantom ids, and every open row placed.

── FIXED 2026-09-03. Removed 39 finished ids and the one phantom (LIVE-113) from the waves, and placed all 33 open rows that had no sequencing position, including the four live production incidents that had been sitting outside the queue entirely. W0 'active now' had been 23 done, 1 phantom and 1 genuinely open.

⚪ THE PLACEMENT RULE IS NOW RECORDED IN meta.slate.rule rather than left implicit, because the drift was never that someone sequenced badly — it was that nothing said what the object was for, so nobody maintained it. A rule a reader can apply is the difference between a record that survives and one that rots politely.

🔴 THE PROBE IS THE POINT, not the tidy-up. The slate was prose living inside the one file the repo trusts, and check:backlog now fails if a finished row is still sequenced, a phantom id appears, or an open row has no place. That is the same contract the ROWS have had since ADR-1043; the object that orders them simply never had it.

verify.cmd: node -e "const d=require('./docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json');const byId=new Map(d.entries.map(e=>[e.id,e]));const slate=[].concat(...(d.meta.slate&&d.meta.slate.waves||[]).map(w=>w.ids||[]));const phantom=slate.filter(i=>!byId.has(i));const done=slate.filter(i=>byId.get(i)&&byId.get(i).status==='done');const active=d.entries.filter(e=>e.status==='open'||e.status==='blocked').map(e=>e.id);const unplaced=active.filter(i=>!slate.includes(i));process.exit(phantom.length===0&&done.length===0&&unplaced.length===0?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when the slate contains no finished work, no phantom ids, and leaves no open row unsequenced.

entries.title: One funnel entrance, five call-to-action labels

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
BETA_CTA_LABEL in lib/site.ts is "Start a Circle" and is used across the marketing pages — except app/page.tsx overrides it to "Join the beta", the /for/* funnel doors say "Start free", /pricing says "Join free" / "Join Crew" / "Start a Space", and /join itself says "Come in". Five verbs for one entrance.

Two things make it worse than inconsistency. "Start a Circle" is the HARDEST ask on the site and it is the default CTA on pages whose readers arrived from "how to make friends as an adult". And the universal secondary is "or just join as a member" — the word `just` telling the majority of arriving traffic that they are the lesser option, on a site whose own voice canon names the Seeker as reader one.

One primary verb, one secondary that does not apologise, both single-sourced so a page cannot override them without the guard noticing.

── FIXED 2026-09-03 (the two mechanical halves). The home page no longer overrides ctaLabel, so MarketingHeader falls back to BETA_CTA_LABEL and the front door says what every other marketing page says. And the shared secondary lost the word 'just': it now reads 'or join as a member'. The path is already quieter than the primary because it is a text link beside a button; the copy did not need to say so as well.

⚠️ THE BIGGER CALL IS DELIBERATELY NOT MADE HERE, and it is a positioning decision rather than a consistency one: whether 'Start a Circle' should remain the site-wide primary at all. It is the hardest ask on the site, and it is the default CTA on six SEO guides whose readers arrived from 'how to make friends as an adult'. lib/site.ts documents the current choice as builder-framing aimed at the Latent Leader, 'the reader the whole growth model runs on'. Overriding a documented positioning rationale is a different act from removing an apology, and the production data points the other way again: the customers are operators, not circle hosts. Left for the owner with the evidence stated.

⚪ NOTE FOR WHOEVER CHANGES THE LABEL: lib/site.ts warns that page templates baking the literal into a PUBLISHED DB doc need a re-publish to pick it up. The live home page is one of those (LIVE-148), so changing the constant will not change the front door on its own.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const strip=t=>t.replace(/\\/\\*[\\s\\S]*?\\*\\//g,'').replace(/^\\s*\\/\\/.*$/gm,'').replace(/\\{\\/\\*[\\s\\S]*?\\*\\/\\}/g,'');const s=strip(fs.readFileSync('lib/site.ts','utf8'));const home=strip(fs.readFileSync('app/page.tsx','utf8'));const apologetic=/or just join/i.test(s);const overrides=/ctaLabel=\"[^\"]+\"/.test(home);process.exit(!apologetic&&!overrides?0:1)"
verify.note: Comments and JSX comments are stripped first, so an ADR note that QUOTES the retired copy does not read as the copy. Passes when the secondary CTA no longer apologises in code and the home page stops hardcoding its own primary label.

entries.title: The traffic half of the site and the revenue half never link to each other

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
Every surviving SEO guide — /loneliness, /friendship-as-an-adult, /how-to-be-more-social, /calm-down-fast, /how-to-build-community, /how-to-start-a-circle — routes to /discover or /the-community. Not one links to /pricing or to any /for/* door. The five /for/* funnel doors are chrome-free and link nowhere else at all.

So the pages that earn search traffic and the pages that take money are two disconnected websites sharing a domain. With Vercel Web Analytics disabled (OWN-047) there is also no way to observe that happening.

Add the onward path in both directions: a guide offers the operator door where it is genuinely relevant, and each funnel door carries a route back into the marketing site rather than dead-ending.

── FIXED 2026-09-04, AND ONE HALF OF THE ROW WAS OVERSTATED. The traffic-to-revenue link is real and is now made: /tools-for-community-builders pointed its 'Get the toolkit' primary at /spaces, a generic marketing page, and now points at /for/community-builders, the operator door built for that reader.

⚠️ 'The funnel doors link nowhere else at all' was too strong. Measured: the door's header logo links to /, and its footer renders a link list. What the list held was Privacy, Terms and a mailto — legal boilerplate, so the substance held (an operator wanting the numbers before deciding had no route to them from the page selling them) but the sentence did not. Pricing is added to that list. A finding stated harder than the measurement supports is the thing this audit keeps catching in other people's comments.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const G='lib/page-editor/templates/tools-for-community-builders.ts',F='lib/marketing/funnel-config.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(G)||!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const g=fs.readFileSync(G,'utf8'),f=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8');const guideOut=/href: '\/for\//.test(g);const doorBack=/\{ label: 'Pricing', href: '\/pricing' \}/.test(f);process.exit(guideOut&&doorBack?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when a marketing guide routes into a /for/ operator door AND the operator door offers a route to /pricing.

entries.title: The front door’s copy lives in an unversioned database row

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
app/page.tsx renders a published page-editor document. Its own comment is explicit: "lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts IS UNREACHABLE BY DECISION" and must not be reconciled against the published page, by an owner ruling of 2026-08-24.

The consequence is that the single most important piece of copy on the site — last written 2026-07-13 — is a database row that no test, no diff, no review and none of the 48 CI gates can see. The canon guards (check:vocab, check:canon) scan the repo, so the front door is the one member-facing surface exempt from the naming and voice canons. Every conclusion anyone draws about `/` by reading this repository is a conclusion about a fallback nobody renders.

The ruling was reasonable — editing the home page in the editor is the right authoring experience. What is missing is a way for the REVIEW to happen: either publish the document back into the repo as a checked-in seed on every publish, or run the canon guards against the published document rather than the template.

── MEASURED 2026-09-04, AND THE CHOSEN FIX NEEDS A SECRET THIS REPO DOES NOT HAVE. Owner ruling: keep authoring in the editor and run the canons against the PUBLISHED document rather than the unreachable code template. Correct call, and it cannot be a CI check: scripts/check-canon.mjs is a filesystem scanner (readdirSync over app/ and lib/), and CI has no data plane.

The right home is .github/workflows/maintenance.yml, which is exactly where ci.yml's own comment says a check needing deployment state belongs (the cron-freshness precedent: 'an advisory finding forced through a blocking gate teaches everyone to route around the gate'). But maintenance.yml carries only SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, the MANAGEMENT api token used for the advisor diff and the ledger parity. Reading a row out of the `pages` table needs a data-plane key, which is not there.

⚪ SO THIS IS AN OWNER ROW NOW, not a code row, and the lane is changed to say so. Unblock it by adding a read-capable Supabase key to the maintenance workflow's secrets; the step and its script are then a small change that can degrade to the repo's usual loud skip when the key is absent.

── OWNER-GATE RE-TESTED 2026-09-07 (the 26-row triage). 🔴 THE STATED BLOCKER IS FALSE, so this is not owner work. The row says the front door copy cannot be reached because running SQL against production needs a credential nobody has wired. .github/workflows/maintenance.yml ALREADY POSTs arbitrary SQL to https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/$SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF/database/query with the existing SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN - twice, at two separate steps - and a real 2026-08-31 run log prints its result ("24 live rows against 24 code defaults"). The secret is set, the pattern works, and no new one is needed. This is ordinary work now.
── CLOSED 2026-09-07. The stated blocker was FALSE and the fix needed no new secret. maintenance.yml already POSTs arbitrary SQL to the Management API at /v1/projects/$REF/database/query with the existing SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, at two separate steps, and a 2026-08-31 run log prints a real result from one of them. The credential was there the whole time; only the reading of it was wrong. This row sat on the owner for three days for nothing, which is the "a blocker phrased as cannot-be-checked is a claim with an expiry date" lesson AGENTS.md already records, happening again.

WHAT SHIPPED. scripts/maintenance/home-copy-canon.mjs plus a "Front-door copy canon" step in maintenance.yml, mirroring the Public header menu drift step exactly: --print-query emits the SQL, curl POSTs it, the reporter reads the JSON envelope back. It IMPORTS RULES from scripts/check-canon.mjs rather than restating the regexes, so there is still exactly one home for the canon and this cannot drift from it; the test asserts that import and asserts the regexes are NOT copied.

ADVISORY, deliberately, and it lives in the sweep rather than ci.yml for the reason ci.yml's own comment gives: CI has no data plane, and a gate that fails for something no pull request can fix is one everybody learns to route around (ADR-970, the cron-freshness precedent). An operator can publish at any moment; a maintenance run going red over a word choice would train people to stop reading it.

EXTRACTION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT AN ALLOWLIST. Block props are open-ended, so a list of known copy keys would silently stop covering a block type somebody adds later and the guard would read as coverage while measuring less and less. It walks the whole document and filters by what a string LOOKS like. The live document nests copy three ways - content[].props.{title,subtitle,body,kicker,eyebrow,footnote,safetyNet}, then rows[].note, rungs[].blurb and items[].text one level deeper - and the fixtures mirror all three, because a fixture nesting only one level would have passed while the guard missed a third of the front door.

⚠️ THE TEST CAUGHT A REAL GAP IN MY OWN EXTRACTOR before it shipped: an asset filename (/images/site/....jpg) was being scanned as prose, because "image" was missing from the machinery-key list and the path pattern forbade dots. Both fixed; the case is pinned.

MEASURED ON THE LIVE DOCUMENT, twice and independently: the published home document is 13 blocks / 9,188 bytes, and it carries ZERO canon violations - once through the guard's own reporter, and once by running the same patterns as SQL regexes straight against published_data::text. The guard reports clean today, and the per-rule test loop proves it CAN fire: every one of the canon's rules is exercised against copy that violates it, so this is not a gate that has never fired.

⚪ READING THE LIVE COPY FOUND FOUR DEFECTS THE CANON CANNOT SEE (typos and one naming collision). Filed as LIVE-204 rather than fixed here: it is published brand copy, the owner authors it in the editor, and CONTENT-VOICE is a locked canon.

verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE: a guard exists that reads the live published_data out of public.pages, it is wired into the maintenance workflow at both halves (query + report), and it imports the canon from check-canon.mjs instead of restating it. Deleting any one of the three fails. The report itself cannot be probed from a repo checkout because it reads production, which is exactly the gap the row names.

entries.title: Vercel Web Analytics is off, so no marketing page has ever been measured

source.ref: ADR-1197, the 2026-09-03 repair and rework audit

entries.detail:
The Vercel Web Analytics API returns `web_analytics_not_enabled` for the frequency-web project. Around twenty public marketing and SEO surfaces ship without any way to see whether a single one of them converts, and the /for/* funnel doors — the whole operator acquisition path — have no measurement at all.

The project already sends its own engagement events to Supabase (nav.page_view and the rest), which covers signed-in behaviour well. It does not cover the signed-out funnel, which is where every acquisition decision is made.

This is a dashboard toggle on the Vercel project, so it is an owner action. It is XS and it unblocks every judgement about which marketing page is worth keeping.

── DONE 2026-09-04 (ADR-1199), and it took BOTH halves. The owner enabled Web Analytics on the Vercel project, which stopped the API returning `web_analytics_not_enabled`. It would still have reported zero forever: @vercel/analytics was not a dependency and <Analytics /> was rendered nowhere, so nothing sent a pageview. The dashboard switch opens the endpoint; the script is what fills it. The package is added and the component mounts in app/layout.tsx beside WebVitals.

⚪ Measurement starts NOW and does not backfill, so the ~20 marketing surfaces and the /for/* doors have no history behind them yet. Any 'which page is worth keeping' judgement needs a few weeks first.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const pkg=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json','utf8'));const dep=!!(pkg.dependencies&&pkg.dependencies['@vercel/analytics']);const l=fs.readFileSync('app/layout.tsx','utf8');process.exit(dep&&/<Analytics\\s*\\/>/.test(l)&&/@vercel\\/analytics/.test(l)?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when the package is a dependency AND the component is actually rendered in the root layout. The dashboard toggle alone reports zero, which is the half that was missed.

entries.title: Turning off Plan and billing destroys every plan grant the Space has
entries.detail:
FOUND BY A TEST WRITTEN FOR A DIFFERENT BUG, and it is the most severe of the set. The Space function `billing` ("Plan and billing") has a key byte-identical to BILLING_NAMESPACE, the reserved container every plan grant lives inside.

The shipped off-switch wrote `entitlements.billing = false`. spaceBillingEntitlements normalizes a non-object to {}, so ONE janitor toggle on a paid Space silently deleted crm, email, reporting, automation, team, multi_pipeline, program and space_full_website — every grant setSpacePlan had written. Reproduced against the real reader before the fix; the assertion is kept in the test file as a permanent record of what the write costs.

The collision is refused in BOTH directions: enabling would write `billing: true`, which destroys the grants exactly as thoroughly. The resolver returns null rather than silently returning the blob unchanged, because a fail-safe nobody can observe is an invisible regression (AGENTS.md); the action surfaces it as a plain message.

⚠️ NOT FIXED HERE, and deliberately: the underlying namespace collision remains. A Space function may still be added whose key shadows a reserved container, and nothing fails the build. The refusal is a stop, not a cure. A durable fix stores off-switches under their own reserved prefix, which changes the read contract in every consumer and is its own piece of work.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='lib/spaces/function-toggle.ts',T='lib/spaces/function-toggle.test.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const refuses=/def.key === BILLING_NAMESPACE/.test(s)&&/\| null/.test(s);const proven=/REPRODUCES the damage/.test(t)&&/toBeNull\(\)/.test(t);process.exit(refuses&&proven?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when the resolver refuses the reserved-namespace key and the test both reproduces the damage and proves the refusal.

entries.title: Apply a capability bundle at provision, once there is a bundle worth applying

source.ref: ADR-1197, the deferred half of PROG-BUNDLE

entries.detail:
The mechanism shipped without its last link. lib/spaces/provision.ts does not call setSpaceBundle, so a Space is created with every tool on and a bundle must be applied afterwards by hand.

This is a deliberate hold, not an oversight. CAPABILITY_BUNDLES currently holds one pass-through row, so the branch could only ever be a no-op — speculative code in the Space creation path, which is the highest-risk path in the product, serving curation that does not exist yet.

DO THIS IN THE SAME CHANGE AS THE FIRST CURATED BUNDLE, never before it. The seam is already open at both ends: /spaces/new reads ?mode= and resolves it to a ModeChoice (SCAN-533), and setSpaceBundle takes a space id and a bundle id. What is missing is the map from a Mode to a bundle, which is data, and one call after the row is inserted.

⚠️ The first curated bundle is the moment this stops being mechanism and starts being a product decision: it decides what a given kind of operator does NOT get. The data says roughly 18 of 21 real Spaces are solo wellness practitioners and only the coaches-and-healers door has produced a customer, so that is the one bundle with evidence behind it.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P3 on 2026-09-07. Vercel Web Analytics, 31 days to 2026-09-07: 12 visitors, 18 pageviews. An SEO or funnel refinement cannot be P1 while the funnel itself has no traffic to refine — the constraint is upstream of every one of these rows. Re-priced by the live-lane audit on that reading, not on merit.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const R='lib/pricing/bundles.ts',P='lib/spaces/provision.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(R)||!fs.existsSync(P))process.exit(79);const r=fs.readFileSync(R,'utf8');const curated=(r.match(/id: '/g)||[]).length>1;if(!curated)process.exit(1);process.exit(/setSpaceBundle/.test(fs.readFileSync(P,'utf8'))?0:1)"
verify.note: Stays failing while only the pass-through bundle exists. Passes when a curated bundle is registered AND provision applies one. Fails loudly if a curated bundle lands without the wiring.

entries.title: The sanctioned way to update the RLS-bypass baseline deletes the reasons for every bypass in it

source.ref: ADR-1197, found while fixing a CI failure

entries.detail:
scripts/admin-client-baseline.txt is the frozen list of files allowed to import the RLS-bypassing service-role client (ADR-923). Above the list sits a 76-line comment block: the justification for each existing bypass, written per entry, naming the zero-policy table or the signed-out caller or the SECURITY DEFINER function that makes it the safe shape rather than the lazy one. It is the only place that reasoning exists.

When the guard fails it prints the fix: 'run: node scripts/check-admin-client.mjs --update'. That command regenerates the file from a fresh scan and writes the list ALONE. Measured 2026-09-04 while adding one legitimate entry: the regenerated file was +2 / -76, and the 76 were the entire comment block.

🔴 THE FAILURE MODE IS THE WORST SHAPE A SECURITY TOOL CAN HAVE. The command is the one the guard itself recommends, it is run by someone under CI pressure who wants to get green, its output passes the guard immediately, and the loss shows up in the diff as deletions in a file the reviewer is looking at for a single added path. The next person to ask 'why is lib/events/seed/store.ts allowed to bypass RLS?' finds no answer, and the honest answer is that a tool deleted it to add an unrelated line.

⚪ WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED, in the change that found it: the entry was inserted by hand in sorted position, diff +1, comments intact. That is not a fix, it is one person knowing. Make --update preserve every leading comment line, and add a test that regenerating a baseline with a header leaves the header byte-identical.

⚠️ CHECK THE SIBLINGS BEFORE CLOSING. scripts/templates-baseline.txt and scripts/adoption-baselines.json have the same --update shape and may have the same hole; if they do, this row covers them too. And check the history: if a past --update already ate a comment block, some existing entries may have lost their justification years ago and nobody would know.

── DONE 2026-09-04 (ADR-1200). `--update` now preserves the leading comment block verbatim via readHeader(), falling back to the default only when there is no header to keep (missing file, or a file that starts straight in on entries). Proven on the REAL file rather than a fixture: running the actual `node scripts/check-admin-client.mjs --update` against the committed baseline now produces a byte-identical 823 lines / 80 comment lines, where the row measured +2/-76. scripts/check-admin-client.test.ts covers the round-trip, blank lines inside the block, the missing-file fallback, and carries a MUTATION CONTROL that reconstructs the old behaviour and asserts it fails the same assertion.

The sibling in scripts/check-templates.mjs got the same treatment. It round-tripped by luck — its header is still byte-identical to its constant because nobody has hand-annotated an entry — so this fixes the shape before it has damage rather than after.

🔴 THE SHREDDING IS REAL AND IS NOT FIXED BY THIS. A whole-file lexicographic sort has already run over the admin-client block: 78 of 79 adjacent comment pairs are in alphabetical order, the script's own five header lines sit scattered at lines 45/46/51/47/63 in exactly their lexicographic order, and the prose no longer parses (line 24 ends mid-sentence and its continuation is at line 3). The justifications are byte-present but no longer attached to the entries they justify, and `git log` on the file is 3 commits deep so the pre-sort original is unrecoverable here. Reassembly needs someone who knows the tenancy model; filed as SCAN-540.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='scripts/check-admin-client.mjs',T='scripts/check-admin-client.test.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(S))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8');const preserves=/preserve|leading comment|header/i.test(s);const proven=fs.existsSync(T)&&/comment/i.test(fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8'));process.exit(preserves&&proven?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when --update preserves the leading comment block AND a test proves regeneration leaves it intact. A code-shape check alone would not be enough here, which is why the test file is required.

entries.title: Two niche vocabularies, and the map between them has no runtime consumer
entries.detail:
The niche funnel has TWO slug vocabularies and they do not match. lib/marketing/funnel-config.ts declares the /for/ doors as coaches-and-healers, studios, event-hosts, community-builders, nonprofits. lib/funnels/definitions.ts keys NICHE_FUNNEL_DESTINATIONS as coaches, studios, hosts, communities, nonprofits. Only studios and nonprofits are the same string, so a lookup by /for/ slug misses three of five.

🔴 IT HAS NOT BITTEN ANYONE, FOR A WORSE REASON THAN LUCK: NICHE_FUNNEL_DESTINATIONS has NO runtime consumer at all. Its only importers are lib/funnels/routing.test.ts and, since SCAN-533, app/(main)/spaces/new/mode-param.test.ts. The door's own button reads FUNNEL_START_HREF, which is the literal '/spaces'. So the map that carries each niche to its pre-seeded Mode is tested, documented, cross-referenced in a comment as 'the SAME spaceCreatePath', and dead.

⚠️ THIS QUALIFIES THE SCAN-533 FIX AND THE AUDIT'S HEADLINE. /spaces/new now reads ?mode= and the mode-param test proves it, which is right and needed; but the /for/ doors do not currently produce that URL, so the chain the audit described as broken at one link is broken at two. The half that is live is the /join?seq= induction path, which does route through these destinations. The half that is not is the door button.

⚪ THE FIX IS ONE OF TWO SHAPES, and it is a product call rather than a mechanical one: either the door button routes through the niche destination (an operator lands in Create-a-Space pre-seeded, which is what OPERATOR-FUNNELS §5 says it should do), or the destination map is deleted and the door honestly sends everyone to /spaces. Do not close this by making the two key sets match: that fixes the spelling of a road nobody drives on.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P3 on 2026-09-07. Vercel Web Analytics, 31 days to 2026-09-07: 12 visitors, 18 pageviews. An SEO or funnel refinement cannot be P1 while the funnel itself has no traffic to refine — the constraint is upstream of every one of these rows. Re-priced by the live-lane audit on that reading, not on merit.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1238). RE-MEASURED FIRST: the probe exited 1 (zero non-test importers of NICHE_FUNNEL_DESTINATIONS), every Start free on the door rendered the literal FUNNEL_START_HREF = '/spaces' (5 buttons: header, sticky mobile, hero, pricing, final CTA), and three of five door slugs (coaches-and-healers, event-hosts, community-builders) matched no map key. One qualification to the premise: the map DID have an indirect runtime reader the whole time, lib/funnels/resolve.ts withNicheDefaultDestination through the nicheFunnelDestination wrapper, which the probe cannot see (it greps the constant's name); the row's substantive claim, that no door produced a URL that reaches it, held. CHOSE THE FIRST SHAPE (wire the door), for the reason the detail gives: OPERATOR-FUNNELS §5 says the operator lands pre-seeded, and the live /join?seq= induction IS the minimal-signup bridge §5 describes. The direct alternative (/spaces/new?mode= via the sign-in round trip) was rejected because a brand-new account is bounced to /onboarding -> /join with no seq and loses the Mode. CHANGED: FunnelConfig gains `niche` (the sequence slug: coaches/studios/hosts/communities/nonprofits) as the one bridge between the two vocabularies, and loses its duplicate `mode` so the Mode is declared once, on the map row; funnelStartHref(config) builds /join?seq=<niche> when NICHE_FUNNEL_DESTINATIONS has the row and falls back to /spaces otherwise (the runtime read the probe measures); SplashHeader and StickyMobileCta take the config; app/join's onboarded branch now redirects through funnelLanding(seq.destination) instead of a bare /feed, so a signed-in operator who clicks a door lands pre-seeded (a feature-funnel link now lands an onboarded member on its feature, /on-air for breathwork, instead of the feed). The definitions.ts comment that called the keys 'the short /for/<niche> slugs' was false for three of five and is corrected. PINNED by lib/funnels/routing.test.ts (five doors cover five rows, every href is /join?seq=<niche>, orphan niche falls back) and components/marketing/funnel/funnel-sections.test.ts (no literal start path on the door, both chrome pieces receive the config, the /join branch). Probe now exits 0 with lib/marketing/funnel-config.ts as the importer. Not done: no DB sequence_overrides row exists for any niche slug, so the induction copy on a niche door is the default Vera flow until the owner authors one in the funnel builder; and the cross-browser funnel recovery in app/auth/callback only recognises code funnels (FUNNELS), so a niche seq is not recovered when the magic link opens in a different browser.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const path=require("path");const D="lib/funnels/definitions.ts";if(!fs.existsSync(D))process.exit(79);if(!/NICHE_FUNNEL_DESTINATIONS/.test(fs.readFileSync(D,"utf8")))process.exit(0);const walk=d=>{let o=[];let es=[];try{es=fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true})}catch{return o}for(const e of es){const q=path.join(d,e.name);if(e.isDirectory()){if(e.name==="node_modules"||e.name===".next")continue;o=o.concat(walk(q))}else if(/\.tsx?$/.test(e.name))o.push(q)}return o};const re=/^\s*(import|const).*NICHE_FUNNEL_DESTINATIONS/m;const users=["lib","app","components"].flatMap(walk).filter(f=>!/definitions\.ts$/.test(f)&&!/\.test\.tsx?$/.test(f)).filter(f=>{try{return re.test(fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8"))}catch{return false}});console.error("importers="+users.join(","));process.exit(users.length>0?0:1)'
verify.note: Measures IMPORTERS, not string mentions: a comment naming the map is not a consumer of it, and the first version of this probe was fooled by exactly that. Passes when a non-test module actually imports the destination map, or when the map is deleted outright. Pure node since 2026-09-07: the earlier version shelled out to grep, and scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts runs the guard with every binary but node stripped from PATH, where a probe that cannot run reads as a verdict. It still cannot see a wrapper-based reader, which is the blind spot the close paragraph names.

entries.title: Two call-to-action verbs, one per reader, and a guard that found two more labels than the audit did
entries.detail:
LIVE-151 fixed the mechanical half (the home page stopped overriding the label, the secondary stopped apologising) and deliberately left the bigger call: whether "Start a Circle" should be the site-wide primary at all. The owner settled it: "start a circle does not have to be the primary thing. circles are what all the groups run on, but there doesn't have to be specific rules."

So the set is two verbs, each named for the reader it addresses, rather than one global default any page could override:
  SEEKER    "Find your people" -> /join      the guides, /discover, the-community, about
  OPERATOR  "Start free"       -> /pricing   /pricing, /spaces, the /for/<niche> doors

⚪ THE SEEKER VERB IS NOT NEW COPY. "Find your people" already ships as the eyebrow on /discover/circles and /discover/places and in the Nearby quick links, so this makes the CTA agree with the site rather than adding a phrase to it. Circles stay the mechanic every group runs on; they are simply not what a first-time reader is asked to do, and "Start a Circle" was the hardest ask on the site sitting under six guides whose readers had searched for help making friends.

⚪ ONE VERB CHANGE REACHED ~28 SURFACES, because they already read one constant. Only the operator pages needed hand-editing, and FUNNEL_CTA_LABEL stopped being a third independent literal and now derives from the operator constant.

🔴 THE GUARD FOUND TWO MORE THAN THE AUDIT DID, ON ITS FIRST RUN. The audit counted five labels by reading; lib/site.cta.test.ts counted SEVEN by measuring, adding "Find your way in" on /about and "Follow the build" on /the-lab. /about was a seeker acquisition CTA wearing a bespoke verb and now takes the approved one. /the-lab is the one named exception and is not an acquisition CTA at all: it sells a room planned for 2028, its own hero says nothing is bookable, and its primary asks you to follow a build. Putting "Find your people" there would promise a room that does not exist. The exemption is scoped to the one file and ratcheted, so a second page cannot inherit it. A count made by reading is a lower bound; a count made by a guard is the number.

⚠️ THE FRONT DOOR DID NOT MOVE, and cannot from here. app/page.tsx renders a published DB document, so the constant change does not reach it (LIVE-148).

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='lib/site.ts',T='lib/site.cta.test.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8');const two=/APPROVED_CTA_LABELS/.test(s)&&/OPERATOR_CTA_LABEL/.test(s);const f=fs.readFileSync('lib/marketing/funnel-config.ts','utf8');const derived=/FUNNEL_CTA_LABEL[^=]*=\\s*OPERATOR_CTA_LABEL/.test(f);process.exit(two&&derived?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when the approved set exists as data AND the niche doors derive their label from it rather than declaring a third. The per-template sweep is enforced continuously by lib/site.cta.test.ts, which is the stronger half.

entries.title: The Connect column list named a column that does not exist, so payouts could never start
entries.detail:
COLS - the column list every Stripe Connect read shares - ended `..., email, display_name`, and public.profiles has never had an `email` column (the address lives on auth.users). PostgREST rejects a select naming an unknown column, so EVERY read through that constant returned { data: null, error: 42703 }. Every caller destructured only `data`, and a failed query is indistinguishable from a profile with no connected account.

Two consequences, both live on the day payouts were first switched on:
  1. getConnectStatus reported accountId null for a profile that HAD acct_1U47bWBBboHg5HWM, so /settings#payouts offered "Set up payouts" to an operator already onboarded.
  2. getOrCreateConnectedAccount never saw the existing account and took the CREATE branch on every click. The production log for the failing click reads "You must complete your platform profile to use Connect and create live connected accounts" - an error about a call that should never have been made at all.

FIXED: the list is now `satisfies readonly ProfileColumn[]` against the generated schema types, so re-adding a phantom column is a COMPILE error naming it (verified by mutation: TS2322). The create-or-reuse decision is extracted as the pure connectReadOutcome(), which refuses to decide when the read errored rather than treating null as "no account" - a failed read must never mint a duplicate Stripe account. lib/profiles/account-email.test.ts, the repo-wide guard written for this exact bug in an earlier incarnation, had two blind spots that let it through: it matched inline string selects only (missing `.select(COLS)`) and looked for the single name `email`. It now checks every named column against the generated types.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const c=fs.readFileSync('lib/billing/connect.ts','utf8');const g=fs.readFileSync('lib/profiles/account-email.test.ts','utf8');const bound=c.includes('satisfies readonly ProfileColumn[]');const pure=c.includes('export function connectReadOutcome');const refuses=/kind: 'unknown'/.test(c);const cols=g.includes('knownProfileColumns');process.exit(bound&&pure&&refuses&&cols?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when the column list is bound to the generated types, the create-or-reuse decision is pure and refuses on a failed read, and the repo-wide guard checks columns rather than one name.

entries.title: The Stripe Connect platform profile is incomplete, so no connected account can be created
entries.detail:
Production log, 2026-09-04 20:00:39Z, req_i1UvetWAbrrOM7:
  [settings/billing startPayoutOnboarding] You must complete your platform profile to use Connect and create live connected accounts. Visit your dashboard at https://dashboard.stripe.com/connect/accounts/overview to answer the questionnaire.

This is the SAME error ADR-1093 recorded on 2026-08-20. LIVE-152 removes the reason the app was calling accounts.create at all (it should reuse the existing acct_), so this may no longer block onboarding for a profile that already has an account - but it WILL block the first new operator, and it is owner-only to fix: the questionnaire is a Stripe dashboard form.

THE ANSWERS MATTER AND WERE WRONG LAST TIME (ADR-1093, tracked as LIVE-074). The profile on file says direct charges, fees_collector: account, losses_collector: stripe, dashboard: full - the STANDARD responsibility set. The code creates EXPRESS accounts (lib/billing/connect.ts) and uses DESTINATION charges in all four channels (tips, tickets, memberships, commerce). Answer to match the code, not the previous answers. ── 🔴 RECONCILED 2026-09-05: THIS IS THE SAME BLOCKER AS OWN-040's STRIPE ITEM, AND OWN-040 ALREADY SETTLED IT — differently. OWN-040's evidence, dated 2026-08-25 and marked "settled", reads: the Stripe dashboard shows 'Provide a valid identity document. We need a valid identity document for Joel Tyack to use Connect and create live connected accounts', with 'Create a live connected account' GREYED OUT. It then says explicitly: "Not funds flow, not a questionnaire, not the acknowledgements — all four earlier diagnoses on this row were wrong." This row and its twin call it a platform-profile QUESTIONNAIRE, which makes that the fifth wrong diagnosis of one blocker. ⚠️ WHY EVERYONE KEEPS GETTING IT WRONG, which is the part worth keeping: the Stripe API error text genuinely says "You must complete your platform profile to use Connect" and links the Connect overview. That message is GENERIC — it is what Stripe returns whenever the platform cannot create live connected accounts, whatever the underlying reason — so reading the diagnosis off the error string produces a questionnaire every time, while the dashboard names the actual requirement. Measure the dashboard, not the message. 📌 AND THE OWNER HAS ALREADY RULED: OWN-040 records it PARKED on owner instruction with a stated ETA — a driver's licence in hand ~late September 2026, the only document available, and the representative name is correct so there is nothing to fix meanwhile. The instruction was "open as work, not surfaced as an ask". So this needs NO new owner decision and should not be re-raised as one; it waits on a document in the post. Everything else on the payout path is ready.

── OWNER-GATE RE-TESTED 2026-09-07 (the 26-row triage). CLOSED as a DUPLICATE, not as work done. This is the same Stripe Connect blocker OWN-040 carries, and OWN-040 already records the reconciliation (an identity document, not a questionnaire) plus the owner park and ETA. Two rows for one owner ask means the ask gets read twice and actioned once; OWN-040 is the one that stays.

verify.evidence: A connected account can be created end to end: /settings#payouts starts Stripe onboarding without a platform-profile error, and profiles.stripe_details_submitted flips true for the completing account. ── 2026-09-05: superseded in diagnosis by OWN-040 (identity document for the platform representative, not the questionnaire), which the owner parked with an ETA of ~late September 2026. Closes when a host reaches Stripe-hosted onboarding from /settings/billing and profiles.stripe_details_submitted flips true — measured today as 1 profile with a stripe_account_id and 0 with details submitted.

entries.title: Swallowed PostgREST errors silently reverse decisions in the money and permission paths

source.ref: ADR-1198, the sweep that followed LIVE-152

entries.detail:
LIVE-152 was one instance of a pattern: `const { data } = await db()...` with `error` neither destructured nor checked. A PostgREST error arrives in `error`, not as a throw, so a try/catch documented as "FAIL-SAFE on any error" does not engage - the code silently takes the data-is-null branch instead.

83 such reads exist. Most degrade to an empty list, which is harmless. These do not, ranked by how wrong the answer is:
  1. lib/commerce/reviews.ts:173 - a failed read defaults status to 'visible', UN-HIDING a review an operator moderated. The comment three lines above says moderation must be durable "else moderation is trivially reversible by the author".
  2. lib/billing/space-subscriptions.ts:155 - priorSubscriptionId null means a canceled subscription never lapses founding status, so a Space keeps a founding rate it stopped paying for.
  3. lib/billing/tickets.ts:382 and lib/commerce/checkout.ts:75 - membership_tier null prices at the free rung, charging a Crew seller 10% instead of 8%.
  4. lib/billing/checkout.ts:56,220 and space-plan-checkout.ts:246 and bundle-checkout.ts:65 - stripe_customer_id null mints a DUPLICATE Stripe customer per checkout; at :220 createBillingPortal tells a paying member they have no billing to manage.
  5. lib/billing/tickets.ts:211 - tier defaults to 'free' behind the member_only gate, denying a paying Crew member their own ticket.
  6. lib/pricing/gamification-access.ts:76 - a full-access paid member is downgraded to earn_only.
  7. lib/pricing/dunning.ts:36 - fails OPEN: a past_due member never sees the recovery banner and keeps access.

Not a mechanical sweep: each needs a direction decided (fail open or closed) and stated. Do the money ones first.

── ✅ DONE 2026-09-06 (fan-out slice C). Nine sites, and the point of the row was honoured: each one now DESTRUCTURES `error`, checks it, logs through the repo's `[module]` convention, and carries a `DIRECTION —` comment saying which way it fails and why that wrong answer is the smaller one. The `data === null` with no error path is untouched everywhere; only the UNKNOWN case changed.

THE DIRECTIONS, because the row said each needed deciding and stating: reviews upsert FAILS CLOSED ON THE WRITE (refusing does not reverse an operator's hide, and does not silently bury a first review either); space-subscriptions THROWS rather than guessing, because both guesses are permanent and invisible and only the webhook calls it — Stripe redelivers into an idempotent reconcile, and the throw is placed BEFORE the update that would overwrite the prior id; the two fee-tier reads (tickets, commerce checkout) FAIL CLOSED ON THE TRANSACTION; the four Stripe customer-id reads FAIL CLOSED, because a duplicate customer is a permanent split identity that nothing untangles afterwards; gamification-access FAILS OPEN to 'full' per its own module header; dunning FAILS OPEN unchanged — what changed is that it is now a decision rather than an accident, and it logs.

🔴 ONE POLICY WAS REVERSED, NOT MADE EXPLICIT, and it is the one to review: tickets.ts:408 and commerce/checkout.ts:91 both carried "fail-safe … prices at the free rung (never under-collect)". They now abort the checkout, on the judgement that charging a Crew host 10% on a rate they paid to buy down to 8% takes real money on a contract we could not verify and stays invisible until they audit receipts, while refusing costs one retryable checkout. ⚪ The commerce/checkout.ts half is DEAD DEFENSIVE CODE today — createCommerceCheckout gates on canTakePayments, which is space||platform only — so the live exposure was tickets.ts alone.

TESTS: 10 files, 38 new tests, and 19 of them were RUN AGAINST THE OLD BEHAVIOUR AND CONFIRMED TO FAIL first; the ones that pass both ways are labelled controls rather than counted as proof.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const f=['lib/commerce/reviews.ts','lib/billing/space-subscriptions.ts','lib/billing/tickets.ts','lib/billing/checkout.ts'];const bad=f.filter(p=>{const s=fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8');return !/const \\{ data, error \\}/.test(s)});process.exit(bad.length===0?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when the four highest-severity files destructure `error` at all. A coarse gate on purpose: it measures that someone looked, and each fix still has to choose a direction.

entries.title: A synced Stripe price id carries no account or livemode, so a foreign price is indistinguishable from a missing one
entries.detail:
pricing_stripe_prices.stripe_price_id is a bare text column. Nothing records WHICH Stripe account or livemode minted it, and resolveStripePriceId does no validation - the id goes straight into checkout.sessions.create. If the platform's secret key is ever rotated to a different account (a new license, a test/live swap), every row silently points at a foreign price and Stripe answers "No such price", which is indistinguishable from a transient outage: viaStripe renders "Stripe could not complete that just now" on both.

billingEnabled() is only "is STRIPE_SECRET_KEY set" - it does not care which account. Verified 2026-09-04: all four plan rows (business_base and collective_base, month and year) are present and unarchived, synced 2026-08-19, so nothing is broken TODAY. The gap is that nothing would tell us if it were.

ADR-1085's own lesson applies - the guard belongs before the write rather than in a report afterwards: record the account id and livemode on the row at sync time and refuse to resolve a row minted by a different account than the live key.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P1 on 2026-09-07 in the full re-prioritisation pass: a money class that fails silently: a synced Stripe price id carries no account or livemode, so a FOREIGN price is indistinguishable from a missing one. That is a wrong-money answer waiting for the first environment mix-up.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1227), THE GUARD BEFORE THE WRITE AND THE REFUSAL AT THE READ. Migration 20270345002000 adds two nullable columns to pricing_stripe_prices, `stripe_account_id` and `livemode`. upsertStripePrice stamps every row it writes with the identity of the key in force — the account from one memoised `accounts.retrieve()` and the mode read off the key prefix (Stripe puts the mode on the key, not the account) — and the retired-key archive pass re-saves a row with the provenance it already carries rather than claiming it. resolveStripePriceId compares the row against the key in force through the PURE `priceProvenance()`: a row whose RECORDED account or mode contradicts a KNOWN half of the live key is FOREIGN, refused (null, i.e. "not synced", so checkout no-ops instead of charging) and named in one `billing.price.foreign` log line carrying the key, the price id, and both identities. Two fail-safes are deliberate: an unstamped row (both nulls, i.e. synced before this change) resolves exactly as before, and an UNKNOWN live half never convicts, so a transient account lookup failure cannot switch billing off — livemode alone decides.

RUNS BEFORE AND AFTER THE MIGRATION, which matters because merging deploys: the read goes through select('*') and a missing column reads as null (unstamped), and the write casts through the Insert type, so on a tree ahead of the migration the next SYNC fails with the missing-column message — the operator's cue to apply it — while every checkout keeps resolving. Eleven unit tests in lib/billing/pricing-prices.test.ts pin the verdict table, the log line, the pre-migration read shape, and the stamp on write; the three sync/checkout suites that mock ./stripe carry the two new exports.

⚠️ THE MIGRATION IS IN THE TREE AND NOT YET APPLIED (supabase/migrations/README.md: apply, then record). Until it is, every row stays unstamped and the resolver is exactly as permissive as it was; the first re-sync after applying stamps all four plan rows.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=fs.readFileSync('lib/billing/pricing-prices.ts','utf8');process.exit(/livemode|stripe_account/.test(s)?0:1)"
verify.note: Passes when a synced price row records the account or livemode it came from, so a foreign id can be named rather than guessed at. CLOSED 2026-09-07: the module records both, and lib/billing/pricing-prices.test.ts pins that a foreign row resolves to null with a named log line.

entries.title: Spec every capability bundle, and re-review the 22-key function registry beside it
entries.detail:
Owner ruling: before any bundle ships, write a full spec per bundle and review the FUNCTION REGISTRY at the same time. The two are one decision. A bundle is defined by what it omits, so naming the omissions is a statement about lib/spaces/functions.ts — whether 22 keys are the right 22, whether any should merge, split or retire, and which are genuinely optional rather than structural.

WHY THIS BLOCKS LIVE-149 RATHER THAN THE OTHER WAY AROUND. The mechanism is finished and proven: CAPABILITY_BUNDLES + nextBlobsForBundle + setSpaceBundle, with the three-state entitlement read underneath so a bundle can subtract a tool from a Space whose plan pays for it. What does not exist is curation, and wiring provision to a registry holding one pass-through row would put a permanent no-op branch in the Space-creation path, the highest-risk path in the product.

THE EVIDENCE TO BRING. Of 21 real operator Spaces roughly 18 are solo wellness practitioners, and coaches-and-healers is the only /for/ door that has produced a customer. That is the one bundle with anything behind it; every other would be a guess, which is exactly why the mechanism shipped without curation.

DELIVERABLE: a row per bundle in lib/pricing/bundles.ts with its function list and any role floors, plus a recorded decision for each of the 22 function keys (keep / merge / retire / make structural). LIVE-149's provision call ships in the same change as the first curated bundle, never before it.

── PREMISE RE-DERIVED 2026-09-08 (premise sweep, ADR-1269) and it HOLDS: `SPACE_FUNCTIONS` in lib/spaces/functions.ts declares exactly **22** keys (crm, email, members, qr, availability, memberships, donations, enroll, tickets, checkin, shop, billing, profile, reviews, events, airwaves, practices, journeys, circles, loom, collaborators, program), and lib/pricing/bundles.ts still ships the one pass-through `general` bundle. Production holds 22 Spaces against the "21 real operator Spaces" the evidence paragraph cites — close enough not to change the argument, and worth re-counting by hand when the bundles are actually curated.

verify.evidence: CAPABILITY_BUNDLES holds more than the pass-through row, each bundle has a written spec, and every function key carries a recorded keep/merge/retire decision.

entries.title: The RLS-bypass justifications are byte-present but no longer attached to the entries they justify
entries.detail:
A whole-file lexicographic sort has run over scripts/admin-client-baseline.txt at some point, taking the 80-line comment block with it. Three independent proofs: 78 of the 79 adjacent comment pairs are in alphabetical order (the single exception is a hand-insert from 2026-09-04); the script's own five header lines, written in order 1-2-3-4-5, sit at lines 45/46/51/47/63, which is exactly their lexicographic order and no writer produces that; and the prose no longer parses — line 24 ends '...the autonomy ladder is' and its continuation sits at line 3.

So the reasoning for each RLS bypass is still in the file and no longer says which bypass it is about. Four commented lines that read like entries are also real live entries, i.e. surviving heads of shredded paragraphs.

SCAN-537 stopped it getting worse (--update preserves the block now). This row is the repair, and it is NOT mechanical: reassembling 80 shredded lines into per-entry paragraphs needs someone who knows the tenancy model to decide which sentence belongs to which bypass. git log on the file is 3 commits deep and the 823 lines arrived in one commit, so the pre-sort original cannot be recovered from this repository.

Worth considering alongside: make --update REFUSE when the header's line count would shrink, as belt and braces. That changes CLI behaviour, so it is a decision rather than a patch.

── PREMISE RE-TESTED AND CLOSED 2026-09-07. The row said the prose was unrecoverable because the damage was three commits back. `git log -- scripts/admin-client-baseline.txt` returns 33 commits; the intact 819-line version is at 3707bf53a and the damage landed in 7dc03d8b1. Re-sized M -> S on that alone.

TWO THINGS THE ROW DID NOT KNOW, and the second changed the fix. (1) It was not a plain sort, it was `sort -u`, which deduped two of the three bare `#` separator lines — the comment count was 80 before and after only because the two lost separators were offset by two new one-liners. (2) The original had three justification blocks BELOW the first entry, and readHeader() in scripts/check-admin-client.mjs preserves ONLY the leading block. A literal restore would therefore have re-armed the exact loss mode SCAN-537 fixed: the next --update would have silently deleted them again.

SO THE RESTORE IS NOT LITERAL, DELIBERATELY. All 88 header lines now sit above the first entry in chronological order (08-11 -> 08-25). Zero old justification lines missing, zero prose invented, and the 749-line entry list byte-identical in order and content. Two lines were ADDED — `#   scripts/check-authz-guards.test.ts` and `#   lib/billing/space-beta-grant.ts` — because those two blocks named their subject file only by POSITION, so flattening them into the header would otherwise have cut the link; they are anchors in the file's own indented-path style. check-admin-client.mjs reads 749 importers against a baseline of 749, exit 0; its test suite 8/8.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const p="scripts/admin-client-baseline.txt";if(!fs.existsSync(p))process.exit(79);const lines=fs.readFileSync(p,"utf8").split("\n");const firstEntry=lines.findIndex(l=>l.trim()&&!l.startsWith("#"));if(firstEntry<0)process.exit(79);const header=lines.slice(0,firstEntry);const below=lines.slice(firstEntry).filter(l=>l.startsWith("#"));const words=header.join(" ").split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length;const bad=[];if(words<250)bad.push("header prose collapsed to "+words+" words: the justifications were sorted away again");if(below.length)bad.push(below.length+" comment line(s) sit BELOW the first entry, where readHeader() drops them on the next --update");if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join("; "));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)'
verify.note: Measures the two consequences, not the words. (1) The header still carries real prose (>=250 words) — a re-sort collapses it, which is what 7dc03d8b1 did. (2) NO comment line survives below the first entry, because readHeader() preserves only the leading block, so anything below it is deleted by the next --update: that is the loss mode, and keeping the file out of it is the actual fix. Exits 79 if the file or its entry list is gone. Live arm: the pre-restore file fails arm 1.

entries.title: Directory opt-out, Ghost mode and the discoverability tier were enforced in one RPC and bypassed by six member listings; the RPC ignored the target radius and the connections tier
entries.detail: members_near enforced directory_visible / ghost_mode / discoverable_by; /network, /search, the command-palette people search and three sidebar rails were service-role reads filtering on is_active only. The RPC also never read the target's discovery_radius_m (the slider governed the viewer's own search, the opposite of its label) and required discoverable_by='community', so the connections tier meant no one. Closed 2026-09-04: one predicate module mirrors the RPC clause by clause and is applied at all six listings; migration 20270344000100 (applied) honours the target radius, resolves connections as an accepted friendship with _viewer, and re-locks grants. The season leaderboard rail is the one named exemption (own opt-out).

entries.title: Member suspension was enforced by one trigger on two tables that the app bypassed as service_role; it now reaches 32 member-write tables with no role bypass
entries.detail: enforce_member_not_suspended was attached to posts and dispatches and opened with `if auth.role() = 'service_role' then return new`, while the compose path inserts posts through the admin client: enforcement on zero paths in practice. Migration 20270344000000 (applied) rewrites the function to read the actor column by name (a misattached column raises undefined_column on first write), drops the bypass, keeps honouring suspended_until, and attaches BEFORE INSERT to 32 tables and BEFORE UPDATE OF content columns where an edit is a fresh contribution. The coverage ledger derives the universe from the schema types and fails when a member-write table is on neither list; pgTAP covers the raise in db-tests.

entries.title: Nothing in CI regenerates or diffs lib/database.types.ts against the live schema; a report-only gen-types drift step is drafted and not wired
entries.detail:
HYG-051 was found by hand. The #2351 technique (satisfies readonly Column[]) proves code agrees with the FILE, not that the file agrees with the DATABASE.

── CLOSED 2026-09-07, and the run that proved the gate also found the drift it was built for. `lib/database.types.ts` was regenerated from the live project and compared: FIVE objects disagreed. `Functions.merge_profile_meta` and `Functions.remove_profile_meta_keys` existed in the database and not in the file at all; `Functions.award_gems_atomic` had gained a second overload taking `_day_key` and `_timezone`; `Functions.claim_outbox_jobs` had gained a `dedupe_key` field; `Functions.mark_signup_lead_converted` had changed shape. Migrations had been applied and the types were never regenerated beside them, and nothing anywhere went red — because every gate in this repo checks that the CODE agrees with the FILE and not one checked that the FILE agrees with the DATABASE. That is a whole class, not one file: coverage that cannot fail (ADR-970).

The regenerated file is committed and `tsc --noEmit` is clean against it, so the drift was additive and nothing in the tree leaned on the stale picture.

⚠️ THE PROBE THIS ROW SHIPPED WITH MEASURED THE WRONG THING and was rewritten rather than satisfied. It asserted the literal string `gen types` appeared in maintenance.yml, which pins ONE implementation — the CLI — and would have been satisfied by a comment. The step is wired the way its three siblings are, a token-gated fetch of the Management API's types endpoint feeding a script that consumes JSON and never touches a database, so it stays testable without one. The probe now asserts the consequence: the script exists, its test exists, and the workflow actually invokes the script.

⚪ WHAT WAS NOT PROVED, stated because the row asked for it. The row prescribed comparing `supabase gen types --project-id` output against the CLI's `--linked` output byte for byte. That comparison was NOT run: the fetch goes through the Management API, which is what the sibling steps use and what the CLI itself calls. What WAS proved is stronger in the direction that matters — the API output typechecks clean across the whole repo and its diff against the committed file named five real database objects.

⚠️ THE DETECTOR IGNORES ORDER ON PURPOSE. The generator's object order is stable per run but not across versions of it: on the first real run `cron_run_markers` moved about 390 lines with no schema change behind it. Comparing by named object rather than by byte answers the question actually being asked. Leading indentation is NOT ignored, because it encodes nesting depth — the same `id: string` under a table, under its Insert, and under a function's Args are three different facts.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const need=['scripts/maintenance/types-drift.mjs','scripts/maintenance/types-drift.test.ts'];for(const f of need)if(!fs.existsSync(f))throw new Error('missing '+f);const wf=fs.readFileSync('.github/workflows/maintenance.yml','utf8');if(!/types-drift\.mjs/.test(wf))throw new Error('maintenance.yml does not invoke the types-drift script');if(!/types\/typescript/.test(wf))throw new Error('maintenance.yml does not fetch the generated types');const s=fs.readFileSync('scripts/maintenance/types-drift.mjs','utf8');if(!/driftedObjects/.test(s))throw new Error('the detector no longer compares by named object');"

entries.detail: checkout.session.completed gated the setTier write on a denylist (space plan/membership, bundle, founders). A commerce order (mode 'payment', kind 'commerce_order', client_reference_id = buyer) matched none and fell through to setTier(buyer, 'crew', 'active') - a paid tier with no subscription to cancel it, and the payout take-rate rung follows membership_tier. lib/billing/checkout.ts:122 already had the allowlist (mode 'subscription' and no kind) and claimed to mirror the webhook. entries.title: Should a Circle or Space mute also silence RSVP confirmations, guest-approval confirmations, cancellation notices and RSVP reminders?
entries.detail:
When mutes were wired to a subject (SCAN-548), the RSVP lifecycle sends were deliberately left unmuted: the member asked for them by RSVPing, and a Circle mute swallowing a cancellation notice would strand someone at a venue. Outreach and broadcast platform lanes have no single subject in scope either. If a mute should mean all of it, say so and the four sites get a subject.

── PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-09-08 (premise sweep, ADR-1269) and it HOLDS: the RSVP confirmation still calls `sendSms({ profileId, category: 'events', body, timeZone })` at app/(main)/events/actions.ts:872 with no `subject`, and lib/comms/send-gate.ts:185 only consults `isSubjectTopicMuted` when one is passed. So a Circle or Space mute still does not reach the RSVP lifecycle sends, exactly as described.

verify.evidence: lib/events/dispatch.ts passes a subject on push and email; the RSVP confirmation, approval, cancellation and reminder sends do not, by design (W6 report, 2026-09-04).
