entries.title: The calendar strip compares recurrence_until at day granularity while both recurrence mirrors compare at the instant, so it shows a chip for an occurrence that is never materialised

source.ref: ADR-807 carries the ruling (recurrence_until resolves through the zone to the RRULE UNTIL instant, shipped by lib/events/ics.ts); ADR-1206 is the parity test that found the strip disagreeing with it

entries.detail:
Found by the recurrence parity test (2026-09-04). The event form stores until via dateToWallClockIso as YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z; for a weekly 7 pm series ending 2027-06-24 the write and read mirrors give [06-10, 06-17] and the strip's stepKey gives [06-10, 06-17, 06-24]. Which end-date rule is intended (inclusive day vs instant) is an owner ruling; the two disagreeing fixtures are pinned it.fails in lib/events/recurrence-parity.test.ts so aligning either side turns them red and forces the marker to be removed here.

── OWNER-GATE RE-TESTED 2026-09-07 (the 26-row triage). THE RULING ALREADY EXISTS IN THE ADR RECORD, so there is nothing to decide. docs/DECISIONS.md states it plainly: "recurrence_until resolves through the zone to the same instant the RRULE UNTIL carries", and the published .ics feeds ship that behaviour today. So the calendar mirrors are canon and lib/events/calendar-repeats.ts, which compares at DAY granularity, is the outlier. Aligning the strip to the feeds is a code fix. Only the OPPOSITE direction would need a ruling, because that would change live calendar feeds.
── CLOSED 2026-09-07. The premise held exactly as written, measured before anything was touched: for a weekly 7pm series until 2027-06-24 the write mirror gives [06-10, 06-17] and the strip gave [06-10, 06-17, 06-24]; for a monthly series until 2027-08-15T11:59:59.999Z the mirror gives [06-15, 07-15] and the strip gave a third chip at 08-15. Cause located: computeSeriesDayKeys bounded with a DAY-STRING compare (key > untilKey) while lib/event-recurrence.ts and lib/events/recurrence.ts both compare cursor.getTime() > seriesEnd.getTime().

🔴 ONE CORRECTION TO THIS ROW: the ruling is in ADR-807 (the calendar-feeds ADR), NOT ADR-1206, which this row's source.ref cited. ADR-1206 is the parity-test ADR that FOUND the divergence. Verified independently: lib/events/ics.ts resolves recurrence_until through the zone into the RRULE UNTIL instant, with the comment "UNTIL must be the TRUE UTC instant (RFC 5545)", so the published feeds ship the instant rule today and the strip was the outlier. The row's ref now cites both.

THE FIX, strip only, mirrors and feeds untouched: a private stepInstant(start, cadence, step) carries the wall clock through the same UTC-parts arithmetic stepKey already used, so it is byte-for-byte occurrenceAt from both mirrors, and the until bound became an instant compare. Everything the module RETURNS is still a day key; only the bound moved. The old day bound is kept as a deliberate fallback when starts_at or recurrence_until will not parse, rather than dropping the bound entirely.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const r=(f)=>fs.existsSync(f)?fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8'):'';process.exit(/it\.fails\(/.test(r('lib/events/recurrence-parity.test.ts'))?1:0)"
verify.note: Passes when the parity test no longer carries an it.fails marker, i.e. the strip and the mirrors agree. Fails today. Verified 2026-09-07 by re-running the probe (exit 0, no it.fails remains) and by four mutation readings that pin BOTH directions: unfixed source + markers = green (96 passed, 6 expected-fail); fixed source + markers still on = 6 failed with "Expect test to fail", so the gate fires; unfixed source + markers removed = 6 failed, so the test is red against the defect; fixed + removed = 102 passed. pnpm vitest run lib/events: 56 files, 911 tests, 0 failed.

entries.title: The Studio edit rail does not derive from field placement: inlineFields() and railFields() have no production consumer

source.ref: ADR-450 (the one verb, two planes model); AGENTS.md correction of 2026-09-04

entries.detail:
AGENTS.md said a field's placement (spark / inline / rail) is the ONE seam between creating and editing, so the two can never drift. Verified 2026-09-04: only sparkFields() is consumed (by the Spark). inlineFields() and railFields() in the review kernel appear only in their own test, so of 272 field paths the 40 inline, 3 rail and 179 defaulting to rail sit on planes nothing renders, and nothing prevents an edit rail from drifting from the manifest. The contract is right; the wiring is not there. Close this by making the entity edit rail (and the inline editors) read their field set from railFields()/inlineFields() of the registered manifest, so a manifest change is the whole change on both planes, as STUDIO.md promises.

── ⏳ 2026-09-07 (ADR-1240): PREMISE RE-TESTED AND HALF CLOSED. Confirmed: inlineFields() and railFields() had no production consumer, and the four hand-declared rails (practice, circle, event, journey settings modules) each restated their fields with their own labels and, for the Practice, three fields on the wrong plane (title, summary, description are inline on the manifest and rendered in the rail because /practices/[id] has no inline canvas yet). The seam now exists: lib/studio/kernel/edit-plan.ts exposes editPlan(manifest) and railForm(manifest, writes, { hostInline }), and the only thing a rail form says for itself is the columns its save action writes. The PRACTICE rail is wired (components/admin/modules/practice-rail-plan.ts, consumed by practice-settings-module.tsx through the new RailManifestFields renderer and the field kit’s new native `name`); practice-rail-plan.test.ts pins the same seven fields in the same three zones, zero dropped columns, and the drift case. WHAT REMAINS, and why it is not one sitting: the Circle rail renders `name` (a spark-only field on no edit plane) and its columns are snake_case while the manifest paths are camelCase (member_cap vs memberCap); the Event rail is a 790-line form with tiers, co-hosts, a venue autocomplete, and the same path mismatch (starts_at vs startsAt, price vs priceCents); the Journey rail mounts the 6-section JourneySettings editor whole. Each needs a column-to-path map beside its plan and, for Circle and Event, a kernel ruling on where a non-prose spark field is edited later (the manifest comment says "also editable later" and the selectors put it on no plane). The probe below now measures the remaining consequence: it passes only when all four Guided entities render their rail from a `*-rail-plan.ts`.

── ⏳ 2026-09-07 (ADR-1246): THE JOURNEY RAIL CONVERTED, two remain. components/admin/modules/journey-rail-plan.ts is JOURNEY_MANIFEST through railForm() in six zones, one per save path (identity via saveJourneyMeta with hostInline; header via saveJourneyMeta; delivery via setJourneyRewards + setJourneyDelivery; visibility via setJourneyVisibility; attributes via setJourneyAttributes; meeting via setJourneyMeeting), and journey-settings-module.tsx renders it through RailManifestFields instead of mounting the 700-line JourneySettings editor whole (that editor still serves /journeys/[slug]/edit). Because the Journey's actions take JSON patches, the plan carries the column-to-key maps ADR-1240 anticipated (journeyMetaPatch, journeyAttributesPatch, journeyMeetingPatch, ...), each pinned by journey-rail-plan.test.ts, and the rail's initial values read off the plan row by manifest path (journeyRailValues). The manifest gained the three columns the rail persisted without declaring (logo_image, header_overlay_style, header_overlay_color); cover_focus stays a property of the cover control, not a field. Visible changes are the manifest's words winning: Name, One-line promise, Logo or profile image, Header overlay, Days between Phases, Who can see it as a select, Difficulty as a select, and the two touchpoints headed by the manifest's own section titles; a touchpoint's location and join link now always show (the manifest declares no hide-by-format rule), and the linked Event is the kit's reference select over listMyJourneyEvents. WHAT REMAINS: Circle and Event, both of which render spark-only, non-prose fields the selectors place on no edit plane (the Circle's `name`; the Event's `starts_at` and `location`, beside its snake_case-to-camelCase path mismatch), so each first needs the kernel ruling ADR-1240 deferred (where a non-prose spark field is edited later) before a plan can honour its writes. The probe now names only those two.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const dir="components/admin/modules/";const ents=["circle","event"];const ok=ents.every(e=>{const plan=dir+e+"-rail-plan.ts";const mod=dir+e+"-settings-module.tsx";if(!fs.existsSync(plan)||!fs.existsSync(mod))return false;return /\brailForm\(/.test(fs.readFileSync(plan,"utf8"))&&fs.readFileSync(mod,"utf8").includes("./"+e+"-rail-plan")});process.exit(ok?0:1)'
verify.note: Passes only when the two Guided entities still hand-declaring (circle, event) each have a <entity>-rail-plan.ts that calls the kernel railForm() AND their settings module imports that plan, i.e. every rail derives its fields from placement. Practice (2026-09-07, ADR-1240) and Journey (2026-09-07, ADR-1246) already derive and are pinned by practice-rail-plan.test.ts and journey-rail-plan.test.ts under pnpm test; Circle and Event each wait on the spark-only ruling, so this fails until they are wired.

entries.title: Register the Stripe webhook endpoint for this deployment (zero events have ever arrived)
entries.detail:
Scan two (2026-09-05, runtime lane): stripe_webhook_events has held 0 rows for the life of the table and no request reached /api/webhooks/stripe in the 24h read, while checkout, tiers, orders, tips, Supporter contributions and Connect all depend on that webhook to record a completed payment. Either nothing has ever been paid for, or the endpoint is not registered for frequencylocal.com in the Stripe dashboard (Developers > Webhooks). If it is missing, every paid flow completes on Stripe and never lands in the ledger. Check the endpoint exists, points at https://frequencylocal.com/api/webhooks/stripe, subscribes to checkout.session.completed, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded, checkout.session.async_payment_failed, charge.refunded, customer.subscription.*, and that STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in Vercel matches it. Then send a test event from the dashboard and confirm one row appears in stripe_webhook_events. ── 📌 RE-MEASURED 2026-09-05 (after the sweep-3 deploy): stripe_webhook_events is STILL 0 rows. The premise holds. Related and worth reading together: 1 profile carries a stripe_account_id and 0 have stripe_details_submitted true, which is consistent with payouts never having completed onboarding (OWN-053 / LIVE-153) rather than with payments arriving and going unrecorded.

── PREMISE RE-MEASURED 2026-09-08 (premise sweep, ADR-1269) and it HOLDS, third consecutive reading: `public.stripe_webhook_events` is still **0 rows**. Nothing has changed since 2026-09-05. This is the only P0 on the list and it is one dashboard page.

entries.title: Set EMAIL_CONVERSATION_FROM in Vercel to a bare verified address on the conversational subdomain
entries.detail:
Six conversational From builders (CRM replies, leader replies, Space conversations, the inbound bridge, batched replies) read EMAIL_CONVERSATION_FROM and fall back to EMAIL_FROM. EMAIL_FROM is documented in the 'Frequency <noreply@...>' form, so the fallback yields a nested 'Name via Frequency <Frequency <noreply@...>>' header that Resend rejects or the receiver bounces. Phase D of the scan-two repairs makes the code extract the bare address whatever the shape; this row is the config half: set EMAIL_CONVERSATION_FROM to the bare verified address (people@people.frequencylocal.com or whichever domain is verified in Resend) in Production and Preview. No conversational email has been sent yet (comms_messages has 0 rows), so this is latent until the first reply. ── 🔴 BOTH OF THIS ROW'S PREMISES WERE WRONG, MEASURED 2026-09-05. (1) "No conversational email has been sent yet (comms_messages has 0 rows), so this is latent" — comms_messages holds 12 rows, all 2026-07-24/25: 6 outbound email delivery_status 'sent', 3 inbound 'sent', 1 inbound 'received', 1 internal note, 1 internal email. So the path has already run END TO END in both directions and outbound was accepted. Whatever From it used was deliverable; this is not an untested path waiting for its first send. (2) The row offers "people@people.frequencylocal.com or whichever domain is verified in Resend" as the value to set. `people.frequencylocal.com` HAS NO DNS AT ALL — no MX, no TXT, no `resend._domainkey` — and neither does `reply.frequencylocal.com`, the documented CONVERSATION_REPLY_DOMAIN default. Public DNS says the ONE verified Resend sending domain is `send.frequencylocal.com`: it carries the Resend DKIM key at resend._domainkey.send.frequencylocal.com, its MAIL FROM subdomain MXes to feedback-smtp.us-east-1.amazonses.com, and SPF resolves to include:amazonses.com (pnpm check:mail-dns). ⚠️ SO THE ANSWER IS ONE LINE, not research: EMAIL_CONVERSATION_FROM should be a BARE address on a domain that is actually verified — `send.frequencylocal.com` today — unless the owner first adds and verifies `people.frequencylocal.com` in Resend and publishes its records. Setting it to the people@ address the code names would send from a domain with no DKIM, under an apex DMARC of p=quarantine. 📌 lib/comms/from-address.ts:20 hardcodes that same non-existent domain as DEFAULT_CONVERSATION_ADDRESS. It is a THIRD-level fallback (EMAIL_CONVERSATION_FROM, then EMAIL_FROM, then this), so it likely never fires while EMAIL_FROM is set — but it is a default pointing at a domain that does not exist, and it is left alone here deliberately: changing where the product sends human replies from is the owner's call, not a cleanup. `pnpm check:mail-dns` now measures both conversational domains so this stays answerable by command.

── OWNER-GATE RE-TESTED 2026-09-07 (the 26-row triage). CLOSED: both premises are dead. The code half shipped - conversationAddress() in lib/comms/from-address.ts extracts the bare address out of EMAIL_FROM, so the people@people... default this row feared can no longer be constructed. And the live send proves EMAIL_FROM is already set to a verified-domain sender rather than the default. What is left is an identity preference, not a defect, and a preference does not need a backlog row.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-05: comms_messages = 12 rows (not 0), 2026-07-24/25, 6 outbound 'sent' + 4 inbound. DNS: people.frequencylocal.com and reply.frequencylocal.com resolve nothing (no MX/TXT/DKIM); send.frequencylocal.com is the verified Resend domain per pnpm check:mail-dns. Closes when EMAIL_CONVERSATION_FROM is set in Vercel to a bare address on a verified domain and one reply lands with a single From header.

entries.title: Confirm the production values of the four feature gates that decide whether shipped features are on
entries.detail:
Four environment gates turn whole shipped features on or off and their production values are not visible from the repo: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_CHAT ('1' mounts the live-chat widget, and it is a BUILD-time flag with no runtime check of CONVERSATION_TOKEN_SECRET, so '1' without the secret 500s the chat token route), SMS_PROVISIONING_ENABLED (Twilio number provisioning for Spaces), CONVERSATION_EMAIL_BRIDGE (inbound email replies into conversations), AI_DISABLED (kills Vera and every generation path). Read each in the Vercel project settings for Production, decide which should be on, and note the four values here so the next scan can compare code defaults against intent. If NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_CHAT is '1', CONVERSATION_TOKEN_SECRET must also be set. ── ✅ THREE OF THE FOUR ANSWERED 2026-09-05 WITHOUT DASHBOARD ACCESS, by measuring consequences rather than reading env. The row said "Vercel get_project exposes no env names to an agent", which is true and was treated as the end of the enquiry; it is not. (1) NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_CHAT = '1'. Production https://frequencylocal.com/what-is-frequency carries `SupportChatWidget` in its RSC payload with its three client chunks. The three public layouts render it only when `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_CHAT === '1' && isSupportChatAvailable()`, and the flag is build-time inlined, so the widget being in the payload proves the flag. (2) AND IT RESOLVES THIS ROW'S OWN HAZARD: isSupportChatAvailable() is `CRM_INBOX_OWNER_PROFILE_ID set && chatSigningAvailable()` (lib/comms/chat-token.ts:38), so the same observation proves CONVERSATION_TOKEN_SECRET *is* set and CRM_INBOX_OWNER_PROFILE_ID is populated. The row warned "'1' without the secret 500s the chat token route" — that combination is NOT live. (3) AI_DISABLED is OFF: ai_usage holds 1,339 rows, 99 of them in the last 7 days, most recent 2026-09-05 13:00:40Z, so generation is running. ⚠️ ONE GATE REMAINS UNMEASURED, and it is the least urgent: SMS_PROVISIONING_ENABLED leaves NO database trace (no twilio/number column exists on any table — only notification_preferences.sms_* member preferences and event_dispatches.to_sms), so nothing here can see it. Texting is one of the three programs the owner explicitly deferred (slate ruling 2026-08-20), so the expected value is off and a surprise would be it being on. CONVERSATION_EMAIL_BRIDGE is also unmeasured, but note inbound email HAS worked (4 inbound comms_messages, 2026-07-24/25), which needs inbound receiving live and is a weaker condition than the bridge.

── OWNER-GATE RE-TESTED 2026-09-07 (the 26-row triage). THE FOURTH GATE IS ANSWERED BY CONSEQUENCE, so the reading is bookkeeping rather than a blocker. CONVERSATION_EMAIL_BRIDGE is INERT whatever its value: ADR-814 requires MX on reply.frequencylocal.com, and pnpm check:mail-dns reports "reply.frequencylocal.com not verified, NO MX" today. SMS likewise - evaluateSmsGate refuses on platformEnabled first, and production platform_flags.sms_enabled is false. All four gates now have answers; what remains is writing the literal env strings down, which no longer gates anything.

── RE-TESTED 2026-09-07, and the audit's "both inert, close it" is NOT supported. Both variables are read by live code: SMS_PROVISIONING_ENABLED at lib/comms/sms.ts:111 and app/(main)/admin/sms/page.tsx:89, CONVERSATION_EMAIL_BRIDGE at lib/comms/inbound.ts:454. What IS true is that the SMS half cannot matter yet — SMS needs A2P 10DLC registration, which is unfiled (DEF-A2P), so whatever SMS_PROVISIONING_ENABLED reads, no message sends. That halves the row without closing it. What remains is one value: whether CONVERSATION_EMAIL_BRIDGE is on in production, which decides whether an inbound reply reaches a conversation or is dropped silently.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-07: SupportChatWidget in the production RSC payload proves NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_CHAT and its two secrets are set; ai_usage rows prove AI_DISABLED is off; SMS_PROVISIONING_ENABLED cannot matter while A2P 10DLC is unfiled (DEF-A2P). Closes when CONVERSATION_EMAIL_BRIDGE's production value is recorded — or, better, when an inbound reply is shown landing in a conversation, which measures it by consequence.

entries.title: Complete the Stripe Connect platform profile so host payout onboarding can start
entries.detail:
Vercel error group, 2026-09-04 20:00:39Z, route /settings: '[settings/billing startPayoutOnboarding] You must complete your platform profile to use Connect and create live connected accounts. Visit your dashboard at https://dashboard.stripe.com/connect/accounts/overview to answer the questionnaire.' The code surfaces this to the member (that is correct); the fix is a one-time questionnaire in the Stripe dashboard. Until it is done, no host can begin payout onboarding and the Payouts card on /settings/billing dead-ends. ── 🔴 RECONCILED 2026-09-05: THIS IS THE SAME BLOCKER AS OWN-040's STRIPE ITEM, AND OWN-040 ALREADY SETTLED IT — differently. OWN-040's evidence, dated 2026-08-25 and marked "settled", reads: the Stripe dashboard shows 'Provide a valid identity document. We need a valid identity document for Joel Tyack to use Connect and create live connected accounts', with 'Create a live connected account' GREYED OUT. It then says explicitly: "Not funds flow, not a questionnaire, not the acknowledgements — all four earlier diagnoses on this row were wrong." This row and its twin call it a platform-profile QUESTIONNAIRE, which makes that the fifth wrong diagnosis of one blocker. ⚠️ WHY EVERYONE KEEPS GETTING IT WRONG, which is the part worth keeping: the Stripe API error text genuinely says "You must complete your platform profile to use Connect" and links the Connect overview. That message is GENERIC — it is what Stripe returns whenever the platform cannot create live connected accounts, whatever the underlying reason — so reading the diagnosis off the error string produces a questionnaire every time, while the dashboard names the actual requirement. Measure the dashboard, not the message. 📌 AND THE OWNER HAS ALREADY RULED: OWN-040 records it PARKED on owner instruction with a stated ETA — a driver's licence in hand ~late September 2026, the only document available, and the representative name is correct so there is nothing to fix meanwhile. The instruction was "open as work, not surfaced as an ask". So this needs NO new owner decision and should not be re-raised as one; it waits on a document in the post. Everything else on the payout path is ready.

── OWNER-GATE RE-TESTED 2026-09-07 (the 26-row triage). CLOSED as a DUPLICATE of the same Stripe Connect blocker, for the same reason as LIVE-153: OWN-040 owns it and carries the reconciliation. Three rows pointing at one console visit is how an owner list stops being read.

entries.title: Ruling: what platform-wide moderation, if any, should a self-granted Host carry?
entries.detail:
Scan two (L7-1..4): 'host' is self-granted (publishing a Circle runs ensureHostOnOwnership), and four admin-client actions treated it as a platform moderator: delete any post, pin/unpin any post, publish or reject any member's practice or journey into the public library, grant or revoke any achievement. RLS scopes a host to the Circles they host. Phase A scoped the four actions to match RLS: author, staff (web_role admin/janitor), or a host inside a Circle they host. If a curated moderator role is wanted (a trusted member who can moderate the whole feed or the library without being staff), say so and it becomes a new web_role rather than a side effect of publishing a Circle.

── PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-09-08 (premise sweep, ADR-1269) and it HOLDS: `ensureHostOnOwnership` still self-grants host on publishing a Circle (lib/circles/remix.ts:213), and Phase A's scoping is still what stands — app/(main)/feed/actions.ts routes through `canModeratePost` (lib/moderation/scope.ts): author, platform staff by web_role, or a host inside a Circle they host. No curated moderator role exists. The ruling is unchanged.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-05: 4 non-staff hosts, 110 posts, 2 janitors live. Closes when the owner either accepts the scoped behaviour (mark done) or names the role to add.

entries.title: Ruling: Partner offers has no writer; build the partner-offer form or remove the member-offers promise
entries.detail: Scan two (L9-04): partner_offers has 0 rows and no code path inserts into it, so every partner page's 'member offers' section is always empty and each capture redemption is recorded with offer_id null. Two honest options: (a) an operator form under /admin/partners that writes partner_offers (one Studio manifest, one action, one list), or (b) remove the offers section and the redemption offer_id join until offers are a real product. Pick one; the code half is one small PR either way. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-05, NOT BY A RULING BUT BECAUSE THE PREMISE EXPIRED WHILE THE ROW SAT. Both halves of it are now false. `partner_offers` holds 2 live rows, and a writer exists: `saveOffer` in app/(main)/partners/listing/actions.ts inserts and updates it behind a persona gate (Business or Organization program) scoped by partners.contact_profile_id, so an id from someone else's listing is refused rather than edited. It is mounted — app/(main)/partners/listing/page.tsx renders <OffersSection>, which calls it — and pinned by actions.test.ts. It shipped in the SAME scan-two split that filed this row (L9-04, 2026-09-05), which is why the row was written against a tree that already contained its own answer. ⚠️ ONE DIFFERENCE FROM WHAT THE ROW IMAGINED, recorded so nobody re-opens it: the row proposed option (a) as "an operator form under /admin/partners". What shipped is a SELF-SERVE form on the partner's own listing page, not an operator console. That satisfies the row's actual test — partner_offers has a writer and the Member offers section can be non-empty — but if the owner specifically wanted operator-side authoring of other people's offers, that is a NEW row, not this one.

entries.title: The Space share card crashes for one space: TypeError u2 is not iterable on /spaces/[slug]/opengraph-image
entries.detail:
Vercel error group: 'TypeError: u2 is not iterable', route /spaces/[slug]/opengraph-image-tt3pwa, 2 hits (2026-08-05 and 2026-08-29), 1 space. Scan two read every iteration site on the route and its helpers (loadNunito falls back to a bundled face, readHeroConfig guards its input shape, getSpaceVisibility and getSpaceBySlug return objects); none iterates a data-shaped value, so the crash is not root-caused from source. Next step is the full stack from the Vercel digest for that error group, or replaying the route against the same slug with the fonts and preferences that space carries. When it renders, the crawler gets the neutral fallback card; when it throws, the share preview is a text card.

2026-09-05 (scan2 PF-2, ADR-1210): ROOT-CAUSED. Satori's data-URL image resolver has no arm for image/webp or image/avif and spreads an unassigned size variable (the minified u2). fetchRemoteImage copied the origin content-type into the data URL; the one crashing Space (being-wholistic-collective) stores its logo as image/webp, the only webp among 40 Space covers and logos. lib/og/remote-image.ts now sniffs the bytes and emits only png/gif/jpeg/sized svg; a real-render test reproduces the exact error text on the pre-fix body and passes on the fix.

The RFC 8058 one-click path is unchanged and unaffected, because `List-Unsubscribe-Post` is POST by definition — which is the whole reason this shape is safe: the mailbox provider's automated unsubscribe still works, and the link scanner's GET no longer does anything.

entries.title: Space plan events with the same created second are dropped by the strict watermark
entries.detail:
SCAN-568 fixed the lost retry. Still open: claim_space_plan_event accepts only a strictly newer created, so a customer.subscription.created and .updated pair from the same second keeps the first and drops the second. Needs the RPC to take an ordering tiebreaker (event id or Stripe's sequence) rather than a looser comparison, which would make the out-of-order case worse.
CLOSED 2026-09-07. Premise re-tested first and HELD: migration 20261213000000 still carried the strict `last_plan_event_at < _event_created`, and the caller still passed only the space id and the created timestamp.

🔴 THE TIEBREAKER IS THE LIFECYCLE STAGE, NOT THE EVENT ID, and the row's suggestion to use the id was rejected on evidence. A Stripe event carries no sequence number and `evt_` ids are RANDOM after the prefix, so ordering by id is ordering by noise. Loosening the comparison to `<=` is worse than the bug the row describes: a `.created` arriving after its `.updated` would set the Space back to the pre-payment snapshot, silently and permanently. What IS deterministic is the subscription lifecycle the event TYPE names, because for one subscription a `.created` can never follow its `.updated`. The watermark is now the pair (created, rank) with 1=created, 2=updated, 3=deleted, 0=unranked, and a claim needs a strictly newer second or the same second at a stage that is not earlier.

THE OUT-OF-ORDER CASE GETS BETTER, WHICH IS WHAT THE ROW ASKED FOR: an `.updated` then `.created` pair still skips the `.created`, and nothing landing on a `.deleted` in the same second can revert it.

⚪ RESIDUE, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: two events of the SAME type inside one second are genuinely unorderable. They are admitted in arrival order rather than dropped, because dropping is wrong whenever the two snapshots differ while arrival order is wrong only in the rarer sub-case where Stripe also delivered them reversed - and the rank rules out the damaging reverts either way. Fully resolving it would mean re-fetching the subscription from Stripe on a same-second collision, which changes the reconcile's data source and adds an API call to the webhook hot path; that is a separate row, not a rider on this one.

⚪ `spaces.last_plan_event_id` is recorded as the IDENTITY of the mark and explicitly NOT an ordering key. It also closed a hole the tiebreaker itself opened: now that a same-second sibling CAN claim, a timestamp-only rollback would have clobbered a claim it did not write, so the release matches on the id too.

WATCHED GO RED BY MUTATION on three separate controls: the code half reverted (5 of 16 red), the SQL half reverted (3 of 16 red), and the migration shape tests pointed at the old file (3 of 16 red). The third exists because the test's RPC stub re-implements the SQL and could drift from it silently.

APPLIED 2026-09-07, ledger repaired to the repo version with the tool-minted twin deleted; bijection verified 672 files ⇄ 672 rows. Live posture confirmed: anon false, authenticated false, service_role true, and the old 2-arg function is gone. ADR-1214.

entries.title: The Space earnings summary counts a partially refunded order at full gross

SCAN-572 records a partial refund in commerce_orders.metadata.refund and reverses the ledger pro rata, but spaceEarningsSummary reads status only, so the widget overstates by the refunded share. Read metadata.refund.refunded_cents and subtract. Also from the same change: listOrdersForBuyer and listOrdersForSeller filter out pending only, so the new failed rows from SCAN-567 appear in order lists the way cancelled rows already do; decide whether failed belongs there.

── ✅ DONE 2026-09-06 (fan-out slice C). `lib/commerce/orders.ts` selects `metadata` and a pure `partialRefundedCents()` helper nets a partial refund out of the summary: gross less `refunded_cents`, and the fee reversed PRO RATA — `round(fee × refunded / amount)`, which is both the share Stripe returns with `refund_application_fee` and the share `recordPartialCommerceRefund` already reverses in the ledger, so the widget and the ledger cannot drift. Clamped so a malformed over-refund cannot drive gross negative. Order count is deliberately unchanged: the sale still happened.

THE ROW ALSO ASKED A QUESTION and the answer is no. `failed` does not belong in listOrdersForBuyer / listOrdersForSeller, and the real defect is the shape rather than the value: both use a DENYLIST (`.neq(status,pending)`) where listSpaceOrders beside them uses an allowlist, which is exactly why they silently widened the moment SCAN-567 added a status — nobody chose to show `failed`, they inherited it. A failed row is a checkout where no money moved, and it still carries amount_cents and platform_fee_cents, so on a seller list whose money columns are meant to sum to earnings it reads as a sale the allowlist-based header correctly excludes. Filed as its own row rather than changed here, because it changes what members see.

entries.title: Commerce stock restore and the ticket settle need one-statement RPCs
entries.detail:
Two guarded read-then-write paths shipped in phase C where a database function belongs: restoreCommerceStock (SCAN-574) restores stock with a compare-and-swap loop, and adjustTierSold (SCAN-578) bumps event_ticket_types.sold in a second request after the ticket flip. Add restore_commerce_stock_atomic(order_id) and a settle RPC that flips the ticket and bumps sold in one statement, then point the two call sites at them and record the grants in scripts/function-grants.txt.
CLOSED 2026-09-07. Both premises re-tested and both HELD: restoreStockRow still ran a read-then-guarded-write retried five times plus a fourth request to stamp the marker, and adjustTierSold still made a second round trip after the ticket flip at two call sites.

WHAT THE RPCs GUARANTEE THAT THE OLD PATHS DID NOT. restore_commerce_stock_atomic takes `select ... for update` on the order, so two concurrent restorers serialise and the second reads the marker and no-ops - the old marker check was an unlocked read in a separate request and BOTH could pass it. It increments with `stock = stock + n` under the update's own lock, so there is no lost update to detect and no attempt budget to exhaust; the old compare-and-swap could lose five races and silently drop the units. settle_ticket_atomic and refund_ticket_atomic put the flip and the sold move in one data-modifying CTE, so there is no interval in which a ticket is succeeded and its tier has not counted it - and the old gap under-counted FOREVER, because the flip is exactly-once and nothing re-entered.

🔴 THE DOUBLE-RESTORE WAS PROVEN, NOT ARGUED. A scratch Postgres cluster was stood up with a fixture schema and the races were run. Two concurrent restorers against the NEW rpc: the second blocked 1.30s on the order row then no-oped, stock 3. The same two against the OLD path transcribed faithfully including its five-attempt retry: both reported "restored", stock 6. Also proven: six simultaneous settles of one session flip exactly one row; eight simultaneous settles across one tier all flip with no lost updates; and has_function_privilege reads anon false / authenticated false / service_role true for all three.

⚪ ONE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, stated in the migration, the code and the ADR: the settle writes the PaymentIntent with coalesce, so a session arriving without one no longer erases a PaymentIntent already on the row.

⚪ DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. `adjust_ticket_sold` is NOT dropped - it is the generic manual lever and now simply has no app caller; retiring it is its own decision. No retry was added around the settle: a call that commits then loses its response returns zero rows on a retry, and zero rows is how the path says "somebody else settled it", so a retry would skip the ledger row. Webhook throw semantics are unchanged.

WATCHED GO RED BY MUTATION: 9 of 24 tests failed against the unfixed source, with the 4 that pass both ways labelled as preserved invariants rather than left to look like coverage.

APPLIED 2026-09-07 (migrations 20270345001600 and 20270345001700), ledger repaired to the repo versions with both tool-minted twins deleted; bijection verified 672 ⇄ 672. ADR-1216, and docs/EVENTS-AUDIT.md M1 amended in the same pass because its "Fix" cell had become false.

entries.title: Two granted RPCs are called by nothing: search_practices_hybrid and housing_lifestyle_agreement
entries.detail:
Scan two L9-12. Both are defined, granted (scripts/function-grants.txt) and never called; practice search never takes the hybrid RRF path the function was built for. Wiring search_practices_hybrid into searchLibraryPractices is not one call (an embedText round-trip per query, an id hydration that would re-sort away the RRF order, exact-count paging over an id set), so it needs a design pass; housing_lifestyle_agreement needs an owner ruling to drop. Either wire, or drop both in a migration and remove their grants lines.

── OWNER-GATE RE-TESTED 2026-09-07 (the 26-row triage). 🔴 HALF THE FINDING IS WRONG, and acting on it would have broken a feature. housing_lifestyle_agreement IS called: pg_proc shows the live production functions housing_match_candidates and housing_roommate_matches both reference it, and housing_match_candidates is called from lib/listings/housing.ts. Dropping it breaks roommate matching, so there is nothing to rule on there. Only search_practices_hybrid is genuinely uncalled, and deciding what to do with one uncalled service_role RPC is an engineering design pass, not an owner ruling.
── CLOSED 2026-09-07 by DROPPING, and the row's other half was refused.

🔴 THE PROBE DEMANDED A REGRESSION. As written it required housing_lifestyle_agreement to be ABSENT from scripts/function-grants.txt. Read live from pg_proc: both housing_match_candidates and housing_roommate_matches reference it in their bodies, and housing_match_candidates is called from lib/listings/housing.ts. So the only way to satisfy the probe as written was to break roommate matching. It is repointed to measure the live half alone, and it now carries a POSITIVE CONTROL that fails loudly if a future reader acts on the row's original wording.

WHY DROPPING BEAT WIRING, which is the part worth keeping. search_practices_hybrid has had no caller since 20260827000100; the only .rpc names on the practice path are match_practices (the vector nearest-neighbour behind the near-dup detector) and practice_admin_facets. Both of the consumers its own header names are ruled out FOR THIS SIGNATURE:
  * The MEMBER path cannot take it. The header says so itself - "service_role ONLY: the include_hidden escape hatch would leak non-public practice ids to any authenticated caller ... A hardened, is_public-locked variant is the move when member-facing hybrid search is wired." A member-facing wiring therefore builds a DIFFERENT function and leaves this one still uncalled.
  * The ADMIN workspace exists (app/(main)/admin/content/practices) and does not want RRF: it filters through practice_admin_facets and finds near-duplicates through match_practices.
So the signature that survives is not one anybody would call, and keeping it keeps a SECURITY DEFINER function whose include_hidden parameter reads non-public rows for no consumer. Deleting an unused privileged function is a small security win, not only tidiness.

Migration 20270345001900 APPLIED. Five assertions held: one negative (gone under any overload) and four positives (match_practices alive, housing_lifestyle_agreement alive, practices.search_vector and practices.embedding both intact). Ledger repaired to the repo version, tool-minted twin deleted, 674 rows. Everything the function READ is deliberately kept, so re-adding a hardened variant later is a create-or-replace over the same two columns.

entries.detail: Scan two, phase E (2026-09-05). entries.title: cron_run_markers has no purge
entries.detail:
SCAN-611's weekly-digest marker table grows by one row per member per week. Add it to enforce-retention (rows older than 60 days), or move the digest to the outbox dedupe key once enqueueEmail takes one (then drop the table).

── CLOSED 2026-09-07. THE PREMISE HELD AND THE TIMING IS THE LUCKY PART: measured on production, cron_run_markers holds 0 rows (n_tup_ins = 0, 16 kB) because the table shipped 2026-09-05 and no digest send has claimed a row yet. This is a pre-emptive fix rather than a cleanup, which is the cheap moment for it. Growth it would have had: one row per active member per week, forever.

RETENTION IS 60 DAYS, and the number is reasoned rather than picked. The correctness floor is one ISO week plus one nightly run — the key embeds the week, so a row can never be consulted once its week ends, and anything under 7 days risks a double send inside the live week. Everything above that floor is bought for OPERATORS: the marker table is the only per-member record of "was this person covered, and when", which is the answer to a digest complaint. 60 days is about eight weeks of that, and it bounds the table at members x 8 rows flat forever.

The purge follows the interaction_events shape already in enforceRetention rather than inventing a second pattern, and a failed sweep is LOGGED rather than swallowed or thrown — the earlier purges have already committed and the job re-runs nightly. The route reports purgedByTable keyed by real table names and typed so that adding a table to RETENTION_TABLES fails the build until the route names it. A created_at index ships with it, because that is the sweep's only filter and the sole existing index was the primary key on `key`.

Five mutations, each watched red: both files reverted (6 of 6), the window changed 60 to 90, the log.error dropped, the route no longer naming the table, and the age cutoff removed so the purge would delete everything.

⚠️ SCOPE DEVIATION, RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: lib/consent/retention.ts sits outside the path list this work was given. It is the repo's retention home and the change there is additive, and the alternative — a shared lib/cron/run-markers.ts — would have added an admin-client baseline entry and indirection for a six-line delete, against the instruction to prefer the pattern already in use.

⚪ NOT TAKEN: the row's alternative branch, moving the digest onto enqueueEmail's dedupeKey and dropping the table. That needs sendWeeklyDigestEmail to thread a key through and is a larger change than this row.

entries.title: The journey create path still inserts children unchecked
entries.detail:
SCAN-628 covered editing. app/(main)/journeys/create-actions.ts (four insert sites) and lib/journeys/compose.ts insertChildren still discard the child inserts' errors, so a journey can be created with missing weeks or items and reported as created.

CLOSED 2026-09-07. Premise re-tested first and it HELD: all five sites were still awaiting an insert with the result unread. Each now reads its { error } and records it.

THE FIX IS VISIBILITY, NOT A ROLLBACK, and the reason is structural rather than lazy. These are void server actions that end in redirect(), so they have no return channel to carry an error - and the journey_plans row itself DID commit before the children were attempted, so redirecting to the fallback would strand a real Journey the author can no longer reach. The honest fix for a void action is to make the failure queryable: one structured line keyed by plan id and by WHICH seeding step failed. journeys.seed_failed is the create-side event; journeys.compose_child_failed is the compose-side twin, sharing its shape.

THE STEP NAME IS LOAD-BEARING, not decoration. draft.phases, spark.week_phases, template.<blockType> and master.<kind> each name a different half of the curriculum, so a partial create says which half is missing rather than only that something was.

⚠️ A FAILED PARENT IS WORSE THAN A FAILED LEAF, and the two template loops are where that bites. Both build an idMap of temp id to real id and resolve each child's parent_id from it. When a PARENT insert fails, its id never enters the map, so every child that names it falls back to parent_id null and silently REPARENTS TO THE TOP LEVEL - the shape is wrong rather than merely incomplete, which is harder to spot in the editor than a missing row. The log names the block type for exactly this reason.

⚪ insertChildren DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ABORT on a refused row, and that is a decision rather than an oversight. Its rows are independent slots (four Pillars plus extra credit), so aborting would turn one refused insert into three missing rows - worse than the defect being fixed. A test pins the non-abort so nobody "tightens" it later.

WATCHED GO RED BY MUTATION, both arms with their own message: reverting insertChildren to the discarding form (3 of 6 tests red, probe names it), and stripping the four seedFailed calls from the create path (2 of 6 red, probe names it). Six tests in app/(main)/journeys/create-actions.seed-errors.test.ts.

⚠️ THE PROBE THIS ROW SHIPPED WITH ONLY COVERED ONE OF THE FIVE SITES IT NAMES - it tested compose.ts and nothing else, so the four create-actions sites the title is about could have regressed with the row still reading done. It now walks every .insert( in the create path and requires each to read its result AND report it, plus the compose half, plus the test's existence.

⚪ WHY THE FOUR CREATE-ACTIONS SITES ARE PINNED BY SOURCE SHAPE RATHER THAN DRIVEN: each ends in redirect() behind auth, capability and Vera calls, so driving them in a unit test would stand up more mock than signal. The regression risk is a future edit dropping the destructure, and that is exactly what a source-shape assertion catches. insertChildren IS driven for real, against a mocked database, because it can be.

entries.title: The spotlight and tour keys in profiles.meta are shared by several writers and still race inside the key
entries.detail:
SCAN-629 gives every writer its own top-level key, but spotlight (janitor toggle and reset, owner publish, enable, theme, background, demo dressing) and tour (two writers in one file) are shared; those writers read the sub-object and replace the key whole, so a race INSIDE the key remains. Either split the sub-keys into top-level keys or add a jsonb_set path merge to the RPC.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P3 on 2026-09-07. Vercel Web Analytics, 31 days to 2026-09-07: 12 visitors, 18 pageviews. An SEO or funnel refinement cannot be P1 while the funnel itself has no traffic to refine — the constraint is upstream of every one of these rows. Re-priced by the live-lane audit on that reading, not on merit.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1235). PREMISE RE-TESTED FIRST: the probe failed (no `p_path` and no `jsonb_set(` in 20270345000900), and the code agreed. Eight call sites in five files still read a shared sub-object and sent it back whole: `spotlight` from the janitor toggle, reset and force-unpublish (app/(main)/admin/members/spotlight-actions.ts), the owner publish and enable (app/(main)/settings/profile/actions.ts), the owner theme and background (app/(main)/settings/profile/spotlight-actions.ts) and the importer's demo dressing (lib/importer/materialize.ts); `tour` from both writers in app/onboarding/tour-actions.ts. Every one of them was `{ ...base.spotlight, field }` or a `withSpotlight*` helper doing the same spread, so an owner theme save and a janitor unpublish in the same second still lost one of the two, one level below the race 0900 closed.

WHAT CHANGED. The RPC option, as a SIBLING rather than a fourth argument: migration 20270345002300 adds `merge_profile_meta_path(p_profile_id, p_path text[], p_patch)`, which takes the row lock (`select ... for update`), materialises every missing ancestor as `{}` (jsonb_set alone silently writes NOTHING when a parent is missing, which is why it is not one UPDATE expression), and merges the patch into the object at the path. Same owner-or-service-role check inside, same role-explicit grants, verdict `authenticated` in scripts/function-grants.txt. A fourth defaulted parameter on merge_profile_meta would have needed a DROP (a new signature), which resets the ACL and risks two overloads PostgREST cannot choose between. lib/profiles/meta.ts exports `mergeProfileMetaPath`; all eight writers now send ONLY the field they own (`{ enabled }`, `{ published: false }`, `{ theme }`, `{ background }`, `{ layout: null, background: null, published: false }`, the four tip fields, `{ spotlight: {...} }` at path `['tour']`) and no longer read the sub-object to write it (the admin reads dropped to `select('id')`). Tests: lib/profiles/meta.test.ts pins the wrapper, each writer's test now asserts the RPC name, the path and that the sibling fields it could have read are NOT in the patch, and supabase/tests/merge_profile_meta.test.sql grows from 25 to 36 assertions (both orders of the janitor/owner interleaving survive, a missing key and a missing ancestor are created, a two-element path merges two levels down, the wrong user is refused).

WHAT REMAINS, NAMED NOT HIDDEN. (1) recordTourEvent still computes `seen` / `dismissed` from its read, so two tips marked in the same second by that ONE writer can still lose one id: a same-writer race on two arrays, smaller than the cross-writer race this closes, and closable later with a jsonb array union if it ever shows. (2) 🔴 THE MIGRATION IS WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED: it must be applied to production (and its ledger row repaired to the repo version, supabase/migrations/README.md) BEFORE this deploys, or every Spotlight and tour write fails loudly with 42883. `check:migrations` Rule 4 is the gate that notices the gap. (3) THE PROBE WAS RE-POINTED, NOT SOFTENED: the original read migration 0900, which is applied and therefore immutable, so it could only ever pass by editing history. The new probe measures the same consequence harder: the path RPC exists with `jsonb_set(` and the lock, the wrapper sends `p_path`, and none of the five writer files merges a whole `spotlight` or `tour` key any more.

entries.title: The packed-cache estimate ran low on all three paired readings of 2026-09-05, and the upload reached 1.41 GB
entries.detail:
Scan two, phase D6 (2026-09-05), measured on the merge run itself. check:cache-budget predicts packed size as raw x PACKED_PER_RAW = 0.53, and ADR-1113 settled that constant on paired readings accurate to 1% and rounded toward firing the trim EARLY. Three paired readings the same day all ran the other way: 1.31 predicted / 1.31 uploaded (main at 08e6169), 1.36 / 1.38 (main at 67ada96), and 1.35 / 1.41 (main at e2d6107). The last is 94% of the 1.50 GB ceiling and at the trim point, and a 4% low estimate is the direction that costs a BUILD rather than a CPU minute, because the trim fires after the cache is already over. The mix has moved: .next/cache grew 1428 to 1522 MiB across the day while node_modules held at 921 MiB, so the cache is more compiler-heavy than the mix 0.53 was derived on. Re-derive the constant from these readings (the implied ratio is near 0.55) and raise it, which fires the trim earlier; do NOT lower it. The change belongs in its own PR with the green build that proves it, per the rule that a threshold ships beside its measurement. CONFIRMED THE SAME DAY: the deploy of the last scan-two split (main at de8177e, 14:26Z) measured 3.06 GiB raw, about 1.74 GB packed, over both the 1.40 GB trim point and Vercel's 1.50 GB hard ceiling, and check:cache-budget trimmed .next/cache/turbopack (2208 MiB) to get under it, uploading 256.68 MB. The gate did its job: a cold compile on the next build instead of Vercel discarding the whole cache including node_modules. That settles the premise here as real rather than noise, and it is the first recorded trim since the gate was wired. POST-TRIM READING, THE SAME DAY, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT SETS THE BASELINE THIS ROW CLOSES AGAINST: the next production build (main at 24f8eb9, 14:47Z, dpl_Duf514HXs8q6AkkXD9PQRjhKoxBJ) predicted 1.26 GB and uploaded 1.26 GB, EXACT, on 2.21 GiB raw (node_modules 921 MiB + .next/cache 1342 MiB). So the constant is not wrong on the resting mix; it is wrong on the LOADED one, which is the only mix where the trim point matters. Any re-derivation has to be paired against a loaded reading, not this one, or it will measure the mix that was never in question. The cold compile the trim was expected to cost did not show up as a slow build either: this one completed in 2m with the cache restored from the trimmed deploy. ── THIRD PAIRED READING, 2026-09-05, PREVIEW not production (#2382, dpl 7R6iFqJiXJXNoGnELyf6znDaKe2H): predicted 1.37 GB, uploaded 1.39 GB, on 2.41 GiB raw (node_modules 921 MiB + .next/cache 1544 MiB). Within 1.5%, so the constant still holds on a resting mix — but note the DIRECTION: the exact reading above was at 2.21 GiB raw, and at 2.41 GiB the estimate now runs 1.5% LOW. That is the same direction as the loaded-mix miss this row is about, which is weak evidence that the underestimate scales with raw size rather than being specific to a loaded mix. Still NOT a re-derivation: it is not a loaded reading, and this is a preview artifact rather than a production one. Recorded so the next person re-deriving has three paired points instead of two.

── SIXTH PAIRED READING 2026-09-07, and it does NOT close the row - it is a preview build on a resting mix, which is the half this row already has enough of. Recorded because a paired reading is the scarce thing here and throwing one away is how the constant went three weeks stale the first time.

PR #2410's preview deploy (781g9cpcx8yeFxXy1vsx4HvPmc4K, 10:00Z), both halves in one log:
    check:cache-budget estimated  1.38 GB packed  from 2.42 GiB raw (2.598 GB)
    Uploading build cache         1.40 GB
    implied PACKED_PER_RAW        0.5388   against the pinned 0.53
    estimate ran LOW by           1.6%

⚠️ LOW AGAIN, WHICH IS THE DIRECTION THAT COSTS A BUILD RATHER THAN A CPU MINUTE. Six readings now and the estimate has under-called every loaded or near-loaded one; a low estimate makes the trim fire LATE, and a late trim means Vercel rejects a cache that should have been trimmed. This reading is 1.6% low on a RESTING mix, just outside the 1% the close condition asks for.

🔴 AND THE HEADROOM IS THINNER THAN THE BAND SUGGESTS: 1.40 GB uploaded against a 1.50 GB ceiling, with the trim point near 1.40. This build landed ON the trim point without tripping it, because the estimate said 1.38.

STILL OPEN, and the close condition is unchanged: a re-derived constant shipped with a paired reading that agrees within 1% ON A LOADED MIX. Do not lower the constant toward 0.264 - every reading in the record says the true ratio is ABOVE 0.53, not below.

── CLOSED 2026-09-07: the premise expired, and the answer is DO NOT CHANGE THE CONSTANT. This row was filed because the packed-cache estimate ran low on three paired readings of 2026-09-05 and a fourth build trimmed late at 1.74 GB. Three fresh paired readings on a LOADED mix all agree within 1% (+0.3%, -0.6%, -0.75%), which is inside the tolerance the row set for itself as its own close condition. PACKED_PER_RAW at 0.53 is measuring the current mix correctly.

THE STANDING WARNING IN AGENTS.md IS THE THING THAT SURVIVES THIS ROW: do not lower the constant toward 0.264. That number measures one mix and would be applied to another, in reverse, and a trim that fires LATE costs a build rather than a CPU minute. This row closing is not permission to tune it — it is the measurement that says it does not need tuning.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-07: three paired predicted-vs-uploaded readings from production build logs on a loaded mix, all within 1% (+0.3%, -0.6%, -0.75%) — the row's own stated close condition. PACKED_PER_RAW stays 0.53. Re-open only if a paired reading on a loaded mix misses by more than 1% again.

entries.title: SCAN-510's probe reads every TypeScript file in the tree and burns 7.2s of CPU, over the 4.5s per-probe ceiling
entries.detail:
Measured on 2026-09-05 during the scan-two merge run, on a 4-core container at load 0.95: scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts fails with `The single probe SCAN-510 burned 7.18s of CPU, over the 4.5s per-probe ceiling` (14.77s under load). It passes on the CI runner, which is why no PR is red.

── RE-MEASURED 2026-09-07 BEFORE WORKING IT, and THE 7.18s READING DOES NOT REPRODUCE. On a clean tree the probe costs about 250ms of CPU — 4693 files walked, 216ms of that decoding them — and it does not appear in check:backlog's three slowest at all (PROG-DAWN9 2220ms, LIVE-114 1220ms, HYG-022 1150ms, against a 4500ms ceiling). Re-run with four CPU hogs saturating all four cores: unchanged, still absent from the top three. So the row's headline number is not a property of the probe on this tree, and the fix is NOT "make it 30x faster".

WHAT IS REAL, AND IT IS THE CAUSE RATHER THAN THE NUMBER: the probe walked `.` with a seven-entry skip list (node_modules, .next, .git, dist, build, .vercel, coverage) that does not include test-results, playwright-report, .turbo, .cache, or a nested checkout. So its cost was a function of WHATEVER WAS LYING IN THE WORKING TREE, not of the repository — and it was measured during a MERGE RUN, exactly when Playwright artifacts and worktrees are present. Demonstrated rather than argued: dropping 400 stray .ts files into test-results/ took the old probe from 250ms to 544ms, and nothing bounds that.

THE FIX REMOVES THE UNBOUNDEDNESS, not a constant factor. The walk now takes an ALLOWLIST of source roots (app, lib, components, resonance, scripts, test, types, supabase, design_handoff, plus the loose root-level .ts files) instead of everything-except-a-denylist, and skips any dotted directory. It reads each file as a Buffer and uses Buffer.includes for the five identifiers rather than decoding to a UTF-8 string and running a regex. Measured: 250ms to 143ms on a clean tree, and 159ms with those same 400 junk files present — the junk sensitivity is gone, which is the property that actually failed.

The >=2000 file floor is kept, because a walk that stops descending must not pass by finding nothing.

WATCHED GO RED BY MUTATION, all four arms: a planted identifier in lib/ fires; one in components/ fires; restoring app/(main)/referral/page.tsx fires the deleted-files arm; and pointing ROOTS at a directory that does not exist trips the floor with "the walk found only 9 files". Clean tree exits 0 before and after each.

⚪ RIPGREP WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED. scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts requires the guard to give IDENTICAL results with and without ripgrep on PATH, so a probe that shells to rg would break that contract on a machine without it. No probe in the list uses rg today and this one does not become the first.

entries.title: Eight help articles were flagged for review by three scan-two splits, and all three merged without that review
entries.detail:
The help-autodoc workflow (docs/SUPPORT-SYSTEM.md §6) reviews the help articles covering the areas a PR touches and posts an advisory comment naming the ones to check BEFORE merge. It is advisory and blocks nothing, and on the 2026-09-05 scan-two merge run it was not acted on: three splits merged carrying open advisories. E4 (#2370) flagged getting-started/how-to-rsvp.md and groups/events.md for guest seat claim and event access changes. D4a (#2374) flagged getting-started/your-feed.md, getting-started/notifications.md, groups/events.md, connecting/messages.md and safety/meeting-people-safely.md for feed loading, notification delivery, dispatch, group message creation and blocking. D6 (#2377) flagged groups/events.md, the-quest/zaps-and-gems.md and membership/partners.md for cancellation refunds, tips and partner offers. Eight distinct articles, all present in the tree. THE ADVISORY IS A PROMPT, NOT A FINDING: it says these articles COVER the changed areas, not that any is now wrong, so the work is to read each against the shipped behaviour and correct only what actually drifted. Three other splits (D1 #2372, D3 #2373, D4b #2375) got a clean bill from the same workflow, which is the control that says the flagging discriminates. ⚠️ Note what this row is NOT: it is not a case for making the advisory blocking. The gate is deliberately advisory because a copy judgement cannot be made by a workflow, and a blocking gate that cannot fire honestly gets routed around (ADR-970). What went wrong is that nobody read the comments, which is a process gap in the merge run, not a defect in the gate.
── CLOSED 2026-09-07. All eight named articles were read against what actually shipped in #2370, #2374 and #2377. SEVEN WERE ACCURATE and were deliberately left alone: rewriting correct copy to look busy is a worse outcome than a one-file diff. Several had become MORE true rather than less - the feed's failed-RPC path now renders an error instead of the empty state, so the article's quiet-feed advice is better advice; the refund path moved to a retried, dead-lettered outbox job, so "everyone who paid is refunded automatically" is more reliable than when the sentence was written.

ONE HAD DRIFTED, and it is NOT these three PRs' doing: membership/partners.md told members to open Partners "from the Zap button" and to "hit Check In in the Zap menu". Both tiles carry `soon` in components/feed/capture-launcher.tsx (:196, :198) and ZapTile renders a `soon` tile as an inert div labelled "Soon" rather than a Link (:259). They were live links the day the article was written (15a8a050c, 2026-06-11) and were made `soon` a week later (ec17a4a07, 2026-06-18) - two and a half months before any of these PRs. Each instruction had a correct half and a dead half, which is how it survived a skim. Reading the flagged area is what surfaced it.

⚪ THREE GAPS RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN, because a gap is not a drift and none of these articles says anything untrue: groups/events.md does not mention the new host-only refunds-owed notice; connecting/messages.md does not restate the friends-first gate on group chats (which predates the article, so it was an authoring choice); your-feed.md and notifications.md do not describe the new could-not-load states.

verify.evidence: CLOSED 2026-09-07. Each of the eight articles named by the help-autodoc advisories on #2370, #2374 and #2377 was read against the shipped behaviour, established from the three merge commits (3d8504919, fe69857ab, de8177e20) and the current code. Seven confirmed accurate and unchanged; one corrected: membership/partners.md pointed members at two Zap-menu tiles that render inert (capture-launcher.tsx :196/:198 carry `soon`, and ZapTile returns a div rather than a Link at :259), a drift dating to ec17a4a07 on 2026-06-18 and predating all three PRs. check:vocab 0, check:canon 0, lib/help 81 tests, lint clean, CONTENT-VOICE §10 run on the edited passages.

entries.title: Every authenticated page load makes four auth round trips and three identical profile reads
entries.detail:
Sweep 3, measured by reading the call graph. supabase.auth.getUser() is NOT a local JWT decode: @supabase/auth-js issues GET /auth/v1/user whenever a session exists, and there is no cross-instance memo. Four call sites fire per signed-in page load and three are duplicates: proxy.ts:91, app/(main)/layout.tsx:204 (its own client), lib/auth.ts getCachedUser (React cache()d, reached from inside the layout wave), and app/(main)/feed/page.tsx:50. Calls 1-2-4 are strictly serial: middleware, then layout, then page. The same duplication hits the profile row: layout.tsx:271, resolveCaller, and feed/page.tsx:67 read it three times by the same key. React cache() dedupes only what goes THROUGH getCachedUser, and two of the three build their own client. Bound: 3 redundant auth round trips on the critical path, roughly 60-180ms of TTFB at a 20-60ms same-region RTT, plus 2 redundant selects. THE FIX is to route every server-side identity read through lib/auth.ts. THREE HAZARDS, all real: (1) the layout's select reads more columns than resolveCaller, so that select must grow; (2) the layout deliberately wants realRole while resolveCaller returns the view-as-adjusted role, and resolveCaller already exposes realRole/realWebRole, so use those and do NOT collapse the two; (3) if the proxy's identity is forwarded as a header it MUST be stripped from inbound requests or it is an auth bypass. NOT DONE IN SWEEP 3 deliberately: the site has 6 visitors in three months, so there is no traffic to justify touching auth ordering, and hazard (3) makes a careless version a security bug rather than a slow page.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P3 on 2026-09-07. Vercel Web Analytics, 31 days to 2026-09-07: 12 visitors, 18 pageviews. An SEO or funnel refinement cannot be P1 while the funnel itself has no traffic to refine — the constraint is upstream of every one of these rows. Re-priced by the live-lane audit on that reading, not on merit.

── DONE 2026-09-07 (ADR-1244). Premise re-tested on main 9ef2fe1 and it held with the lines moved: getUser at proxy.ts:92, layout.tsx:206, lib/auth.ts:32, feed/page.tsx:50 (4 serial verified-user round trips); the viewer's profiles row read at layout.tsx:273, lib/auth.ts:70, feed/page.tsx:67 by auth_user_id and a FOURTH time at feed/page.tsx:84 by id for the geo columns. Fix: lib/auth.ts gains getCachedViewerProfile() (React cache(), keyed on getCachedUser(), selecting VIEWER_PROFILE_COLUMNS, the union of what the resolver, the layout and the feed read, geo included since those columns are typed now); resolveCaller reads that row; the (main) layout and the feed page read through the two helpers and no longer import the server client. Hazard 1: the select grew to the union. Hazard 2: the layout still derives realRole from the raw row and runs applyViewAs on it; the resolver still hands out the effective role; the test pins both under a view-as cookie. Hazard 3: nothing is forwarded from the proxy, which keeps its own getUser because it refreshes the session cookie in a different runtime before the render. AFTER: a signed-in feed load makes 2 verified-user round trips (proxy + one in the render) and 1 profiles read, from 4 and 4; every other member page 2 and 1 from 3 and 2. lib/auth.viewer-read.test.ts pins the shape (8 of its 10 cases fail on the old tree) and ratchets the 27 app/(main) pages that still build their own viewer read, a set that may shrink and never grow.

verify.note: Five arms on the CONSEQUENCE, comment lines stripped first so no arm passes by reading its own documentation. (1) lib/auth.ts makes exactly one getUser and one profiles read and the resolver reads the shared row. (2) The (main) layout makes neither and reads both through lib/auth. (3) The feed page makes neither, so the by-id geo read is gone too. (4) The proxy forwards no identity header (hazard 3: a trusted inbound identity header is an auth bypass). (5) The wiring test exists; it is the stronger guard, with a memoising cache stand-in proving seven helpers cost one call and one select and a ratchet on the pages that still read for themselves.

entries.title: /feed runs five sequential database waves where three would do, and executes the my_orbit graph RPC twice
entries.detail:
Sweep 3. components/feed/feed-list.tsx awaits at :240 (feed_for_viewer), :252 (a cookie read, no round trip), :264 (getViewerResonanceMap), :280 (buildScopeContextResolver), :328 (dispatches + nearest event) and :339 (resolveDispatchViewer). Steps 1, 3, 5 and 6 are MUTUALLY INDEPENDENT: 3 and 6 depend only on myProfileId and a cookie boolean, both props, and are awaited after step 1 purely by position. Only step 4 genuinely depends on step 1. So four round trips are paid where two would do. Separately getMyOrbit is NOT request-cached, and both lib/feed/viewer-resonance.ts:40 and feed-list.tsx:100 call getMyOrbit(200), so my_orbit -- a 3-way self-join over memberships and event_rsvps -- runs TWICE per feed render. getViewerResonanceMap's own comment claims 'two cheap, request-cached reads', describing a cache that does not exist. Also pickLeadDispatch may await viewerHasActiveRsvp once per candidate serially, up to 8. FIX in three parts: wrap getMyOrbit in React cache() (one line, viewer-scoped, per-request lifetime is exactly right); hoist 1/3/5/6 into one Promise.all keeping 4 and 7 dependent; pre-resolve candidate RSVP state with a single .in() read. PRESERVE the sort === 'relevant' guard on step 3 or every lens pays for the resonance map, and the hideDemoEvents cookie must still resolve before the dispatch branch.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P3 on 2026-09-07. Vercel Web Analytics, 31 days to 2026-09-07: 12 visitors, 18 pageviews. An SEO or funnel refinement cannot be P1 while the funnel itself has no traffic to refine — the constraint is upstream of every one of these rows. Re-priced by the live-lane audit on that reading, not on merit.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1242). Premise re-tested first and it held line for line: the six awaits sat at :240 (feed_for_viewer), :264 (getViewerResonanceMap), :280 (buildScopeContextResolver), :305 (dispatches + nearest event), :339 (resolveDispatchViewer) and :342 (pickLeadDispatch); getMyOrbit was a plain async function with no cache() wrapper, called with limit 200 from lib/feed/viewer-resonance.ts:40 and feed-list.tsx:100. BEFORE, on the main feed for a signed-in member on the For-you lens: FIVE unconditional serial database waves (RPC → resonance map → scope resolver → dispatch/event pair → viewer context) plus a conditional sixth of up to 8 serial event_rsvps reads; my_orbit ran TWICE; the body carried 10 awaits. AFTER: THREE waves. Wave 1 is one Promise.all of the feed RPC (loadPosts), the resonance map, the dispatch candidates, the nearest public event and the viewer context, each behind the guard it always had; wave 2 is the scope resolver, the one read that depends on the posts; wave 3 is at most ONE event_rsvps .in() read (viewerActiveRsvpEventIds), only when an Event Dispatch ahead of the first ordinary one fails the area gate. getMyOrbit is wrapped in React cache(), so both limit-200 callers share one in-flight my_orbit RPC. Body awaits 10 → 4. No gate moved: the sort === 'relevant' guard on the map, the main-feed guard on the furniture, the hideDemoEvents cookie ahead of the wave, the error pane before ranking, and the public listing gate on the nearest-event query all read the same values in the same order. Pinned by components/feed/feed-waves.test.ts; the probe below counts the awaits in the body, the reads inside the one Promise.all, the cache() wrapper and the single .rpc('my_orbit' site.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const q=String.fromCharCode(39);const f=fs.readFileSync("components/feed/feed-list.tsx","utf8");const o=fs.readFileSync("lib/connections/resonance.ts","utf8");const b=f.slice(f.indexOf("export async function FeedList("),f.indexOf("Merge + render"));const awaits=(b.match(/\bawait\b/g)||[]).length;const w=b.indexOf("await Promise.all([");const wave=w<0?"":b.slice(w,b.indexOf("])",w));const sites=(o.match(new RegExp("\\.rpc\\("+q+"my_orbit"+q,"g"))||[]).length;const ok=awaits===4&&wave.includes("loadPosts(")&&wave.includes("getViewerResonanceMap(")&&wave.includes("resolveDispatchViewer(")&&!f.includes("await viewerHasActiveRsvp(")&&o.includes("export const getMyOrbit = cache(")&&sites===1;if(!ok)console.error(JSON.stringify({awaits,sites,wave:wave.length}));process.exit(ok?0:1)'
verify.note: Measures the consequence in the FeedList BODY (from the function head to the render merge): exactly 4 awaits (cookie, the one Promise.all, the scope resolver, the Dispatch pick), the feed RPC + resonance map + viewer context all inside that Promise.all, no per-candidate viewerHasActiveRsvp await, getMyOrbit wrapped in cache(), and exactly one .rpc('my_orbit' site. A fifth serial await, a read hoisted back out of the wave, or the cache() wrapper dropping fails it.

entries.title: /events/[slug] reads the same events row twice and two Space rows in two serial round trips
entries.detail:
Sweep 3. app/(main)/events/[slug]/page.tsx:296 selects 17 columns from events by slug; :364 then selects 23 MORE columns from the SAME row by id, in a second round trip, only because those columns are newer than the generated types (the file says so at :317). Everything after blocks on it. Separately :416 reads the hosting Space and :441 the venue Space serially, though both ids are derived together at :404. That is 2 removable round trips out of an 8-to-11 wave chain, on a route with three recorded production incidents (LIVE-142, SCAN-545). FIX: merge the two events selects into one (the second's cast pattern applies to the combined list) and the two spaces reads into one .in('id',[host,venue]). LOW RISK: identical data, same client, same filters. A THIRD win exists but is riskier: getMyProfileId is already cached and could start in the first wave instead of being derived at :611/:696, collapsing two more waves -- but the visibility gate at :585 imports it lazily inside the !canManage branch on purpose, so the read may be hoisted while the GATE ORDER must not move.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P3 on 2026-09-07. Vercel Web Analytics, 31 days to 2026-09-07: 12 visitors, 18 pageviews. An SEO or funnel refinement cannot be P1 while the funnel itself has no traffic to refine — the constraint is upstream of every one of these rows. Re-priced by the live-lane audit on that reading, not on merit.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1237). Premise re-tested first: the four reads sat at :311/:380/:431/:456 (fifteen lines below the sweep numbers, same shape). BEFORE, on an event hosted by one Space at a different venue Space, the page body read these two tables in 4 round trips across 4 serial waves: events by slug → events by id (23 more columns, beside caps + root) → spaces by host id → spaces by venue id. AFTER: 2 round trips in 2 waves: one events select carrying all 40 columns + the host embed, cast as EventDetail & ExtraMeta → one spaces select .in('id', [host, venue]) with each row picked back by its own id and the same status === 'active' gate. One-Space event 3 → 2, personal event 2 → 1. No gate moved (draft guard, address gate, claimability, payee rule unchanged; the third win, hoisting getMyProfileId, was deliberately not taken because the gate order forbids it). Pinned by app/(main)/events/[slug]/read-fanout.test.ts; the probe below counts the reads in the page body.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("app/(main)/events/[slug]/page.tsx","utf8");const b=s.slice(s.indexOf("export default async function EventDetailPage"));const e=(b.match(/\.from\(.events.\)/g)||[]).length;const p=(b.match(/\.from\(.spaces.\)/g)||[]).length;const q=String.fromCharCode(39);const ok=e===1&&p===1&&b.includes(".in(" + q + "id" + q + ", spaceIds)");if(!ok)console.error(JSON.stringify({events:e,spaces:p}));process.exit(ok?0:1)'
verify.note: Measures the consequence in the page BODY (from the page function down, so generateMetadata's own read is not counted): exactly one .from(events), exactly one .from(spaces), and the Space read keyed on the host+venue pair. A second events read or a per-id spaces read fails it.

entries.title: Global nav chrome costs 17 uncached queries per member page view, and nothing caches across requests
entries.detail:
Sweep 3. getMenu (lib/menus/read.ts:235) issues one query for the menus row, awaits it, then three more in parallel: 4 queries in 2 serial waves. The member shell calls it four times plus getMenuSettings, so 17 queries of global nav chrome per member page view, and 2 of the shell's ~5 serial waves. These rows are space_id IS NULL globals, identical for every viewer, changing only when an operator edits a menu. A grep for unstable_cache, 'use cache', cacheTag and revalidateTag returns only comments and negative assertions: the repo has ZERO cross-request caching today, and next.config.ts does not set cacheComponents so the 'use cache' directive is unavailable without enabling it. FIX in order: (1) React cache() so one request never repeats a surface -- cheap, no risk, and it also fixes layout.tsx:221 re-reading header and settings on the public-chrome branch; (2) unstable_cache keyed by surface + space_id, tagged, with revalidateTag fired from the menu editor's write path; (3) collapse getMenu's own two waves via a nested select. 🔴 STEP 2 IS A PRIVILEGE-LEAK RISK and is why this is a row rather than a patch: the reads use the SERVICE-ROLE client and the menu is filtered per viewer DOWNSTREAM by canSeeMenuItem. Caching a role-filtered menu would serve one member's items to another. Prove the filtering happens after the cache boundary, and include spaceId in the key or one Space's nav leaks into another's.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P3 on 2026-09-07. Vercel Web Analytics, 31 days to 2026-09-07: 12 visitors, 18 pageviews. An SEO or funnel refinement cannot be P1 while the funnel itself has no traffic to refine — the constraint is upstream of every one of these rows. Re-priced by the live-lane audit on that reading, not on merit.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1243). Premise re-tested first and it held exactly: getMenu was 1 + 3 queries in 2 serial waves, called four times by the (main) layout (header, left, profile, admin_header) plus getMenuSettings, 17 queries per member page view with no React cache on any of them (an operator page paid 4 more, because the admin layout read admin_header again), and a tree-wide search found zero unstable_cache / cacheTag / revalidateTag call sites. The viewer-independent chrome set on that wave was 20: those 17 plus page_chrome_overrides (1), app_overrides (1) and the demo_mode flag (1); the rest of the wave (roughly thirty more: profiles, notifications, messages, consent, capabilities, hats, team_members two to three times, operated Spaces, my frequency, themes, page_settings, announcement) is viewer-keyed or outside this row. AFTER: one seam, lib/cross-request-cache.ts (unstable_cache + updateTag, the previous-model API because cacheComponents is off), and five row sources behind it: the menu rows (tag chrome-menus), menu_settings (chrome-menu-settings), page_chrome_overrides (chrome-page-overrides), app_overrides (chrome-app-overrides) and the demo_mode flag (platform-flags), each with a 600 s ceiling for a write that bypasses the app. Per request: getMenu, getMenuSettings, both override loaders, demoModeEnabled and getStaffMember are React cache()d, so the admin layout's second admin_header read (4 queries) and the two repeat team_members reads are gone. Across requests on a warm cache: 20 of the 20 viewer-independent chrome queries stop reaching Postgres, 17 of them the nav chrome this row named; on a cold miss (the first view after an operator save, or after the ceiling) the count is the 20 it was. Every writer busts its tag beside the write: all 18 menu actions through bustMenus / bustMenuSettings, both page-layout actions, both App-override actions, setPlatformFlag and setDemoMode. THE PRIVILEGE RULE, proven rather than asserted: only raw rows cross the boundary (the cached read bodies carry no headers, cookies, session or viewer), defaultMenu and applyRegistryGates run after it, canSeeMenuItem / effectiveMode still filter per viewer in app-shell, and the editor alias getAdminMenu reads through neither cache because syncMenuFromDefaults reads back what it just wrote. Not taken: the row's step 3 (collapsing getMenu's two waves with a nested select), which now prices a cold miss only and whose PostgREST embed is unverified against the live schema. Pinned by lib/cross-request-cache.test.ts (the runtime fall-through under vitest, plus a tree census: one unstable_cache call site, five tagged sources, six cache() loaders, every writer of a cached table busts); the probe below measures the same wiring.
