verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const r=(p)=>fs.existsSync(p)?fs.readFileSync(p,"utf8"):"";const n=(s,re)=>(s.match(re)||[]).length;const read=r("lib/menus/read.ts");const src=r("lib/layout/chrome-sources.ts");const flags=r("lib/platform-flags.ts");const acts=r("lib/menus/actions.ts");const layout=r("app/(main)/layout.tsx");const seam=r("lib/cross-request-cache.ts");const sites=n(read,/crossRequestCached\(/g)+n(src,/crossRequestCached\(/g)+n(flags,/crossRequestCached\(/g);const tags=/CHROME_CACHE_TAGS\.menus\]/.test(read)&&/CHROME_CACHE_TAGS\.menuSettings\]/.test(read)&&/CHROME_CACHE_TAGS\.pageChrome\]/.test(src)&&/CHROME_CACHE_TAGS\.appOverrides\]/.test(src)&&/CHROME_CACHE_TAGS\.platformFlags\]/.test(flags);const deduped=/const getMenuCached = cache\(/.test(read)&&/getMenuSettings = cache\(/.test(read)&&/loadCachedChromeOverrides = cache\(/.test(src)&&/loadCachedAppOverrides = cache\(/.test(src);const busts=n(acts,/invalidateCacheTag\(CHROME_CACHE_TAGS\.menus\)/g)===1&&n(acts,/invalidateCacheTag\(CHROME_CACHE_TAGS\.menuSettings\)/g)===1&&n(acts,/revalidatePath\(.\/., .layout.\)/g)===2;const shell=/loadCachedChromeOverrides\(\)/.test(layout)&&/loadCachedAppOverrides\(/.test(layout)&&!/\bloadChromeOverrides\(/.test(layout)&&!/\bloadAppOverrides\(/.test(layout);const seamOnly=n(seam,/unstable_cache\(/g)===1&&!/unstable_cache\(/.test(read)&&!/unstable_cache\(/.test(src);const ok=sites===5&&tags&&deduped&&busts&&shell&&seamOnly;if(!ok)console.error(JSON.stringify({sites,tags,deduped,busts,shell,seamOnly}));process.exit(ok?0:1)'
verify.note: Measures the wiring, not the title: exactly five crossRequestCached sources carrying their five tags; the shell loaders React-cached; the menu write path with its two tag busts and only the two helper revalidatePath calls left; the (main) layout reading both override tables through the cached sources and neither direct loader; and unstable_cache called in the seam alone. Fails on the tree before ADR-1243 (no seam, no sources) and on a tree that adds a cross-request read outside the census.

entries.title: Public Circle URLs are raw UUIDs although circles.slug is NOT NULL and the reader already returns it
entries.detail:
Sweep 3 (SEO). app/sitemap.ts advertised /discover/circles/<uuid>, and app/discover/circles/[id]/page.tsx keyed its canonical, openGraph.url, hero and breadcrumb on circle.id; lib/jsonld.ts built both circle urls from it too. The slug was ALREADY IN HAND: circles.slug is non-null in the generated types, public_circles returns it, and PublicCircle carries it - it was read on every one of these pages and thrown away. A UUID carries no keyword signal, is unquotable in an AI answer, and is the string a citation, a QR print run and a share link all freeze.

CLOSED 2026-09-07. Migration 20270345001400 adds public_circle_by_slug; lib/discover.ts gains getPublicCircle(slugOrId) resolving on the UUID shape exactly as getPublicPractice has since LIVE-052; the sitemap, canonical, openGraph.url, hero lookup, breadcrumb and both JSON-LD builders key on the slug; and the UUID form 308s to it so printed QR codes and existing citations survive as redirects rather than as a second address for the same page.

A SIBLING RPC, NOT A WIDENING, and the reason matters. public_circle_by_id is left exactly as it is: its signature is pinned by the browser-execute revoke ledger (20270304000000), and the UUID form has to keep resolving or the 308 has nothing to redirect FROM. This mirrors public_event_by_slug beside its by-id twin, the shape the codebase already uses for this problem one entity over.

THE VISIBILITY CONTRACT IS THE HALF THAT COULD LEAK, so it is proven rather than asserted. A by-slug lookup one clause laxer than the by-id lookup is a privacy hole with a friendlier URL - it would let anyone enumerate a fully-hidden circle by guessing its name. The test rewrites the one clause that is allowed to differ and then asserts the two function bodies are IDENTICAL, and both leak arms were watched go red: dropping private.can_see_circle, and widening the status filter. Confirmed live as the anon role after applying: for every circle in the table, public_circle_by_id and public_circle_by_slug return the same row count.

THE OG CARD ROUTE WOULD HAVE FAILED SILENTLY, and the row did not name it. app/discover/circles/[id]/opengraph-image.tsx receives the same segment the page does. Left reading by id only, it would have handed a slug to an RPC typed `_id uuid`, failed, and fallen through to the generic branded card - every share of a public Circle losing its name, with the fallback indistinguishable from "circle not found". It resolves slug-or-id now.

TWO INTERNAL LINKS WERE POINTED AT THE SLUG, and one of them was doing pointless work. app/(main)/layout.tsx fetched 200 circles to translate a slug INTO an id for the public-twin link; both routes are keyed by the slug now, so the read stays only as the EXISTENCE check (a circle with no public twin must resolve to null, not to a link into a 404) and the comment says so. lib/nav/public-twin.ts's rule comment was corrected for the same reason: it stays `lookup` rather than becoming `direct`, and the reason is the existence check, not the key.

⚪ ONE LINK DELIBERATELY LEFT ON THE UUID. app/discover/events/[slug]/page.tsx links a host circle by event.circle_id, and PublicEvent carries circle_id and circle_name but no circle_slug - surfacing it means changing public_event_by_slug, which is a different RPC and a different row. The 308 handles that link correctly today; it costs one hop.

⚪ THE MIGRATION IS APPLIED. Ledger repaired to the REPO version and the tool-minted twin deleted - and the twin is worth knowing about: apply_migration minted 20260907043043 from the real clock, which sorts into the MIDDLE of this repo's fictional 2027-prefixed ledger rather than at the end, so `order by version desc limit 5` cannot see it. Bijection verified exactly: 669 files, 669 ledger rows, repo version present, twin gone. lib/database.types.ts regenerated; HYG-052's own drift detector reports exactly one new object (Functions.public_circle_by_slug), nothing changed and nothing lost, which is the gate built two rows ago doing its job on its first live use.

entries.title: All 57 help articles ship an Article node with no image and no datePublished, and share one OG card
entries.detail:
Sweep 3 (SEO). app/(help)/help/[category]/[slug]/page.tsx calls articleSchema with title, description, path and updated only. lib/jsonld.ts emits image and datePublished only when passed, so all 57 nodes carry neither; Google lists image as REQUIRED for the Article rich result and datePublished as recommended. The frontmatter cannot supply the date: across all 57 the key set is title, description, category, order, updated, audience, featureKeys, status (+ role on 7). There is an updated, no published. Separately app/(help)/opengraph-image.tsx is a ROUTE-GROUP file with a fixed wordmark and the literal 'HELP CENTER', taking no params, so all 57 articles, 10 categories and /help/changelog share one identical card. Same defect SCAN-201 and SCAN-202 closed for podcast Shows and city hubs; help was not included. FIX in one PR: backfill a published date from git log --diff-filter=A and pass it through; pass image pointing at a per-article OG route; add app/(help)/help/[category]/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx reading params, reusing cardResponse + loadNunito, keeping the group card as the fallback for /help and the category indexes. ⚠️ BUDGET IT: a new per-entity OG route costs check:og-trace headroom, which read 18 + 64 of 100 on the last production build.
── CLOSED 2026-09-07, AND THE ROW WAS HALF-STALE 26 HOURS AFTER IT WAS WRITTEN. It was measured 2026-09-05; PR #2391 (9da46bf34, merged 2026-09-06) had already added a published key to all 57 articles AND wired both image and datePublished into the article page. Re-measured on origin/main before any work: 57/57 carry published in frontmatter, and page.tsx already passes published and image. So the row's central claim - "the frontmatter cannot supply the date ... there is an updated, no published" - was false, and the git log --diff-filter=A backfill it proposed was never needed. That backfill would also have been WRONG: Vercel builds from a shallow clone and CI checks out depth-1, so git history is absent at build time and every date would have come back empty with no gate noticing.

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINED was the OG-card half, and that is what shipped: a per-article opengraph-image route reading params, a matching twitter-image (required, because mergeStaticMetadata only overrides twitter when the segment declares its own file, so without it X and Slack keep the group card), and the schema extracted out of the page JSX into lib/help/article-jsonld.ts. The extraction is the point rather than tidiness: the inline node was untestable, which is how the fields went missing in the first place. The route-group card stays the fallback for /help, the category indexes and /help/changelog.

🔴 A LIVE DEFECT WAS FOUND ON THE WAY, and it had shipped. The EXISTING /help card drew white type on a bright beach photograph: its scrim was styled position:absolute + inset:0 with no display, and Satori implements NEITHER the inset shorthand NOR CSS's initial display:block, so the gradient resolved to 0x0 and painted nothing. Measured mean luminance 207 against a legibility threshold of 60. NOTHING COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: the route returned 200 with a valid JPEG of normal size, and check:og-trace was green - a swallowed failure with no gate that notices, the exact shape AGENTS.md names. Fixed with an explicit box and display, and pinned by a pixel-luminance assertion so it cannot regress silently.

BUDGET, measured rather than argued: predicted +2 rasterising and +0 incidental (the only page below [slug]/ already inherited libvips from the group card above it), then built and read the gate: 18 -> 20 rasterising, incidental 64 -> 64, identical to the 2026-09-05 production reading, against a budget of 100. No budget raised. ⚠️ That is a LOCAL artifact read and the gate says so itself; the authoritative reading is postbuild on the Vercel deploy, which is where AGENTS.md puts the artifact gates.

⚪ A SEPARATE FINDING IS FILED AS LIVE-205 rather than fixed here: lib/jsonld.ts emits unhashed per-entity OG URLs for events and Spaces, which 404.

verify.evidence: CLOSED 2026-09-07. Help articles carry image + datePublished (the latter was already true as of #2391, re-measured 57/57 on origin/main) and now have a per-article OG card: app/(help)/help/[category]/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx plus twitter-image.tsx, with the route-group card kept as the fallback for /help, the category indexes and /help/changelog. Schema extracted to lib/help/article-jsonld.ts so it is testable. Three red-then-green readings: reverting the schema call drops image/published and fails 5 tests with the corpus test naming all 57 articles; making the card ignore params fails "draws two different articles as two different cards" byte-identically; restoring inset:0 on the scrims fails at mean luminance 207 against a threshold of 60. check:help 57 articles / 36-of-36 core, check:seo 0, lint 0, tsc clean, 8 test files green. check:og-trace read 20 rasterising + 64 incidental of 100 on a local artifact; the authoritative reading is postbuild on the deploy.

entries.title: Seven public Space profile tabs are indexable and canonical but advertised nowhere
entries.detail:
Sweep 3 (SEO). app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/(profile)/ holds seven crawlable tabs beside the profile root: book, calendar, circles, collaborators, reviews, shop and [page]. Each has generateMetadata routed through spaceProfileMetadata, which stamps a per-tab title and its own canonical, and none sets robots.index false -- so all seven are indexable. app/sitemap.ts advertises only /spaces/<slug> plus the podcasts routes, and scripts/check-seo.mjs cannot see them because Scan C walks static routes while these sit under [slug]. About 7 tabs x 20 networked Spaces = ~140 indexable URLs reachable only by crawl-through, and /shop and /calendar carry exactly the commercial and local-intent content a local answer-engine query wants. FIX: expand spaceRoutes to emit the tabs a Space actually HAS, gated the way the pages gate themselves (storefront published + shop feature on, >=1 review, >=1 circle) so an empty tab never gets a URL -- the pattern podcastRoutes already uses -- at priority 0.5 under the profile's 0.6. If a tab is deliberately unwanted the alternative is teaching spaceProfileMetadata to noindex it; declaring nothing is the state to leave behind either way.

── CLOSED 2026-09-07 by #2387. lib/spaces/discovery.ts exports listNetworkedSpaceProfileTabs and app/sitemap.ts awaits it at the spaceRoutes section, emitting only the tabs a Space actually HAS, each gated the way its own page gates itself, at priority 0.5 under the profile root. ⚪ THE ROW WAS manual AND THEREFORE CLOSED NOTHING WHEN ITS CODE SHIPPED: the six sibling rows in that PR carried real probes and went done with the merge, while this one sat open behind an evidence string nothing evaluates. That is the manual-row cost ADR-970 accepts, and it is worth seeing once - a manual row does not fail the build, so it also does not NOTICE its own fix. It carries a cmd probe now, because the consequence became measurable the moment the reader existed: the probe asserts the export, the import, the await, and that the reader still gates on the Space row. Watched go RED by mutation before it was trusted - against f4d868fb3 (the commit before the crawl slice) it exits 1 naming the missing export, and exits 0 on the merged tree.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const disc=fs.readFileSync('lib/spaces/discovery.ts','utf8');const sm=fs.readFileSync('app/sitemap.ts','utf8');if(!/export const listNetworkedSpaceProfileTabs\b/.test(disc))throw new Error('discovery.ts does not export the tab reader');if(!/listNetworkedSpaceProfileTabs/.test(sm.split('\n').slice(0,60).join('\n')))throw new Error('app/sitemap.ts does not import it');if(!/await listNetworkedSpaceProfileTabs\(\)/.test(sm))throw new Error('app/sitemap.ts never awaits it - tabs reach no sitemap');if(!/entitlements|preferences/.test(disc.slice(disc.indexOf('listNetworkedSpaceProfileTabs'))))throw new Error('the tab reader does not gate on the Space row');"

entries.title: The Journey Gem bonus still pays a retired ladder, and three help articles describe a different number
entries.detail:
Sweep 3 (content). lib/quest/complete.ts:275 pays JOURNEY_GEM_BONUS of {25,50,100}, which docs/NAMING.md's Economy section declares RETIRED by ADR-305. A member finishing a third Journey is paid 200 Gems while /the-quest and three help articles describe 100. 🔴 THIS IS AN OWNER RULING, not a doc edit and not a code edit, which is why sweep 3 recorded it rather than picking a side: lowering the payout is a live economy change that members have already been paid under, and raising the documented number ratifies a ladder the naming canon says was retired. Whichever way it goes, the code, NAMING.md, /the-quest and the three help articles must land in the same change, because today a member can read two different numbers for the same action.

── OWNER-GATE RE-TESTED 2026-09-07 (the 26-row triage). THE RULING ALREADY EXISTS AND THE EXPOSURE IS ONE ROW. docs/NAMING.md and ADR-305 both say it: finishing a Journey pays +75 Zaps and a Pillar Trophy, and the escalating per-Journey Gem ladder (Initiate 25 / Adept 50 / Master 100) is marked RETIRED. Live check: reward_grants holds exactly ONE journey-finish Gem grant in the products history - 25 Gems on 2026-08-03 - beside its matching 75 Zaps. Nobody has ever been paid 50 or 100. So this is code and docs catching up with a decision already made, not a new economy decision.
── CLOSED 2026-09-07, and the fix was CODE-ONLY. The ruling already existed (docs/NAMING.md and ADR-305: finishing pays +75 Zaps and a Pillar Trophy; the escalating ladder is RETIRED), so nothing needed deciding.

🔴 THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG IN ITS MEMBER-FACING HALF, and enumerating every surface before editing is what found it. EVERY member-facing surface was already on canon: content/help/the-quest/your-journey.md, season-challenges.md, season-ranks.md and zaps-and-gems.md, the /the-quest body (lib/page-editor/templates/the-quest.ts), REWARDS-ECONOMY.md, ECONOMY-AND-JOURNEYS.md and the leader-training article all say +75 Zaps, a Pillar Trophy, and the Certificate's own 100 Gems. NO member-facing string anywhere stated the ladder. The row said three help articles describe a different number; they do not. The only thing out of step was lib/quest/complete.ts, which PAID it.

EXPOSURE MEASURED LIVE rather than taken on trust: reward_grants holds exactly ONE journey.finish.gems row, 25 Gems, granted 2026-08-03, at rank 1. Nobody has ever been paid the 50 or the 100 tier, so retiring the ladder takes nothing from any member and no clawback arises. A third finish would have paid 100 ladder Gems ON TOP of the Certificate's 100, i.e. 200 where every doc says 100, but no member ever reached it.

WHAT CHANGED: lib/quest/complete.ts drops the grant and the now-unused grantGemsOnce helper and stops returning gems; lib/gamification.ts drops the retired JOURNEY_GEM_BONUS constant, which nothing referenced once the payout went, and its comment; and the four places whose PROSE still asserted the ladder is live were corrected in the same pass, per the AGENTS.md rule that a doc contradicting the code gets fixed alongside it: docs/GLOSSARY.md (three passages), docs/GAMIFICATION-AUDIT.md, docs/QUEST-UI-REDESIGN.md and the function doc on lib/journeys/grants.ts.

verify.evidence: CLOSED 2026-09-07. One number is paid and documented everywhere: +75 Zaps and a Pillar Trophy on every finish, plus the Certificate’s own 100 Gems on the third. lib/quest/complete.ts grants no Gems for a Journey finish and lib/gamification.ts no longer declares JOURNEY_GEM_BONUS (grep finds the name only in the guard that forbids it). Pinned two ways in lib/quest, both mutation-proven: a behavioural test that a fresh completion writes no gems reward_grant and no gem_transactions row (1 failed against unfixed source, showing amount 25 under rule journey.finish.gems, then 5 files / 57 tests green), and a source-shape guard that complete.ts does not reference JOURNEY_GEM_BONUS (its positive control fired when the name was appended back, then reverted). Live exposure read the same day: exactly ONE journey.finish.gems row, 25 Gems, 2026-08-03, rank 1; the 50 and 100 tiers were never paid to anyone. Member-facing copy needed no edit because every help article, the /the-quest body and all economy docs already stated the canon numbers; the stale INTERNAL prose asserting the ladder was corrected in the same change.

entries.title: The app-space-console visual baseline is 158px stale, and pr-compare is not required so PRs keep merging past its red
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-05 from a pr-compare failure on #2382. All four /spaces/danieltyack/manage checks (desktop+mobile x dawn-light+dawn-dark) fail with 'Expected an image 390px by 2859px, received 390px by 3017px' - the live page is 158px taller than the committed baseline. ⚠️ NOT that PR's: the identical failure, same route and the same exact 2859 to 3017 pair, is in the pr-compare log of claude/scan2-d6 (run 33971217197), a backend-only PR touching check-ins, refunds and tips that renders none of this route - and that PR merged into main anyway. Playwright retried twice with byte-identical pixel counts, so it is deterministic, not a flake. ── THIS IS SCAN-507 RECURRING, WHICH IS THE POINT. SCAN-507 closed 2026-08-25 after the owner dispatched e2e-manual.yml (update_baselines + capture_shell) to recapture these same four PNGs at 3133 to 3154px; #2329 recaptured again to the current 2859. Three weeks later the same surface is 158px out. SCAN-507's own detail named the consequence and it has now come true a second time: 'a check that is red for a reason nobody owns trains everyone to ignore it, and then it reads as coverage' (ADR-970). At least eight PRs merged red on this in one day (scan2 D1/D3/D4a/D4b/D5b/D6/E4/E3b). ── WHY IT KEEPS RECURRING, which is the part worth fixing rather than re-photographing: this baseline is a fullPage shot of a surface whose body is LIVE PRODUCTION DATA - a Space console whose card count grows as the account's Space gains content. visual.spec.ts already knows this shape; its own note on Surface.viewportOnly says 'a full-page baseline of a live, shared stream measures WHEN it was taken, not how it looks', and that reasoning applies to this surface, but the surface is not marked viewportOnly. So recapture is a repeating owner chore with no end state, and every gap between chores is a red check everyone learns to merge past. THE OPTIONS, for an owner ruling rather than a patch: (a) mark app-space-console viewportOnly so it photographs the first screen and stops measuring the content count, which is what that note prescribes, at the cost of below-fold coverage; (b) seed a fixed fixture Space for the shell surfaces so the page stops depending on live data; (c) keep recapturing on a schedule and accept the red windows. ⚠️ Related but NOT the same row: LIVE-125 (open) is about the gate being blind to control-sized changes on tall pages; this row is about the baseline going stale by data drift. Note also that pr-compare is not a required check (LIVE-049), so none of this blocks a merge - which is exactly why it has been ignored eight times.

── RE-MEASURED 2026-09-07 and RE-SIZED XS -> S, because a recapture does not close it. The same pr-compare run carries TWO REAL ACCESSIBILITY FAILURES beside the pixel drift — a contrast failure and a serious-severity violation — and neither is a stale baseline: recapturing accepts the pixels and leaves both violations exactly where they are. The row read as "one dispatch and it is done"; it is one dispatch AND two a11y fixes. The stale numbers in this row are also wrong: the drift is 175px, not the 158px recorded.

🔴 ── CORRECTION 2026-09-07, FROM THE PRIMARY SOURCE, AND IT REVERSES AN EDIT MADE EARLIER THE SAME DAY. This row was re-titled to read "175px stale" on an audit note. The number was WRONG and the row was right the first time. pr-compare job 101775815865 (PR #2417, head bbb8dc349) prints it exactly: `Expected an image 390px by 2859px, received 390px by 3017px`, four times. 3017 - 2859 = 158. The original 158 stands.

⚠️ AND THE SECOND HALF OF THAT AUDIT NOTE IS UNVERIFIED. It said the same run carries two real accessibility failures (a contrast failure and a serious-severity violation) that a recapture will not clear, and that claim is why this row was re-sized XS -> S. The job output does not support it: 4 failed, 140 passed, 28 skipped, and every one of the four failures is a toHaveScreenshot pixel comparison on /spaces/danieltyack/manage across dawn-light x dawn-dark x desktop x mobile. No axe result, no contrast result, nothing else red. WHERE TO SETTLE IT, and my own first guess was WRONG so it is worth naming: I wrote that the a11y claim might belong to a different job. It does not. .github/workflows/e2e.yml says in its own header that pr-compare is smoke + a11y + visual — ONE check over TWO STEPS: "Smoke + a11y suite" (line 338, pnpm test:e2e) and then "Visual compare" (line 357, marked always() precisely so an a11y failure above cannot hide a pixel regression below). Playwright prints one summary per invocation, so the 4 failed / 140 passed I read is the VISUAL step summary alone. The a11y step has its own summary, earlier in the same log, and I did not read it. So the claim is PLAUSIBLE AND UNSETTLED rather than unsupported, and settling it costs exactly one thing: read the "Smoke + a11y suite" step summary in job 101775815865. The size stays S until somebody does. What IS settled: on that head every other check was green — lighthouse, test, lint, analyze, checks, drift, CodeQL — so whatever that step says, nothing outside pr-compare is red.

THE GENERAL POINT, since this row has now carried a wrong number in two directions: a number that arrives from a summary rather than from the log that produced it is a claim, not a measurement. This one cost an edit that made a correct row incorrect.

⚪ THE SAME RUN ALSO REPORTS A SECOND, SEPARATE BLIND SPOT, already owned: seven /admin surfaces did not photograph at all because the PW_MEMBER_EMAIL account bounces off the /admin role floor. The workflow names it itself — backlog HYG-027 — so it needs no new row, but it means the 4/11 surface coverage in that log is a floor, not a score.

✅ ── SETTLED 2026-09-07, AND THE AUDIT WAS RIGHT WHERE I SAID IT WAS UNSUPPORTED. The a11y step DID fail. I had read only the visual step's Playwright summary; the GitHub jobs API lists the steps and step 9, "Smoke + a11y suite", is `failure` beside step 10, "Visual compare". Two summaries, one job, and I quoted the second while reasoning about the first.

🔴 THE A11Y HALF IS A REAL DEFECT AND IT IS NOT ON THIS PAGE — it is in lib/spaces/accent.ts, it affects EVERY Space with a custom hex accent, and it is now LIVE-211. That is why this row narrows: what is left here is the visual recapture alone, which is the owner-dispatched half, so S -> XS.

THE THREE FAILING A11Y TESTS, all one root cause: desktop full audit (dawn-light), desktop contrast-only (dawn-dark), mobile full audit (dawn-light). Each reports exactly one serious element, `.eyebrow`, colour-contrast — 4.23 on light and 4.14 on dark against a 4.5 requirement. Six further elements matched named waivers and are correctly not counted.

⚠️ A PROCESS NOTE WORTH MORE THAN THE FINDING. This row carried a wrong pixel number (175 for 158) taken from an audit summary, and then a wrong dismissal ("unsupported") taken from a partial log read. Both were corrections that made the row worse. The rule that would have prevented both: read the artefact that produced the number — the step list before the step output, the failing step's own summary before the job's last one.

── 2026-09-07 16:21Z, pr-compare run 34141927302 (PR #2420): the a11y half is GREEN now that LIVE-211 shipped (165 passed, 0 failed). What remains is exactly the four app-space-console screenshots, still 158px out on mobile (2859 vs 3017) and now 175px on desktop (1985 vs 2160). Recapture is the whole of what is left.

── 🟢 DISPATCHED AND MEASURED 2026-09-08, AND THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE WAS THE FIRST THING TO FALL. This row said the recapture is "an owner-dispatched e2e-manual.yml run" and was sized and sequenced around that. It is not owner-only: e2e-manual.yml is a workflow_dispatch, an agent can trigger it, and run 34174895830 did — update_baselines + capture_shell against production, on a branch, with the member session minting cleanly. That is the third premise on this list to expire on the word "owner" (ADR-1082 caught three the same way), and it cost one tool call to test.

WHAT THE RUN ACTUALLY WROTE, and why only 4 of its 142 files are in this change. The capture rewrote EVERY committed baseline. Both halves were measured against origin/main before anything was taken:

  4 of 142 changed DIMENSIONS, and they are exactly this row's four:
      app-space-console desktop  1280x1985 -> 1280x1972
      app-space-console mobile    390x2859 ->  390x2765
  138 of 142 changed BYTES at BYTE-IDENTICAL DIMENSIONS, by 15,000-26,543 differing pixels each, measured with pixelmatch's own YIQ colour delta at Playwright's configured threshold (0.2), with anti-alias detection omitted so every figure is an UPPER BOUND. Worst: app-nearby desktop, 26,543 px. 138 of 138 are over the 400 px budget LIVE-125 set, by up to 66x.

⚠️ THOSE 138 ARE NOT CONTENT DRIFT, AND THE DIMENSIONS ARE THE PROOF. A full-page capture of a page whose content changed moves its HEIGHT; not one of the 138 moved by a single pixel while 15,000+ pixels inside it changed. That signature is rasterisation, not content — ADR-1165's cross-runner divergence, on marketing surfaces nothing has edited. So committing the recapture whole would have laundered a 138-surface rendering difference into the baselines under a row that names four files. Only the four are taken here. The 138 are filed as LIVE-212, because they qualify LIVE-125's budget rather than this row's recapture.

🔴 AND THE RUN REFUTED OPTION (c) OF THIS ROW'S OWN THREE, WHICH IS THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE PIXELS. Option (c) was "keep recapturing on a schedule and accept the red windows". pr-compare run 34141927302 read this surface at 390x3017 at 16:21Z on 2026-09-07. This capture read it at 390x2765 at 00:56Z on 2026-09-08 — 252 px apart, eight hours apart, against the same production, with no deploy between them that touches the route. A baseline that drifts 252 px in eight hours cannot be held by any recapture cadence. The surface is a fullPage shot of live production data and the suite's own note on Surface.viewportOnly already says what that measures: WHEN it was taken, not how it looks.

SO THE RULING NARROWS TO TWO, and it is still the owner's: (a) mark app-space-console viewportOnly, which is what that note prescribes, at the cost of below-fold coverage; or (b) seed a fixed fixture Space so the page stops depending on live data. This change buys the interval before whichever lands — it makes today's four checks comparable again instead of aborting on a dimension mismatch — and it does not close the row.

── ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-08 (ADR-1273): THE 138 WERE NOT RASTERISATION. "A full-page capture of a page whose content changed moves its HEIGHT" is false for the change that actually happened: the 2026-09-04 CTA sweep (#2348) changed the words inside fixed-size buttons on every public page, and the committed baselines were captured that day from a branch preview that had not merged it. Two production captures fifteen minutes apart were byte-identical on 144/144 files (runs 34181605405 / 34182476256), and the bands of the diff sit on the header, hero and footer CTAs. The four PNGs this row took were correct; the 138 it refused were correct too, and the full recapture landed under LIVE-212. The sentence "138 of the recapture's 142 files were rejected on measurement" in #2457's title measured a count and inferred a cause; the reader that says WHERE is pnpm visual:bands. Nothing here changes this row's open half: pr-compare is still not a required check, and it had been red on 140 of 144 surfaces since 2026-09-04 without stopping a merge.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-08: dispatched (run 34174895830, update_baselines + capture_shell against production) — the "owner-dispatched" premise had expired. 4 of 142 baselines changed dimensions and they are this row's four (mobile 2859 -> 2765, desktop 1985 -> 1972); those four are taken. The other 138 changed 15,000-26,543 px at byte-identical dimensions, which is rasterisation rather than content, and are filed as LIVE-212 rather than committed. Option (c) is refuted by measurement: the surface read 3017 px at 16:21Z on 2026-09-07 and 2765 px at 00:56Z on 2026-09-08. Closes when the owner rules between viewportOnly and a fixture Space, and the four checks pass on a PR that did not itself recapture them.

entries.title: A Space's custom accent is darkened by one theme-blind constant, so its eyebrow fails contrast in BOTH themes at once
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-07 by reading the a11y half of pr-compare job 101775815865, which LIVE-186 had recorded only as "two accessibility failures". It is one defect, it is in the design system rather than on the page, and it reaches every Space that sets a custom hex accent.

THE MECHANISM, one line: `hexAccentVars` derives `--color-primary-strong` as `color-mix(in srgb, ${hex} 72%, black)`. That mixes toward BLACK by a fixed 72%, and the SAME derived value is then used on the light ground and the dark ground. `PageHeading` renders its eyebrow as `text-primary-strong`, so on a themed Space the eyebrow takes that value in both themes.

MEASURED, and the numbers reproduce the CI log to within 0.01. The space in the failing run carries a brand accent of about #1FB6C5; 72% toward black gives #16838E. Against the light ground #faf8f4 that is 4.24 (CI logged 4.23). Against the dark ground #17120b it is 4.14 (CI logged 4.14). The requirement is 4.5. It fails BOTH, which is the tell that no single value was ever going to work.

🔴 AND THE FIX DIRECTIONS ARE OPPOSITE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. Re-deriving from the same accent: the LIGHT ground clears 4.5 at a 68% mix (#157C86, 4.65) — darker. The DARK ground clears 4.5 at a 76% mix (#178A96, 4.53) — LIGHTER. 72% sits in the dead zone between them, failing both by a hair. Darkening helps on light and HURTS on dark, because on a near-black ground you are moving the text toward the background. So the constant cannot be retuned; the derivation has to be per-theme, or clamped by measured contrast against the ground it will actually sit on.

⚠️ THE MATH TO DO IT WITH IS ALREADY IN THIS FILE. `readableTextOn` (line 43) does proper sRGB relative luminance with the 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722 weighting and the 0.179 WCAG crossover, to pick black or white text sitting ON the accent. The built-in FAMILIES were contrast-checked by hand too — one carries the comment "#11827A on white is 4.67:1 (AA)". Only the HEX path skips the check: it applies a fixed mix and never measures the result. The gap is not knowledge, it is that one path was never held to the standard the others were.

THE WORK: derive `--color-primary-strong` per theme (a light-ground value and a dark-ground value) and pick the mix by measuring contrast against that ground rather than by a constant — the luminance helper is right there. Then re-run the @a11y suite against a themed Space. ⚠️ It is a design-system change touching every themed Space, so the DIRECTION should be confirmed before it ships: a per-theme constant pair is the cheap fix, a measured clamp is the durable one, and they are not the same amount of work.

WHY P1: it is a live accessibility barrier on a member-facing page, it is agent-workable (unlike the recapture half it was bundled with), and the a11y ratchet is already red on it, so the gate is doing its job and being merged past — the same mechanism LIVE-125 describes.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1224), THE DURABLE FIX RATHER THAN THE CHEAP ONE. The row asked for the direction to be confirmed before shipping: a per-theme constant PAIR (cheap) or a measured clamp (durable). A constant pair fails the same way for the next brand colour — 68/76 are the numbers for ONE accent — so the hex path now MEASURES. `strongShades(hex)` walks the accent toward black (light) and toward white (dark) in whole-percent steps and keeps the FIRST shade that reads >= 4.52:1 against the hardest ground of that theme (the darkest light ground, the lightest dark ground, across DAWN and midnight), then emits `--color-primary-strong: light-dark(<light>, <dark>)`. The browser resolves it from the `color-scheme` the mode already sets on :root / .dark / every skin block, and the portal hook copies the inline string verbatim, so a Spark or Dialog opened from a themed Space carries both halves.

MEASURED, on the CI accent: #1FB6C5 -> light-dark(#147882, #1fb6c5). The light half reads 4.59 on the hardest light ground; the dark half is the accent itself at 6.10, because on a near-black ground the brand colour already reads and darkening it was the whole defect. The old #16838E is pinned in the test as failing both grounds. Nine accents (the CI one, the host amber, a navy, a yellow, black, white, three saturated primaries) are asserted >= 4.5 against EVERY ground of their theme, not only the hardest.

THE GATE THAT NOTICES: the ground lists are pinned BOTH WAYS to app/globals.css — every measured ground is a declared canvas/surface/surface-elevated value, and every declared one is measured — so a new skin ground fails a unit test instead of silently un-measuring the derivation. Fail-safe for a browser without light-dark(): the inline declaration is dropped and the host token inherits, legible and un-branded, rather than a value that fails contrast. -hover and -bg are unchanged: -hover is a button GROUND (its text is the luminance-picked text-on-primary) and -bg is a translucent tint, so neither is the text slot this row measured.

⚠️ NOT YET RE-RUN AGAINST A THEMED SPACE IN CI: the @a11y suite needs the deployed preview and the member account, which pr-compare provides on the PR. The probe measures the derivation; the a11y step on this PR's pr-compare run is the reading that closes the loop, and LIVE-186 (the pixel half of the same job) is unchanged by this.

── ✅ PROVEN IN CI 2026-09-07 16:21Z, pr-compare run 34141927302 on PR #2420 (head deaa67d): the "Smoke + a11y suite" step reads 165 passed, 112 skipped, 0 failed — against 3 failed on main's head 101775815865, all three the `.eyebrow` colour-contrast on the themed Space. The visual step's four failures in the same job are app-space-console only (1280x1985 vs 2160, 390x2859 vs 3017), which is LIVE-186's drift and untouched by this row.

verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE — that the hex path still produces ONE value for both grounds. Passes when the derivation either stops being a bare color-mix or gains a theme discriminator (light-dark(), a prefers-color-scheme branch, a data-theme branch, or a per-theme builder). Comment lines are stripped, so a TODO describing the fix cannot close it. Exits 79 if the file is gone. It deliberately does NOT assert a particular mix percentage: 68/76 are the numbers for ONE accent, and a fix that only retunes the constant for that accent would pass a percentage check while still failing every other brand colour. ── THREE ARMS PROVEN 2026-09-07, because a probe whose passing arm was never exercised is a row that can never close. (1) The tree as it stands exits 1 and names the offending line. (2) Rewriting the derivation as light-dark(color-mix(... 68%, black), color-mix(... 76%, black)) exits 0, so a real per-theme fix DOES close it. (3) Adding only a comment that names light-dark / prefers-color-scheme / data-theme still exits 1, so prose cannot launder it — the shape-not-truth failure this repo names in four ADRs. The tree was restored clean after each. ── CLOSED 2026-09-07: passes because the derivation is light-dark(<measured light>, <measured dark>) — lib/spaces/accent.test.ts holds the contrast arms.

entries.title: Four seeded demo products ship picsum.photos placeholder art, and the sitemap submits them WITH image nodes
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-06 by reading the LIVE sitemap in the hour after the owner submitted it to Search Console. Four /store/<uuid> entries carry an <image:image><image:loc> pointing at picsum.photos — the lorem-ipsum image service — e.g. https://picsum.photos/seed/tee/600/400 for a tee, plus pins, tote and stickers. MEASURED, not inferred: commerce_products with images matching picsum = 4, all status='active', so they are live products rather than drafts. Scope is exactly those 4 rows: the same query across practices, quests, store_items, spaces and events returns 0, because the practice and Journey picsum seeds introduced by migrations 20260606130000 and 20260622000000 were replaced as those files' own comments promised. This is the residue. ⚠️ WHY IT MATTERS MORE TODAY THAN YESTERDAY: until the sitemap was submitted nothing crawled these URLs, so seeded art cost nothing. Google requires sitemap image URLs to be on a domain you own or have verified, so a picsum.photos image node is at best ignored and at worst counts against the page; and a crawler that does fetch it sees stock placeholder art presented as product photography on a commerce URL. THE FIX IS A DATA EDIT, NOT CODE: give the four products real images, or move them off status='active' so they leave both the storefront and the sitemap. Deleting them is equally fine, they are demo rows. Nothing changes in app/sitemap.ts, which is correctly reporting what the table says.

── ✅ DONE 2026-09-06 (fan-out slice A), and the fix is CODE rather than the data edit the row proposed, because measuring the rows first changed the answer. All four products are `is_demo: true`, `owner_kind: 'platform'`, `market_published: false`, `status: 'active'` — they are seed dressing, not drafts someone forgot. So editing four rows would have fixed today and left the next demo seed to do it again. app/sitemap.ts now filters `!p.isDemo` on storeRoutes, which drops the whole demo row rather than just its image, since a picsum URL in an image sitemap is placeholder art presented as product photography.

⚪ DELIBERATELY NOT FILTERED IN listShopProducts, although that is where it would be shorter: that reader also feeds the /store storefront, and whether demo dressing appears in the shop is a product decision that is not this row's to make. The test pins that a demo product emits no /store URL while a real one does, and was confirmed to fail against the pre-change code.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("app/sitemap.ts","utf8");process.exit(/isDemo/.test(s)?0:1)'
verify.note: The row was manual against a production count; the durable consequence is the sitemap filter, so the probe measures that instead. A demo row reaching the crawl surface again means this filter was removed.

entries.title: A practice called untitled-practice-2 is public and in the submitted sitemap
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-06 in the live sitemap: https://frequencylocal.com/discover/practices/untitled-practice-2 is submitted for indexing at priority 0.5. Measured: 1 of 21 rows in practices has a slug beginning 'untitled'. It is a placeholder somebody created and never named, and it is now public, crawlable and pointed at by the sitemap that went to Search Console today. Thin content under a meaningless slug is the clearest low-quality signal available on a domain with no ranking history to spend. THE FIX IS A DATA EDIT: name it and give it a real slug, or unpublish it. ⚠️ THE GENERAL CASE IS WORTH A THOUGHT RATHER THAN A SWEEP: nothing stops the next unnamed draft reaching the sitemap the same way, because the reader asks whether a practice is public, not whether anyone finished writing it. If a second one appears, the row to file is a publish-time guard, not another rename.

── ✅ DONE 2026-09-06, and the premise was HALF WRONG in the direction that changes the fix. The row read the slug as a placeholder nobody had named. The row is titled `Daily Hypnosis` and has been since 2026-07-01: only the SLUG said untitled. So it was never thin content — it was a real practice wearing a meaningless URL, and unpublishing it (the row's other suggested fix) would have removed a good page.

WHAT SHIPPED: the slug is renamed to `daily-hypnosis` in production (id d61634a3…, verified: 0 practices now have a slug beginning `untitled`), and next.config.ts gains a permanent 308 from `/discover/practices/untitled-practice-2`, because that exact URL was submitted to Search Console the day before and a rename without it would have 404'd the thing the sitemap advertises.

🔴 THE CAUSE, which the row asked someone to think about rather than sweep: `uniquePracticeSlug` (lib/practices.ts:1691) is called at CREATE (:1361) and FORK (:1778) and nowhere else — `updatePractice` never re-mints a slug. So this was not one careless draft; EVERY practice created before it is named keeps `untitled-practice-N` as its public URL for good, no matter how well it is titled afterwards, and the Vera rename path at app/(main)/practices/actions.ts:388 sets exactly that title. The row said 'if a second one appears, the row to file is a publish-time guard'. The cause is stronger evidence than a second occurrence, so the guard is filed now as LIVE-201 rather than waiting for the next one to reach a crawler.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-06: `select count(*) from practices where slug like 'untitled%'` returns 0 (was 1). The renamed row keeps its submitted URL via a 308 in next.config.ts. The recurrence guard is LIVE-201.

entries.title: Nothing emits event.rsvp, so the RSVP step of the Circle funnel can never be measured
entries.detail:
The circle_to_rsvp funnel's final step is declared coverage:'unimplemented' in lib/analytics/journeys.ts, and the declaration is CORRECT: grep finds no emitter for event.rsvp anywhere in app/ or lib/, and engagement_events holds 0 rows for it. The funnel therefore refuses to report a conversion for that step, which is the honest behaviour and precisely what the registry was built to do. ── WHY NOW rather than whenever: RSVP is the conversion this product exists to produce, and the sitemap went to Search Console today. Every visitor who now arrives from search and RSVPs will be invisible in the one readout built to measure whether any of it worked. The registry's other 17 steps were re-verified against production on 2026-09-06 and all 17 are accurate; this is the single remaining hole. ── ⚠️ ITS TWIN WAS ALREADY FIXED AND NOBODY NOTICED, which is the reason to act rather than assume. land_to_beta/account_created carried the same 'unimplemented' declaration and the same 'nothing emits it' note until 2026-09-06, while app/auth/callback/route.ts had been emitting account.created with an idempotency key and production held 7 rows. journeys.test.ts pinned the stale pair, so a green test asserted a claim whose subject had changed underneath it. That step is now 'observed'; this one is the real gap. THE FIX: emit event.rsvp from the RSVP path with the same exactly-once shape, an idempotency key on profile plus event so a re-RSVP cannot double count.

── ✅ DONE 2026-09-06 (fan-out slice E). `event.rsvp` is emitted from BOTH member RSVP writers — toggleRSVP and setRsvpStatus — through `track()` rather than raw recordEngagementEvent, because it is a registered taxonomy event and so also needs the GA4 server-side mirror. The idempotency key is `event.rsvp:<eventId>:<profileId>`, so a re-RSVP cannot double count. It fires only on a CONFIRMED PERSISTED SEAT: not waitlist, not host-pending, not on a refused write. The QR door routes through setRsvpStatus, so it is covered without a second emitter.

⚪ THE REGISTRY NOW READS 'emitted', NOT 'observed', and the distinction is the row's own point. journeys.ts defines `observed` as emitted AND rows existing in the ledger today; the emitter ships now and no production row exists yet, so declaring 'observed' would have been precisely the stale unverifiable claim this row was filed about. Both values remove the step from journeyGaps(), so the funnel reports the conversion either way. Promote to 'observed' from a production read, not from this change.

THE EXACTLY-ONCE TEST IS NOT VACUOUS: it drives first RSVP → withdraw → re-join → the second path, asserts the action emitted MORE THAN ONCE so the dedupe is load-bearing, that every emit carried the same key, and that the ledger holds one row. Signed-out guest RSVPs carry no profile id and so cannot carry the key; they enter the funnel when claimed at sign-in.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const walk=(d,o)=>{for(const e of fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true})){if(e.name==='node_modules'||e.name.startsWith('.'))continue;const f=d+'/'+e.name;if(e.isDirectory())walk(f,o);else if(/\\.tsx?$/.test(f)&&!/\\.test\\.|journeys\\.ts$|events\\.ts$/.test(f))o.push(f)}return o};const files=[...walk('app',[]),...walk('lib',[])];if(files.length<500){console.error('walk found only '+files.length+' files - not descending, a clean result would prove nothing');process.exit(1)}const hit=files.filter(f=>/event\\.rsvp/.test(fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8')));process.exit(hit.length?0:1)"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE: some file outside the registry and the taxonomy references event.rsvp, i.e. an emitter exists. journeys.ts and events.ts merely NAME the marker and are excluded, or the row would close on its own declaration. Carries a 500-file walk floor so a walk that stopped descending cannot report a clean tree and pass by not looking (ADR-970).

entries.title: The proxy sets a 90-day attribution cookie on robots.txt and sitemap.xml, so crawler fetches land in attribution
entries.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 from live response headers rather than inferred. GET https://frequencylocal.com/robots.txt returns a set-cookie for fq_attr carrying landing:"/robots.txt" with Max-Age=7776000, and sitemap.xml returns the same with landing:"/sitemap.xml". The cause is proxy.ts's matcher, which excludes _next internals and static image extensions and nothing else, so the first-touch attribution middleware runs on both files. TWO CONSEQUENCES, both small and both real: every crawler request carries a pointless Set-Cookie, and any bot that keeps cookies gets a first-touch record whose landing page is robots.txt — noise in exactly the acquisition data that becomes worth reading now that the sitemap is submitted and organic traffic is expected for the first time. THE FIX is one matcher entry: add robots.txt, sitemap.xml and the llms files to the negative lookahead beside the static assets. Left unmade deliberately — proxy.ts is the highest-traffic file in the codebase and its matcher governs auth and tenancy as well as attribution, so a scan finding does not justify editing it in the same pass. It wants its own change with the proxy tests run against it.

── ✅ DONE 2026-09-06 (fan-out slice A). proxy.ts:284 adds `robots\.txt$|sitemap\.xml$|llms\.txt$|llms-full\.txt$` to the matcher's negative lookahead, and NOTHING ELSE in that file changed — the row was explicit that the matcher governs auth and tenancy as well as attribution. The exclusion was verified by compiling the literal and asserting path by path: the four files are excluded, and `/`, `/feed`, `/spaces/foo`, `/api/x`, `/settings` and `/blog/robots.txt` all still run the proxy.

verify.cmd: node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('proxy.ts','utf8');const m=s.match(/matcher:\s*\[([\s\S]*?)\]/);if(!m)process.exit(1);process.exit(/robots|sitemap/.test(m[1])?0:1)"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE at its source: proxy.ts’s matcher names robots or sitemap, i.e. those paths are excluded from middleware. Fails today, passes when the exclusion lands, and reads the matcher block specifically so an unrelated mention of the word elsewhere in the file cannot close it.

entries.title: Fourteen cron routes have hit the 300s ceiling 314 times, and no row owns a per-invocation work budget for them

source.ref: LIVE-124, the non-page half it scoped out

entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit, from LIVE-124's own tail: "THE PART THAT SURVIVES IS A DIFFERENT ROW'S SHAPE: the 314 non-page timeouts. Fourteen distinct /api/cron/* routes appear. A cron that runs past 300s is a work-per-invocation problem — it wants batching or a smaller window, not a page-performance fix … Scope this row to those, or close it and open the cron-budget row cleanly." Neither happened; LIVE-124 stayed scoped to the page timeouts and the cron half had no home. A cron that times out at the platform ceiling does not just fail once: with the claim-then-send discipline of ADR-1212 the unfinished tail is retried next run, so a cron whose window grows faster than its budget falls further behind every invocation, and the heartbeat reads it as a 500 each time. THE WORK: from the Vercel 7-day error read, list the fourteen routes with their counts; for each, either bound the work per invocation (a batch size and a resumable cursor, the campaign-runner pattern) or shrink the window, and record the chosen budget in the route header. Measure before and after: the same get_runtime_errors read, filtered to /api/cron, should show the Task-timed-out group at zero on deployments carrying the change.
── ⚠️ PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-09-07 AND THE HEADLINE NUMBER HAS EXPIRED. This row's stated work opens "from the Vercel 7-day error read, list the fourteen routes with their counts". That read was run today and the honest answer is that there are NO cron timeouts in the current 7-day window: the `Task timed out after 300 seconds` group does not appear in the project's grouped runtime errors at all, so the fourteen routes cannot be listed from it and their counts are zero.

🔴 THAT IS NOT A CLOSE, AND THE ROW SHOULD NOT BE CLOSED ON IT. The 314 was measured in a window containing a 35-minute Supabase outage, so a quiet week says the crons are not currently falling behind - it does not say their per-invocation budget is bounded, which is what this row is actually about. A cron whose window grows faster than its budget is a defect that shows up the first busy week, and the absence of an error group is exactly the kind of evidence ADR-970 warns reads as coverage without being coverage.

WHAT THIS CHANGES IS THE INSTRUMENT, not the work. The error group was never the right measurement: it only fires at the 300s CEILING, so it can only see a cron that has already failed. Re-scope the first step to read DURATION rather than errors - the platform's own per-invocation function duration for the /api/cron/* routes - so a cron trending toward the ceiling is visible before it hits it. The remaining work (bound each cron's per-invocation window, batch or narrow it) is unchanged and undone.

── 🟢 THE RE-SCOPED FIRST STEP IS DONE 2026-09-07: THE INSTRUMENT NOW EXISTS ON EVERY CRON, and the row's remaining work (bounding each budget) is unchanged and still open.

WHAT THE READ FOUND. log.time was already available and EIGHT of TWENTY-SEVEN cron routes had adopted it. That is the shape of an instrument that will never be complete: the nineteen without it include process-queue, the busiest of them all at 720 invocations a day, and a cron added next month would have started uninstrumented again. So the timer went into withCronHeartbeat - the wrapper every cron already goes through - rather than into nineteen route files. Coverage is now structural, and scripts/cron-freshness.test.ts ALREADY fails a scheduled cron that is not wrapped, so the guard keeping it universal existed and needed no new gate.

⚠️ NOT log.time AROUND THE HANDLER, deliberately. log.time decides ok by whether the function threw, and a cron that RETURNS a 500 has not thrown - it would log the loudest failure mode as a success. The seam reads the response status instead, the same rule the fail-ping already used. The clock also stops BEFORE the heartbeat ping, which is a third-party network call and is not the job's work.

FIRST READINGS, production dpl_BU432fbGAwdpwvBZHU2JKR9a4VGW, 2026-09-07 09:45Z, from the eight routes that were already instrumented, against a 300,000 ms ceiling:
    cron.journey_drips     533 ms
    cron.space_campaigns   134 ms
    cron.space_drips       127 ms
    cron.nurture           115 ms

🔴 AND THOSE NUMBERS PROVE ALMOST NOTHING YET, which is the honest thing to say about them. Every counts line in the same window reads zero - due 0, claimed 0, sent 0, scanned 1 - so these are the durations of a cron with NO WORK TO DO. They are a floor, not a budget: they measure the fixed cost of waking up, connecting and finding nothing. The reading this row actually needs is the same query on a busy week, which is why the instrument had to land first.

INVOCATION VOLUME, same 24h window, for whoever sets the budgets: process-queue 720, publish-scheduled / space-drips / conversation-batches / space-campaigns 288 each, season-go-live and embed-room-messages 144, event-reminders / space-follower-event-reminders / nurture 96, journey-drips / referral-release / embed-events 48, practice-lifecycle 24, and eleven dailies at 1. A budget is per invocation, so the busiest route is where an unbounded window compounds fastest.

WHAT REMAINS, unchanged: each route states a per-invocation budget and either batches to it or narrows its window. The close condition moves off the error group, which could only ever see a cron that had already hit the ceiling: chart cron.run duration_ms by job over a busy week and require every route to sit under its stated budget.

── ✅ THE INSTRUMENT IS VERIFIED ON THE REAL THING, 2026-09-07 10:10-10:12Z, production dpl_5oUSQMBARsRkFPWc7WH8DQqZWuGo. Not "the tests pass" - the line is queryable in production runtime logs, which is the reading AGENTS.md demands of any gate before it is believed.

AND IT PAID FOR ITSELF IN THE FIRST TWO MINUTES. Five of the eight routes sampled had NO duration instrument before this change, and one of them is the slowest thing on the board:

    publish-scheduled      1896 ms   <- previously uninstrumented, and 14x the next slowest
    embed-room-messages     392 ms   <- previously uninstrumented
    conversation-batches    196 ms   <- previously uninstrumented
    space-campaigns         136 ms
    space-drips             137 ms
    season-go-live          129 ms   <- previously uninstrumented
    process-queue       128/132 ms   <- previously uninstrumented, and the busiest at 720/day

publish-scheduled is exactly the kind of reading the old instrument could NEVER have produced: it is nowhere near the 300s ceiling, so the error group would stay silent about it forever, and it is nonetheless an order of magnitude above its neighbours on an IDLE system. Whether that is a fixed startup cost or work that scales is now a question the data can answer over a busy week; before today it was not even askable.

⚪ A FREE CROSS-CHECK CAME WITH IT: on the two routes that already carried log.time, the seam's timer and the route's own agree to within a millisecond (space_drips 137 vs 137, space_campaigns 135 vs 136). Two independent timers measuring the same span is a stronger argument that the number means what it says than either alone.

── 🔴 CORRECTION 2026-09-07 11:20Z: THE 1896 ms READING WAS A COLD START, AND THE CLAIM BUILT ON IT WAS WRONG. This row said publish-scheduled ran at 1896 ms, "14x the next slowest", and called it exactly the reading the old instrument could never have produced. That was generalised from ONE sample, taken minutes after the instrument itself deployed.

Fourteen readings of the same route over the following 70 minutes, every five minutes:
    1896, 122, 121, 116, 121, 121, 114, 121, 356, 127, 376, 117, 138, 155

The 1896 is the FIRST cron.run line the route ever emitted (10:10:41Z, the first invocation on dpl_5oUSQMBARsRkFPWc7WH8DQqZWuGo, the deploy that shipped the instrument). Every subsequent reading is 114-376 ms with a median near 121. publish-scheduled is an ordinary cron, not an outlier, and there is no 14x anything.

⚪ WHAT SURVIVES, and it is the part that matters: the instrument works, five previously-uninstrumented routes are now visible, and the correction was only possible BECAUSE the line is emitted every five minutes. A single reading looked like a finding; fourteen readings made it a cold start. That is the instrument doing its job on its own first claim.

⚠️ THE LESSON IS THE ONE THIS ROW ALREADY CARRIED ABOUT IDLE READINGS, applied one level up: an idle reading proves nothing about budgets, and a SINGLE reading proves nothing about anything. n=1 is not a measurement, and the fact that it came from a real production log made it feel like one. Do not quote a per-invocation duration from fewer than a handful of samples, and mark the first invocation on a new deployment as what it is.

STILL UNCHANGED: the window remains idle (every counts line reads due 0 / sent 0 / processed 0), so none of these numbers say anything about per-invocation BUDGETS, which is what this row is actually about. That still needs a loaded week.

── 🟢 THE BUDGET HALF IS STATED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1229), AND THE ROW STAYS OPEN FOR THE READING THAT CLOSES IT. Every route now carries a per-invocation budget through the seam it is already wrapped in: withCronHeartbeat takes an optional `{ budgetMs }`, defaults it to DEFAULT_CRON_BUDGET_MS (a fifth of the 300 s ceiling, 60 s), and the `cron.run` line gains `budget_ms` + `over_budget`; crossing the budget also emits a `cron.over_budget` warning, so the chart this row asks for has a line to read against rather than only the ceiling the old error group could never see a route approach. All 27 routes ride the default today, on purpose: nothing in the idle readings above says which route needs more, and a number set before the busy week is a guess dressed as a budget. A route that proves it needs more declares it beside its handler, where the number is reviewed with the work it bounds.

WHAT STILL CLOSES THIS ROW, unchanged: a `cron.run` read over a BUSY week showing every route under its stated budget, or the routes that are not batched or narrowed to it. The instrument now says which those are the first time it happens.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1252): EVERY ROUTE APPLIES A PER-INVOCATION BUDGET, AND A SOURCE-SHAPE TEST MEASURES THE APPLICATION. The row's remaining work was to bound each cron's window; that is done through one pure module, lib/cron/budget.ts (cronBudget(items) with a latching 240 s clock, take(rows), and summary(processed, remaining)), applied inside every handler in the campaign-runner shape and proven by app/api/cron/budget.test.ts, which walks the real route tree (floor 27), strips comments, and fails a route that does not import the module, call it with a literal N inside a function, apply it (budget.items on the driving query, budget.take, or budget.exhausted in the loop), and log budget.summary. Seven positive controls fail synthetic routes in each of those ways. The probe below carries the same checks.

MEASURED FIRST, 2026-09-07, before any change. Class (a) already bounded (a batch size and a resumable claim/cursor); (b) bounded window, unbounded fan-out inside it; (c) unbounded. The N column is the budget each route now declares and applies.

    route                            /day   class  driver before                                              N     bound after
    billing-renewals                    1   (b)    every active agreement due in 30d, no limit                 200   take() sorted by paid_through; the touch stamp is the claim
    conversation-batches              288   (a)    limit 1000 + row claim; digests limit 1000 + watermark    1000   budget.items passed to both flushes; digests ordered oldest-first
    demo-decay                          1   (b)    every demo circle, no limit; reals capped at 500            500   limit + clock in both loops; report.visited/remaining
    embed-events                       48   (a)    backfill limit 100, null embedding is the cursor            100   budget.items
    embed-help                          1   (b*)   fixed repo corpus, hash-skipped                              500   BOUNDED BY DESIGN (stated + summary)
    embed-library                       1   (a)    limit 500, null embedding is the cursor                      500   budget.items
    embed-practices                     1   (a)    limit 100, null embedding is the cursor                      100   budget.items
    embed-room-messages               144   (a)    limit 150, returns remaining                                 150   budget.items; summary(embedded, remaining)
    enforce-retention                   1   (b*)   four bulk statements, no per-row work                          4   BOUNDED BY DESIGN (stated + summary)
    event-occurrences                   1   (b)    every recurring anchor, per-anchor generate, no limit      2000   .order(created_at).limit + clock; NO cursor (see below)
    event-reminders                    96   (b)    events in window, then every RSVP, claim per RSVP           500   take() soonest-first on events and RSVPs + clock; the claim resumes
    journey-drips                      48   (a)    limit 200 + send ledger                                      200   budget.items
    journey-prompt                     24   (c)    EVERY enrolled member, loader + insert + push, no limit    2000   take() sorted + clock; per-day dedupe; NO cursor (see below)
    lifecycle-triggers                  1   (c)    EVERY active membership with a flag down, no limit          500   .order(joined_at asc).limit + clock; the flags are the claim
    nurture                            96   (a)    limit 200 + status flip                                      200   budget.items
    practice-lifecycle                 24   (a)    SWEEP_CAP 2000 per phase, no clock                          2000   limit passed to all three phases + clock; result.remaining
    process-queue                     720   (a)    claim_outbox_jobs limit 25 under SKIP LOCKED                  25   budget.items
    publish-scheduled                 288   (b)    every due dispatch, no limit                                 200   .order(scheduled_for).limit; the status flip is the claim
    referral-release                   48   (b)    events limit 3000, then every unsettled candidate           200   slice + clock; a released pair is settled next run
    refresh-traits                      1   (b)    whole-population RPCs; resonance anchors 2000, embeddings 500  2000   limitAnchors from budget.items; traits half whole-population by design; NO cursor on the opted-in read
    season-go-live                    144   (b*)   one promotion per run                                          1   BOUNDED BY DESIGN (stated + summary(promoted, due - promoted))
    space-campaigns                   288   (a)    limit 100 + sending lease + ledger (ADR-1212)                100   budget.items
    space-drips                       288   (a)    limit 200 + enrollment lease (ADR-1212)                      200   budget.items
    space-follower-event-reminders     96   (b)    events in window, then every follower, sent ledger          200   .order(starts_at).limit per lead + clock in both loops; the ledger resumes
    summarize-vera-memory               1   (a)    limit 50 + claim                                              50   budget.items
    vera-owner-brief                    1   (b)    every operator + every Space owner, no limit                 200   slice + clock; per-day dedupe read; NO cursor (see below)
    weekly-digest                    1/wk   (c)    EVERY active member, assemble + gate + claim + send, no limit  2000  take() sorted + clock; per-week marker claim; NO cursor (see below)

Twelve (a), twelve (b) of which three are bounded by their own shape, three (c). All 27 now carry the marker; the allowlist of still-unbounded routes is EMPTY, and BOUNDED_BY_DESIGN in the test is frozen to the three starred rows with a reason beside each.

⚠️ FOUR ROUTES HAVE A CLOCK BUT NO CURSOR, RECORDED HERE AS THE NEXT ROW, NOT HIDDEN. journey-prompt, weekly-digest and vera-owner-brief dedupe per day or per week, so a cut-off run re-reads a sorted head at one read per member before the dedupe says no; event-occurrences and the resonance read in refresh-traits re-read the same head because generation writes nothing on the anchor. Each wants a watermark column (a generated-at or prompted-at stamp) so the driving query can order by staleness; no migration was added on this row per its instructions. Their N is set above today's population so the 240 s clock is the bound that matters, and stopped_on_time: true on any of them is the reading that opens the cursor row.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: what any cron sends or writes per item. The heartbeat seam and its 60 s expected-duration reading (ADR-1229) are untouched; the module's clock is a different number answering a different question. The busy-week cron.run read is still worth taking, and the row no longer waits on it.

entries.title: A member can choose a Daily or Weekly email digest, and the batcher that would honour it was never built
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's code sweep: a marker in the tree that promised later work, with no row owning it. lib/notification-preferences.ts:190 exports DIGEST_BATCHER_EXISTS = false with the comment "The cron was a follow-up that never shipped … Flip this to true in the same commit that ships the batcher." The consequence is member-facing: the notification settings offer per-category frequencies (the freq_* columns), a member who picks Daily or Weekly is recorded as having done so, and every send still goes realtime because nothing reads those columns and batches. /api/cron/weekly-digest is the COMMUNITY digest (lib/digest), not this. So the preference is a switch wired to nothing — the class of failure SCAN-548 closed for mutes ("hide the ten switches nothing reads, make a mute actually mute"), and this is the one it left. THE WORK, in the order the file itself prescribes: a batcher cron that reads freq_* per profile, collects the deferred realtime sends for the window (the outbox already carries a dedupeKey and the cron marker table from ADR-1212), sends one email per category per window, and flips DIGEST_BATCHER_EXISTS to true in the same change so shouldDeferToDigest starts deferring. Until then the honest alternative is SCAN-548's: hide the Daily/Weekly options rather than record a choice nothing honours. Either closes the row; leaving the switch visible and inert does not.
── CLOSED 2026-09-07 ON THE ROW'S SECOND PATH, AND ITS PREMISE HAD ALREADY EXPIRED WHEN IT WAS FILED. The row's title claim - "a member can choose a Daily or Weekly email digest" - is FALSE and was false a month before the row was written. The owner removed the per-topic Frequency column on 2026-08-10; measured on this tree, ZERO .tsx files anywhere under app/ or components/ mention daily_digest or weekly_digest, and the settings form's own comment at form.tsx:118 records the column being taken out. So the row was describing a switch that no longer exists.

MEASURED IN PRODUCTION rather than reasoned about: notification_preferences carries ONE row, and every one of its six freq_* columns reads 'realtime'. Nobody has a stored digest cadence, so there is no cohort silently receiving nothing and no backfill to run. That is the question the row actually turned on, and it took one query.

The row named both closing paths itself - ship the batcher, or hide the options - and said either closes it. The second shipped. What remains is correct rather than residual: DIGEST_BATCHER_EXISTS stays false and isFrequencyDeferred stays gated on it, so even a tampered payload that stores 'daily_digest' sends realtime instead of muting. The two values stay in NOTIFICATION_FREQUENCIES and in the check constraint deliberately: they are what makes a legacy stored value READABLE, and normalizeFrequency coerces anything else to realtime.

⚪ THE OWNER'S 2026-08-10 CALL EXISTED ONLY AS A COMMENT IN ONE FILE until now. ADR-1219 records it against ADR-615, which is the decision that introduced the frequency selector - a decision doc that still described a live feature. The batcher remains buildable and the constant is still the seam; this row closes because the member-facing defect is gone, not because the idea was abandoned.

verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE of the path actually taken, in two arms, and both are mutation-proven. Arm 1: no rendered component anywhere under app/ or components/ offers a digest cadence, so a member cannot record a choice nothing honours (adding one .tsx naming daily_digest fails it). Arm 2: the deferral is still gated on DIGEST_BATCHER_EXISTS, so a legacy or tampered stored value sends realtime rather than muting (removing the guard line fails it). Comment lines are stripped first so arm 2 cannot pass by reading the documentation above the function. If the batcher is ever built, the options come back and arm 1 SHOULD fail - re-point it at DIGEST_BATCHER_EXISTS === true, which is what the original probe measured.

entries.title: Two create entry points still bypass the governed create layer, each blocked on a kernel ruling (18 named in UNROUTED on 2026-08-11, 3 after ADR-1249, 2 after ADR-1262)
entries.detail: FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's code sweep: a marker in the tree that promised later work, with no row owning it. scripts/check-creates.mjs:266-290 holds UNROUTED, a Map of 18 create entry points that "SHOULD route and do not yet (ADR-988 shipped the layer with no adopters…)", every entry dated 2026-08-11, under a header that says "🔴 THE CONTRACT IS THEREFORE UNENFORCED TODAY. Every line below is real, unaudited create volume." The gate is a ratchet — the list may only shrink — and it has not shrunk once in 26 days, because a ratchet with no row is a ratchet nobody turns. The backlog mentions ADR-988 nowhere. THE WORK: route each entry through the governed layer (createWithGovernance or whichever the ADR names) and delete its UNROUTED line in the same change; one entry per small PR is fine, and the gate's own test proves each removal. Do not shorten the list by deleting lines for entries that still bypass. PROGRESS 2026-09-07 (ADR-1249): premise re-tested on main f19a1f9 before the work: UNROUTED still held all 18, none had adopted, and node scripts/check-creates.mjs printed 1 of 19 entry points routed. Routed 15 in one PR through proposeAndConfirmCreate, the one-tap wrapper added beside confirmCreate in lib/ai/vera/create-entity.ts (a member tapping Create in a wizard is both phases performed by the person, ADR-988 §1): Circle createDraftFromSparkAction, createBlankDraftAction, createSpaceCircleAction; Event createEvent; Journey createJourneyDraftAction, createJourneyFromSparkAction, createJourneyFromTemplateAction; Practice createPracticeFromSparkAction, createPracticeAction, createPracticeDraftAction; Space createSpace, createBusinessSpace; Listing createListingAction; Product createMakerProductAction, createSpaceProductAction. Every writer and its input are unchanged; each road keeps its own gate ahead of the layer and its own error surface behind it. 3 remain (18 to 3), and none is an effort gap: each, routed as it stands, would refuse a create the road accepts today. createSpacePracticeAction is deliberately open to a free Space manager while CREATE_GATES makes practice a Crew-only capability the layer re-checks at the write (needs a per-road scoped gate, the ruling ADR-1240 also deferred); saveDraft is born with no startsAt while the Event manifest requires one (needs a ruling on whether a draft-status Event is a create); createHousingListingAction accepts no city while the Housing manifest requires it (needs the form and the manifest to agree). Each reason is on its UNROUTED line, and scripts/check-creates.test.ts now asserts the 15 positively and caps UNROUTED at 3, so the ratchet cannot slip back. PROGRESS 2026-09-08 (ADR-1262): premise re-tested on main 02587021b before the work — node scripts/check-creates.mjs printed 16 of 19 entry points routed and 3 named in UNROUTED, so the row's "eighteen" had expired on 2026-09-07 while the work had not; the title now carries the real count. Routed the third: createHousingListingAction. Its line named the smallest of the three rulings — the Housing manifest declares city required (one of the eight questions its Spark asks) while the shared housing form left the input optional and the action stored null, so checkCreateDraft would have refused a post the road accepts. The ruling taken: the manifest wins. The form asks for a city, and BOTH housing actions enforce it server-side ahead of the layer (updateHousingListingAction states it mirrors create field for field, and a save that would blank an existing city is refused too). The road then routes through proposeAndConfirmCreate with the writer, its input and the housing extension row unchanged; housing's gate is scoped, so the layer records it rather than becoming a second one. scripts/check-creates.test.ts asserts the routed key positively, caps UNROUTED at 2, and asserts the city rule in all three places that must agree. 2 remain, both still blocked on rulings this row cannot take on its own: createSpacePracticeAction needs the per-road scoped gate ADR-1240 deferred, and saveDraft needs a ruling on whether a draft-status Event is a create at all. The probe is unchanged and still fails: it closes only when UNROUTED is empty.

verify.cmd: node -e 'import("./scripts/check-creates.mjs").then(m=>process.exit(m.UNROUTED&&m.UNROUTED.size===0?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(79))'
verify.note: The module exports UNROUTED and only runs its gate under a main guard, so importing it is a pure read. Closes when the map is empty. Exit 79 if the import itself fails, so a broken module is not read as a verdict.
