entries.title: The journey-prompt cron fires at one UTC morning for everyone and says it cannot do better because profiles have no timezone, which they have
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's code sweep: a marker in the tree that promised later work, with no row owning it. app/api/cron/journey-prompt/route.ts:9 reads "Timezone-aware local morning is a follow-up (the codebase has no per-profile timezone yet — see app/api/cron/event-reminders)." The premise expired: profiles.home_timezone exists and is read by lib/comms/sms.ts:13, and SCAN-106 already moved Vera's dispatch onto it. So the prompt lands at a fixed UTC hour, which is late morning for one coast and before dawn for the other, for a feature whose whole point is a morning nudge. THE WORK: resolve each candidate's local hour from home_timezone (the SMS path is the pattern), send when it is morning there, and keep the date-stamped push tag as the once-per-day guard. A member with no timezone set keeps today's behaviour.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P1 on 2026-09-07 in the full re-prioritisation pass: a repair whose blocker is a false statement in the code: the journey-prompt cron fires at one UTC morning for every member and says it cannot do better because profiles have no timezone — they have one. Ready to work, member-facing every day.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1225). PREMISE RE-TESTED AND IT HELD: the header still said profiles carry no timezone, and profiles.home_timezone is read by the SMS quiet-hours gate, lib/member-day.ts, the practice day and Vera's dispatch. THE SHAPE: the schedule is hourly (`0 * * * *`), and each run asks lib/journeys/prompt-morning.ts `morningFor(now, tz)` per member — due when it is LOCAL_MORNING_HOUR (8) in their zone, and for a member with no zone on file (or an unparseable one) due at LEGACY_UTC_HOUR (13), which is the old daily schedule verbatim, so nobody the change cannot improve sees any change. The dedupe key and the push tag now carry the member's LOCAL day, so Auckland at 20:00Z on the 5th is keyed to the 6th, and one member gets one prompt per local day across 24 runs. The timezone gate runs BEFORE the per-member loader (one batched `.in('id')` read of home_timezone, chunked at 500), so the 23 runs a member is not due cost no loader call; the new `notDue` count separates "not their morning" from "nothing left to do". hourInZone joined lib/time/zone.ts beside dayInZone.

⚠️ ONE SIDE-EFFECT FOR THE OWNER, stated rather than hidden: the cron-freshness contract (scripts/cron-freshness.mjs) now derives a 2 h fresh-by window for journey-prompt instead of 2 days, so the matching Healthchecks.io check period must be set to hourly or it will page on the first missed hour — that is the third-party side of OWN-005 and is not settable from the repo. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's cron table says hourly; check-arch-doc holds at 27 claims.

verify.note: Passes when no file in the route directory still claims the codebase has no per-profile timezone. The consequence (an hourly schedule, and a per-member local-morning gate) is pinned by app/api/cron/journey-prompt/route.test.ts: a Pacific member is not due at 13:00Z and is due at 15:00Z, Auckland's key carries their own day, and a member with no zone keeps 13:00 UTC.

entries.title: Three "remove at launch" items have no launch date and no owner: the temporary induction renders, the beta switch, and the switched-off flyer downloads
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's code sweep: a marker in the tree that promised later work, with no row owning it. Three things in the tree are labelled temporary against a launch that has no date. (1) components/onboarding/renders/*.tsx — eight files each headed "TEMPORARY, disposable SVG … deleted with the induction at launch"; OWN-030 (done) renamed the induction to Funnels and its own close says "the front door was replaced, never removed". (2) lib/core/beta.ts:1 "Beta launch switch (TEMPORARY)", plus catalog rows tagged temporary in lib/apps/catalog.ts:131-134 and lib/library/element-catalog.ts:69-74. (3) Entry-point flyer downloads: app/(main)/entry-points/entry-points-client.tsx:325 says they are "turned off for now (kept on the dev list, BACKLOG § Entry-point flyer designer)" — that doc is retired and the four flyer rows are all event-cover work, so the builder is shipped, hidden, and owned by nothing; lib/entry-points/flyer.ts:9 names the blocker (a bundled font for PNG export). THE RULING: (a) is there a launch date, or is beta the steady state — if the latter, the TEMPORARY labels are wrong and should say so; (b) flyer downloads: ship them (bundle the font, XS) or delete the builder. Each answer is a small code change filed as its own row; this row closes when the three are ruled.

🔴 ── ITEM 3 RE-TESTED 2026-09-07, AND THE AUDIT THAT CLEARED IT WAS WRONG. A premise sweep read this row as "blocked on bundling a font, and the font shipped in 349733c4f, therefore no longer blocked". The technical half is true — LiberationSans Regular + Bold are committed, lib/entry-points/flyer-raster.ts loads them memoized with a best-effort degrade, and the route serves ?format=svg|png behind the owner gate. The INFERENCE is false. There are no commented-out anchors to restore: they were DELETED in b7c862005, one day AFTER the font shipped, in a commit titled "feat(qr): flyers off" whose message states the reason — flyer downloads are off pending a proper flyer designer (layout picker, editable poster, brand presets) "rather than the fixed template". That is a product deferral, not a technical blocker, and restoring the two links would ship the fixed-template flyer, which is exactly one of the two options this row asks the owner to rule between. So item 3 stays owner-gated on the ruling, not on the font.

What was fixed without pre-empting the ruling: the stale comment at app/(main)/entry-points/entry-points-client.tsx:325 pointed at docs/BACKLOG.md (retired 2026-06-15) and implied a technical blocker; it now says both downloads work today, are simply unlinked, and that what is pending is a product ruling. lib/entry-points/flyer.ts lost its "a PNG export needs a bundled font — a follow-up" line for what actually shipped.

GENERAL LESSON, and it is the sharper half: a premise sweep that finds the STATED blocker expired has established only that the stated blocker expired. It has not established that the work is unblocked. This one had the evidence in reach — the deletion commit is one `git log` away and says why in its own message — and skipped it because the font finding felt conclusive.

THE ASK, three rulings: (1) do the eight components/onboarding/renders/*.tsx survive launch, or get deleted with the induction; (2) does lib/core/beta.ts stay after launch; (3) entry-point flyers - relink the two download buttons on the FIXED template now (XS), or keep them off until a flyer designer ships (which becomes its own row). The font blocker is gone either way.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-07: eight TEMPORARY render files present, lib/core/beta.ts header unchanged, and the two flyer download anchors deleted in b7c862005 pending a flyer-designer decision (the font blocker they were originally attributed to expired in 349733c4f). Closes with the two rulings recorded and the follow-on rows filed.

entries.title: Six adoption debt classes have a ratchet and no owner, and handrolled-eyebrow was raised on purpose last week

source.ref: handrolled-eyebrow, raw-px-arbitrary, literal-display-type, shadow-literals, adhoc-progress, handrolled-icon-button

entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's code sweep: a marker in the tree that promised later work, with no row owning it. scripts/adoption-baselines.json is the live design-debt scoreboard and check:adoption is advisory by owner decision (OWN-004). Of its non-zero classes, literal-radius, raw-button-bg, raw-input, raw-select and raw-textarea are owned by PROG-DAWN3 (which records input as "not a sweep" and the last two as on their floors). SIX ARE OWNED BY NOTHING: handrolled-eyebrow 589 (LIVE-025 and LIVE-038 both closed; the count was RAISED by one on 2026-09-05, deliberately banked under L9-05), raw-px-arbitrary 116, literal-display-type 94, shadow-literals 50, adhoc-progress 8, handrolled-icon-button 3. A ratchet that only ever moves when a sweep happens to touch it is a scoreboard nobody reads. THE WORK is a decision per class, then the sweep it implies: record which are "keep" (the raw-input precedent — say why in the baseline's own note) and give the rest a slice rule the way ADR-1119 cut the button sweep by shape. The eyebrow class is the one with the most sites and the most recent movement, so start there. P3 because the gate is advisory and nothing member-facing is wrong; it is filed so the six classes stop being invisible.

── PROGRESS 2026-09-07 (ADR-1256). All six classes RE-MEASURED on today's tree first: every one read exactly its 2026-09-06 figure, so the counts had not expired. Each now carries its decision in a `note` on its own entry in scripts/adoption-baselines.json, beside the number it governs, because a decision recorded anywhere else is one that gets made again (and check:one-list forbids the new document that would otherwise hold it). `note` is documentation only: frozen.basis hashes mode + patterns + absent + include + exclude, so writing one can never move a count.

THE SIX DECISIONS, and what reading the sites changed:
  · handrolled-eyebrow 589 -> 550 — SLICE, by the class list's own shape (badge 92 / role-size 107 / small 323 / other 28). Instrument in the repo: node scripts/eyebrow-bucket.mjs. SLICE 1 SHIPPED: tracking-wide + font-semibold at text-meta, 73 sites in 52 files, the 39 in 28 files not import-reachable from a surface test/e2e/visual.spec.ts photographs converted to the composite `eyebrow` utility. The class stops being flagged as a raised floor. Next: --tracking wider (16/12), --tracking widest (16/12). Slice target 484.
  · raw-px-arbitrary 116 — KEEP, the raw-input precedent. 50 of 116 are capacity minimums where px IS the unit; of the 66 sizing sites exactly 5 land on the spacing scale, 4 of them the app shell's Zap glyph carve. Not a sweep.
  · literal-display-type 94 — SLICE, by RESPONSIVE LADDER: 22 elements carry a literal pair that steps at a breakpoint (48 of the 94 sites), which is a hand-rolled clamp, and a --text-display-* role already IS a clamp. The 46 single-literal sites stay per-site judgments. Slice target 46.
  · shadow-literals 50 — SLICE, by WHO CHOSE THE SHADOW: 17 chrome sites go to lift-1/2/3; the other 33 are a value a MEMBER picked through the page editor's none|sm|md|lg picker and wait on a product change with a stored-value migration. Slice target 33.
  · adhoc-progress 8 — KEEP, and four of the eight are not progress bars at all: two files render an avatar twice with style={{ width: size, height: size }} beside rounded-pill. At most two real candidates. A tripwire, not a queue.
  · handrolled-icon-button 3 — KEEP. All three read in source, all three on photographed surfaces, each encoding a density decision its own comment already records.

STAYS OPEN because two of the three slice rules have shipped nothing yet and the eyebrow rule has two slices left. The probe now measures that: every class carries a note, and every class carrying a slice rule is at or under the floor its rule reaches. It reads 3 classes owed today.

── PROGRESS 2026-09-08 (ADR-1260). All three slice-bearing classes RE-MEASURED on today's main before anything was touched, and all three read exactly their 2026-09-07 figure: handrolled-eyebrow 550, literal-display-type 94, shadow-literals 50. The counts had not expired.

TWO SLICES SHIPPED, both pure continuations of the rules ADR-1256 recorded, so neither needed a new decision:
  · handrolled-eyebrow 550 -> 533. Slices 2 and 3 by the instrument, node scripts/eyebrow-bucket.mjs: `--tracking wider` 16 sites in 12 files and `--tracking widest` 16 in 12. The 17 sites in 14 files NOT import-reachable from a surface test/e2e/visual.spec.ts photographs took the composite `eyebrow` utility and kept their layout and colour; the other 15 are watched and stay.
  · literal-display-type 94 -> 77. The ladder set re-read as 22 elements over 48 sites, unchanged. Exactly one file carrying them is unwatched -- components/marketing/funnel/funnel-sections.tsx, reached only from app/for/[niche] -- and its 8 elements over 17 sites took the role covering their top step (4xl->5xl->6xl to text-display-h1, 4xl->5xl to h2, 3xl->4xl to h3), each keeping its own explicit leading-*.

🔴 THE THIRD SLICE SHIPPED NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE FINDING (ADR-1260 amends its rule). shadow-literals stays 50. Its 17 chrome sites are 9 watched and 8 unwatched, and reading the 8 says NONE converts: four pair the literal with a coloured `shadow-primary/NN` companion that .lift-* would repaint in neutral ink, one is `md:shadow-2xl` and .lift-3 is a plain class no variant can reach, and the last three are floating popovers whose own transition IS the affordance -- .lift-1/2/3 are UNLAYERED and set `transition` themselves, so a lift clobbers the fade, and .lift-2:hover adds 2px of travel under the cursor of a menu. The rule now carries those three preconditions in the class's note.

STAYS OPEN, and now for ONE reason across all three classes: what is left is WATCHED. 49 eyebrow sites (34 slice-1 leftovers + 15 from slices 2-3), 31 display-ladder sites, and 9 of the 17 shadow chrome sites all sit on surfaces the visual suite photographs, and a baseline recapture is owner-dispatched on a runner. ⏳ OWNER ACTION: one visual-baseline recapture unblocks 80 mechanical conversions that the instruments already name. No floor was raised; both moved classes were re-frozen with their own reason.

── RE-TESTED 2026-09-08 (premise sweep, ADR-1269). The six baselines are unchanged on today's tree (handrolled-eyebrow 533 / slice target 484 · raw-px-arbitrary 116 · literal-display-type 77 / 46 · shadow-literals 50 / 33 · adhoc-progress 8 · handrolled-icon-button 3), each with its recorded HYG-055 note, so the 80 watched conversions are still owed.

🔴 THE BLOCKER EXPIRED, THE WORK DID NOT. "⏳ OWNER ACTION: one visual-baseline recapture" was wrong about who can do it: `.github/workflows/e2e-manual.yml` is a `workflow_dispatch`, and an agent dispatched run 34174895830 against production on 2026-09-08 00:55Z with `update_baselines + capture_shell`, which succeeded. The `ownerAction: account` is DROPPED; nothing here waits on the owner. A recapture rewrites every PNG whose page has changed since the last capture, and on 2026-09-08 that was all 138 of them: the #2457 reading that called them "cross-runner noise" was wrong (ADR-1273), they were the 2026-09-04 CTA sweep. Before taking a slice's recapture, read where its pixels sit with pnpm visual:bands origin/main <runner commit>; take a file whose bands are the slice's own change or a change already on main, and question one whose band is somewhere the slice did not touch.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const j=require("./scripts/adoption-baselines.json");const K=["handrolled-eyebrow","raw-px-arbitrary","literal-display-type","shadow-literals","adhoc-progress","handrolled-icon-button"];const bad=[];for(const k of K){const e=j.entries.find(x=>x.key===k);if(!e){bad.push(k+": no entry in the baseline file");continue}if(typeof e.note!=="string"||e.note.length<200||e.note.indexOf("HYG-055")<0){bad.push(k+": no recorded decision (keep or slice rule) in its note");continue}if(typeof e.sliceTarget==="number"&&e.baseline>e.sliceTarget)bad.push(k+": slice rule recorded but "+(e.baseline-e.sliceTarget)+" site(s) unshipped (baseline "+e.baseline+" > slice target "+e.sliceTarget+")")}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join("; "));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)'
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE, not the title: each of the six ownerless classes carries a recorded decision on its own entry in scripts/adoption-baselines.json, and each class whose decision is a SLICE has reached the floor its rule reaches (sliceTarget). Fails while a class has no note, and fails while a slice rule is recorded but unshipped, so the row cannot close on a decision nobody acted on. Pure node, no shell pipeline.

entries.title: Four comments in the tree describe a follow-up that already shipped, one of them rendered to operators as workflow guidance
entries.detail:

entries.title: Nothing rate-limits Vera chat or any composer; only /help/ask carries a limiter
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's docs sweep: work a live plan or ADR names as open, deferred or "a follow-up", with no row owning it. EDITOR-ARCHITECTURE §9's table of AI-layer gaps records that the only rate-limited AI door is /help/ask; Vera chat and every generation path (blurbs, drafts, the Space copilot) are budget-gated by the ledger (which LIVE-194 shows is mis-priced) and by nothing per-request. A signed-in member can therefore drive a paid model in a tight loop until a budget trips. Verified 2026-09-06 as far as a grep can: no rate-limit helper is referenced from lib/ai. RE-TEST THE PREMISE by walking the Vera and composer server actions for any limiter before building one. THE WORK: one per-profile sliding-window limiter (the /help/ask one is the pattern) applied at each AI door, returning the same member-voice refusal the budget gate uses. The same table names three further gaps that belong to PROG-E8 rather than here — Vera's loop re-sends the system prompt every round (against ADR-041), no streaming, and no zod on any AI path — and they are recorded on that row so they stop living only in a doc.
CLOSED 2026-09-07, and re-testing the premise first found it WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT MADE IT WORSE.

🔴 `/help/ask` DID NOT EXIST. The row named it as the one rate-limited AI door and told the next reader to reuse it as the pattern. Scan two DELETED app/(help)/help/ask/route.ts on 2026-09-05 because nothing called it, two days before this row was filed - the deletion note is in components/admin/admin-footer.tsx and lib/help/drift.test.ts. So the true state was not "one of N doors is covered", it was ZERO of N, and the exemplar to copy was gone. Verified properly rather than by grep: every featureOverBudget call site (44 files, the honest census of AI doors) was checked against every rateLimitOk call site and the overlap was EMPTY.

THE WORK: lib/ai/rate-limit.ts is a thin policy layer over the generic rateLimitOk the row's exemplar was itself built on, so no new storage and no migration. 21 doors now pass through it, covering Vera chat, all seven Sparks, every entity quality gate, the Space copilot, grounded help, the anonymous Ask Vera door, and the compose/edit paths for circles, journeys, practices and listings. Every door refuses EXACTLY as it already refuses when over budget, so there is no new refusal vocabulary; the one judgement call is that the quality gate reuses its "paused" line rather than its budget line, because the budget line says "again tomorrow" and that is false of a window that clears in a minute.

⚪ THE DOORS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNLIMITED ARE NAMED WITH REASONS in UNLIMITED_DOORS: doors that delegate to an already-throttled one, actorless work (cron sweeps and queue workers, where a per-actor window is the wrong tool and would break the legitimate batch), and operator importers that loop by design. Those stay bounded by the daily caps alone.

THE RATCHET IS THE DURABLE HALF: featureOverBudget call sites ARE the door census, so a door added later that gates on budget but not on the window fails CI unless it is named with a reason. The list may shrink and may only grow with a stated reason.

⚠️ THE UNCONFIGURED POLICY IS `allow`, AGAINST lib/rate-limit's production default of `deny`, and that is deliberate: denying would switch off every AI surface at once, each degrading to its fallback with no error anywhere for an operator to see, while allowing leaves an unconfigured deploy exactly where it stood and still bounded by the daily caps and the global ceiling.

🔴 BUT ALLOW-AND-SILENT IS THE FAILURE AGENTS.md NAMES, so it was closed in the same pass: /api/status now publishes monitoring.rateLimit beside monitoring.sentry, booleanised from whether a client was built and never a URL or a token. "Is throttling on in this deployment?" is one curl, exactly as LIVE-053 made "is the error recorder on?" one curl. A fail-safe that cannot be seen to have fired reads as coverage without being coverage.

WATCHED GO RED: 6 of 22 tests failed against the unlimited tree (the coverage ratchet listing all 17 unthrottled doors, plus five per-door refusals), and every negative test is paired with a positive control that passes in both states - one of which caught a false pass where retrieval was simply empty. ADR-1215, and EDITOR-ARCHITECTURE §9's gaps table corrected because it was false in two ways.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-06: no rate-limit reference under lib/ai; the doc table stands. Closes when every AI door (Vera chat, blurb/draft generation, the Space copilot) passes through one per-profile limiter and a test proves the refusal.

entries.title: ADR-1192 left the Space accent unscoped on the manage, settings, CRM, marketing and podcast subtrees, and nothing guards any of it
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's docs sweep: work a live plan or ADR names as open, deferred or "a follow-up", with no row owning it. ADR-1192's closing section lists what it did not do, and none of it was filed. Verified 2026-09-06: only app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/(profile)/layout.tsx wraps AccentScope, so the manage, settings, crm and marketing subtrees and the public, sitemap-listed podcasts subtree render a Space with no accent scope; app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx:198 still hardcodes borderRadius: 28 where the theme carries the radius; components/spaces/accent-scope.tsx:26 types theme as string rather than SpaceThemeId, so a misspelt theme id is silently unstyled. THE WORK: wrap the remaining subtrees (the podcasts one first, it is public), type the prop, replace the literal, and add the guard the ADR asked for — a source-shape test that every route under spaces/[slug] renders inside an AccentScope.

── CLOSED 2026-09-07, AND THE PREMISE WAS UNDERSTATED. AccentScope was mounted in exactly ONE place under /spaces/[slug] — (profile)/layout.tsx — and a walk of the real route tree found THIRTY-FIVE route entries with no accent scope at all, not the five subtrees this row named. All five named subtrees confirmed unscoped (manage 6 routes, settings 15, crm 5, marketing 1, podcasts 2), plus edit-page, loom, journeys, messages, practices and [slug]/loading.tsx which the row did not name. One correction to the row: the fifth subtree is `podcasts`; there is no `portal` subtree.

THE FIX IS ONE HOIST, NOT FIVE WRAPPERS. The accent and theme are functions of the Space alone and constant across the whole segment, so they belong in the layout that already resolves the Space: [slug]/layout.tsx now wraps children in a single AccentScope, and (profile)/layout.tsx's now-redundant one is removed so the scope has exactly one source. SpaceBreadcrumbs stays outside it deliberately — shell wayfinding, not the Space's page. Five subtrees became scoped without a line being written in any of them; for edit-page that is a fidelity fix, because the Puck preview of the Space landing now renders under the same scope the public route does.

Also: AccentScope's `theme` is typed SpaceThemeId rather than string (tsc was already clean, so every call site was passing the union), and opengraph-image.tsx's bare `borderRadius: 28` becomes a named COVER_RADIUS = 24 in the file's existing mirrored-token block, pinned by test to --radius-cover.

⚠️ THE ROW'S OWN PROBE WAS A SHAPE PROBE AND DID NOT MEASURE THE MAIN WORK. It regexed for the absence of `borderRadius: 28` and of `theme?: string`, so it passed if the OG file were DELETED, if 28 became 31, and it said nothing whatever about whether any subtree was scoped — which is the bulk of the row. The row's own note conceded this and asked for a source-shape test when one existed. It exists, and the probe is now that test.

The guard walks the real route tree rather than listing subtrees, because a list is the thing that rots. Five tests, each watched red: against the unfixed tree it named all 35 unscoped routes; a second AccentScope planted in manage/layout.tsx tripped the exactly-once arm; breaking the route regex tripped a floor test that exists precisely because the first two arms pass vacuously if the walk finds nothing.

⚪ ADR-1192 IS AMENDED IN THE SAME PASS. Its loading.tsx paragraph said the skeleton "cannot use the role tokens" because AccentScope lived one level down. That was a true statement about a fixable arrangement rather than a law, and the hoist makes it false. The skeleton's markup is still left on --radius-cover, which reads identically either side of the scope.

⚪ NOT DONE, and filed rather than smuggled in: test/e2e/overflow.spec.ts covers /manage but not the public profile. ADR-1192 names it in the same paragraph, but it is a Playwright coverage gap rather than accent scoping.

entries.title: Operator dashboards count every occurrence of a repeating event as an event, and no series-wide cancel exists
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's docs sweep: work a live plan or ADR names as open, deferred or "a follow-up", with no row owning it. EVENTS-SERIES-BUILD-PLAN's named follow-ups were never filed. The two with a member- or operator-facing consequence: SERIES-COUNT — "a series-aware count helper for the ~9 inflated operator dashboards and lib/spaces/discovery.ts", against its own R20 reading that dashboards "overstate by ~60x" for a weekly series; and SERIES-CANCEL — no series-wide cancel exists, so cancelling a recurring event is one occurrence at a time. RE-TEST THE PREMISE FIRST: the 60x figure predates the collapseSeriesRows work (LIVE-081), so measure a Space dashboard against a known weekly series before writing the helper. The other six tags (SERIES-PD/RANK/PIN/MAIN/PICKER/EMBED) are polish and ride with DEF-DOMAIN. Closes with one count helper used by the dashboards and discovery, and a cancel that takes a series.
── CLOSED 2026-09-07. Both halves shipped: a series-aware count helper used by every count site, and a cancel that takes a series. ADR-1218 and ADR-1217 record the rulings.

🔴 THE ROW ASKED FOR ITS PREMISE TO BE RE-TESTED, AND BOTH OF ITS NUMBERS WERE STALE. Measured against production before any code: 21 upcoming non-cancelled events collapse to 5 series-aware, and concretely TWO Spaces each show 9 in the directory where 1 is true. The aggregate is 4.2x, not the "~60x" the row carries - a 60x reading needs a DAILY series (61 rows in the horizon) and production runs weekly ones. The row's "~9 operator dashboards" was stale too: there are ELEVEN count sites and only six are operator dashboards. The defect was entirely real; only its size was wrong.

SERIES-COUNT. countSeries / countSeriesBy sit beside collapseSeriesRows, and countSeries IS collapseSeriesRows(rows, {perSeries:1}).length - the fold itself rather than a copy, so a count and the list beneath it cannot drift and there is still exactly one definition of parent_event_id ?? id. countSeriesBy buckets FIRST then folds per bucket, the only correct order. All 11 sites wired, pinned by a source-level ratchet that fails if any regresses to head:true. lib/events/store.ts gained SERIES_COLUMNS in its SELECT, which is load-bearing rather than decorative: three readers count its rows and without those columns the fold is a SILENT NO-OP.

Three behaviour changes ride along, stated rather than buried: /admin's "Events ahead" now excludes cancelled events (the old head:true had NO is_cancelled filter, so it had been counting them - an incidental bug fix); the Space calendar summary and the public hero stat move to upcomingEventFloor() so a 7pm class no longer drops off at 7:01pm; and five head:true tallies became row reads capped at SERIES_WIDE_READ.

SERIES-CANCEL. cancelSeries flips future dates only (via isEventPast, the repo's shared predicate - a naive Date compare turns 8 of 9 tests red because starts_at is a wall clock), no-ops on already-cancelled behind two guards, is idempotent through the .eq(is_cancelled,false) transition guard, and is PER-OCCURRENCE rather than a bulk UPDATE. That last one inverts the obvious answer for a reason worth keeping: a bulk statement COMMITS and then fans out, so a crash part-way leaves rows cancelled with NO refund queued and permanently unreachable behind the idempotency guard. Refunds stay entirely in LIVE-161's outbox path; cancelSeries never calls Stripe. Verified by reading the body, not the report.

⚪ RESIDUE FILED AS LIVE-206 rather than silently dropped: two counts computed inside Postgres that need a migration, an entitlement quota whose fold would LOOSEN a cap (an owner call), two /admin consoles still cancelling one date at a time, and three list-shaped fold gaps.

verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE on both halves: a count helper exists, it is the FOLD rather than a second definition of a series (the perSeries:1 collapse), the Spaces directory actually uses it, and a cancel takes a series. Comment lines are stripped first so the probe cannot read its own documentation and pass by existing. The per-site coverage is pinned separately and more strictly by components/events/series-count-wiring.test.ts, which fails if any of the 11 sites regresses to head:true. ⚠️ The discovery detector requires CALL syntax (countSeries(...) / countSeriesBy(...)): a bare substring match was tried first and let a renamed identifier (countSeriesByX) satisfy it, i.e. a probe that could not detect the regression it exists for.

entries.title: the crawlable event page published a Pacific offset on a Europe/London event, because no anon read carried time_zone
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit; PREMISE RE-TESTED AND CORRECTED 2026-09-07, then closed the same day (ADR-1223).

THE ROW WAS RIGHT THAT IT WOULD BREAK AND WRONG ABOUT WHAT BREAKS. It predicted "the first event hosted elsewhere shows the wrong hour on the crawlable page". The wrong hour never appears: `events.starts_at` stores the host's WALL CLOCK as UTC parts, so formatting those parts renders the right clock face in any zone. What breaks is the OFFSET in the structured data, which is worse, because a human never sees it and Google always does. Production on 2026-09-07 held 61 America/Los_Angeles and — for the first time — 1 Europe/London public published event, and /discover/events/royal-reset-friday-float-2026-09-11 was publishing `startDate: "2026-09-11T10:33:00-07:00"`: the right wall clock against the wrong instant, eight hours out, four days before the event.

AND THE FIX WAS A QUARTER OF THE ROW'S SIZE. The row said "add time_zone to both RPCs in a new migration". No migration was needed. app/discover/events/_data.ts already reads `events` directly with the ANON client under RLS — the same precedent LIVE-133 set for the cover — so the zone rides along on a select this page was making anyway. Widening `public_event_by_slug` would have meant a DROP + CREATE on a SECURITY DEFINER function granted to `anon`, a far larger blast radius than the defect. One column on two existing selects; the canonical /events/<slug> page was already correct and is untouched.

SHIPPED: `time_zone` added to EventEnrichment (required, not optional), to the getEventEnrichment select, and to SAFE_COLUMNS/SafeEventRow/toEnriched for the hub path; app/discover/events/_data.test.ts pins both halves — the select literal (the row casts are `as unknown as`, so a dropped column typechecks and silently returns undefined) and the published offset, with the exact production string as the positive control.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const p="app/discover/events/_data.ts";if(!fs.existsSync(p))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(p,"utf8");const cols=(s.match(/const SAFE_COLUMNS =\s*\n?\s*\x60([^\x60]*)\x60/)||[])[1]||"";const sel=(s.match(/\.select\(\s*\x27([^\x27]*cover_image_path[^\x27]*)\x27\s*\)/)||[])[1]||"";if(!cols||!sel)process.exit(79);const miss=[["SAFE_COLUMNS",cols],["getEventEnrichment select",sel]].filter(([,c])=>!/\btime_zone\b/.test(c)).map(([n])=>n);if(miss.length){console.error("anon events read omits time_zone, so the JSON-LD startDate falls back to HOME_TZ: "+miss.join(", "));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)'
verify.note: Reads the two anon `events` selects that feed the schema.org Event — SAFE_COLUMNS (the city x category hubs) and the per-slug getEventEnrichment select — and fails if either stops naming time_zone. That is the CONSEQUENCE arm, not the title: both row shapes are `as unknown as` casts, so dropping the column from the select literal typechecks cleanly and hands eventSchema an undefined zone, which silently falls back to HOME_TZ. Exits 79 (skip) if the file or either literal is gone, so a refactor reports honestly instead of passing. Live arm verified 2026-09-07: removing time_zone from SAFE_COLUMNS exits 1.

entries.title: the cron heartbeat swallowed a rejected ping, so a monitor that had stopped listening looked exactly like a monitor that was fine
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-07 while re-testing OWN-005, and it is a different defect from that row: OWN-005 is about Healthchecks.io's 20-check free-tier cap (7 of 27 crons unmonitored, owner-gated). This is about the 20 that ARE monitored.

`pingHeartbeat` awaited `fetch` and never looked at the response. `fetch` does not throw on 4xx or 5xx, so a Healthchecks rejection — a deleted check, a revoked ping URL, a rate limit — resolved normally and the function returned as if the beat had landed. The catch arm only ever saw transport failures. The consequence is the worst shape a monitoring bug can take: the dashboard goes quiet, the quiet reads as healthy, and nothing anywhere says the pings stopped being accepted. That is precisely the rule AGENTS.md states as "every fail-safe needs a gate that notices it fired" — a swallowed error is an invisible regression — applied to the fail-safe that exists to notice things.

SHIPPED: `!res.ok` now emits `log.warn("cron.heartbeat.ping_failed", { job, fail, status, error })` — the SAME event name and field shape as the existing transport-failure line, so one query finds both, with `status` as what distinguishes them (a transport error has none). No throw, no return-type change, and no new control flow around the cron's own outcome: a rejected ping must never turn a successful job into a failed one.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const p="lib/observability/cron-heartbeat.ts";if(!fs.existsSync(p))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(p,"utf8").split("\n").filter(l=>!/^\s*(\/\/|\*|\/\*)/.test(l)).join("\n");const i=s.indexOf("pingHeartbeat");if(i<0)process.exit(79);const body=s.slice(i);if(!/res\.ok|response\.ok|\.status\s*[<>=]/.test(body)){console.error("pingHeartbeat never inspects the response status: a Healthchecks rejection resolves normally and is swallowed");process.exit(1)}if(!/ping_failed/.test(body)){console.error("pingHeartbeat inspects the status but emits no log for a rejection");process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)'
verify.note: Reads pingHeartbeat with comment lines stripped (so the words in a comment cannot pass it) and requires BOTH arms of the consequence: that the response status is inspected at all, and that a rejection produces a log line. Either half alone is the bug — inspecting without logging is still silence. Exits 79 if the file or the function is gone.

entries.title: A streaming abort surfaces as a production error on eleven .rsc routes, and nothing says whether it is a real failure
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-07 from the production error groups, where it had no owner. "The destination stream closed early", count 19, users 4, first 2026-08-17, last 2026-09-03, across ELEVEN routes and all of them .rsc: /marketplace, /housing, /spaces/directory, /index, /crew, /network/contacts, /classifieds, /nearby, /network, /events/[slug], /people/[handle].

THE SHAPE IS THE WHOLE DIAGNOSIS AND IT POINTS AWAY FROM A BUG. Eleven unrelated routes with nothing in common except that each is an RSC payload request, four users, nineteen occurrences in three weeks — that is what a client navigating away mid-stream looks like, not what a broken route looks like. A defect in shared code would cluster; a defect in one route would not spread to ten others.

⚠️ BUT "PROBABLY BENIGN" IS NOT A FINDING, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS A ROW RATHER THAN A NOTE. It sits in the same error list as real defects, so every future reader spends the same minutes ruling it out, and if a genuine stream failure ever lands on these routes it arrives already camouflaged. The repo rule is that a swallowed error is an invisible regression; the mirror of it is that an unexplained error is a permanent tax on reading the list.

THE WORK, XS: confirm the benign reading against one sample (an aborted request has no response and no downstream effect), then either filter this digest out of the error surface at the reporting boundary with a comment naming the digest and why, or record it in docs/OBSERVABILITY-BASELINES.md as known-benign with its digest. Either way the next reader gets an answer instead of a re-investigation. Do NOT silence it by catching more broadly — that is how a real stream failure disappears.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1236). PREMISE RE-TESTED FIRST, against production, read-only. The group is still there and still unowned: Vercel runtime errors for the last 7 days list "The destination stream closed early." at count 19, users 4, first 2026-08-17T14:22:46Z, last 2026-09-03T06:12:55Z, digest 3689792676, across the same eleven .rsc routes. THE ONE SAMPLE THE ROW ASKED FOR SETTLES IT: the production log at 06:12:55Z on 2026-09-03 holds SEVEN of these in the same second from one deployment (dpl_DVQUVrBG1EYQ32hHvdK11XZ3h2cW), on /crew, /marketplace, /housing, /classifieds, /spaces/directory, /network and /nearby, and every one of the seven requests is GET ... 200. Seven unrelated routes in one second is one client prefetching a menu of links; the same client then navigated and the router cancelled the prefetches it no longer needed. An aborted request had no response owed and no downstream effect. Source confirms the message: react-server-dom-webpack-server registers a `close` listener on the destination and cancels the render with a plain Error carrying exactly that text; Next's createReactServerErrorHandler drops an abort only when err.name is AbortError or ResponseAborted, so this plain Error falls through, is given a digest, is console.error'd, and is handed to onRequestError.

WHAT CHANGED, both halves the row offered. (1) The reporting boundary: instrumentation.ts onRequestError now consults isClientAbortedStream (lib/observability/request-error.ts) before Sentry.captureRequestError, and the classifier matches the EXACT message, names the digest, and explains the sample in its header. It is not a broad catch: a different stream failure, a substring, a bare digest, or a non-error all still report, and instrumentation.test.ts holds that positive control alongside the abort case. (2) The record: docs/OBSERVABILITY-BASELINES.md §7 "Known-benign error groups" carries the digest, the routes, the sample, and how to tell this row from a real stream failure. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, stated so nobody re-derives it: the Vercel group will keep appearing, because Next logs the error itself BEFORE calling onRequestError and nothing in userland reaches that line; §7 is the answer for that surface. The row started manual; its probe is now a cmd that fails if the digest leaves the doc, if the classifier stops matching the exact message, or if instrumentation.ts stops consulting it before Sentry.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const C=(f)=>fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8').replace(/\\/\\*[\\s\\S]*?\\*\\//g,'').replace(/^\\s*\\/\\/.*$/gm,'');const D='docs/OBSERVABILITY-BASELINES.md',R='lib/observability/request-error.ts',I='instrumentation.ts';for(const f of [D,R,I])if(!fs.existsSync(f))process.exit(79);if(!/3689792676/.test(fs.readFileSync(D,'utf8'))){console.error('digest 3689792676 is no longer recorded as known-benign in OBSERVABILITY-BASELINES.md');process.exit(1)}const r=C(R);if(!/'The destination stream closed early\\.'/.test(r)||!/export function isClientAbortedStream/.test(r)){console.error('the classifier no longer matches the exact client-abort message');process.exit(1)}const i=C(I);const at=i.indexOf('isClientAbortedStream('),cap=i.indexOf('captureRequestError(');if(at<0||cap<0||at>cap){console.error('instrumentation.ts no longer consults isClientAbortedStream before Sentry.captureRequestError');process.exit(1)}if(!fs.existsSync('instrumentation.test.ts')||!fs.existsSync('lib/observability/request-error.test.ts'))process.exit(1)"
verify.note: Fails if the digest leaves the doc, if the classifier loses the exact-message match, or if instrumentation.ts stops consulting it ahead of Sentry. Exit 79 = a named file moved; re-point, do not delete.

entries.title: The visual suite has no viewport narrower than 390px and no header-band surface, two follow-ups ADR-1035 named

source.ref: ADR-1035, the two named follow-ups; re-measured and re-scoped by ADR-1270

entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's docs sweep: work a live plan or ADR names as open, deferred or "a follow-up", with no row owning it. ADR-1035 closed with two follow-ups: "a viewport-only capture of the header band as its own surface, and a second mobile project narrower than 390px."

── PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-09-08 before the work (ADR-1270). Two of the three claims hold; the third is FALSE and it is the one the row leaned on.
✅ playwright.config.ts had exactly two projects, desktop 1280x800 and mobile 390x844.
✅ overflow.spec.ts drives 320/360/390 as a MEASUREMENT and nothing photographed at 320 — all 144 committed baselines were 390 or 1280 wide.
🔴 "HYG-033 is a truncation only a 320px capture would have caught" is wrong. The bottom 70px of the committed app-feed--dawn-light-mobile.png — a 390-wide baseline already in the tree — renders the tab bar as `Menu · Feed · Communi… · Zap · Events · The QuestMarketpL…`. The truncation is AT 390 and always was. A baseline does not catch a defect, it catches a CHANGE: everything in that capture was there when the capture was taken, so it is the reference.
🔴 And ADR-1035's stated REASON for the header-band surface has expired. It asked for one because maxDiffPixelRatio 0.02 made a 64px header ~0.35% of an 18,000px capture; ADR-1258 replaced that with an absolute maxDiffPixels 400, so a header change fails home/about and fourteen more baselines at both existing widths today. Building it at 1280 and 390 would have been eight PNGs re-photographing gated pixels.

THE WORK, on the terms that survived the re-measurement (ADR-1270): a third project `narrow` 320x568 carrying a per-project testMatch so it photographs and only photographs — no third @smoke column, and no third set of unmeasured @a11y contexts. It captures the member shell (the rail, dock and seven `min-w-0 flex-1` tab slots lay out by division: 45.7px a slot at 320 against 55.7px at 390) and the header band at `/` with viewportOnly, narrow-only, four states. The 16 public surfaces and the 7 operator routes are skipped there with the reason attached. Twelve new PNGs, zero moved — no existing surface's path, flags or capture mode changes, which is what makes the capture run reviewable under ADR-1264. baseline-distinctness.test.ts stopped mirroring the config's viewports and now derives them from config.projects, so the next project arrives with its real numbers instead of being held to desktop's 1280.

⚠️ THE BAND'S PATH IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT `/`. `viewportOnly` gives up the height signal that tells a real capture from a protection wall, so baseline-distinctness.test.ts falls back to light-vs-dark repaint at a 90% bar — a bar measured on FULL-PAGE captures, where body copy inverts across thousands of pixels. A first screen is hero-dominated and does not inherit that headroom. Cropping the committed 390-wide baselines to their first 568px, dawn light vs dawn dark: `/` 92.8% (🔴 over the bar, it would have failed on capture), /discover 87.0%, /pricing 85.1%, /about 84.4%, eleven more between 69% and 83%, and /how-to-build-community 1.1%. Every marketing page renders the SAME band, so the subject moved to the article page and the margin came with it.

✅ CLOSED 2026-09-08. The `narrow` project (320x568) and the header-band surface are in playwright.config.ts / test/e2e/surfaces.ts, and the CAPTURE has landed: twelve baselines, all 320 wide — the four viewportOnly slugs (header-band, app-feed, app-space-console) at exactly 320x568 as baseline-distinctness.test.ts requires, and the two fullPage ones at 320x2825 (/nearby) and 320x11169 (/settings). The runner touched 150 files; 138 pre-existing baselines were MODIFIED at BYTE-IDENTICAL dimensions (0 of 138 changed WxH, read from the PNG IHDR on both sides) and were restored rather than committed, per ADR-1264 and LIVE-212 — this change is allowed to add twelve files and to move none, and the net diff is exactly 12 A / 0 M / 0 D. The 320 capture also confirms this row's neighbour HYG-033 at its own width: the new app-feed--dawn-light-narrow.png renders `Menu · Feed · Commu… · Zap · Events · The Q… · Market…`, three labels truncated at 45.7px a slot, exactly as HYG-033's arithmetic predicted.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),p="test/e2e/__screenshots__/visual.spec.ts";const f=fs.readdirSync(p).filter(n=>n.endsWith("-narrow.png"));if(f.length<2||!f.some(n=>n.startsWith("header-band--"))||!f.some(n=>n.startsWith("app-")))process.exit(1);const b=Buffer.alloc(24),d=fs.openSync(p+"/"+f[0],"r");fs.readSync(d,b,0,24,0);fs.closeSync(d);process.exit(b.readUInt32BE(16)===320?0:1)'
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE, not the config line. A grep for `width: 320` in playwright.config.ts passes the moment the project is declared — while the suite still photographs nothing at that width, which is the whole defect. This reads the committed baselines instead: a narrow capture of the header band AND one of the member shell must exist, and the first one's PNG IHDR must say 320 wide. It stays red until a capture run against a real deployment commits them.

entries.title: Lift 3d: no gate that an animated class sits inside a reduced-motion guard, and slideUp was the one keyframe that did not
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's docs sweep: work a live plan or ADR names as open, deferred or "a follow-up", with no row owning it. UX-MATURITY-PLAN lifts 3c (a focus-visible/keyboard sweep) and 3d (reduced-motion completeness, with a 3a-script arm: "every keyframe class must appear inside a prefers-reduced-motion guard block or carry a documented exemption") are listed "not yet started" and have no row. Verified 2026-09-06: no file under scripts/ or test/ references prefers-reduced-motion, and roughly 27 outline-none sites carry no focus replacement on the same line. The specific overlays LIVE-015 and SCAN-402/403 fixed were instances; the lift is the sweep plus the instrument. THE WORK: 3d first, because it is a guard (a check over app/globals.css and the component css that every @keyframes user is inside a reduced-motion block or listed as an exemption, wired into pnpm test), then the 3c sweep against the a11y ratchet.

── SPLIT AND SHIPPED 2026-09-07. This row bundled two unrelated lifts and the bundle is why neither moved: 3c (the focus-visible sweep) is a UI pass and 3d is a gate, and a row that needs both closes on neither. 3c is now HYG-065; this row is 3d alone.

🔴 IT FOUND A LIVE BUG, WHICH IS THE POINT OF BUILDING THE GATE RATHER THAN AUDITING ONCE. There is no blanket `* { animation: none }` — the reduced-motion block at app/globals.css:1105 collapses the --motion-* tokens and Tailwind's .animate-pulse/.animate-spin, nothing more. Ten of eleven keyframes carried their own guard; `slideUp` carried none, and two of its seventeen call sites omitted `motion-safe:` — components/ui/toast.tsx:124 and app/join/(induction)/induction.tsx:686. A member who has asked their OS to reduce motion got a sliding toast on every notification.

⚠️ AND THE FINDING WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN. components/journey/v2/trophy-celebration.tsx:86 carries a comment saying exactly this — "@keyframes slideUp carries no guard of its own in globals.css, so every consumer must add motion-safe:" — and fixed only its own call site. Prose noticed; nothing enforced; the two that were wrong stayed wrong. That is the whole argument for lift 3d in one file.

SHIPPED: motion-safe: on both call sites; a CSS BACKSTOP in globals.css neutralising the slideUp class inside a reduced-motion block, so the keyframe is safe by construction rather than by every future author remembering a prefix; components/ui/toast.test.tsx tightened (its toContain passed either way, which is why it never caught this); and scripts/check-reduced-motion.test.ts, a brace-aware source reader that skips @keyframes bodies, finds each keyframe's real consumers from animation:/animation-name: declarations, and requires every consumer selector to be neutralised inside a reduced-motion block. Keyframes applied from outside the stylesheet are declared in EXTERNALLY_APPLIED and the test VERIFIES the guard selector each entry names actually exists, so the map is an index and never the evidence. Walk floors (>=11 keyframes, >=10 neutralised selectors, >=120 rules) per the check-admin-client MIN_IMPORTERS lesson: a parser that silently finds nothing must fail, not report success.

CONTROLS PROVEN: the gate red on exactly slideUp before the fix and on nothing else; the other ten green while it was red; deleting the new backstop from the live file turns it red again; an in-test mutation removing a real guard turns exactly that keyframe red; an EXTERNALLY_APPLIED entry claiming a guard the CSS lacks still fails.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const g="app/globals.css";const t="scripts/check-reduced-motion.test.ts";if(!fs.existsSync(g)||!fs.existsSync(t))process.exit(79);const css=fs.readFileSync(g,"utf8");const red=[...css.matchAll(/@media[^{]*prefers-reduced-motion[^{]*\{/g)];if(!red.length)process.exit(79);let guarded=false;for(const m of red){let i=m.index+m[0].length,depth=1;while(i<css.length&&depth>0){const c=css[i];if(c==="{")depth++;else if(c==="}")depth--;i++}if(/slideUp/.test(css.slice(m.index,i)))guarded=true}const bad=[];if(!guarded)bad.push("globals.css has no reduced-motion rule naming slideUp");for(const f of ["components/ui/toast.tsx","app/join/(induction)/induction.tsx"]){if(!fs.existsSync(f))continue;const s=fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8");for(const line of s.split("\n")){if(/animate-\[slideUp/.test(line)&&!/motion-safe:|motion-reduce:/.test(line))bad.push(f+" applies slideUp with no motion-safe: guard")}}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join("; "));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)'
verify.note: Two arms, both consequence. (1) The CSS BACKSTOP: walks each prefers-reduced-motion block brace-aware and requires one of them to name slideUp — the guard that makes the keyframe safe whatever a future call site forgets. (2) The two call sites this row actually fixed must still carry motion-safe:. The old probe was a grep-present for the words "prefers-reduced-motion" under scripts/ — the shape-not-truth pattern AGENTS.md names: it passed the moment any file mentioned the phrase, and it passed while the bug was live. Exits 79 if globals.css or the gate file is gone.

entries.title: Lift 3c: the focus-visible sweep, never started and hidden inside a two-lift row for a month
entries.detail:
SPLIT OUT OF HYG-058 on 2026-09-07. That row bundled 3c and 3d, and the bundle is why neither moved for a month: they share a plan section and nothing else. 3d was a gate over the stylesheet; 3c is a keyboard-focus pass over interactive elements — every control a keyboard reaches shows a visible focus ring, and a hand-rolled control does not silently drop the one the browser gave it. A row that closes on neither half reads as "in progress" forever, which is exactly what happened.

WHY P3 AND NOT HIGHER: this is real accessibility debt with no measured instance yet — unlike 3d, which was filed as a gate and immediately turned up a live reduced-motion defect. The sweep needs its own measurement first (which controls actually lose the ring), and the honest place for an unmeasured sweep is behind the rows that carry evidence.

THE WORK: enumerate interactive elements that set their own outline/ring, confirm each has a :focus-visible state, and land a gate in the same shape as scripts/check-reduced-motion.test.ts — brace-aware, consequence-measuring, with a positive control — rather than a one-time pass that decays.

CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1250). THE PREMISE WAS RE-TESTED FIRST AND THE WORDS WERE NOT THE THING. Census across app/, components/ and lib/: 110 `outline-none` sites, 0 `outline-0`, 0 `ring-0`, and not one of the 110 lost its ring by saying it, because the global ring in app/globals.css is an unlayered `:focus-visible` rule that already sets `outline: none` and paints the ring as a 3px box-shadow. The ring WAS lost at 109 sites by two mechanisms that contain no such word: (1) 107 lifted, keyboard-reachable controls in 81 files (buttons, links, three search inputs including the sign-in email field, the Space console module rows, both lightboxes) whose `.lift-*` box-shadow, unlayered and later in the sheet, beat the global ring and every `focus-visible:ring-*` utility on them; roughly a third carried such a utility as dead CSS. Two sites, both in the card kit (EntityCard and RowCard), had remembered `ring-focus`; 107 had not. (2) 2 Tiptap contenteditable editors (the email canvas and the Space canvas slots) that no branch of the ring rule reached.

FIXED, 109 of 109, from two rules in one file rather than 81 per-site edits: a by-construction backstop `:where(.lift-1, .lift-2, .lift-3):where(button, a, select, summary, input, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"]), [contenteditable]:not([contenteditable="false"])):focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px }` below `.ring-focus`, the same shape as the reduced-motion gate's `[class*="animate-[slideUp"]` backstop; and `[contenteditable]:not([contenteditable="false"])` added to the global ring list beside `summary`. Before: 109 reachable controls painting nothing on tab. After: 0, with 2,900+ classed elements walked, 900+ reachable, 106 lifted controls green.

THE GATE: scripts/check-focus-visible.test.ts, in check-reduced-motion's shape and under `pnpm test`. It reads the ring list, the ring-beating classes and the outline-restoring rules OUT OF globals.css (brace-aware, @layer-aware, nothing hand-typed), walks every JSX opening element brace-aware with comments blanked, plus Tiptap's editorProps class, and fails a lifted reachable element no outline rule reaches, a contenteditable surface nothing rings, or a detached control string whose lift makes its focus utility dead. CONTROLS PROVEN (18 tests): positive control green; deleting `ring-focus` from a lifted link turns exactly that site red; a `focus-visible:ring-2` utility does NOT rescue a lifted control; narrowing the backstop reach turns the lifted button red and leaves the lifted link green; blinding the ring rule to contenteditable turns the editor red; deleting the backstop from the LIVE sheet turns 107 sites red and only them; dropping `button` from the LIVE backstop turns exactly the lifted buttons red. Deliberately left alone: the EntityCard shape (a lifted overflow-hidden surface whose child link's box-shadow ring the parent clips) stays on `.ring-focus`'s `:has` arm and its own test; `focus-visible:shadow-none` utilities on native fields are inert under the unlayered ring; the 110 `outline-none` tokens are harmless and were not swept.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const g="app/globals.css",t="scripts/check-focus-visible.test.ts";if(!fs.existsSync(g)||!fs.existsSync(t)){console.error("gate or sheet missing");process.exit(1)}const css=fs.readFileSync(g,"utf8").replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g,"");const rules=[];(function walk(s,layered){let i=0,start=0;while(i<s.length){const c=s[i];if(c==="{"){const pre=s.slice(start,i).replace(/\s+/g," ").trim();let d=1,j=i+1;while(j<s.length&&d>0){if(s[j]==="{")d++;else if(s[j]==="}")d--;j++}const body=s.slice(i+1,j-1);if(pre.startsWith("@")){if(!/^@keyframes\b/.test(pre))walk(body,layered||/^@layer\b/.test(pre))}else if(pre)rules.push({sel:pre,body,layered});i=j;start=j}else if(c==="}"||c===";"){i++;start=i}else i++}})(css,false);const paints=(b,p)=>{const m=new RegExp("(?:^|[;\\s])"+p+"\\s*:\\s*([^;}]*)").exec(b);return !!m&&m[1].trim()!==""&&!/^(none|0)$/.test(m[1].trim())};const bad=[];const ring=rules.find(r=>!r.layered&&/:where\([^{]*\bbutton\b[^{]*\):focus-visible/.test(r.sel)&&paints(r.body,"box-shadow"));if(!ring)bad.push("no unlayered :focus-visible box-shadow ring rule names button");else if(!/\[contenteditable\]/.test(ring.sel))bad.push("the global ring rule does not list [contenteditable], so Tiptap editors paint nothing on tab");const back=rules.find(r=>!r.layered&&/:where\(\s*\.lift-1\b[^)]*\.lift-2\b[^)]*\.lift-3\b[^)]*\)/.test(r.sel)&&/:focus-visible/.test(r.sel)&&paints(r.body,"outline"));if(!back)bad.push("no unlayered :focus-visible outline rule restores the ring for .lift-1/2/3, so every lifted control paints its drop shadow over the ring");else for(const k of ["button","a","input","textarea","select","summary","[tabindex]","[contenteditable]"])if(!back.sel.includes(k))bad.push("the lift backstop does not reach "+k);const gate=fs.readFileSync(t,"utf8");for(const n of ["positive control","mutation control: deleting the backstop from the LIVE sheet","mutation control: dropping `button` from the LIVE backstop"])if(!gate.includes(n))bad.push("gate is missing its \""+n+"\" control");if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join("; "));process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Three arms, all consequence, all pure node. (1) The SHEET is parsed brace-aware and @layer-aware and must hold an unlayered :focus-visible box-shadow ring rule that names button AND lists [contenteditable], the branch the two Tiptap editors needed. (2) The same parse must find the unlayered :focus-visible OUTLINE rule keyed on .lift-1/2/3 that reaches every kind the ring reaches; that rule is what makes 107 lifted controls paint, and deleting it or narrowing its reach fails here before the gate runs. (3) The gate file must still carry its positive control and its two live-sheet mutation controls, so the row cannot read done on a gate that has never been seen to fire. Comments are stripped before the parse so no arm can pass by reading its own documentation. The stronger behavioural guard is the gate itself, scripts/check-focus-visible.test.ts, under pnpm test.

entries.title: Every query baseline and the SLO snapshot in OBSERVABILITY-BASELINES still read "pending capture"
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's docs sweep. docs/OBSERVABILITY-BASELINES.md defines the query baselines and the SLO snapshot the observability program measures against, and every reading cell was a placeholder. A baseline that was never captured is a ratchet with no floor.

── CLOSED 2026-09-07, AND THE REMEDY IS NOT THE ONE THE ROW IMPLIED. "Capture the baseline" was the obvious reading; measuring the database first showed it would have been actively harmful.

THE DATASET CANNOT SUPPORT A BASELINE YET, measured rather than assumed: posts 0, circles 0, circle_profiles 0, memberships 0, room_messages 0, friendships 1, event_rsvps 5, practice_logs 14, spaces 22, profiles 58, events 67. Only engagement_events has volume, at 39,492 rows / 26 MB. THREE OF THE FIVE HOT PATHS READ TABLES THAT ARE EMPTY. Numbers captured here would encode "every plan is an instant scan of nothing", and the first real traffic would blow through them for reasons that have nothing to do with a regression — a ratchet that fires on success, which is how a check trains people to ignore it (ADR-970). The doc's own methodology says so: a p95 is meaningless without the data volume it ran against.

So the file now carries MEASURED FACTS where they exist and a STATED GATE where they do not: region us-west-2, Postgres 17.6, the full per-table row counts and sizes at a dated capture, and an explicit volume threshold at which §2a should be re-run (posts >= 1,000 · circles >= 50 with circle_profiles >= 500 · profiles >= 500 · event_rsvps >= 1,000). The honest floor today is that there is no floor, said with numbers.

🔴 TWO REAL BUGS WERE FOUND BY TRYING TO FOLLOW THE DOC, which is the argument for trying rather than reasoning about it. (1) scripts/perf-baseline.mjs printed capture SQL for a function that DOES NOT EXIST: it passed a viewer uuid as the first argument, while the live signature is feed_for_viewer(_sort text, _limit int, _lat float8, _lng float8, _radius_m int) and takes no viewer id at all. It failed with `function feed_for_viewer(uuid, integer, unknown) does not exist`. Fixed, with the real signature and the reason recorded at the line. entries.title: The event cover's intrinsic aspect is not captured at upload, so the poster band still trades on a guess
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 by the backlog audit's docs sweep: work a live plan or ADR names as open, deferred or "a follow-up", with no row owning it. ADR-1196 closed the poster-band aspect trade (LIVE-146) and named the change that removes the trade entirely: "capture the cover's intrinsic aspect in the browser at upload and store it on events.theme beside coverFocus." It was recorded as a trailing sentence inside a done row. The browser already decodes the image for blurhash and palette (lib/library/image-describe.ts), so width and height are one more field from the same decode; the poster band then reads a real ratio instead of the fallback. Closes when the upload path stores the aspect and components/media/poster-band.tsx reads it.

CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1248). Premise re-tested first and it held: events.theme carried coverFocus, heroHeight, marketListed and checkInEnabled and nothing about size; components/media/poster-band.tsx took only the tier height class, so its shape was the ladder, not the poster; the browser decoded the cover in the focal picker and in prepareImageForUpload and reported dimensions to nobody. The seam chosen is the focal picker rather than the upload control: components/ui/image-focal-picker.tsx now reports naturalWidth and naturalHeight through an onImageLoad prop, and components/admin/modules/event-header-controls.tsx stores width / height on events.theme.coverAspect through updateEventCoverFocus (a fourth optional argument, validated server-side by lib/events/cover-aspect.ts, bounded 0.2 to 5, and never computed on the server). That seam re-measures every time the preview changes, which is every time the gallery re-crowns its first photo, so a swapped cover measures itself the moment its preview appears; a plain focus drag leaves the value alone. The band takes aspect plus maxHeightClass (lib/layout/cover-height.ts posterMaxHeightClass, the same ladder as max-h-*) and becomes the poster's own shape up to the tier; absent either, it renders byte for byte what it rendered before. The event page passes the value only when the hero IS the uploaded cover, so a scanned poster never wears the cover's shape; the public twin under app/discover/events carries cover_aspect the same way. Not done here, on purpose: the create form stores no aspect (the first open of the header controls measures it), and no theme key is cleared when a cover changes outside the settings panel, because that clear would race the picker's write on the same jsonb bag. lib/events/cover-aspect.test.ts pins the parser and the round-trip; components/media/poster-band.test.tsx pins the shaped path, the byte-identical fallback, the ladder derivation and the page wiring.

verify.note: Four arms on the CONSEQUENCE, comments stripped first so no arm can pass by reading its own documentation. The band sizes by aspect-ratio and chooses the ceiling over the height only when shaped; the event page reads the stored value and passes it; the header controls measure in the browser and the action validates and writes it; and neither the action nor the band names sharp, which is the fan-out this row was never allowed to buy (DEPLOY-SAFETY).

entries.title: Backlog probe attribution comes from the parent process, so the guard can only run serially and every budget around it is a cliff

source.ref: childCpuMs() and the serial probe loop

entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06, carrying the half of HYG-042 that a raised timeout does not fix. check-backlog.mjs measures each probe by reading cutime+cstime from /proc/self/stat around a spawnSync — attribution that works ONLY because the probes run one at a time. So the guard cannot be parallelised without going blind on per-probe cost, which is the signal LIVE-034 exists to provide, and every budget around it (the two vitest timeouts, the 4.5s per-probe ceiling) is a cliff that has to be re-read as the list grows. 387 probes now cost ~34s wall per run, and the parity case runs the whole set twice.

OPTION (b), as HYG-042 framed it: have every `node -e` probe report its own process.cpuUsage() on exit, so attribution survives any amount of parallelism because it no longer comes from the parent. 🔴 ITS KNOWN HOLE, stated by the row that proposed it: it does not cover cmd probes that are not node, so the ceiling would go blind on exactly the probes most likely to be expensive — a guard that cannot see the thing it exists to watch is ADR-970 with the roles reversed. Whoever builds this owes an answer for the non-node case (refuse one at validation time, or wrap it) in the same change.

⚪ STILL AN OWNER DECISION on whether it is worth building at all: the cheap half is done, and the list is not growing fast enough to make the budgets unworkable soon. Filed so the choice survives HYG-042 being closed rather than dying with it.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P1 on 2026-09-07 in the full re-prioritisation pass: an instrument that keeps a gate honest: probe attribution comes from the parent process, so check:backlog can only run serially and every budget around it is a cliff rather than a slope.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1226), OPTION (b) WITH ITS HOLE CLOSED. Every cmd probe's node process now preloads scripts/backlog-probe-cpu.mjs (NODE_OPTIONS=--import, appended so a runner's own NODE_OPTIONS survives) and on exit writes `probe-cpu <ms>` to fd 3, a pipe the guard opens per probe for exactly that line. The number is process.cpuUsage() plus the CPU of the children the probe itself waited for, read from the PROBE's own /proc/self/stat, so a probe that shells out to tsc is still charged for it — the half the parent-side reading used to see and a pure self-report would have lost. Attribution therefore comes from the probe, not from the parent, and the parent no longer reads its reaped-children counters at all.

THE NON-NODE HOLE THE ROW DEMANDED AN ANSWER FOR: refused at validation time. validate() fails a cmd probe that does not run under node, with the message saying what to write instead. Seven probes in the file were plain grep pipelines (LIVE-126, SCAN-523/525/526/528/529/530); each was rewritten as a node -e body reading the same files for the same strings, and its verdict was checked identical before and after the rewrite (one mutation control on SCAN-523 flipped to 1 as it should). Both parity arms of the contract test hold.

AND THE SERIAL CONSTRAINT IS GONE, which was the point: the probes now run through a pool of min(4, cores). Measured on this container, the full guard fell from ~34 s wall to 9.1 s (user CPU 23.9 s, unchanged in kind), with n=346 attributed and 0 unattributed. probe-cost and guard-cost print the same lines the contract test parses, plus an `unattributed=N` tail when a probe reported nothing and `N in flight` on the guard line so a reading says how it was taken.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("scripts/check-backlog.mjs","utf8");process.exit(/cpuUsage/.test(s)&&!/cutime/.test(s)?0:1)'
verify.note: Closes when per-probe cost comes from each probe reporting its own cpuUsage rather than from the parent reading cutime/cstime. Both halves matter: adding cpuUsage while keeping the parent read would leave the serial constraint exactly where it is. CLOSED 2026-09-07: check-backlog.mjs sums the probes' own reports (cpuUsage in backlog-probe-cpu.mjs) and no longer reads the parent's reaped-children counters.

entries.title: A practice named after it is created keeps its untitled-practice-N URL for good, because no path re-mints a slug

source.ref: uniquePracticeSlug and its two call sites

entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-06 from LIVE-188's root cause, which was found by fixing the one row and asking why it existed. `uniquePracticeSlug` (lib/practices.ts:1691) has exactly two callers: create (:1361) and fork (:1778). `updatePractice` (:1586) writes a title and never revisits the slug. So the public URL of a practice is frozen at the moment it is created, and the create path defaults an unnamed practice to the title 'Untitled practice' — which slugs to `untitled-practice-N`. The Vera path at app/(main)/practices/actions.ts:388 then sets a real title on exactly those practices and leaves the URL alone. That is the whole mechanism, and it produced a submitted-to-Search-Console URL reading `untitled-practice-2` for a practice titled 'Daily Hypnosis' since July.

🔴 THE FIX HAS ONE HARD CONSTRAINT: never break a URL that is already public. Re-mint the slug when a title is first set on a practice whose slug still matches the untitled placeholder AND which is not yet public. A practice that IS public keeps its URL and needs a deliberate rename plus a redirect, exactly as LIVE-188 did — do not automate that half, because a silent slug change on an indexed page splits its crawl signal.

WORTH CHECKING IN THE SAME PASS, from the same reading: whether Journeys, Circles and Spaces mint their slugs the same way. Practices were found by the sitemap; the others were not looked at.

── CLOSED 2026-09-07. `updatePractice` re-mints the slug when a title is written, and every clause is load-bearing: only when a title is being written; only when the current slug is STILL the untitled placeholder, so a slug any real title earned at create or fork is never touched; only while the practice is PRIVATE; and only when the new title yields a real root that is not the placeholder again, so re-saving a still-unnamed practice cannot bump it to untitled-practice-3. The pre-edit row is read at most once, shared with the weight-class clamp that already read it.

🔴 A PUBLIC PRACTICE KEEPS ITS URL, and that is the constraint rather than an omission. A silent slug change on an indexed page splits its crawl signal, so renaming a public practice stays a deliberate act — rename plus a 308, exactly how LIVE-188 was handled. No practice_slug_redirects row is written either: a private practice's placeholder URL was never public, resolvePracticeSlugRedirect refuses a non-public target anyway, so the row would be inert at write time and would go stale when the freed placeholder slug is re-issued.

⚪ EXISTING STOCK HEALS ON THE NEXT TITLE EDIT, not on any edit. Broadening the trigger would cost an extra read on every updatePractice; that trade is stated in the code and pinned by a test.

Seven mutations, each watched red: the whole file reverted (3 tests), the is_public gate removed, the placeholder-shape gate removed, the placeholder-root gate removed, the empty-root guard removed, uniquePracticeSlug swapped for the bare root, and the trigger keyed on row shape rather than a title write. Re-verified independently after the agent reported: reverting lib/practices.ts to main fails exactly 3 of 9, and all 9 pass restored.

⚠️ THE ROW'S OWN PROBE READS ONLY THE FIRST 4000 CHARS of updatePractice. A first draft placed the block at the end of that long function and the probe FAILED — the probe is a window, not a search. Moving it beside the title write satisfied the probe and is the better home regardless.

verify.note: Passes when updatePractice can re-mint a slug at all. Deliberately narrow: it proves the seam exists, and the not-yet-public gate is pinned by the unit test the row asks for rather than by a grep.

entries.title: The ledger fold takes meta.slate wholesale from main, so it hands back a backlog that contradicts itself

source.ref: HYG-032 fold driver · HYG-047 slate contract

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-07 by hitting it five times in one night. mergeBacklog merged ENTRIES by row id and then emitted `{ ...theirs, entries: merged }`, so every non-entry key came from main unread. That is right for `schema`, `lanes` and `rules`, which a branch has no opinion about, and WRONG for meta.slate, which is a VIEW OVER THE ENTRIES the fold has just changed. A branch that closed a row and dropped it from the slate had that drop discarded, so the tool emitted a file whose slate listed finished work as active — exactly what HYG-047 measures ("the slate inside the verified backlog is itself unverified"), and check:backlog went red on the fold's own output.

MEASURED, NOT THEORISED: the seven-PR audit stack of 2026-09-06/07 was folded five times (slice-consent, slice-measurement, slice-crawl-surface twice, and the LIVE-184 close) and HYG-047 fired on ALL FIVE, each fixed by hand with the same three lines. A tool that exists so this file is never hand-edited cannot hand back a file that needs hand-editing.

THE FIX FOLDS THE SLATE ON THE SAME PRINCIPLE AS THE ENTRIES — main's order first, this branch's additions appended — and then reconciles it against the MERGED entries, which are the authority on status. It drops a row that is done, an id naming no row, and a duplicate placement when the two sides filed the same row into different waves. It reports each drop on stdout, because the old failure was invisible at fold time and surfaced several commands later.

⚪ IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PLACE AN UNPLACED OPEN ROW. HYG-047 fails on one and that failure is correct: which wave a row belongs to is a judgement about build ORDER, and inventing one to go green is how a slate starts lying. Five of the eight new tests fail against the pre-fix driver; the other three are labelled controls rather than counted as proof.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=fs.readFileSync('scripts/maintenance/fold-ledger-docs.mjs','utf8');if(!/function foldSlate/.test(s))throw new Error('the fold no longer reconciles meta.slate');if(!/status === 'done'/.test(s))throw new Error('foldSlate no longer drops finished rows');const t=fs.readFileSync('scripts/maintenance/fold-ledger-docs.test.ts','utf8');if(!/meta.slate is folded beside the entries/.test(t))throw new Error('the slate fold has no test');"

entries.notes: Filed and closed in the same change, per the rule that a gate is wired beside the run that proves it.
