entries.title: Journeys freeze an untitled-journey-<random> slug at creation, and those URLs are in the sitemap
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-07 from LIVE-201's fix, by asking whether the same mechanism exists elsewhere. It does, and the journey case is WORSE because journey slugs are in the sitemap.

app/(main)/journeys/create-actions.ts creates with title 'Untitled journey'. lib/journey-plans.ts mints slug: slugify(input.title), and that local slugify APPENDS A RANDOM 6-CHAR SUFFIX, so an unnamed journey is born `untitled-journey-a1b2c3`. The update path writes the title and never revisits the slug, exactly as updatePractice did before LIVE-201.

CLOSED 2026-09-07 by porting LIVE-201's re-mint, clause for clause, onto the update path. slugify is now split into slugRoot (the deterministic part) + the random suffix, because the gate has to ask "is this slug still the untitled placeholder" and "does the new title yield a real root", and neither question can be asked of a function that appends randomness.

The four clauses are the four LIVE-201 found the hard way, and the third and fourth are why nothing else moves: the slug is re-minted only when a title is being written, only when the new title yields a root that is not the placeholder again, only when the current slug still matches the placeholder SHAPE, and only while the journey is still PRIVATE.

WATCHED GO RED BY MUTATION, three arms, each with its own message: removing the re-mint block entirely; removing the visibility gate alone; and replacing the placeholder-shape test with `true`. Nine tests in lib/journey-plans-remint-slug.test.ts drive the real updatePlan against a mocked database and assert on the UPDATE PAYLOAD - what actually lands in the slug column - and two of them go red against the pre-fix code while seven pass trivially, which is the correct split: seven assert a URL that must NOT move.

THE ROW'S OWN PROBE NAMED A FUNCTION THAT DOES NOT EXIST, and re-testing the premise before working the row is what caught it. The row said `updateJourneyPlan`; lib/journey-plans.ts exports `updatePlan`. The probe would have thrown "updateJourneyPlan is gone; re-scope this row" forever, reading as an honest "not done" for entirely the wrong reason. Rewritten against the real function and mutation-tested.

THE ROW OVERSTATED THE EXPOSURE, slightly, and the corrected version is still the reason this was P1. app/sitemap.ts emits /discover/journeys/<slug> from listPublicJourneys, which filters `visibility = 'public'` - so the crawled set is journeys named after creation AND THEN PUBLISHED, not every journey named after creation. The private ones were never advertised. That is also exactly why the private gate is the right seam: the re-mint happens before publish, so the placeholder can no longer reach the sitemap at all, and a journey already public keeps the URL Search Console has.

CIRCLES ARE THE SAME SHAPE AND WERE DELIBERATELY NOT DONE HERE. lib/circles/draft.ts defaults the name to 'New circle' and mints from it; publishCircle in lib/circles/remix.ts returns c.slug without re-minting. A circle is draft-until-publish so the placeholder URL is never crawlable while it is wrong, and publish is a different seam from a title write - it is its own row, not a rider on this one.

SPACES ARE CLEAN: lib/spaces/provision.ts mints from an operator-typed name and has no 'Untitled' default, so there is no placeholder to freeze.

entries.title: The member Event page has thrown a Server-to-Client serialization error for ten weeks, and no row owned it
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-07 by re-measuring LIVE-124's premise, not by a gate — the third time a runtime-error read has paid, after LIVE-053 and LIVE-124 itself. It is now the LARGEST error group in production by a wide margin and no row owned it.

Vercel grouped runtime errors, project frequency-web, trailing 7 days: `Error: Only plain objects, and a few built-ins, can be passed to Client Components from Server Components. Classes or null prototypes are not supported.` count=33, users=14, route /events/[slug], first 2026-06-27T21:11:21Z, last 2026-09-03T17:27:54Z, lastDeployment dpl_DVQUVrBG1EYQ32hHvdK11XZ3h2cW. TEN WEEKS, fourteen real members, on the member Event detail page - the single most-linked page the product has - and it ran unrecorded the whole time, exactly the "a real production error ran unrecorded" shape LIVE-053 names.

TWO DIGESTS, so it is two call sites or two branches, not one: 1047665748 and 4155556756.

⚠️ THE LOGGED VALUE IS `{}`, AND THAT IS THE STRONGEST CLUE IN THE RECORD. An object that renders as `{}` has no enumerable own properties, which rules OUT a plain row from Supabase and rules IN a class instance whose state is non-enumerable or lives behind accessors - an Error, a PostgrestError, a Stripe SDK response object, or a null-prototype object. A Date is NOT a candidate: React serialises Dates across the boundary, and the page's own Dates are converted with toISOString before they reach a prop anyway (page.tsx:1773).

WHAT WAS EXCLUDED BY READING THE TREE, recorded so nobody re-runs it. app/(main)/events/[slug]/page.tsx is 2,254 lines and imports four local client components plus three shared ones. Checked and clean: EventCheckInButton (eventId only), ClaimRequestCta (eventId + a string), HostRequestCta (eventId + HostAskSpace[]), TicketButton (TicketTierView[] is explicitly mapped field-by-field at page.tsx:793, and every other prop is a primitive or a two-field literal), RsvpControls (every prop a primitive at the call site), InlineText (a bound server action, which is the supported pattern). SeriesDatesRail, PosterBand, EventDetailTemplate, WarmProof, GuestCheckInPrompt and JsonLd are SERVER components, so they cannot be the boundary themselves - but they can pass a page-supplied value onward to one, and that path is NOT yet walked.

🔴 THE CALL SITE IS NOT NAMED YET, AND NOTHING SHOULD BE PATCHED UNTIL IT IS. LIVE-053's record is the precedent and it is explicit: "Do not raise a guard until the call site is named." A speculative `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))` sprinkled at a plausible boundary is the shape-not-truth move this repo names in four ADRs - it would silence the error without anyone knowing which value was wrong, and the next one would land somewhere else.

NEXT STEP, in order of cost: (1) walk the props EventDetailTemplate and the block registry forward into the client components they render, since a server component passing a page-supplied value onward is the one path this pass did not close; (2) failing that, map digest 1047665748 against the deployed build's source map, the same move that named LIVE-053's site; (3) the branch is reachable by about 3 users a week, so a reproduction is plausible from an event row with whatever optional relation the clean branches lack - claim state, Connect status, or a ticket tier with a membership gate are the three richest candidates because each pulls an object from an SDK or a join rather than a mapped literal.

⚪ A SECOND, SMALLER GROUP WAS SEEN IN THE SAME READ AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT FILED AS A DEFECT: `Error: The destination stream closed early.` count=19, users=4, across eleven `.rsc` routes. That is the signature of a client navigating away mid-stream and is expected traffic, not a bug; it is recorded here so the next reader does not file it twice. If it ever concentrates on ONE route it stops being benign.
── SECOND PASS 2026-09-07, same session. The call site is STILL not named, and this records what the pass excluded so the third does not repeat it.

🔴 THE SHARED TEMPLATE CHAIN IS EXCLUDED BY THE ROUTE ITSELF, and this is the strongest deduction available without a source map. EventDetailTemplate is a server component over DetailTemplate, whose only client descendants are Breadcrumbs and PageAdminBar. Both render on EVERY detail page in the product. The error group names exactly ONE route. A defect in that chain would appear on all of them, so the offending value is page-specific data or an events-specific component, not the shell.

ALSO EXCLUDED, by reading the call sites: the Set hazard is already handled (`caps={Array.from(eventCaps)}` at page.tsx:1992 and :2002 — somebody met this before); SeriesDatesRail, PosterBand, WarmProof, GuestCheckInPrompt and JsonLd are server components and cannot be the boundary; GuestRsvpForm takes two primitives; seriesRailDates is plain rows selected field-by-field in lib/events/series-dates.ts; and there is no object SPREAD into any component in the file.

WHAT REMAINS UNWALKED, and it is now a short list: the stored-block / page_config widget render path, and the `belonging` subtree behind its own Suspense. Those are the two places a page-supplied value is handed to a component this pass did not follow.
── THIRD PASS 2026-09-07, and it CLOSES BOTH remaining paths. The static analysis is now exhausted, which is a result rather than a dead end: it removes two of the row's three proposed next steps and leaves one.

BOTH PATHS THE SECOND PASS LEFT OPEN ARE CLEAN. The `belonging` Suspense subtree renders EventBelonging, VenueCredit and HostHovercard, and all three are SERVER components - HostHovercard was the strongest remaining candidate because it is the one place the page hands a raw joined row onward whole (`host={event.host}`), and it turns out never to reach a client boundary. And there IS NO page_config block render path on this route at all: the second pass named it from the shape of other detail pages, and app/(main)/events/[slug]/page.tsx simply has none.

⚠️ SO THE OFFENDING VALUE IS NOT IN THIS PAGE'S RENDER TREE. Every client boundary reachable from it passes a primitive, a two-field literal, or a field-by-field mapped array. That is now checked exhaustively rather than sampled.

🔴 WHICH REFRAMES THE ROW, and this is the pass's real finding: A SERVER ACTION'S RETURN VALUE ALSO CROSSES THE SERVER-TO-CLIENT BOUNDARY, and the platform attributes the throw to the ROUTE THE ACTION WAS INVOKED FROM rather than to the file that returned it. That fits every observed fact better than a render-time prop does: it explains the route specificity without implicating the shared shell, it explains a rate of roughly three a week (the branch needs someone to actually press a control AND that path to return the bad value, rather than merely loading the page), and it explains two digests as two actions or two error branches.

⚪ THE EVENT SURFACE'S OWN ACTIONS WERE THEN CHECKED AND ARE ALSO CLEAN: ticket-actions, claim-actions, ticket-tier-actions, social-actions, host-transfer-actions, events/actions.ts and events/admin-actions.ts return string literals for every error (`{ ok: false, error: 'sign_in' }` and friends), never a raw PostgrestError. So if the action hypothesis is right, the action is one this page invokes from somewhere else in the tree, or the value rides on a SUCCESS return rather than an error one.

NEXT STEP IS NOW SINGULAR: map digest 1047665748 against the deployed build's source map. Options (1) and (3) from the original list are spent - the render tree is walked and the reproduction guess had three candidates that are all now excluded. This is the same move that named LIVE-053's call site after two passes of reading the tree failed, and it is the cheapest remaining thing that can actually name a file and a line.
🔴 CORRECTION, SAME PASS, BEFORE THE NEXT STEP ABOVE IS ACTED ON: THE SOURCE MAP ROUTE DOES NOT WORK ON THIS ERROR, and the row's captured sample already says so. Both samples carry their whole stack as the single line `at ignore-listed frames` - React ignore-lists the RSC serializer frames, so unlike LIVE-053 (whose group printed real chunk-and-column frames such as `at c (lib_1b8tszi._.js:2:11541)`) there is NOTHING here to map. Writing "source-map the digest" as the singular next step would have sent the next reader after a frame that does not exist. Naming that now is cheaper than discovering it later, which is this row's own lesson about LIVE-053's three "an agent cannot look" blockers, applied in reverse.

SO THE REAL NEXT STEP IS A REPRODUCTION, and the action hypothesis makes it a cheap one rather than a hunt: instrument rather than guess. The value is only ever seen at the boundary, so the way to name it is to make the boundary talk - wrap the suspect return or prop in a dev-only assertion that logs the offending key and constructor name before React refuses it, ship it behind the same log discipline as LIVE-053's errorStack, and read the next occurrence. Roughly three a week means about two days to a named value. That is instrumentation for a defect already proven to exist, not a speculative guard on a hypothetical one, so it does not violate the rule this row opened with.

── FOURTH PASS 2026-09-07, and it REPLACES the third pass's next step rather than executing it. The third pass concluded "instrument the boundary and read the next occurrence, roughly two days to a named value". Before building that, the premise was re-measured — which is what this repo's own rule says to do, and it changed the answer.

🔴 THE ERROR HAS NOT RECURRED. Re-read 2026-09-07 14:35Z on a 4-day window: count 3, users 2, and the group's LAST occurrence is still 2026-09-03T17:27:54Z, on deployment dpl_DVQUVrBG1EYQ32hHvdK11XZ3h2cW (commit 4bf92a6bd, production since 2026-09-02). Production has deployed continuously since — six production deploys on 2026-09-07 alone — and zero occurrences on any of them.

⚠️ THAT IS SUGGESTIVE AND IT IS NOT PROOF, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS THE POINT. 33 occurrences over the 68 days since 2026-06-27 is 0.49/day, so 3.5 quiet days expects 1.7 and P(zero) is about 0.18 — roughly one time in five by chance alone. Reporting "it stopped" on this reading would be the n=1 mistake ADR-1221 was written about, made from a production log, which is exactly what made that one feel like a measurement.

SO THE NEXT STEP IS TO READ THE CLOCK, NOT TO BUILD AN INSTRUMENT. The row's own close condition is already a 7-day quiet window; the clock started 2026-09-03T17:27:54Z and runs out 2026-09-10T17:27Z. At the historical rate a 7-day silence has P about 0.033 — a real signal rather than a coincidence. If it is still silent then, this closes as fixed incidentally by one of the ~30 PRs that shipped between 09-03 and 09-07, and the honest close names that it was never diagnosed. If it fires again, the boundary assertion is built with a live branch to catch, which is far cheaper than building it now and instrumenting a path that may no longer be reachable.

ONE MORE EXCLUSION, RECORDED SO THE LIST STAYS COMPLETE: `searchParams`. It was never named in the first three passes and it is the one remaining class of page-supplied value that is not a plain object — Next resolves it to an object React can refuse. It is CLEAN here: page.tsx:298 awaits it into `sp`, :303 destructures four strings out of it, :308 passes `sp.door` (a string) to doorNoteFor, and `sp` itself reaches no component. Every reference in the file is one of those three lines.

RE-PRICED P1 -> P2 on the same reading: a P1 is a repair ready to work, and there is nothing to work until the window closes or the error returns.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1230) AS A DUPLICATE OF SCAN-545, AND THE PREMISE WAS FALSE ON THE DAY IT WAS FILED. The title says no row owned this error. SCAN-545 (done 2026-09-04, lib/events/reactions-core.ts, ADR-1201 item 5) owned it: aggregate() built its result with Object.create(null) and getEventPostReactions, a server action the EventActivity mount effect calls on every event page with at least one post, returned that null-prototype map straight to Flight. PR #2366 carried the fix to production at 2026-09-05T12:17Z (dpl_6gcnzawuMRV89dP1y5DcqnhSSNx5, commit 67ada96). LIVE-124’s own close paragraph, written 2026-09-06, already cited SCAN-545 for this group; this row was opened the next morning by re-measuring LIVE-124’s premise and did not read LIVE-124’s close.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. (1) The React 19.2.8 flight server in node_modules: the throw appends describeObjectForErrorMessage(parent, key), and a bare `{}` is only ever printed for its emptyRoot sentinel, i.e. when the refused value is a serialisation ROOT: a task model (a server action’s return value or a resolved Promise prop), a Server Component’s return value, or a Fragment’s direct children. A prop nested in JSX prints the props object with carets, never `{}`. So the first pass’s "strongest clue" excluded every render-tree prop on its own, and passes two through four walked the one place the value could not be. (2) The import graph from the page plus its seventeen widget modules: 392 files, 14 server-action modules reachable from client components on the route; the only one whose return value is built by a fold over caller-supplied keys is lib/events/reactions.ts. (3) Vercel runtime logs, production, error level, trailing 2 days at 2026-09-07 16:05Z: one line in the whole project, on /api/cron/weekly-digest, none on /events/[slug]. get_runtime_errors returned no groups at all for the project on any window in the same minutes, including windows that must contain the 2026-09-03 occurrences three earlier reads saw, so that instrument’s silence is recorded as silence, not as a zero.

⚠️ TWO EXCLUSIONS ABOVE ARE WRONG AND STAY IN THE RECORD SO THEY ARE NOT REUSED: the third pass’s "there IS NO page_config block render path on this route" (the whole interior is <PageModules>, stamped through lib/events/active-event.ts, which is where EventActivity renders from), and the fourth pass’s clock (the fix had already been in production for two days when the clock was set).

WHAT CHANGED. No product code: the source fix is SCAN-545’s. lib/events/reactions-core.test.ts now walks the WHOLE return tree with Flight’s exact predicate on every path the action can return, with positive controls for the walker and for the pre-fix shape, so a nested null-prototype bucket is a red test too. The probe below is a runtime measurement: it imports the fold and applies the same predicate, and exits 79 (indeterminate) if the import itself cannot run.

verify.cmd: node --no-warnings -e "import('./lib/events/reactions-core.ts').then((m)=>{const bad=(v,at)=>{if(typeof v!=='object'||v===null||v instanceof Date)return[];if(Array.isArray(v))return v.flatMap((x,i)=>bad(x,at+'['+i+']'));const p=Object.getPrototypeOf(v);const here=(p===Object.prototype||(p!==null&&Object.getPrototypeOf(p)===null))?[]:[at];return here.concat(Object.keys(v).flatMap((k)=>bad(v[k],at+'.'+k)))};const rows=[{post_id:'p1',kind:'🔥',profile_id:'me'},{post_id:'p2',kind:'👋',profile_id:'x'}];const fails=[...bad(m.aggregate(rows,['p1','p2','__proto__'],'me'),'$'),...bad(m.aggregate([],['p1'],null),'$'),...bad(m.aggregate([],[],null),'$')];if(fails.length){console.error('Flight would refuse',fails);process.exit(1)}}).catch((e)=>{console.error('cannot import the fold:',e.message);process.exit(79)})"
verify.note: A runtime measurement, not a grep: imports lib/events/reactions-core.ts (it has no imports of its own, so Node 22 loads it directly), calls aggregate on the populated, shaped-empty and no-ids paths with __proto__ among the keys, and applies React Flight’s exact acceptance predicate (proto is Object.prototype, or a prototype whose own prototype is null) to every reachable value. Exit 1 names the refused path; exit 79 means the import itself failed and the probe could not look.
verify.evidence: Closed 2026-09-07 as a duplicate of SCAN-545 (fixed 2026-09-04, in production since 2026-09-05T12:17Z on dpl_6gcnzawuMRV89dP1y5DcqnhSSNx5). Vercel runtime logs, production, error level, trailing 2 days read 2026-09-07 16:05Z: no line on /events/[slug]. The probe ran green on the same day.

entries.title: A wording call is still live on the published front door: "the third spaces are failing us" reads as third PLACES and collides with the Space noun

source.ref: the copy is not in this repo: pages.published_data where slug=home, read live 2026-09-07 while closing LIVE-148

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-07 by the work that closed LIVE-148 — not by the guard it shipped, but by a human reading the copy the guard finally made reachable. That is the row working as intended: the front door had been unreviewable since 2026-07-13, and the first read of it found four things.

All four confirmed present in the live document by SQL regex against published_data::text, not inferred:

1. "The feed isn't you friend." — should be "your friend". In the Text block home-problem-b, the third block on the page.
2. "We all feeling that separation." — should be "We're all feeling". Same block, last sentence. (It also carries a trailing space.)
3. "Show up Tuesda" — TRUNCATED. In the Marquee block home-marquee, item 5 of 6. The marquee scrolls this past every visitor.
4. "the third spaces are failing us" — same Text block. TWO issues: the established term is "third PLACES" (Oldenburg), and "spaces" collides with Space, which NAMING.md makes a product proper noun. On the front door the collision is the more expensive of the two.

🔴 NOT FIXED BY THE AGENT THAT FOUND IT, deliberately. This is published brand copy on the most-linked page the product has; the owner authors it in the page editor at /pages/home, and CONTENT-VOICE is a locked canon. Typos 1-3 are unambiguous errors rather than style calls, so they are safe to correct verbatim; item 4 is a wording decision and the owner should pick between "third places" and a rephrase that avoids the Space collision entirely.

⚪ WHY THE NEW GUARD DID NOT CATCH THESE. scripts/maintenance/home-copy-canon.mjs runs the NAMING and VOICE canons, which are about retired claims, proper nouns and register. None of these four trips a canon rule: a typo is not a naming violation. A spellchecker over brand copy is a different instrument with a different false-positive profile, and inventing one inside this row would have been scope creep. Whether it is worth building is its own question; the cheap version is that the front door is now readable at all.

✅ 2026-09-08 — DEFECTS 1-3 ARE FIXED IN PRODUCTION. The owner authorised exactly those three and no more, on 2026-09-08. Item 4 was left untouched by the same instruction: the wording is the owner's call, and this row stays open for it alone.

WHAT CHANGED, in `pages` where slug='home' (one row, the root Space, id 0765933e-a8d0-4e18-ae39-e7bf16746ba4): TWO leaf values of a 213-leaf document, written with `jsonb_set` on the two exact paths rather than by rewriting the document.
  · content[2].props.body — the Text block home-problem-b. "The feed isn't you friend." → "The feed isn't your friend.", and "We all feeling that separation. " → "We're all feeling that separation." (the trailing space went with it).
  · content[11].props.items[4].text — the Marquee block home-marquee. "Show up Tuesda" → "Show up Tuesday". That ending is a READING, not a guess: lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts, the seed the published document was authored from, carries `{ text: 'Show up Tuesday' }` at the same position in the same six-item list, and the page's own heading two blocks up already reads "NO ONE TO CALL ON A TUESDAY".

⚠️ BOTH COLUMNS WERE WRITTEN, and that is the load-bearing detail. `publishPage` (app/(main)/edit/actions.ts) writes `data` and `published_data` from the SAME object, so the editor's DRAFT is what gets republished. Fixing only `published_data` would have looked correct until the owner's next save in /pages/home silently restored all three typos. The two columns were byte-identical before (md5 951eda0a8b09d10a5369f6ae4753e488, 9188 bytes) and are byte-identical after (md5 bc837bc9140a8513eb08392827638b75, 9192 bytes).

The write was a COMPARE-AND-SWAP: the UPDATE carried the pre-change md5 of both columns in its WHERE clause, so a concurrent owner save would have made it a no-op instead of a clobber. `updated_at`, `published_at`, `status` and `updated_by` were deliberately left alone — this is a correction to the owner's document, not a new authorship stamp, and the record of who changed what lives here rather than in a timestamp.

REVALIDATION: none was available, and none is needed. `/` is ISR (`export const revalidate = 3600` in app/page.tsx) and the repo has no on-demand revalidate endpoint for it, so the corrected copy reaches the front door within an hour of the write. The one immediate path is the editor's own Publish, which calls `revalidatePath('/')` — and because `data` carries the fix, that republishes the CORRECTED document.

⚪ ONE OBSERVATION FOR WHOEVER PICKS UP ITEM 4: with the three typos gone, what is left is purely a product decision, which is this file's `ruling` action rather than `content` ("URLs or an export only you have"). `ownerAction` is left at `content` because narrowing the ask was authorised and reclassifying it was not.

verify.evidence: Re-measured live 2026-09-08 against pages.published_data where slug=home, by the same SQL regex that found the row. GONE: `isn't you friend` 0 matches, `We all feeling` 0, `Show up Tuesda"` 0. PRESENT and correct: `isn't your friend` 1, `We're all feeling that separation."` 1 (the closing quote proves the trailing space is gone), `Show up Tuesday` 1. STILL PRESENT BY INSTRUCTION: `third spaces` 1 — that is item 4, the owner's wording call, and it is the only thing keeping this row open. Structure unchanged: 13 blocks, block ids home-problem-b and home-marquee intact, 213 leaf values of which exactly 2 differ from the pre-change document (md5 951eda0a8b09d10a5369f6ae4753e488 → bc837bc9140a8513eb08392827638b75). Closes when `third spaces` is gone from the published document, re-measured the same way.

entries.title: Structured data points at per-entity OG cards by their UNHASHED path, so every event and Space schema image is a 404

source.ref: found 2026-09-07 while closing LIVE-183; proven against a built artifact

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-07 by the LIVE-183 work, and PROVEN ON AN ARTIFACT rather than argued.

Next hash-suffixes a metadata image route whose parent path contains a ROUTE GROUP (getMetadataRouteSuffix). Both per-entity OG routes live under one:
  app/(main)/events/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx
  app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx
and the build emits them at opengraph-image-lyffkg and opengraph-image-tt3pwa respectively, read straight out of .next/server.

But lib/jsonld.ts emits the UNHASHED path:
  :208  image: [abs(`/events/${event.slug}/opengraph-image`), abs('/opengraph-image')]
  :539  const ogImage = abs(`/spaces/${space.slug}/opengraph-image`)

So the primary schema image on every event and every Space is a URL that does not exist. The same rule was independently confirmed for the help tree: the predicted suffix 12boxn for /(help)/help/[category]/[slug] matched the emitted artifact exactly.

⚪ NOT A TOTAL OUTAGE, which is why it survived: both nodes carry a fallback image after the bad one (the site card for events, the operator logo and site card for Spaces), so the rich-result bar is still met and no validator screams. The PRIMARY image is simply always dead.

⚪ THIS IS ALSO WHY the help article schema deliberately points at /images/hero.jpg (a real file) rather than at its new card, with a test pinning that so nobody hand-writes a card path in. Hand-writing the hashed path is NOT the fix - the hash is derived by Next and would drift. The fix is to stop hand-writing these URLs at all: let Next inject the card through the metadata API (which is what the help page now does by leaving openGraph.images unset), or resolve the suffix from the build manifest rather than from a template literal.

NOT FIXED IN LIVE-183 because it is different pages with their own verification: this needs a build to confirm the emitted paths for events and Spaces, and the fix changes how two more schema nodes are composed.

── FIX LANDED 2026-09-07, ROW DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. Both hand-written URLs are gone from lib/jsonld.ts: eventSchema and spaceSchema now name only the ROOT card (plus the operator logo for a Space, when set). Verified there are exactly two such sites and no others - every other abs('/opengraph-image') in the file is the root card, and the discover/ and spotlight/ trees are real segments rather than route groups, so nothing there is suffixed.

WHY THE URLS WERE REMOVED RATHER THAN CORRECTED. The suffix is derived from the parent path by Next's own getMetadataRouteSuffix, so hardcoding lyffkg or tt3pwa would satisfy any check that merely looks right and would rot the moment a route group is added, renamed or removed. The SHARE cards are unaffected and still per-entity: those pages leave openGraph.images unset so Next injects the suffixed URL itself, which is the one mechanism that knows the hash. Only the schema image falls back, and it falls back to something real.

⚠️ ONE CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN WORDING, checked rather than assumed. The row said both nodes "carry a fallback image after the bad one, which is why no validator screams". That was nearly reported as false: there is no app/opengraph-image.tsx. There IS app/opengraph-image.jpg - a static file at a path containing no route group, so it is served unsuffixed and the fallback is genuinely fine. The row's claim holds; it just holds for a reason nobody had written down.

🔴 WHY THIS IS STILL OPEN. The close condition is a live 200 for an event and a Space schema image on a deployed build, "measured rather than assumed". Egress from the agent container to frequencylocal.com is refused by the proxy (403 CONNECT tunnel failed), so that measurement cannot be taken here. Closing on the strength of the code change would be exactly the shape this backlog fails rows for. What IS proven in-repo: a mutation-tested guard in lib/jsonld.test.ts that fails on the exact strings which were live until today and passes on the fix, with a positive control that the node still carries an image so it cannot pass by emptiness, and a detector self-test that the pattern fires on the per-entity paths and not on the root card.
── 🔴 CLOSED 2026-09-07, AND THE FIRST FIX FOR THIS ROW REPLACED A DEAD URL WITH A DEAD URL. #2407 repointed nine schema sites from the per-entity card to abs('/opengraph-image'). That is ALSO not an image: app/opengraph-image.jpg is a STATIC metadata file, so Next serves it WITH its extension, and the extensionless path is not a route at all.

MEASURED ON PRODUCTION rather than reasoned about, and the reading is the whole lesson:
  /opengraph-image                              -> 200  text/html   x-matched-path: /   (the home page)
  /events/<slug>/opengraph-image                -> 200  text/html   x-matched-path: /   (the home page)
  /opengraph-image.jpg                          -> 200  image/jpeg  84,049 bytes        (app/opengraph-image.jpg, byte for byte)

⚠️ THIS ROW'S OWN PREMISE WAS WRONG IN THE SAME WAY ITS FIX WAS. It said the per-entity paths "404". They do not. They answer 200 with the home page's HTML, through the app's own catch-all. That is why the defect survived a build, a lint, check:seo, check:og-trace and 14,000 tests: structured data was advertising an HTML DOCUMENT AS AN IMAGE, and nothing except a content-type read can tell the two apart. A 404 would have been visible to any link checker. And this row's stated close condition - "resolves 200 on a deployed build" - would have PASSED on the defect. A close condition can be measurable and still measure the wrong thing.

⚠️ AND THE TESTS PINNED THE DEAD URL TWICE. Two spaceSchema tests asserted the per-Space card; #2407 "corrected" them to ${SITE_URL}/opengraph-image, which is the second dead URL. Both corrections looked right and neither was checked against anything real.

WHAT SHIPPED. One constant, SITE_OG_IMAGE in lib/site.ts, replacing ten hand-written call sites (nine in lib/jsonld.ts, one in lib/listings-shared/listing-seo.ts). And the gate that makes a literal unable to be wrong a third time: every image URL a schema builder emits on our OWN origin must resolve to a real file under app/ or public/. A URL is correct only if something answers it. Twelve builders are exercised; three mutation arms are proven - the extensionless static file, a route-group per-entity card, and the sitemap shape - and each fails naming the URL.

🔴 THE SITEMAP CARRIED THE IDENTICAL DEFECT, IN A FILE THE FIRST FIX NEVER OPENED. app/sitemap.ts:354 and :424 advertised ${SITE_URL}/spaces/<slug>/opengraph-image and ${SITE_URL}/events/<slug>/opengraph-image as image-sitemap entries - the same 200-HTML, shipped to Google directly rather than through a schema node, on every Space and every upcoming event. Removed rather than repointed: the shared site card on every URL would be spam, and carrying each entity's real cover needs the reader to project cover_image_path through the storage helper. That is LIVE-207.

── ✅ CONFIRMED ON PRODUCTION 2026-09-07 10:17Z, which is what this row's ORIGINAL close condition asked for and what the fix before it could not have satisfied. A live event page (/events/breathe-connect-expand-2026-11-05) now carries exactly two of our own OG URLs, and each is the right one in the right place:

    schema.org Event image   https://frequencylocal.com/opengraph-image.jpg
    og:image (share card)    https://frequencylocal.com/events/<slug>/opengraph-image-lyffkg?7ce0045dc0fd86ae

BOTH HALVES BEHAVE AS ADR-1220 SAID THEY WOULD. Structured data names a static file that exists, and the SHARE card is still per-event because the page leaves openGraph.images unset and lets Next inject the hash-suffixed URL - the one mechanism that knows the suffix. The hashed path appearing in the live head is also independent proof of the route-group hashing this row was originally filed about: nobody hand-wrote lyffkg, Next derived it.

⚪ WORTH STATING PLAINLY: the dead URL is gone from the page entirely. Neither the extensionless root card nor the unhashed per-event path appears anywhere in the rendered HTML.

verify.note: Four arms, each measuring a CONSEQUENCE this row got wrong once. (1) The one constant names the extension-bearing path, not the extensionless one that serves the home page. (2) A real file sits behind it - the arm that separates a URL that answers from a URL that looks right. (3) No schema site hand-writes the bare path again. (4) The sitemap advertises no metadata-route image. Comment lines are stripped first, so no arm can pass by reading the documentation above it. The stronger behavioural guard is lib/jsonld.test.ts, which walks twelve builders and requires every self-origin image URL to resolve to a file on disk, with three mutation-proven controls.
verify.evidence: undefined ── CONFIRMED ON PRODUCTION 2026-09-07 10:17Z: a live event page carries schema image https://frequencylocal.com/opengraph-image.jpg (the static file, 200 image/jpeg) and og:image https://frequencylocal.com/events/<slug>/opengraph-image-lyffkg?7ce0045dc0fd86ae (Next-injected, hash-suffixed). Neither dead form appears in the rendered HTML. The live hash is also independent proof of the route-group suffixing this row was filed about.

entries.title: Four series-fold gaps survive LIVE-198: two counts computed inside Postgres, two /admin consoles that cancel one date at a time, and three list sites

source.ref: enumerated 2026-09-07 while closing LIVE-198; deliberately out of that rowic scope

entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-07 by the LIVE-198 work, which wired all ELEVEN in-reach count sites and enumerated what it could not reach. Recorded here rather than dropped, because an enumeration that lives only in a merged PR body is an enumeration nobody finds again.

1. TWO COUNTS COMPUTED INSIDE POSTGRES, so no TS change can fold them: circle_momentum (lib/connections/metrics.ts) and public_events (app/discover/places/_data.ts, components/marketing/blocks.tsx "Events soon"). Neither RPC returns parent_event_id, so the fold has nothing to key on. This needs a MIGRATION that either returns the column or folds in SQL - which is why it was correctly left out of a TS-only change.

2. 🔴 memberEventAllowanceOk (app/(main)/events/actions.ts) IS INFLATED THE SAME WAY BUT MUST NOT BE FOLDED WITHOUT A RULING. It is an ENTITLEMENT QUOTA, not a dashboard: today a member creating a weekly series burns nine of their allowance, and folding it would let one member create nine times as many events. That LOOSENS a cap. Whether a series should cost one allowance or nine is a product decision about what the allowance is FOR, and the agent that found it correctly refused to decide.

3. TWO /admin CONSOLES STILL CANCEL ONE DATE AT A TIME (app/(main)/admin/events/actions.ts, app/(main)/admin/actions.ts). cancelSeries exists and is exposed on the host danger zone; wiring these two is roughly one line each. Left out deliberately to keep a money-path diff small on the night it was written.

4. THREE LIST-SHAPED FOLD GAPS, same family, different shape: the Space dashboard "Coming up" (components/spaces/dashboard/space-dashboard.tsx), components/widgets/entity/entity-cta.tsx, and the /admin/events management table - where per-occurrence is arguably CORRECT, since an operator managing dates wants the dates.

⚪ ALSO DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED and not a gap: /admin's weekly volume bars still count occurrences, because "how busy is the calendar" is honestly a per-date question.

── RE-PRICED P2 -> P1 on 2026-09-07 in the full re-prioritisation pass: a repair on shipped mechanism, ready to work: five series-fold gaps survive LIVE-198 and each one shows a member a wrong count.

── SPLIT 2026-09-07, for the same reason HYG-058 was split the same day: this row bundled agent work with an owner ruling, and a row that needs both closes on neither.

ITEM 2 — memberEventAllowanceOk — IS NOW OWN-063. It is not a fold, it is a question about what the entitlement is FOR: today a member creating a weekly series burns nine of their allowance, and folding it would let one member create nine times as many events. That LOOSENS a cap, and the agent that found it was right to refuse to decide. Leaving it here meant the ask sat inside a live row's detail instead of beside the OWNER section, which is exactly what ownerAction exists to prevent.

WHAT STAYS HERE IS ALL AGENT WORK, and the seam for the largest piece already exists: `cancelSeries` in lib/events/cancellation.ts takes a per-occurrence `canCancel` callback precisely so a second caller can pass its own authorization, and app/(main)/events/admin-actions.ts:286 is the worked example. So the two /admin consoles (cancelEvent in admin/events/actions.ts:201, toggleCancelEvent in admin/actions.ts:894) each need an action beside the existing one that calls it with the console's own gate — requireEventEditor and requireScopedManage respectively — plus the control that invokes it. That is more than the "roughly one line each" this row first estimated, which is why it re-sizes S -> M.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07 (ADR-1228). Each of the three remaining items is folded or carries a recorded decision.

1. THE TWO POSTGRES COUNTS, by migration 20270345002100. circle_momentum.upcoming_events now counts `distinct coalesce(parent_event_id, id)` — same signature, same return type, so `create or replace` and the existing grant. public_events is a LIST, so it is NOT folded in SQL: it gains `parent_event_id` + `recurrence_type` (a `returns table` cannot change under replace, so DROP + CREATE with the ADR-903 gate body copied verbatim and the grants re-applied in the same transaction) and the fold moves to the reader — lib/discover.ts getPublicEvents and the marketing strip's read in lib/page-editor/live-data.ts both over-fetch by seriesFetchLimit and collapse to one card per series, so every discover count (`events.length` on the index pages, the per-city buckets, "Events soon") is a count of gatherings. Ahead of the migration the readers see no parent_event_id, seriesKey() falls back to the id, and the fold is a no-op — today's behaviour exactly.

2. THE TWO /admin CANCEL CONSOLES. cancelEventSeriesAsEditor (admin/events/actions.ts) and cancelEventSeriesScoped (admin/actions.ts) each call lib/events/cancellation.ts cancelSeries with the console's OWN gate passed as `canCancel` — requireEventEditor and requireScopedManage respectively, asked once for the clicked date and once per occurrence — mirroring the host's cancelEventSeries. The edit page loads the series plan beside the event and offers "Cancel N remaining dates" when at least two are to come; the table's CancelToggle offers "Cancel series" on any row that is a series member (the loader now selects SERIES_COLUMNS). Both report every bucket the seam returns, through one describeSeriesCancel.

3. THE THREE LIST SITES. The Space dashboard "Coming up" and the entity CTA block fold to one card per series through listEventsForSpace (whose COLS already carries the columns), pinned in components/events/series-browse-wiring.test.ts beside the two RPC readers. The /admin/events management table is RECORDED AS PER-DATE ON PURPOSE: an operator managing dates wants the dates; what it gained is the series cancel on each row rather than a fold. That decision lives on AdminEvent's comment and here.

verify.evidence: Enumerated 2026-09-07 while closing LIVE-198, which wired the 11 reachable sites; split 2026-09-07 so the entitlement ruling lives in OWN-063 rather than inside this row. Closes when each of the three REMAINING items is either folded or carries a recorded decision not to fold it: the two RPC counts (circle_momentum and public_events, which need a migration returning parent_event_id or folding in SQL — no TS change can reach them), the two /admin cancel consoles (an action beside each existing one, passing the console's own gate into cancelSeries), and the three list-shaped sites (Space dashboard "Coming up", entity-cta, /admin/events table — where per-occurrence is arguably correct for the last, and a recorded decision closes it). ── CLOSED 2026-09-07: circle_momentum folds in SQL and public_events carries the two columns (migration 20270345002100, in the tree, not yet applied); both /admin consoles carry a series cancel through cancelSeries with their own gate; the Space dashboard and entity CTA fold; the /admin/events table stays per-date by recorded decision.

entries.title: Ruling: does a recurring series cost one event allowance or one per date?
entries.detail:
SPLIT OUT OF LIVE-206 on 2026-09-07, because it is the one item in that row an agent must not decide.

`memberEventAllowanceOk` counts OCCURRENCES, like the eleven display counts LIVE-198 folded. But it is not a display count — it is an ENTITLEMENT QUOTA, and that inverts which direction the bug runs. Every other site inflated a number a member merely READS; this one inflates a number that STOPS them. Today a member creating a weekly series burns nine of their allowance for one gathering.

🔴 WHICH IS WHY FOLDING IT IS NOT A BUG FIX. Folding it would let one member create nine times as many events as the cap intends. An agent applying the LIVE-198 pattern here would LOOSEN a paid cap while believing it was correcting an off-by-N, and would be able to point at ten sibling call sites as precedent. The agent that found it refused to decide, correctly, and that refusal is the reason this row exists.

THE ASK, and it is one sentence either way: is the allowance a cap on GATHERINGS (a weekly series costs one, and the fold is right) or on DATES ON THE CALENDAR (a weekly series costs nine, and today's behaviour is right and should be documented rather than changed)? Whichever you pick, the answer gets written into the code as a comment naming this row, because the next agent to read `memberEventAllowanceOk` beside its folded siblings will ask the same question.

── PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-09-08 (premise sweep, ADR-1269) and it HOLDS: `memberEventAllowanceOk` (app/(main)/events/actions.ts:202) still counts ROWS in `events` for the member with no space_id, so a weekly series still burns one allowance per date. Nothing has been folded and nothing should be until the ruling lands.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-07: memberEventAllowanceOk in app/(main)/events/actions.ts counts occurrences, unfolded, while the eleven display counts LIVE-198 reached are folded. Closes when the ruling is recorded — either the count is folded to gatherings, or a comment at that call site states that per-date is deliberate and names this row, so the divergence from its siblings reads as a decision rather than an oversight.

entries.title: The image sitemap now advertises nothing, because what it advertised was the home page
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-07 by the LIVE-205 close. app/sitemap.ts carried an image-sitemap entry on every Space and every upcoming event, and both named a per-entity OG card by its UNHASHED path - a URL that answers 200 with the home page's HTML, not an image. Those entries are now REMOVED rather than repointed, and this row owns putting a real one back.

WHY NOT JUST NAME THE SITE CARD. One shared image on every URL in the sitemap is exactly what an image sitemap is not for; it would be noise at best and read as spam at worst.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY NEEDS. events.cover_image_path and the Space equivalent are storage PATHS, not URLs, so the sitemap readers (listSitemapEventEntries in lib/events/series-seo.ts, and the Spaces discovery reader) must project the column and resolve it through the storage public-URL helper. SitemapEventEntry gains an optional image field; a row with no cover emits no image rather than a placeholder, the same rule LIVE-197 applied to lastModified - an invented value is worse than none.

⚪ NOT URGENT, AND SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS. The sitemap is strictly more honest today than it was: it advertises nothing instead of advertising HTML. The close is a real per-entity image, not the restoration of a URL.

CLOSES WHEN both entry types carry an image URL that resolves to an actual image, proven the way LIVE-205 finally was - by content-type on a deployed build, never by a 200.

── ⚠️ A CONSTRAINT FOUND WHILE SIZING THIS 2026-09-07, AND IT NARROWS THE ANSWER BEFORE ANYONE STARTS. An event has THREE artwork sources and lib/events/hero-url.ts is the one place their precedence lives, but only the FIRST is usable here:

    cover_image_path         -> PUBLIC bucket event-media  -> getPublicUrl()     usable
    poster_path              -> PRIVATE network-contacts   -> createSignedUrl()  never
    details.media.coverPath  -> PRIVATE network-contacts   -> createSignedUrl()  never

🔴 A SIGNED URL MUST NEVER ENTER A SITEMAP. It expires, and an image sitemap full of URLs that 404 in a week is the same defect LIVE-205 just closed - an advertised image that is not there - only on a timer. So the sitemap does NOT reuse resolveEventHeroUrl: it takes the public cover or it emits nothing, and a scanned-poster-only event correctly carries no image. Same rule LIVE-197 applied to lastModified and LIVE-205 to the card: an absent value beats an invented one.

⚪ AND CHECK THE PARITY GUARD BEFORE WRITING THE READ. scripts/check-event-hero-parity.test.ts fails any call site selecting some but not all of EVENT_HERO_COLUMNS, because a partial read silently downgrades a hero. A sitemap read that selects only cover_image_path is deliberately NOT a hero resolution and must not be mistaken for one - either it stays outside the guard's call-site list, or the guard learns the distinction. Decide that explicitly rather than discovering it as a red test.

── CLOSED 2026-09-07, AND THE SPACES HALF TURNED OUT TO BE FREE. The row assumed both sides needed a reader change. Re-measured before writing any: NetworkedSpace already carries coverUrl, because spaces.cover_image_url is stored as a URL rather than a storage path, so app/sitemap.ts had the value in hand the whole time. Only the events side needed the projection.

EVENTS: listSitemapEventEntries now selects cover_image_path and resolves it through the PUBLIC event-media bucket, and SitemapEventEntry gained an optional image. A row with no uploaded cover emits NO image rather than a placeholder or the shared site card - absent beats invented, the same rule LIVE-197 applied to lastmod and LIVE-205 to the card.

🔴 THE CONSTRAINT THIS ROW WAS FILED WITH IS NOW A GUARD, because it is exactly the kind of thing a later reader would "fix" in the wrong direction. lib/events/hero-url.ts is the ONE authority for an event's artwork everywhere else in the app, and reaching for it here would look like consistency - but two of its three sources live in a PRIVATE bucket behind createSignedUrl, and a signed URL EXPIRES. Advertising one is LIVE-205's defect on a timer: an image Google fetches today and cannot fetch next week. So the reader takes cover_image_path and nothing else, and a test fails the source if poster_path, createSignedUrl, posterSignedUrl or resolveEventHeroUrl ever appears in it.

⚪ THE PARITY GUARD WAS CHECKED FIRST rather than discovered as a red test, which is what the row asked for. scripts/check-event-hero-parity.test.ts fails a call site that selects SOME but not all of EVENT_HERO_COLUMNS, and its third arm fails any file naming all THREE tiers. The sitemap reader names ONE tier and is not in HERO_SURFACES, so it trips neither - and that is the correct answer rather than a lucky one: a sitemap entry is deliberately not a hero resolution.

CONTROLS: two mutation arms proven red - selecting poster_path alongside the cover, and emitting the site card as a placeholder when a row has none.

verify.note: Five arms on the CONSEQUENCE. The reader carries the public cover and resolves it without signing; it names NO private-bucket source, which is the arm that matters — a signed URL expires and would turn the sitemap into LIVE-205 on a timer; both entry types emit the image CONDITIONALLY, so a row without a cover advertises nothing rather than a placeholder; and neither names a metadata-route card, which is what LIVE-205 removed. Comment lines are stripped first so no arm can pass by reading its own documentation.

entries.title: notFound() renders the 404 page with a 200 status across the app, and the head still says index, follow

source.ref: measured on production 2026-09-07 while closing LIVE-205

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-07 by the LIVE-205 work, which needed to know what a dead URL actually returns and got an answer that was worse than the row it was chasing. MEASURED ON PRODUCTION, not inferred, and reproduced on a known-good control first (/help returns x-matched-path: /help and the Help Center, so the reader resolves paths correctly rather than collapsing everything to the root).

TWO DISTINCT SHAPES, both 200, both indexable:

1. AN UNMATCHED TOP-LEVEL PATH RETURNS THE HOME PAGE. GET /this-path-does-not-exist-9f3c2a answers 200, content-type text/html, x-matched-path: / - the ROOT route matched - with the home page's title and <meta name="robots" content="index, follow">. Every nonexistent URL on the domain is therefore an indexable duplicate of the front door. This is also what hid LIVE-205 for as long as it was live: a schema image URL pointing at nothing returned a valid 200 HTML page rather than a 404, so no link checker, build, lint or test could see it.

2. A NONEXISTENT ENTITY RETURNS A "NOT FOUND" PAGE WITH A 200 AND index, follow. GET /events/no-such-event-9f3c2a answers 200, x-matched-path: /events/[slug], title "Event not found · Frequency", robots index, follow. The page is honest to a human and a lie to a crawler: a soft 404 is the canonical way to get thin pages indexed and then get the whole directory discounted.

⚠️ WHAT CAUSES SHAPE 1 IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING, AND MUST BE TESTED BEFORE IT IS FIXED. The tree has app/not-found.tsx, no catch-all page at any top level, no rewrite in next.config.ts, none in vercel.json, and proxy.ts returns NextResponse.next() rather than rewriting. The leading candidate is app/(main)/@wizard/[...catchAll]/page.tsx - the parallel-route slot closer from ADR-1017, which is the pattern Next's own parallel-routes doc prescribes, and which is ALSO the documented reason not-found handling stops working for unmatched routes once a slot matches everything. That is a plausible mechanism and nothing here has confirmed it. Confirm it first: a preview deploy with the slot catch-all temporarily removed either restores a 404 on shape 1 or clears the slot entirely, and that is one build.

⚠️ AND check:seo CLAIMS THIS GROUND. It reports that "every crawler-reachable page outside (marketing) declares its intent (advertised, or noindex)" and it passes. It reads SOURCE. Both shapes above are ARTIFACT behaviour - what Vercel actually serves for a path the source never declared - which is the exact split AGENTS.md names about the 2026-08-11 incident: every gate measured the source, none measured the artifact. Whatever fix lands must be gated on a real response, not on a file.

NOT FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE AS LIVE-205, deliberately: that row was structured data, this is routing and not-found semantics across the whole app, the cause of shape 1 is unproven, and the safe fix for shape 2 (call notFound() instead of rendering a soft page, or at minimum emit noindex) is a per-entity decision about what a member should see when a link rots.

── 🔴 SHARPENED THE SAME DAY, AND IT IS ONE DEFECT RATHER THAN TWO SYMPTOMS. Shape 2 was read again for what actually RENDERED, not just what the title said: the body of /events/no-such-event-9f3c2a is app/not-found.tsx - it contains the string "Page not found" and the big "404" - served with an HTTP status of 200 and <meta name="robots" content="index, follow">.

So the finding is not "one event page is a soft 404". It is that notFound() PRODUCES THE 404 UI WITHOUT THE 404 STATUS. app/(main)/events/[slug]/page.tsx calls notFound() at :320 for a missing row and at :467/:602/:606/:614 for a draft, a private event and a non-member - the same call the whole app uses for every gated or missing entity. Every one of those answers 200 today, and the root layout's robots default carries index, follow onto all of them, so a crawler is invited to index the 404 page under every private and every rotted URL in the product.

⚪ THAT ALSO EXPLAINS THE TWO SHAPES AS ONE MECHANISM. Shape 1 (an unmatched path renders the HOME page at x-matched-path: /) and shape 2 (notFound() renders the 404 page at 200) are both what the parallel-routes doc describes when a slot's catch-all matches everything: the router resolves a segment it should not have, and the not-found boundary loses its status. The hypothesis is unchanged and still needs confirming on a build before anything is changed - but it now has TWO independent symptoms to be tested against, and a fix that only restores shape 1 has not finished the job.

⚠️ THE CHEAPEST HONEST INTERIM, if the routing fix proves large: notFound() paths must at minimum emit noindex. A 404 page that says index, follow is the half of this that costs indexing budget today.

── ⚠️ THE HYPOTHESIS IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKED, CHECKED THE SAME DAY, AND THIS CORRECTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE HYPOTHESIS DID. Next's own parallel-routes doc was read (node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/parallel-routes.md) and it does NOT say that a slot catch-all breaks the not-found status. What it says is the opposite-shaped thing: an unmatched slot renders default.js on a hard navigation, "or 404 if default.js doesn't exist" (:92, :101), and it recommends the catch-all slot precisely as the way to close a modal (:485). app/(main)/@wizard/default.tsx EXISTS, so that slot resolves the way the doc intends.

TWO MORE FACTS THAT DO NOT FIT THE HYPOTHESIS EITHER: there is no app/(main)/page.tsx, so the (main) group does not own the root route at all - app/page.tsx does - and nothing in next.config.ts, vercel.json or proxy.ts rewrites to it.

SO THE MECHANISM IS UNKNOWN, and that is the state to work from. Leaving a plausible-but-unsupported cause in this row is worse than leaving none: the next person would spend the build on the wrong control. The two MEASUREMENTS are unchanged and are the solid part - an unmatched path renders app/page.tsx at 200 with x-matched-path: /, and notFound() renders app/not-found.tsx at 200 - and they are what any candidate explanation has to account for. The next diagnostic is a local production build served locally, which answers whether this is the app's routing at all or something in front of it, and costs one build rather than one deploy.

── 🟢 MECHANISM PROVEN 2026-09-07 FROM THE BUILT ARTIFACT, AND IT IS THE HYPOTHESIS THIS ROW HAD JUST RETRACTED. Reading the DOCS said the parallel-routes theory was unsupported, and that retraction was correct about the docs and wrong about the world. Reading the ARTIFACT settles it - the same source-versus-artifact split AGENTS.md names about the 2026-08-11 incident, arrived at twice in one row.

A local production build emits, in .next/routes-manifest.json, a TOP-LEVEL dynamic route:

    /[...catchAll]   regex  ^/(.+?)(?:/)?$

which matches EVERY path on the domain. And .next/app-path-routes-manifest.json names its owner without ambiguity:

    "/(main)/@wizard/[...catchAll]/page"  =>  "/[...catchAll]"

So the parallel-route slot's catch-all - ADR-1017's modal closer - is HOISTED OUT OF THE SLOT into a real top-level route. Every unmatched URL therefore MATCHES something, which is why nothing 404s: an unmatched path resolves through the (main) tree at 200, and notFound() inside a page that did match renders the not-found boundary while the response status stays 200. One mechanism, both shapes.

CONTROL RUN: CONTROL RUN, both directions: with app/(main)/@wizard/[...catchAll]/page.tsx removed, a rebuild emits ZERO root-level dynamic routes and ZERO routes whose regex matches an arbitrary deep path (dynamicRoutes 171 -> 170). Restoring the file brings /[...catchAll] back. One file, one route that matches every URL on the domain.

⚠️ THE FIX IS NOT "DELETE IT", and that is why this row still needs a decision rather than a patch. That catch-all is the pattern Next's own doc PRESCRIBES for closing a modal opened through an intercepting route (parallel-routes.md :485), and ADR-1017 adopted it for a real bug: without it a member who opens a Spark and follows a link inside it carries the modal onto the next page. Deleting it trades an SEO defect for a UX one. The options, none of them free:
  (a) Scope the slot deeper so its catch-all is not hoisted to the root - the slot sits at the (main) group root today, which is why its catch-all becomes /[...catchAll].
  (b) Keep it and make the not-found path explicit: have the catch-all page itself call notFound() when no real route matched, rather than rendering null.
  (c) Close the modal by another mechanism entirely (route-state rather than a matched route), retiring the catch-all.
  Whichever is chosen, the ACCEPTANCE TEST is now cheap and exact and does not need a deploy: build, and assert that routes-manifest.json contains no top-level route whose regex matches an arbitrary path. That is a gate this repo can run on every PR, and it is the one the source-reading check:seo structurally could not be.

⚪ AND THE CHEAP INTERIM STANDS INDEPENDENT OF THE CHOICE: a notFound() path must at minimum emit noindex. That is the half costing indexing budget today.

── 🔴 RE-MEASURED 2026-09-07, TWICE, AND BOTH SHAPES ARE SMALLER THAN THE ROW SAYS. Production was read again through the Vercel deployment reader (the whole HTML this time, not the first robots tag), and the tree was BUILT AND SERVED locally with placeholder env (`next start`, curl with headers) so the answer does not depend on a reader that follows redirects.

SHAPE 2 IS DOCUMENTED NEXT BEHAVIOUR, AND THE NOINDEX IS ALREADY THERE. /events/no-such-event-9f3c2a answers 200 with the not-found body in BOTH places, and the HTML carries TWO robots tags: the root layout's `index, follow` AND `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`. The second is Next's own: node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/loading.md §Status Codes says a notFound() thrown after streaming has begun cannot change the status (the headers are gone), so Next injects noindex into the streamed HTML, and "in the streaming case this does not lead to indexation". The event route streams because app/(main)/events/[slug]/loading.tsx exists. So the "interim" this row asked for — noindex on the notFound path — has been true the whole time; the earlier read stopped at the first robots tag. A REAL 404 status for an entity needs the existence check BEFORE the first Suspense boundary (the docs name proxy or a pre-boundary read), per entity route with a loading.tsx — that is the per-entity decision this row already says is the owner's, and it is a UX call (a friendly streamed 200 with noindex versus a hard 404), not an SEO emergency.

SHAPE 1 IS A REDIRECT, NOT A DUPLICATE. Served locally, /this-path-does-not-exist-9f3c2a answers `307 Location: /`; the production reader followed it, which is where "200, x-matched-path: /, the home page" came from. The mechanism has two halves and the hoisted catch-all is only the first: the `/[...catchAll]` route (still in .next/routes-manifest.json on this tree, regex `^/(.+?)(?:/)?$`) resolves the unmatched path through the member tree, and app/(main)/layout.tsx:270 then sends a signed-out visitor home. A crawler is redirected, so the dead URL is not an indexable copy of the front door; the cost is a 307 where a 404 belongs (a soft-404 signal for crawlers, and a shared dead link that lands on the home page rather than saying so). A signed-in member on an unmatched path was NOT measured (no session locally): with no app/(main)/default.tsx the children slot has nothing to render, and what that looks like is the next thing to read.

RE-PRICED P1 -> P2 on these readings: nothing here indexes a dead URL today. THE RULING IS UNCHANGED AND STILL THE OWNER'S: the catch-all is ADR-1017's deliberate closer, with its own history-sentinel guard in components/studio/wizard-modal.tsx and app/(main)/@wizard/wizard-routes.test.ts pinning its existence; the alternative closer (the modal comparing usePathname() to the route it was mounted for, and the catch-all deleted) is a real design change to a mechanism that was built to fix a real bug, and it should not be swapped from a backlog pass. The acceptance test stays exact and now has a second arm: the manifest carries no route matching an arbitrary path, AND a served unmatched path answers 404 rather than 307.

── ✅ RULED AND SHIPPED 2026-09-08 — OPTION (b), plus the two things implementing it MEASURED. ADR-1267.

THE RULING: keep the parallel-route catch-all, and make the not-found path explicit by having the catch-all page call notFound() when no real route matched, rather than rendering null.

🔴 THE OBVIOUS READING OF THAT IS WRONG, AND THAT IS THE FIRST FINDING. The slot's catch-all does NOT render only on unmatched routes — it renders on EVERY route in the (main) layout. Instrumented on a running build, app/(main)/@wizard/[...catchAll]/page.tsx logged for /events, /spaces/<slug> and /market/<id> alike, because rendering null everywhere the modal is not IS how it closes the modal. A notFound() there would fire on every member page in the product. So the not-found went to the page that renders ONLY when nothing matched: the least specific page in the CHILDREN slot, the new app/(main)/[...catchAll]/page.tsx. The slot closer is unchanged and still returns null; the two files are one mechanism and wizard-routes.test.ts now pins the pair.

🔴 AND A BARE notFound() WOULD HAVE BEEN A SILENT NO-OP, WHICH IS THE SECOND FINDING. A notFound() in a page cannot beat a redirect() in a layout ABOVE it: app/(main)/layout.tsx throws its signed-out redirect from its own body, before React renders any page. Measured in both directions on a running build — with that redirect bypassed, an unmatched path ALREADY answered a real 404 (Next's documented children-slot miss); with it in place, a page-level notFound() still answered 307. The new page therefore declares its params CLOSED (`export const dynamicParams = false` + an empty generateStaticParams), which moves the answer to ROUTING time: no URL resolves to that segment, so Next answers 404 before the layout runs. The notFound() call stays as the statement of intent the gate reads, and as what serves if the config is ever loosened.

ARM 1 IS WIRED AS A GATE, IN postbuild RATHER THAN THE CI GUARDS ARRAY, because it reads the ARTIFACT and CI never builds (DEPLOY-SAFETY.md, ADR-1003). `pnpm check:notfound-routes` (scripts/check-notfound-routes.mjs) reads .next/routes-manifest.json for every route whose regex matches a URL the app declares nowhere, attributes each through .next/app-path-routes-manifest.json, and fails unless a CHILDREN page owns it and calls notFound(). A route whose only owner is an @slot page is this row's exact state and fails by name. ⚠️ THE ARM COULD NOT BE TAKEN LITERALLY: this row wrote it as `the manifest carries no route matching an arbitrary path`, and under option (b) the catch-all STAYS, so that route stays too. What the gate asserts is the consequence the arm was reaching for. Its PR-time half is scripts/check-notfound-routes.test.ts, which drives it against a faithful reconstruction of the pre-fix artifact that MUST fail, because postbuild never runs on a PR.

ARM 2, SERVED LOCALLY ON A PRODUCTION BUILD (next start, curl): /this-path-does-not-exist-9f3c2a and /zzz-no-such/deeper/9f3c2a went 307→/ ⇒ 404, with the not-found body and Next's noindex; / , /events, /help and /sitemap.xml stayed 200; /circles stayed 307 to /sign-in?next=/circles. The route table is unchanged in size (171 dynamic / 285 static); what changed is that /[...catchAll] now has a children owner beside the slot page.

⚪ WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, DELIBERATELY: the entity shape (/events/no-such-event) still answers 200 with the not-found body and Next's injected noindex. That is documented streaming behaviour and this row had already corrected itself twice on it; a hard 404 per entity route means moving the existence check above that route's loading.tsx, which is the per-entity UX call this row always said was the owner's, not part of this ruling.

── RE-MEASURED ON PRODUCTION 2026-09-08 (premise sweep, ADR-1269). THE TITLE OVERSTATES ITS SCOPE IN BOTH CLAUSES, and the correction narrows the row rather than closing it.

GET https://frequencylocal.com/spotlight/zzz-no-such-handle-9x7q → **HTTP 404 Not Found**, `x-matched-path: /spotlight/[handle]`, and the head carries `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`. So a `notFound()` raised inside a route segment that actually MATCHES answers a real 404 today and is not indexable. "with a 200 status ACROSS THE APP" is therefore wrong, and "the head still says index, follow" is only half true: the root layout's `index, follow` is still emitted alongside the `noindex`, and two robots tags on one document is worth fixing on its own, but the restrictive one wins for a crawler, so no dead entity URL is indexable.

WHAT HOLDS IS THE CATCH-ALL, WHICH IS THE HALF THE RULING IS ABOUT. GET https://frequencylocal.com/definitely-not-a-real-path-9x7q resolves through `/[...catchAll]` and ends at the HOME document (title "Frequency · Community Collective", 200 after the redirect is followed) rather than at a 404. That is the soft-404 this row exists for, and the second arm of its acceptance test ("a served unmatched path answers 404 rather than 307") is still unmet. The ruling is unchanged and still the owner's: the catch-all is ADR-1017's deliberate wizard closer.
