entries.title: The Hub and Nexus MANAGE consoles are still twins, and the archived-children defect still lives in one of them
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-07 from HYG-046, which fixed the same defect one layer up and found this one still live underneath.

app/(main)/hubs/admin-actions.ts and app/(main)/nexuses/admin-actions.ts carry the Hub and Nexus MANAGE consoles as hand-maintained twins, and drift #2 from HYG-046 lived there too: the Hub console filters archived children, the Nexus console did not. So the Nexus manage console listed archived Hubs and counted them, exactly as the public Nexus detail page did before HYG-046 - archiveHub's documented purpose ("so it drops out of listings") remained untrue on that surface.

CLOSED 2026-09-07, and the second read was worse than the row described. The row named the People listing. The Insights rollup was reading the same rows through an EMBED - `.select('id, member_cap, hubs ( circles ( member_count ) )')` on the nexus row - and an embed carries no place to put a filter, so all four Insight numbers counted archived Hubs: hubCount listed them, totalMembers summed their circles, and avgPerHub divided by the inflated count. Reading hubs as their own row set, the way the Hub twin reads circles, is what makes the filter expressible at all; that restructure is the substance of this fix, not the .neq beside it.

WATCHED GO RED BY MUTATION, both arms with their own message: dropping the People listing's filter, and restoring the embed in Insights. Five tests in app/(main)/nexuses/nexus-archived-hubs.test.ts drive the real loaders against a mocked database whose builder APPLIES the filters the code asked for, so they measure the rows and counts an operator sees rather than the shape of the call; four go red without the fix and the fifth is the all-active control.

THE PROBE READ ITS OWN DOCUMENTATION ON THE FIRST TRY. The comment explaining this fix quotes the embed it replaced, so the embed check fired on the fixed tree. It strips comment lines before looking - the same mistake SCAN-521 made, caught this time by running the probe on a clean tree before trusting it.

THE TWINNING ITSELF IS STILL OPEN AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED. These two files carry real schema divergence - member_cap, host-vs-guide, and the circles-of-hubs rollup - and they are 'use server' files with per-route action registrations, so unifying them touches the action surface rather than a render path. The archived filter was the small independent half; the twinning is a separate, larger question.

entries.title: Six column-backed image fields cannot hold an AssetRef, and nobody has ruled whether they should

source.ref: ADR-1253, the half HYG-029 could not build

entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-07 out of HYG-029 (ADR-1253), which adopted the AssetRef seam in the three JSONB-backed entity-block writers and could not touch this half.

spaces.brand_logo_url, spaces.cover_image_url, page_content.hero_image, page_settings.og_image_url, page_settings.header_image_url and profiles.header_image_url are TEXT columns. Their pickers (components/ui/header-image-field.tsx, components/admin/inline/inline-cover.tsx, components/spaces/loom/space-loom-studio.tsx, and the Studio spark field-control, which materialises into entity columns on apply) are handed {url, assetId} by the Loom and store the url alone, so a D3 edit or a version rollback of the asset cannot re-point them and D4 block_usage cannot see them.

THE ASK IS A RULING, NOT AN ESTIMATE, and the two exits are not the same size. (a) Companion *_asset_id columns beside each url column: a migration per table with the full ADR-1111 ordering discipline, a write on both sides of every save action, and a read that prefers the id. (b) An explicit decision that column caches stay URL-only until D4 usage indexing needs them, in which case this row closes as ruled and the pickers keep writing urls. Do NOT half-adopt by storing JSON in a text column: every reader of those columns is typed string, so a stored object renders as nothing or as [object Object], and the row that forbids this is the one that filed this row.

── PREMISE RE-MEASURED 2026-09-08 (premise sweep, ADR-1269) against the live schema and it HOLDS: all six columns are still `text` (spaces.brand_logo_url, spaces.cover_image_url, page_content.hero_image, page_settings.og_image_url, page_settings.header_image_url, profiles.header_image_url) and no `*_asset_id` companion exists on any of them. The ruling is unchanged, and so is the warning against half-adopting by storing JSON in a text column.

verify.evidence: Measured 2026-09-07 while closing HYG-029 (ADR-1253): each of the six is a text column, and the picker consumers named above still call onSelect(url) only. Nothing in the repo can choose between a migration and a ruling, so a probe would measure the wrong thing until the ruling exists.

entries.title: The "138 rasterised baselines" were content: the committed set predated the 2026-09-04 CTA sweep, and pr-compare had been red on 140 of 144 surfaces since
entries.source: Measured 2026-09-08 while taking the LIVE-186 recapture apart.
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-08 by refusing to commit a recapture whole. e2e-manual run 34174895830 captured all 144 surfaces against production and rewrote every committed baseline. Four of them are LIVE-186's and moved dimensions. The other 138 kept BYTE-IDENTICAL dimensions and still differed by 15,000-26,543 pixels each, measured with pixelmatch's YIQ colour delta at Playwright's configured threshold (0.2), anti-alias detection omitted so every figure is an upper bound. Worst: app-nearby desktop, 26,543 px. 138 of 138 are over LIVE-125's 400 px budget, by up to 66x.

THE DIMENSIONS ARE WHY THIS IS NOT CONTENT. A full-page capture of a changed page moves its height. Not one of the 138 moved a single pixel in height while 15,000+ pixels inside it changed. Content does not do that; a different rasteriser does.

⚠️ WHAT IT COSTS, AND IT IS NOT THE PIXELS. LIVE-125 set maxDiffPixels to 400 and bounded it at the low end with the only cross-runner reading that existed: ADR-1165's "pr-compare read 123 of 144 surfaces under 400 against baselines from a different runner". That reading is what makes 400 safe rather than brittle. This measurement says the same comparison today puts 138 of 138 OVER it. Either the runner class changed under the suite (LIVE-123 established that Vercel's builders moved from 4-core cle1 to 8-core iad1 Enhanced Build Machines between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-02, and the CI runner is a separate question nobody has asked), or ADR-1165's reading has expired. Until one of those is settled, nobody knows whether a red pr-compare means a regression or a runner, which is the state ADR-970 names: a check that is red for a reason nobody owns trains everyone to ignore it, and then it reads as coverage.

⚪ NOT A REASON TO RAISE THE BUDGET. Raising 400 to clear a rasterisation difference would forgive 66x the smallest control the product draws, which is the exact failure LIVE-125 closed. The fix is to make the comparison and the baseline agree about the machine, not to widen the gate until they need not.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, cheaply and without a deploy: capture the same surface twice on two dispatches and diff capture-against-capture. Same runner class twice ~ 0 px says the divergence is baseline-vs-runner; a large number twice says the capture itself is nondeterministic and the budget is unreachable at any value.

── ✅ MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-09-08 (ADR-1273), AND THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE WAS THE FINDING. The experiment the row prescribed was run: two e2e-manual dispatches on one branch against production (runs 34181605405 at 02:53Z and 34182476256 at 03:08Z, update_baselines + capture_shell). The second run staged NOTHING against the first's commit: 144 of 144 PNGs byte-identical fifteen minutes apart, the strongest determinism reading git can express. And the first run's diff against origin/main reproduced the rejected recapture exactly: 138 files over 400 px, 6 identical, none moving height, app-nearby dawn-light desktop at the same 26,543 px run 34174895830 read at 00:55Z. So the capture is deterministic and the 138 are real.

WHAT THEY ARE, read by band instead of by count (pnpm visual:bands origin/main <runner commit>, the reader this row ships): every public page differs in exactly the rows of its header CTA, its hero CTA and its footer CTA, and the crops show the words. The committed baselines say "Start a Circle" and "Find your way in"; production says "Join free" and "Find your people". That is #2348 (b2a36548, 2026-09-04 19:26Z, "two CTA verbs instead of seven"). The committed set was captured the same day by #2356 against ITS OWN branch preview (frequency-web-git-claud-194b15), which had not merged the sweep, so 138 baselines were born stale. app-settings light mobile differs in one 36-row band where a settings row swapped an icon button for a chevron; app-nearby, app-feed and /discover differ where live counts, member lists and event dates render. Copy inside a fixed box moves zero rows. "Content does not do that" was the wrong physics, and ADR-1258's own ceiling (a 26x26 control) is a same-height change.

WHAT IT COST. pr-compare run 34174785417 (#2423, 00:53Z) read 140 failed / 4 passed / 28 skipped, not the "three eyebrow contrast + four space-console" it was reported as; the re-run on 004664cc9 at 02:37Z failed the same way. Every PR's pr-compare has been red on ~140 surfaces since 2026-09-04, hidden because the check is not required (LIVE-186's other half) and because the number was read as a runner. The 400 px budget's premise stands: pr-compare on the same runner class reads 0 px on a page that has not changed, and the only thing between it and green was a recapture that had been refused on the wrong inference.

WHAT SHIPPED: the branch carries the full recapture of all 144 surfaces, taken 2026-09-08 04:07Z against a PREVIEW deployment of main (this branch's own preview, code-identical to main 88bda6882 for everything that renders), every file's bands read. It is a preview capture and not the 02:59Z production capture on purpose: pr-compare on the recaptured production set read 128 failed / 16 passed, and the band reader put every public page's difference in exactly two viewport-anchored bands (desktop rows 724-782 and 400-435, mobile 768-826 and 422-457). Cropped: the bottom-right band is the support-chat button, present on production and absent on every preview because SUPPORT_CHAT is set only for Vercel's Production environment since #2423 dropped the NEXT_PUBLIC_ fallback; the mid-right band is Vera's edge tab (components/layout/edge-pill.tsx via the launcher's fallback), present on the preview and absent on production. pr-compare photographs previews, so the reference it needs is a preview of main; the two environment-only elements are LIVE-213's to settle. scripts/visual-diff-bands.mjs + pnpm visual:bands, a dependency-free reader that prints WHERE the pixels moved for any two directories or git refs, pinned by scripts/visual-diff-bands.test.ts (every PNG filter type inverted, pixelmatch's YIQ delta, the budget mirrored from playwright.config.ts); e2e-manual.yml rebases a queued second capture with -X theirs instead of dying on a binary conflict (run 34181623788 did); test/e2e/README.md "Reading a capture before taking it". LIVE-186, HYG-055 and LIVE-040 carried the rasterisation sentence and are corrected in the same change (ADR-1269's sweep rule).

verify.evidence: 2026-09-08: runs 34181605405 and 34182476256 (production, 15 min apart) byte-identical on 144/144 PNGs (the second staged nothing); run 1 vs origin/main 88bda6882 = 138 over 400 px / 6 identical / 0 moved height, app-nearby desktop 26,543 px matching run 34174895830; bands sit on header, hero and footer CTAs (the #2348 sweep of 2026-09-04) plus live data on /nearby, /feed, /discover; pr-compare 34174785417 read 140 failed / 4 passed / 28 skipped. Full recapture committed from a preview of main (run on claude/live-212-preview-probe-lbhk4b, 04:07Z) after the production-sourced set read 128 failed on pr-compare for two environment-only fixed elements (support button on production only, Vera edge tab on preview only); pnpm visual:bands ships as the reader.

entries.title: Preview and production render two different fixed elements, so a baseline is only valid for the environment it was photographed on
entries.source: Measured 2026-09-08 by the LIVE-212 control run (ADR-1273).
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-08 when the recaptured baselines, taken against production, failed pr-compare on 128 of 144 surfaces (run 34184015342). pnpm visual:bands put every public page's difference in two viewport-anchored bands and the crops named them: (1) the support-chat button (components/chat/support-chat-widget.tsx, fixed bottom-right) renders on production and on NO preview, because SUPPORT_CHAT is set only in Vercel's Production environment and #2423 removed the NEXT_PUBLIC_ fallback that previews used to read; (2) Vera's edge tab (components/layout/edge-pill.tsx, the launcher's fallback at fixed top-1/2 right-0) renders on the preview and NOT on production. Member surfaces differ by ~900 px for the same two reasons.

CONSEQUENCE. pr-compare photographs a PR's preview, so a production-sourced baseline is red by ~2,500 px on every public page whatever the PR does, and a preview-sourced baseline goes red the moment production and preview are made to agree. The committed set is preview-sourced as of ADR-1273; the 2026-08-31 note (#2329) that warned against production captures was right, for these two elements.

OWNER CONFIG, one value: set SUPPORT_CHAT=1 for the Preview environment in Vercel (Settings, Environment Variables), so previews carry the widget production carries and a preview capture stops encoding its absence. The widget-off state is what #2423's draft warning was about, and it is now the state every preview is in.

OPEN MECHANISM, agent work: why Vera's edge tab renders on the preview and not on production. Nothing in components/vera or lib/vera reads an environment variable; the launcher hides itself when a dock slot exists (vera-launcher.tsx, slotChecked) and falls back to the EdgePill otherwise, so the difference is in what the two deployments render around it. Measure it on a preview and on production with the same session before changing anything; then either make the two agree or mask the tab, never widen the 400 px budget.

── CONTROL READING 2026-09-08 04:26Z, pr-compare on #2469 with the preview-sourced set (job 101934960137): 136 passed / 8 failed / 28 skipped. Every public surface passes on both projects and every MOBILE shell surface passes, so the two environment-only elements above were the whole of the 128. The 8 that remain are the four DESKTOP shell surfaces in both skins: /feed 4,098-4,293 px, /settings 22,866-23,229, /nearby 15,315-15,351, /spaces/<slug>/manage 9,124-9,147. Desktop only means the right rail, which the mobile layout hides and which carries live widgets. That is the third class this row names (live data), now measured: the candidate fix is a mask over the rail's live widgets (GLOBAL_MASK_SELECTORS in test/e2e/surfaces.ts, or a data-visual-mask attribute on the rail), never a larger budget. The 28 skipped are the operator surfaces behind the role floor (HYG-027).

verify.evidence: 2026-09-08: crops of about--dawn-light-desktop rows 700-800 and 380-460, production capture 6374058e vs preview capture ec322387 (claude/live-212-preview-probe-lbhk4b): support button present only on production; edge tab present only on the preview. Closes when a preview capture and a production capture of the same main commit read 0 px on a public surface, or when the tab is masked and SUPPORT_CHAT is set for Preview.

entries.title: The not-found page emits both robots tags: noindex from the boundary and index, follow from the root layout default
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-09-08 while confirming LIVE-208 live: GET /this-path-does-not-exist answers 404 with the not-found body (the row's main claim, confirmed on production), and its head carries TWO robots directives: <meta name="robots" content="noindex"/> from the not-found boundary and <meta name="robots" content="index, follow"/> from the root layout's default metadata. Crawlers resolve conflicting directives to the most restrictive, so noindex wins and this is not a live SEO defect; but the head is not clean and LIVE-208's second sentence ("the head still says index, follow") is still literally true. Override the root default on the not-found path so the head carries one directive. Probe: a source-shape test that the not-found route's metadata sets robots explicitly, and a check:seo arm if it can read the artifact.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-08: production fetch of a dead path shows both meta robots tags in the head (other session's reading, 03:55Z).
